6.msb: So without delay, the king commanded that John’s head be brought in. He sent an executioner, who went and beheaded him in the prison.
6.kjv: And immediately the king sent an executioner, and commanded his head to be brought: and he went and beheaded him in the prison,
6.blb: And immediately the king, having sent an executioner, commanded to be brought his head. And having gone away, he beheaded him in the prison
6.bbe: And straight away the king sent out one of his armed men, and gave him an order to come back with the head: and he went and took off John's head in prison,

6.msb: The man brought John’s head on a platter and presented it to the girl, who gave it to her mother.
6.kjv: And brought his head in a charger, and gave it to the damsel: and the damsel gave it to her mother.
6.blb: and brought his head upon a platter and gave it to the girl, and the girl gave it to her mother.
6.bbe: And came back with the head on a plate, and gave it to the girl; and the girl gave it to her mother.

6.msb: When John’s disciples heard about this, they came and took his body and placed it in a tomb.
6.kjv: And when his disciples heard of it, they came and took up his corpse, and laid it in a tomb.
6.blb: And having heard of it, his disciples came and took up his body and laid it in a tomb.
6.bbe: And when his disciples had news of it, they came and took up his body, and put it in its last resting-place.

6.msb: Meanwhile, the apostles gathered around Jesus and brought Him news of all they had done and taught.
6.kjv: And the apostles gathered themselves together unto Jesus, and told him all things, both what they had done, and what they had taught.
6.blb: And the apostles are gathered together to Jesus, and they reported to Him all things, as much as they did and as much as they taught.
6.bbe: And the twelve came together to Jesus; and they gave him an account of all the things they had done, and all they had been teaching.
6.heading: The Feeding of the Five Thousand

6.msb: And He said to them, “Come with Me privately to a solitary place, and let us rest for a while.” For many people were coming and going, and they did not even have time to eat.
6.kjv: And he said unto them, Come ye yourselves apart into a desert place, and rest a while: for there were many coming and going, and they had no leisure so much as to eat.
6.blb: And He said to them, “Come, you yourselves, apart to a wilderness place, and rest a little.” For those coming and those going were many, and not even were they having opportunity to eat.
6.bbe: And he said to them, Come away by yourselves to a quiet place, and take a rest for a time. Because there were a great number coming and going, and they had no time even for food.

6.msb: So they went away in the boat by themselves to a solitary place.
6.kjv: And they departed into a desert place by ship privately.
6.blb: And they went away in the boat to a wilderness place by themselves.
6.bbe: And they went away in the boat to a waste place by themselves.

6.msb: But many people saw them leaving and recognized Him. They ran together on foot from all the towns and arrived before them.
6.kjv: And the people saw them departing, and many knew him, and ran afoot thither out of all cities, and outwent them, and came together unto him.
6.blb: And many saw them going and recognized, and they ran together there on foot from all the cities and went before them.
6.bbe: And the people saw them going, and a number of them, having knowledge who they were, went running there together on foot from all the towns, and got there before them.

6.msb: When Jesus stepped ashore and saw a large crowd, He had compassion on them, because they were like sheep without a shepherd. And He began to teach them many things.
6.kjv: And Jesus, when he came out, saw much people, and was moved with compassion toward them, because they were as sheep not having a shepherd: and he began to teach them many things.
6.blb: And having gone out, He saw a great crowd and was moved with compassion toward them, because they were like sheep not having a shepherd. And He began to teach them many things.
6.bbe: And he got out, and saw a great mass of people, and he had pity on them, because they were like sheep without a keeper: and he gave them teaching about a number of things.

6.msb: By now the hour was already late. So the disciples came to Jesus and said, “This is a desolate place, and the hour is already late.
6.kjv: And when the day was now far spent, his disciples came unto him, and said, This is a desert place, and now the time is far passed:
6.blb: And the hour already being late, having come to Him, His disciples were saying, “The place is a wilderness, and the hour already is late.
6.bbe: And at the end of the day, his disciples came to him and said, This place is waste land, and it is late:

6.msb: Dismiss the crowd so they can go to the surrounding countryside and villages and buy themselves food, for they have nothing to eat.”
6.kjv: Send them away, that they may go into the country round about, and into the villages, and buy themselves bread: for they have nothing to eat.
6.blb: Dismiss them so that, having gone to the surrounding fields and villages, they might buy for themselves something to eat.”
6.bbe: Send them away, so that they may go into the country and small towns round about, and get some food for themselves.

6.msb: But Jesus told them, “You give them something to eat.” They asked Him, “Should we go out and spend two hundred denarii to give all of them bread to eat?”
6.kjv: He answered and said unto them, Give ye them to eat. And they say unto him, Shall we go and buy two hundred pennyworth of bread, and give them to eat?
6.blb: But answering, He said to them, “You give to them to eat.” And they say to Him, “Having gone away, shall we buy two hundred denarii of loaves and give them to eat?”
6.bbe: But he said to them in answer, Give them food yourselves. And they said to him, Are we to go and get bread for two hundred pence, and give it to them?

6.msb: “Go and see how many loaves you have,” He told them. And after checking, they said, “Five—and two fish.”
6.kjv: He saith unto them, How many loaves have ye? go and see. And when they knew, they say, Five, and two fishes.
6.blb: And He says to them, “How many loaves do you have? Go, see.” And having known, they say, “Five, and two fish.”
6.bbe: And he said to them, How much bread have you? go and see. And when they had seen, they said, Five cakes of bread and two fishes.

6.msb: Then Jesus directed them to have the people sit in groups on the green grass.
6.kjv: And he commanded them to make all sit down by companies upon the green grass.
6.blb: And He commanded them to make them all recline, groups by groups, on the green grass.
6.bbe: And he made them all be seated in groups on the green grass.

6.msb: So they sat down in groups of hundreds and fifties.
6.kjv: And they sat down in ranks, by hundreds, and by fifties.
6.blb: And they sat down groups by groups, by hundreds and by fifties.
6.bbe: And they were placed in groups, by hundreds and by fifties.

6.msb: Taking the five loaves and the two fish and looking up to heaven, Jesus spoke a blessing and broke the loaves. Then He gave them to His disciples to set before the people. And He divided the two fish among them all.
6.kjv: And when he had taken the five loaves and the two fishes, he looked up to heaven, and blessed, and brake the loaves, and gave them to his disciples to set before them; and the two fishes divided he among them all.
6.blb: And having taken the five loaves and the two fish, having looked up to the heaven, He blessed and broke the loaves. And He was giving them to His disciples, so that they might set before them. And He divided the two fish among all.
6.bbe: And he took the five cakes of bread and the two fishes and, looking up to heaven, he said words of blessing over them; and when the cakes were broken, he gave them to the disciples to put before the people; and he made division of the two fishes among them all.

6.msb: They all ate and were satisfied,
6.kjv: And they did all eat, and were filled.
6.blb: And all ate and were satisfied.
6.bbe: And they all took of the food and had enough.

6.msb: and the disciples picked up twelve basketfuls of broken pieces of bread and fish.
6.kjv: And they took up twelve baskets full of the fragments, and of the fishes.
6.blb: And they took up twelve hand-baskets full of fragments, and of the fish.
6.bbe: And they took up twelve baskets full of the broken bits and of the fishes.

6.msb: And there were five thousand men who had eaten the loaves.
6.kjv: And they that did eat of the loaves were about five thousand men.
6.blb: And those having eaten of the loaves were five thousand men.
6.bbe: And those who took of the bread were five thousand men.

6.msb: Immediately Jesus made His disciples get into the boat and go on ahead of Him to Bethsaida, while He dismissed the crowd.
6.kjv: And straightway he constrained his disciples to get into the ship, and to go to the other side before unto Bethsaida, while he sent away the people.
6.blb: And immediately He compelled His disciples to enter into the boat and to go before Him to the other side, to Bethsaida, until He dismisses the crowd.
6.bbe: And straight away he made his disciples get into the boat, and go before him to the other side to Beth-saida, while he himself sent the people away.
6.heading: Jesus Walks on Water

6.msb: After bidding them farewell, He went up on the mountain to pray.
6.kjv: And when he had sent them away, he departed into a mountain to pray.
6.blb: And having taken leave of them, He went away to the mountain to pray.
6.bbe: And after he had sent them away, he went up into a mountain for prayer.

6.msb: When evening came, the boat was in the middle of the sea, and Jesus was alone on land.
6.kjv: And when even was come, the ship was in the midst of the sea, and he alone on the land.
6.blb: And evening having come, the boat was in the midst of the sea, and He alone on the land.
6.bbe: And by evening, the boat was in the middle of the sea, and he by himself on the land.

6.msb: He could see that the disciples were straining to row, because the wind was against them. About the fourth watch of the night, Jesus went out to them, walking on the sea. He intended to pass by them,
6.kjv: And he saw them toiling in rowing; for the wind was contrary unto them: and about the fourth watch of the night he cometh unto them, walking upon the sea, and would have passed by them.
6.blb: And having seen them straining in the rowing—for the wind was contrary to them—about the fourth watch of the night, He goes to them, walking on the sea, and He was wanting to pass by them.
6.bbe: And seeing that they had trouble in getting their boat through the water, because the wind was against them, about the fourth watch of the night he came to them, walking on the sea; and he would have gone past them;

6.msb: but when they saw Him walking on the sea, they cried out, thinking He was a ghost—
6.kjv: But when they saw him walking upon the sea, they supposed it had been a spirit, and cried out:
6.blb: And having seen Him walking on the sea, they thought that He is a ghost, and they cried out.
6.bbe: But they, when they saw him walking on the sea, took him for a spirit, and gave a loud cry:

6.msb: for they all saw Him and were terrified. But Jesus spoke up at once: “Take courage! It is I. Do not be afraid.”
6.kjv: For they all saw him, and were troubled. And immediately he talked with them, and saith unto them, Be of good cheer: it is I; be not afraid.
6.blb: For all saw Him and were troubled. But immediately He spoke with them, and He says to them, “Take courage! I am He! Do not be afraid.”
6.bbe: For they all saw him, and were troubled. But straight away he said to them, Take heart, it is I, have no fear.

6.msb: Then He climbed into the boat with them, and the wind died down. And the disciples were utterly astounded beyond measure, and were marveling.
6.kjv: And he went up unto them into the ship; and the wind ceased: and they were sore amazed in themselves beyond measure, and wondered.
6.blb: And He went up to them into the boat, and the wind abated. And exceedingly in abundance in themselves, they were amazed.
6.bbe: And he went to them into the boat, and the wind went down, and they were full of wonder in themselves;

6.msb: For they had not understood about the loaves because their hearts had been hardened.
6.kjv: For they considered not the miracle of the loaves: for their heart was hardened.
6.blb: For they did not understand about the loaves, but their heart was hardened.
6.bbe: For it was not clear to them about the bread; but their hearts were hard.

6.msb: When they had crossed over, they came to the land of Gennesaret and moored the boat.
6.kjv: And when they had passed over, they came into the land of Gennesaret, and drew to the shore.
6.blb: And having crossed over, they came to the land, to Gennesaret, and they drew to shore.
6.bbe: And when they had gone across, they came to Gennesaret, and got their boat to land.
6.heading: Jesus Heals at Gennesaret

6.msb: As soon as they got out of the boat, the people recognized Jesus
6.kjv: And when they were come out of the ship, straightway they knew him,
6.blb: And on their having come out of the boat, immediately having recognized Him,
6.bbe: And when they had got out of the boat, the people quickly had news of him,

6.msb: and ran through that whole surrounding region, carrying the sick on mats to wherever they heard He was.
6.kjv: And ran through that whole region round about, and began to carry about in beds those that were sick, where they heard he was.
6.blb: they ran around all that region, and they began to carry around on mats those being ill to where they were hearing that He is.
6.bbe: And went running through all the country round about, and took on their beds those who were ill, to where it was said that he was.

6.msb: And wherever He went—villages and towns and countrysides—they laid the sick in the marketplaces and begged Him just to let them touch the fringe of His cloak. And all who touched Him were healed.
6.kjv: And whithersoever he entered, into villages, or cities, or country, they laid the sick in the streets, and besought him that they might touch if it were but the border of his garment: and as many as touched him were made whole.
6.blb: And wherever He was entering into villages or into cities or into fields, they were laying the ailing in the marketplaces and were imploring Him that they might only touch the fringe of His garment. And as many as touched Him were saved.
6.bbe: And wherever he went, into small towns, or great towns, or into the country, they took those who were ill into the market-places, requesting him that they might put their hands even on the edge of his robe: and all those who did so were made well.

7.msb: Then the Pharisees and some of the scribes who had come from Jerusalem gathered around Jesus.
7.kjv: Then came together unto him the Pharisees, and certain of the scribes, which came from Jerusalem.
7.blb: And the Pharisees and some of the scribes having come from Jerusalem are gathered together to Him.
7.bbe: And there came together to him the Pharisees and certain of the scribes who had come from Jerusalem,
7.heading: The Tradition of the Elders

7.msb: And seeing some of His disciples eating with hands that were defiled (that is, unwashed), they found fault.
7.kjv: And when they saw some of his disciples eat bread with defiled, that is to say, with unwashen, hands, they found fault.
7.blb: And they had seen some of His disciples, that with defiled hands—that is, unwashed—they are eating the loaves.
7.bbe: And had seen that some of his disciples took their bread with unclean, that is, unwashed, hands.

7.msb: Now in holding to the tradition of the elders, the Pharisees and all the Jews do not eat until they wash their hands ceremonially.
7.kjv: For the Pharisees, and all the Jews, except they wash their hands oft, eat not, holding the tradition of the elders.
7.blb: (For the Pharisees and all the Jews do not eat unless they wash the hands to the fist, holding to the tradition of the elders;
7.bbe: Now the Pharisees, and all the Jews, do not take food without washing their hands with care, keeping the old rule which has been handed down to them:

7.msb: And on returning from the market, they do not eat unless they wash. And there are many other traditions for them to observe, including the washing of cups, pitchers, kettles, and couches for dining.
7.kjv: And when they come from the market, except they wash, they eat not. And many other things there be, which they have received to hold, as the washing of cups, and pots, brasen vessels, and of tables.
7.blb: and coming from the marketplace, they do not eat unless they immerse; and there are many other things that they received to hold to—immersions of cups and pitchers and bronze vessels and couches.)
7.bbe: And when they come from the market-place, they take no food till their hands are washed; and a number of other orders there are, which have been handed down to them to keep — washings of cups and pots and brass vessels.

7.msb: So the Pharisees and scribes questioned Jesus: “Why do Your disciples not walk according to the tradition of the elders? Instead, they eat with unwashed hands.”
7.kjv: Then the Pharisees and scribes asked him, Why walk not thy disciples according to the tradition of the elders, but eat bread with unwashen hands?
7.blb: And the Pharisees and the scribes questioned Him, “Why do Your disciples not walk according to the tradition of the elders, but eat the bread with defiled hands?”
7.bbe: And the Pharisees and the scribes put the question to him, Why do your disciples not keep the rules of the fathers, but take their bread with unwashed hands?

7.msb: Jesus answered them, “Isaiah prophesied correctly about you hypocrites, as it is written: ‘These people honor Me with their lips, but their hearts are far from Me.
7.kjv: He answered and said unto them, Well hath Esaias prophesied of you hypocrites, as it is written, This people honoureth me with their lips, but their heart is far from me.
7.blb: And He said to them, “Isaiah prophesied correctly about you hypocrites, as it has been written: ‘This people honors Me with the lips, but their heart is kept far away from Me;
7.bbe: And he said, Well did Isaiah say of you, you false ones: These people give me honour with their lips, but their heart is far from me.

7.msb: They worship Me in vain; they teach as doctrine the precepts of men.’
7.kjv: Howbeit in vain do they worship me, teaching for doctrines the commandments of men.
7.blb: and in vain they worship Me, teaching as teachings the precepts of men.’
7.bbe: But their worship is to no purpose, while they give as their teaching the rules of men.

7.msb: You have disregarded the commandment of God to keep the tradition of men—the washing of pitchers and cups, and many other similar things you do.”
7.kjv: For laying aside the commandment of God, ye hold the tradition of men, as the washing of pots and cups: and many other such like things ye do.
7.blb: Having left the commandment of God, you hold to the tradition of men.”
7.bbe: For, turning away from the law of God, you keep the rules of men.

7.msb: He went on to say, “You neatly set aside the command of God to maintain your own tradition.
7.kjv: And he said unto them, Full well ye reject the commandment of God, that ye may keep your own tradition.
7.blb: And He was saying to them, “Nobly do you set aside the commandment of God so that you might keep your tradition.
7.bbe: And he said to them, Truly you put on one side the law of God, so that you may keep the rules which have been handed down to you.

7.msb: For Moses said, ‘Honor your father and your mother’ and ‘Anyone who curses his father or mother must be put to death.’
7.kjv: For Moses said, Honour thy father and thy mother; and, Whoso curseth father or mother, let him die the death:
7.blb: For Moses said, ‘Honor your father and your mother,’ and, ‘The one speaking evil of father or mother, in death let him end.’
7.bbe: For Moses said, Give honour to your father and mother, and, He who says evil of father or mother, let him have the punishment of death:

7.msb: But you say that if a man says to his father or mother, ‘Whatever you would have received from me is Corban’ (that is, a gift devoted to God),
7.kjv: But ye say, If a man shall say to his father or mother, It is Corban, that is to say, a gift, by whatsoever thou mightest be profited by me; he shall be free.
7.blb: But you say that if a man might say to the father or to the mother, ‘Whatever you might be profited from me is Corban’ (that is, a gift),
7.bbe: But you say, If a man says to his father or his mother, That by which you might have had profit from me is Corban, that is to say, Given to God,

7.msb: he is no longer permitted to do anything for his father or mother.
7.kjv: And ye suffer him no more to do ought for his father or his mother;
7.blb: no longer do you permit him to do anything for the father or for the mother,
7.bbe: You no longer let him do anything for his father or his mother;

7.msb: Thus you nullify the word of God by the tradition you have handed down. And you do so in many such matters.”
7.kjv: Making the word of God of none effect through your tradition, which ye have delivered: and many such like things do ye.
7.blb: making void the word of God for your tradition, which you delivered. And you do many things as such.”
7.bbe: Making the word of God of no effect by your rule, which you have given: and a number of other such things you do.

7.msb: Once again Jesus called the whole crowd to Him and said, “All of you, listen to Me and understand:
7.kjv: And when he had called all the people unto him, he said unto them, Hearken unto me every one of you, and understand:
7.blb: And having summoned the crowd again, He was saying to them, “Hear Me, all, and understand:
7.bbe: And turning to the people again, he said to them, Give ear to me all of you, and let my words be clear to you:
7.heading: What Defiles a Man

7.msb: Nothing that enters a man from the outside can defile him; but the things that come out of a man, these are what defile him.
7.kjv: There is nothing from without a man, that entering into him can defile him: but the things which come out of him, those are they that defile the man.
7.blb: There is nothing from outside the man entering into him that is able to defile him; but the things proceeding out of the man are the things defiling the man.”
7.bbe: There is nothing outside the man which, going into him, is able to make him unclean: but the things which come out of the man are those which make the man unclean.

7.msb: If anyone has ears to hear, let him hear.”
7.kjv: If any man have ears to hear, let him hear.

7.msb: After Jesus had left the crowd and gone into the house, His disciples inquired about the parable.
7.kjv: And when he was entered into the house from the people, his disciples asked him concerning the parable.
7.blb: And when He entered into the house from the crowd, His disciples were questioning Him about the parable.
7.bbe: And when he had gone into the house away from all the people, his disciples put questions to him about the saying.

7.msb: “Are you still so dull?” He asked. “Do you not understand? Nothing that enters a man from the outside can defile him,
7.kjv: And he saith unto them, Are ye so without understanding also? Do ye not perceive, that whatsoever thing from without entereth into the man, it cannot defile him;
7.blb: And He says to them, “Thus are you also without understanding? Do you not understand that everything entering into the man from outside is not able to defile him,
7.bbe: And he said to them, Have even you so little wisdom? Do you not see that whatever goes into a man from outside is not able to make him unclean,

7.msb: because it does not enter his heart, but it goes into the stomach and then is eliminated, thus purifying all foods.”
7.kjv: Because it entereth not into his heart, but into the belly, and goeth out into the draught, purging all meats?
7.blb: because it does not enter into his heart, but into the belly, and goes out into the sewer?”—thus purifying all the foods.
7.bbe: Because it goes not into the heart but into the stomach, and goes out with the waste? He said this, making all food clean.

7.msb: He continued: “What comes out of a man, that is what defiles him.
7.kjv: And he said, That which cometh out of the man, that defileth the man.
7.blb: And He was saying, “That which is proceeding out of the man, that defiles the man.
7.bbe: And he said, That which comes out of the man, that makes the man unclean.

7.msb: For from within the hearts of men come evil thoughts, adultery, sexual immorality, murder, theft,
7.kjv: For from within, out of the heart of men, proceed evil thoughts, adulteries, fornications, murders,
7.blb: For from within, out of the heart of men, proceed evil reasonings, sexual immorality, thefts, murders, adulteries,
7.bbe: Because from inside, from the heart of men, come evil thoughts and unclean pleasures,

7.msb: greed, wickedness, deceit, debauchery, envy, slander, arrogance, and foolishness.
7.kjv: Thefts, covetousness, wickedness, deceit, lasciviousness, an evil eye, blasphemy, pride, foolishness:
7.blb: covetous desires, wickednesses, deceit, sensuality, an evil eye, slander, pride, foolishness.
7.bbe: The taking of goods and of life, broken faith between husband and wife, the desire of wealth, wrongdoing, deceit, sins of the flesh, an evil eye, angry words, pride, foolish acts:

7.msb: All these evils come from within, and these are what defile a man.”
7.kjv: All these evil things come from within, and defile the man.
7.blb: All these evils proceed from within, and they defile the man.”
7.bbe: All these evil things come from inside, and make the man unclean.

7.msb: Jesus left that place and went to the region of Tyre and Sidon. Not wanting anyone to know He was there, He entered a house, but was unable to escape their notice.
7.kjv: And from thence he arose, and went into the borders of Tyre and Sidon, and entered into an house, and would have no man know it: but he could not be hid.
7.blb: And from there having risen up, He went away into the borders of Tyre. And having entered into a house, He was wanting no one to know it, and He was not able to be hidden.
7.bbe: And he went away from there to the country of Tyre and Sidon. And he went into a house, desiring that no man might have knowledge of it: and he was not able to keep it secret.
7.heading: The Faith of the Gentile Woman

7.msb: For a woman whose little daughter had an unclean spirit heard about Jesus, and she came and fell at His feet.
7.kjv: For a certain woman, whose young daughter had an unclean spirit, heard of him, and came and fell at his feet:
7.blb: But immediately, having heard about Him, a woman whose little daughter had an unclean spirit, having come, fell at His feet.
7.bbe: But a woman, whose little daughter had an unclean spirit, having had news of him, came straight away and went down at his feet.

7.msb: Now she was a Greek woman of Syrophoenician origin, and she kept asking Jesus to drive the demon out of her daughter.
7.kjv: The woman was a Greek, a Syrophenician by nation; and she besought him that he would cast forth the devil out of her daughter.
7.blb: Now the woman was a Greek, Syrophoenician by race, and she was asking Him that He might cast the demon out of her daughter.
7.bbe: Now the woman was a Greek, a Syro-phoenician by birth: and she made a request to him that he would send the evil spirit out of her daughter.

7.msb: “First let the children have their fill,” Jesus said. “For it is not right to take the children’s bread and toss it to the dogs.”
7.kjv: But Jesus said unto her, Let the children first be filled: for it is not meet to take the children’s bread, and to cast it unto the dogs.
7.blb: And He was saying to her, “Permit the children first to be satisfied; for it is not good to take the bread of the children and to cast it to the dogs.”
7.bbe: And he said to her, Let the children first have their food: for it is not right to take the children's bread and give it to the dogs.

7.msb: “Yes, Lord,” she replied, “for even the dogs under the table eat the children’s crumbs.”
7.kjv: And she answered and said unto him, Yes, Lord: yet the dogs under the table eat of the children’s crumbs.
7.blb: But she answered, and she says to Him, “Yes, Lord, even the dogs under the table eat from the crumbs of the children.”
7.bbe: But she said to him in answer, Yes, Lord: even the dogs under the table take the bits dropped by the children.

7.msb: Then Jesus told her, “Because of this answer, you may go. The demon has left your daughter.”
7.kjv: And he said unto her, For this saying go thy way; the devil is gone out of thy daughter.
7.blb: And He said to her, “Because of this word, go; the demon has gone forth out of your daughter.”
7.bbe: And he said to her, For this saying go your way; the evil spirit has gone out of your daughter.

7.msb: And she went home and found the demon was gone, and her daughter was lying on the bed.
7.kjv: And when she was come to her house, she found the devil gone out, and her daughter laid upon the bed.
7.blb: And having gone away to her house, she found the child laid on the bed, and the demon having gone out.
7.bbe: And she went away to her house, and saw the child on the bed, and the evil spirit gone out.

7.msb: Then Jesus left the region of Tyre and Sidon and went toward the Sea of Galilee and into the region of the Decapolis.
7.kjv: And again, departing from the coasts of Tyre and Sidon, he came unto the sea of Galilee, through the midst of the coasts of Decapolis.
7.blb: And again, having gone out from the borders of Tyre, He went through Sidon to the Sea of Galilee, through the midst of the borders of the Decapolis.
7.bbe: And again he went out from Tyre, and came through Sidon to the sea of Galilee, through the country of Decapolis.
7.heading: The Deaf and Mute Man

7.msb: Some people brought to Him a man who was deaf and hardly able to speak, and they begged Jesus to place His hand on him.
7.kjv: And they bring unto him one that was deaf, and had an impediment in his speech; and they beseech him to put his hand upon him.
7.blb: And they bring to Him a deaf man (and he spoke with difficulty), and they implore Him that He might lay the hand on him.
7.bbe: And they came to him with one who had no power of hearing and had trouble in talking; and they made a request to him to put his hands on him.

7.msb: So Jesus took him aside privately, away from the crowd, and put His fingers into the man’s ears. Then He spit and touched the man’s tongue.
7.kjv: And he took him aside from the multitude, and put his fingers into his ears, and he spit, and touched his tongue;
7.blb: And having taken him away from the crowd by himself, He put His fingers into his ears. And having spit, He touched his tongue.
7.bbe: And he took him on one side from the people privately, and put his fingers into his ears, and he put water from his mouth on the man's tongue with his finger;

7.msb: And looking up to heaven, He sighed deeply and said to him, “Ephphatha!” (which means, “Be opened!”).
7.kjv: And looking up to heaven, he sighed, and saith unto him, Ephphatha, that is, Be opened.
7.blb: And having looked up to heaven, He sighed deeply, and He says to him, “Ephphatha!” (that is, “Be opened!”)
7.bbe: And looking up to heaven, he took a deep breath, and said to him, Ephphatha, that is, Be open.

7.msb: Immediately the man’s ears were opened and his tongue was released, and he began to speak plainly.
7.kjv: And straightway his ears were opened, and the string of his tongue was loosed, and he spake plain.
7.blb: And his ears were opened, and immediately the band of his tongue was loosed, and he was speaking rightly.
7.bbe: And his ears became open, and the band of his tongue was made loose, and his words became clear.

7.msb: Jesus ordered them not to tell anyone. But the more He ordered them, the more widely they proclaimed it.
7.kjv: And he charged them that they should tell no man: but the more he charged them, so much the more a great deal they published it;
7.blb: And He instructed them that they should tell no one. But as much as He was instructing them, they were proclaiming it more abundantly.
7.bbe: And he gave them orders not to give news of it to anyone; but the more he made this request, so much the more they made it public.

7.msb: The people were utterly astonished and said, “He has done all things well! He makes even the deaf hear and the mute speak!”
7.kjv: And were beyond measure astonished, saying, He hath done all things well: he maketh both the deaf to hear, and the dumb to speak.
7.blb: And they were astonished above measure, saying, “He has done all things well! He makes both the deaf to hear and the mute to speak!”
7.bbe: And they were overcome with wonder, saying, He has done all things well: he even gives back the power of hearing and the power of talking to those who have been without them.

8.msb: In those days the crowd became very large, and they had nothing to eat. Jesus called His disciples to Him and said,
8.kjv: In those days the multitude being very great, and having nothing to eat, Jesus called his disciples unto him, and saith unto them,
8.blb: In those days, the crowd again being great and not having what they might eat, having summoned the disciples, He says to them,
8.bbe: In those days again, when there was a great mass of people and they had no food, he made his disciples come to him and said to them,
8.heading: The Feeding of the Four Thousand

8.msb: “I have compassion for this crowd, because they have already been with Me three days and have nothing to eat.
8.kjv: I have compassion on the multitude, because they have now been with me three days, and have nothing to eat:
8.blb: “I have compassion toward the crowd, because already three days they continue with Me and have nothing that they might eat.
8.bbe: I have pity for these people because they have been with me now three days, and have no food;

8.msb: If I send them home hungry, they will faint along the way. For some of them have come a great distance.”
8.kjv: And if I send them away fasting to their own houses, they will faint by the way: for divers of them came from far.
8.blb: And if I shall dismiss them hungry to their house, they will faint on the way. And some of them have come from afar.”
8.bbe: If I send them away to their houses with no food, they will be overcome by weariness on the way; and some of them have come from far.

8.msb: His disciples replied, “Where in this desolate place could anyone find enough bread to feed all these people?”
8.kjv: And his disciples answered him, From whence can a man satisfy these men with bread here in the wilderness?
8.blb: And His disciples answered Him, “From where will anyone be able to satisfy these with loaves here in a wilderness?”
8.bbe: And his disciples said in answer, How will it be possible to get enough bread for these men here in a waste place?

8.msb: “How many loaves do you have?” Jesus asked. “Seven,” they replied.
8.kjv: And he asked them, How many loaves have ye? And they said, Seven.
8.blb: And He was asking them, “How many loaves do you have?” And they said, “Seven.”
8.bbe: And he put the question, How much bread have you? And they said, Seven cakes.

8.msb: And He instructed the crowd to sit down on the ground. Then He took the seven loaves, gave thanks and broke them, and gave them to His disciples to set before the people. And they distributed them to the crowd.
8.kjv: And he commanded the people to sit down on the ground: and he took the seven loaves, and gave thanks, and brake, and gave to his disciples to set before them; and they did set them before the people.
8.blb: And He commands the crowd to recline on the ground. And having taken the seven loaves, having given thanks, He broke them and was giving them to His disciples to set before them. And they set them before the crowd.
8.bbe: And he made the people be seated on the earth: and he took the seven cakes and, having given praise, he gave the broken bread to his disciples to put before them; and they put it before the people.

8.msb: They also had a few small fish, and Jesus blessed them and ordered that these be set before them as well.
8.kjv: And they had a few small fishes: and he blessed, and commanded to set them also before them.
8.blb: And they had a few small fish. And having blessed them, He said to set before them these also.
8.bbe: And they had some small fishes; and blessing them he had them put before the people in the same way.

8.msb: The people ate and were satisfied, and the disciples picked up seven basketfuls of broken pieces that were left over.
8.kjv: So they did eat, and were filled: and they took up of the broken meat that was left seven baskets.
8.blb: And they ate and were satisfied, and they took up an abundance of fragments—seven baskets.
8.bbe: And they took the food, and had enough; and they took up seven baskets full of the broken bits.

8.msb: And about four thousand men who had eaten were present. And when Jesus had dismissed the crowd,
8.kjv: And they that had eaten were about four thousand: and he sent them away.
8.blb: And there were about four thousand. And He dismissed them.
8.bbe: And there were about four thousand people: and he sent them away.

8.msb: He immediately got into the boat with His disciples and went to the district of Dalmanutha.
8.kjv: And straightway he entered into a ship with his disciples, and came into the parts of Dalmanutha.
8.blb: And immediately, having entered into the boat with His disciples, He went to the parts of Dalmanutha.
8.bbe: And he got into the boat with his disciples straight away, and came into the country of Dalmanutha.

8.msb: Then the Pharisees came and began to argue with Jesus, testing Him by demanding from Him a sign from heaven.
8.kjv: And the Pharisees came forth, and began to question with him, seeking of him a sign from heaven, tempting him.
8.blb: And the Pharisees came out and began to dispute with Him, seeking from Him a sign from heaven, testing Him.
8.bbe: And the Pharisees came out and put questions to him, requesting from him a sign from heaven, testing him.
8.heading: The Demand for a Sign

8.msb: Jesus sighed deeply in His spirit and said, “Why does this generation seek after a sign? Truly I tell you, no sign will be given to this generation.”
8.kjv: And he sighed deeply in his spirit, and saith, Why doth this generation seek after a sign? verily I say unto you, There shall no sign be given unto this generation.
8.blb: And having sighed deeply in His spirit, He says, “Why does this generation seek a sign? Truly I say to you, no sign will be given to this generation.”
8.bbe: And he was very sad in spirit, and said, Why is this generation looking for a sign? truly, I say to you, No sign will be given to this generation.

8.msb: And He left them, got back into the boat, and crossed to the other side.
8.kjv: And he left them, and entering into the ship again departed to the other side.
8.blb: And having left them, having embarked again, He went away to the other side.
8.bbe: And he went away from them, and again got into the boat and went across to the other side.

8.msb: Now the disciples had forgotten to take bread, except for one loaf they had with them in the boat.
8.kjv: Now the disciples had forgotten to take bread, neither had they in the ship with them more than one loaf.
8.blb: And they forgot to take loaves, and except one loaf they had nothing with them in the boat.
8.bbe: And they had taken no thought to get bread; and they had only one cake of bread with them in the boat.
8.heading: The Leaven of the Pharisees and of Herod

8.msb: “Watch out!” He cautioned them. “Beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and of Herod.”
8.kjv: And he charged them, saying, Take heed, beware of the leaven of the Pharisees, and of the leaven of Herod.
8.blb: And He was instructing them, saying, “Watch! Take heed of the leaven of the Pharisees and the leaven of Herod.”
8.bbe: And he said to them, Take care to be on the watch against the leaven of the Pharisees and the leaven of Herod.

8.msb: So they began to discuss this with one another, saying, “It is because we have no bread.”
8.kjv: And they reasoned among themselves, saying, It is because we have no bread.
8.blb: And they were reasoning with one another because they had no loaves.
8.bbe: And they said to one another, We have no bread.

8.msb: Aware of their conversation, Jesus asked them, “Why are you debating about having no bread? Do you still not see or understand? Do you still have such hard hearts?
8.kjv: And when Jesus knew it, he saith unto them, Why reason ye, because ye have no bread? perceive ye not yet, neither understand? have ye your heart yet hardened?
8.blb: And having known, He says to them, “Why do you reason that you have no loaves? Do you not yet perceive, nor do you understand? Do you have your heart hardened?
8.bbe: And Jesus, hearing it, said to them, Why are you reasoning among yourselves because you have no bread? do you still not see, and is it still not clear to you? are your hearts so hard?

8.msb: ‘Having eyes, do you not see? And having ears, do you not hear?’ And do you not remember?
8.kjv: Having eyes, see ye not? and having ears, hear ye not? and do ye not remember?
8.blb: ‘Having eyes, do you not see? And having ears, do you not hear?’ And do you not remember?
8.bbe: Having eyes, do you not see? and having ears, have you no hearing? and have you no memory?

8.msb: When I broke the five loaves for the five thousand, how many basketfuls of broken pieces did you collect?” “Twelve,” they answered.
8.kjv: When I brake the five loaves among five thousand, how many baskets full of fragments took ye up? They say unto him, Twelve.
8.blb: When I broke the five loaves for the five thousand, how many hand-baskets full of fragments did you take up?” They say to Him, “Twelve.”
8.bbe: When I made a division of the five cakes of bread among the five thousand, what number of baskets full of broken bits did you take up? They said to him, Twelve.

8.msb: “And when I broke the seven loaves for the four thousand, how many basketfuls of broken pieces did you collect?” “Seven,” they said.
8.kjv: And when the seven among four thousand, how many baskets full of fragments took ye up? And they said, Seven.
8.blb: “When also the seven were for the four thousand, how many baskets full of fragments did you take up?” And they said, “Seven.”
8.bbe: And when the seven among the four thousand, what number of baskets full of broken bits did you take up? And they said to him, Seven.

8.msb: Then He asked them, “How do you still not understand?”
8.kjv: And he said unto them, How is it that ye do not understand?
8.blb: And He was saying to them, “Do you not yet understand?”
8.bbe: And he said to them, Is it still not clear to you?

8.msb: When He arrived at Bethsaida, some people brought a blind man and begged Jesus to touch him.
8.kjv: And he cometh to Bethsaida; and they bring a blind man unto him, and besought him to touch him.
8.blb: And they come to Bethsaida. And they bring to Him a blind man and implore Him that He might touch him.
8.bbe: And they came to Beth-saida. And they took a blind man to him, requesting him to put his hands on him.
8.heading: The Blind Man at Bethsaida

8.msb: So He took the blind man by the hand and led him out of the village. Then He spit on the man’s eyes and placed His hands on him, asking if he could see anything.
8.kjv: And he took the blind man by the hand, and led him out of the town; and when he had spit on his eyes, and put his hands upon him, he asked him if he saw ought.
8.blb: And having taken hold of the hand of the blind man, He led him forth outside of the village. And having spit upon his eyes, having laid the hands upon him, He was asking him, “Do you see anything?”
8.bbe: And he took the blind man by the hand, and went with him out of the town; and when he had put water from his mouth on his eyes, and put his hands on him, he said, Do you see anything?

8.msb: The man looked up and said, “I can see the people, but they look like trees walking around.”
8.kjv: And he looked up, and said, I see men as trees, walking.
8.blb: And having looked up, he was saying, “I see the men, because I see them as trees walking.”
8.bbe: And looking up, he said, I see men; I see them like trees, walking.

8.msb: Once again Jesus placed His hands on the man’s eyes and made him look up, and his sight was restored, and he could see everything clearly.
8.kjv: After that he put his hands again upon his eyes, and made him look up: and he was restored, and saw every man clearly.
8.blb: Then He laid the hands upon his eyes again, and he opened his eyes, and he was restored, and he was seeing everything clearly.
8.bbe: Then again he put his hands on his eyes; and looking hard, he was able to see, and saw all things clearly.

8.msb: Jesus sent him home and said, “Do not go back or tell anyone in the village.”
8.kjv: And he sent him away to his house, saying, Neither go into the town, nor tell it to any in the town.
8.blb: And He sent him to his house, saying, “Do not enter into the village.”
8.bbe: And he sent him away to his house, saying, Do not even go into the town.

8.msb: Then Jesus and His disciples went on to the villages around Caesarea Philippi. On the way, He questioned His disciples: “Who do people say I am?”
8.kjv: And Jesus went out, and his disciples, into the towns of Cæsarea Philippi: and by the way he asked his disciples, saying unto them, Whom do men say that I am?
8.blb: And Jesus and His disciples went out into the villages of Caesarea Philippi. And on the way, He was questioning His disciples, saying to them, “Who do men say I am?”
8.bbe: And Jesus went out, with his disciples, into the little towns round Caesarea Philippi; and on the way he put a question to his disciples, saying, Who do men say that I am?
8.heading: Peter’s Confession of Christ

8.msb: They replied, “Some say John the Baptist; others say Elijah; and still others, one of the prophets.”
8.kjv: And they answered, John the Baptist: but some say, Elias; and others, One of the prophets.
8.blb: And they spoke to Him, saying, “John the Baptist; and others, Elijah; and others, one of the prophets.”
8.bbe: And they made answer, John the Baptist; and others, Elijah; but others, One of the prophets.

8.msb: “But what about you?” Jesus asked. “Who do you say I am?” Peter answered, “You are the Christ.”
8.kjv: And he saith unto them, But whom say ye that I am? And Peter answereth and saith unto him, Thou art the Christ.
8.blb: And He was questioning them, “But you, who do you say I am?” Answering, Peter says to Him, “You are the Christ.”
8.bbe: And he said to them, But who do you say I am? Peter said in answer, You are the Christ.

8.msb: And Jesus warned them not to tell anyone about Him.
8.kjv: And he charged them that they should tell no man of him.
8.blb: And He warned them that they should tell no one concerning Him.
8.bbe: And he put them under orders not to say this of him to anyone.

8.msb: Then He began to teach them that the Son of Man must suffer many things and be rejected by the elders, chief priests, and scribes, and that He must be killed and after three days rise again.
8.kjv: And he began to teach them, that the Son of man must suffer many things, and be rejected of the elders, and of the chief priests, and scribes, and be killed, and after three days rise again.
8.blb: And He began to teach them that it is necessary for the Son of Man to suffer many things, and to be rejected by the elders and the chief priests and the scribes, and to be killed, and after three days to rise again.
8.bbe: And teaching them, he said that the Son of man would have to undergo much, and be hated by those in authority, and the chief priests, and the scribes, and be put to death, and after three days come back from the dead.
8.heading: Christ’s Passion Foretold

8.msb: He spoke this message quite frankly, and Peter took Him aside and began to rebuke Him.
8.kjv: And he spake that saying openly. And Peter took him, and began to rebuke him.
8.blb: And He was speaking openly the word. And Peter, having taken Him aside, began to rebuke Him.
8.bbe: And he said this openly. And Peter took him, and was protesting.

8.msb: But Jesus, turning and looking at His disciples, rebuked Peter and said, “Get behind Me, Satan! For you do not have in mind the things of God, but the things of men.”
8.kjv: But when he had turned about and looked on his disciples, he rebuked Peter, saying, Get thee behind me, Satan: for thou savourest not the things that be of God, but the things that be of men.
8.blb: But having turned and having seen His disciples, He rebuked Peter, and He says, “Get behind Me, Satan, because you do not have in mind the things of God, but the things of men.”
8.bbe: But he, turning about, and seeing his disciples, said sharply to Peter, Get out of my way, Satan: for your mind is not on the things of God, but on the things of men.

8.msb: Then Jesus called the crowd to Him along with His disciples, and He told them, “If anyone wants to follow after Me, he must deny himself and take up his cross and follow Me.
8.kjv: And when he had called the people unto him with his disciples also, he said unto them, Whosoever will come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross, and follow me.
8.blb: And having summoned the crowd with His disciples, He said to them, “If anyone wants to come after Me, let him deny himself and take up his cross and follow Me.
8.bbe: And turning to the mass of people with his disciples, he said to them, If any man has the desire to come after me, let him give up all other desires, and take up his cross and come after me.
8.heading: Take Up Your Cross

8.msb: For whoever wants to save his life will lose it, but whoever loses his life for My sake and for the gospel will save it.
8.kjv: For whosoever will save his life shall lose it; but whosoever shall lose his life for my sake and the gospel’s, the same shall save it.
8.blb: For whoever may want to save his life will lose it, but whoever will lose his life on account of Me and of the gospel, he will save it.
8.bbe: Whoever has a desire to keep his life, will have it taken from him; and whoever gives up his life because of me and the good news, will keep it.

8.msb: What shall it profit a man if he gains the whole world yet forfeits his soul?
8.kjv: For what shall it profit a man, if he shall gain the whole world, and lose his own soul?
8.blb: For what does it profit a man to gain the whole world and to lose his soul?
8.bbe: What profit has a man if he gets all the world with the loss of his life?

8.msb: Or what can a man give in exchange for his soul?
8.kjv: Or what shall a man give in exchange for his soul?
8.blb: For what shall a man give as an exchange for his soul?
8.bbe: And what would a man give in exchange for his life?

8.msb: If anyone is ashamed of Me and My words in this adulterous and sinful generation, the Son of Man will also be ashamed of him when He comes in His Father’s glory with the holy angels.”
8.kjv: Whosoever therefore shall be ashamed of me and of my words in this adulterous and sinful generation; of him also shall the Son of man be ashamed, when he cometh in the glory of his Father with the holy angels.
8.blb: For whoever may be ashamed of Me and My words in this adulterous and sinful generation, the Son of Man also will be ashamed of him when He shall come in the glory of His Father with the holy angels.”
8.bbe: Whoever has a feeling of shame because of me and my words in this false and evil generation, the Son of man will have a feeling of shame because of him, when he comes in the glory of his Father with the holy angels.

9.msb: Then Jesus said to them, “Truly I tell you, there are some standing here who will not taste death before they see the kingdom of God arrive with power.”
9.kjv: And he said unto them, Verily I say unto you, That there be some of them that stand here, which shall not taste of death, till they have seen the kingdom of God come with power.
9.blb: And He was saying to them, “Truly I say to you that there are some of those standing here who shall not taste of death until they shall see the kingdom of God having come in power.”
9.bbe: And he said to them, Truly I say to you, There are some here who will have no taste of death till they see the kingdom of God come with power.
9.heading: The Transfiguration

9.msb: After six days Jesus took with Him Peter, James, and John, and led them up a high mountain by themselves. There He was transfigured before them.
9.kjv: And after six days Jesus taketh with him Peter, and James, and John, and leadeth them up into an high mountain apart by themselves: and he was transfigured before them.
9.blb: And after six days, Jesus takes along Peter and James and John, and He brings them up onto a high mountain by themselves alone. And He was transfigured before them,
9.bbe: And after six days Jesus took with him Peter and James and John, and made them go up with him into a high mountain by themselves: and he was changed in form before them:

9.msb: His clothes became radiantly white as snow, brighter than any launderer on earth could bleach them.
9.kjv: And his raiment became shining, exceeding white as snow; so as no fuller on earth can white them.
9.blb: and His garments became radiant, exceedingly white, such as no launderer on the earth is able thus to whiten them.
9.bbe: And his clothing became shining, very white, as no cleaner on earth would make it.

9.msb: And Elijah and Moses appeared before them, talking with Jesus.
9.kjv: And there appeared unto them Elias with Moses: and they were talking with Jesus.
9.blb: And there appeared to them Elijah with Moses, and they were talking with Jesus.
9.bbe: And there came before them Elijah with Moses, and they were talking with Jesus.

9.msb: Peter said to Jesus, “Rabbi, it is good for us to be here. Let us put up three shelters—one for You, one for Moses, and one for Elijah.”
9.kjv: And Peter answered and said to Jesus, Master, it is good for us to be here: and let us make three tabernacles; one for thee, and one for Moses, and one for Elias.
9.blb: And answering, Peter says to Jesus, “Rabbi, it is good for us to be here. And let us make three tabernacles—one for You, and one for Moses, and one for Elijah.”
9.bbe: And Peter said to Jesus, Master, it is good for us to be here: and let us make three tents; one for you, one for Moses, and one for Elijah.

9.msb: For they were all so terrified that Peter did not know what else to say.
9.kjv: For he wist not what to say; for they were sore afraid.
9.blb: For he did not know what he should answer, for they were terrified.
9.bbe: Because he was not certain what to say, for they were in great fear.

9.msb: Then a cloud appeared and enveloped them, and a voice came from the cloud: “This is My beloved Son. Listen to Him!”
9.kjv: And there was a cloud that overshadowed them: and a voice came out of the cloud, saying, This is my beloved Son: hear him.
9.blb: And there was a cloud overshadowing them, and there was a voice out of the cloud: “This is My Son, the Beloved; listen to Him!”
9.bbe: And a cloud came over them; and a voice came out of the cloud, saying, This is my dearly loved Son, give ear to him.

9.msb: Suddenly, when they looked around, they saw no one with them except Jesus.
9.kjv: And suddenly, when they had looked round about, they saw no man any more, save Jesus only with themselves.
9.blb: And suddenly, having looked around, no longer did they see anyone but Jesus alone with themselves.
9.bbe: And suddenly looking round about, they saw no one any longer, but Jesus only with themselves.

9.msb: As they were coming down the mountain, Jesus admonished them not to tell anyone what they had seen until the Son of Man had risen from the dead.
9.kjv: And as they came down from the mountain, he charged them that they should tell no man what things they had seen, till the Son of man were risen from the dead.
9.blb: And in their coming down from the mountain, He instructed them that they should relate to no one what they saw, except when the Son of Man should rise out from the dead.
9.bbe: And while they were coming down from the mountain, he gave them orders not to give word to any man of the things they had seen, till the Son of man had come back from the dead.

9.msb: So they kept this matter to themselves, discussing what it meant to rise from the dead.
9.kjv: And they kept that saying with themselves, questioning one with another what the rising from the dead should mean.
9.blb: And they kept the word to themselves, discussing what it is to rise out from the dead.
9.bbe: And they kept the saying, questioning among themselves what the coming back from the dead might be.

9.msb: And they asked Jesus, “Why do the scribes say that Elijah must come first?”
9.kjv: And they asked him, saying, Why say the scribes that Elias must first come?
9.blb: And they were questioning Him, saying, “The scribes say that it is necessary for Elijah to come first.”
9.bbe: And they put a question to him, saying, Why do the scribes say that Elijah has to come first?

9.msb: He replied, “Elijah does indeed come first, and he restores all things. Why then is it written that the Son of Man must suffer many things and be rejected?
9.kjv: And he answered and told them, Elias verily cometh first, and restoreth all things; and how it is written of the Son of man, that he must suffer many things, and be set at nought.
9.blb: And He was saying to them, “Elijah indeed, having come first, restores all things. And how has it been written about the Son of Man that He should suffer many things and be set at nothing?
9.bbe: And he said to them, Truly, Elijah does come first, and puts all things in order; and how is it said in the Writings that the Son of man will go through much sorrow and be made as nothing?

9.msb: But I tell you that Elijah has indeed come, and they have done to him whatever they wished, just as it is written about him.”
9.kjv: But I say unto you, That Elias is indeed come, and they have done unto him whatsoever they listed, as it is written of him.
9.blb: But I say to you that Elijah has also come, and they did to him whatever they were wanting, as it has been written of him.”
9.bbe: But I say to you that Elijah has come, and they have done to him whatever they were pleased to do, even as the Writings say about him.

9.msb: When Jesus returned to the other disciples, He saw a large crowd around them, and scribes arguing with them.
9.kjv: And when he came to his disciples, he saw a great multitude about them, and the scribes questioning with them.
9.blb: And having come to the disciples, they saw a great crowd around them, and scribes disputing with them.
9.bbe: And when they came to the disciples, they saw a great mass of people about them, and scribes questioning them.
9.heading: The Boy with an Evil Spirit

9.msb: As soon as all the people saw Jesus, they were filled with awe and ran to greet Him.
9.kjv: And straightway all the people, when they beheld him, were greatly amazed, and running to him saluted him.
9.blb: And immediately all the crowd, having seen Him, were greatly amazed, and running to Him, they were greeting Him.
9.bbe: And straight away all the people, when they saw him, were full of wonder, and running to him, gave him worship.

9.msb: “What are you disputing with them?” He asked the scribes.
9.kjv: And he asked the scribes, What question ye with them?
9.blb: And He questioned them, “What are you disputing with them?”
9.bbe: And he said, What are you questioning them about?

9.msb: Someone in the crowd replied, “Teacher, I brought You my son, who has a spirit that makes him mute.
9.kjv: And one of the multitude answered and said, Master, I have brought unto thee my son, which hath a dumb spirit;
9.blb: And one out of the crowd answered Him, “Teacher, I brought to You my son, having a mute spirit.
9.bbe: And one of the number said to him in answer, Master, I came to you with my son, who has in him a spirit which takes away his power of talking;

9.msb: Whenever it seizes him, it throws him to the ground. He foams at the mouth, gnashes his teeth, and becomes rigid. I asked Your disciples to drive it out, but they were unable.”
9.kjv: And wheresoever he taketh him, he teareth him: and he foameth, and gnasheth with his teeth, and pineth away: and I spake to thy disciples that they should cast him out; and they could not.
9.blb: And wherever it might seize him, it throws him down, and he foams and gnashes his teeth and is withering away. And I spoke to Your disciples that they might cast it out, and they did not have the strength.”
9.bbe: And wherever it takes him, it puts him down violently, streaming at the lips and twisted with pain; and his strength goes from him; and I made a request to your disciples to send it out, and they were not able.

9.msb: “O unbelieving generation!” Jesus replied. “How long must I remain with you? How long must I put up with you? Bring the boy to Me.”
9.kjv: He answereth him, and saith, O faithless generation, how long shall I be with you? how long shall I suffer you? bring him unto me.
9.blb: And answering them, He says, “O unbelieving generation, until when will I be with you? Until when will I bear with you? Bring him to Me.”
9.bbe: And he said to them in answer, O generation without faith, how long will I have to be with you? how long will I put up with you? let him come to me.

9.msb: So they brought him, and seeing Jesus, the spirit immediately threw the boy into a convulsion. He fell to the ground and rolled around, foaming at the mouth.
9.kjv: And they brought him unto him: and when he saw him, straightway the spirit tare him; and he fell on the ground, and wallowed foaming.
9.blb: And they brought him to Him, and having seen Him, the spirit immediately threw him into convulsions. And having fallen upon the ground, he was rolling around, foaming.
9.bbe: And they took him to him: and when he saw him, the spirit in him straight away became violent; and he went down on the earth, rolling about and streaming at the lips.

9.msb: Jesus asked the boy’s father, “How long has this been with him?” “From childhood,” he said.
9.kjv: And he asked his father, How long is it ago since this came unto him? And he said, Of a child.
9.blb: And He questioned his father, “How long a time is it that this has been with him?” And he said, “From childhood.”
9.bbe: And Jesus questioning the father said, How long has he been like this? And he said, From a child.

9.msb: “It often throws him into the fire or into the water, trying to kill him. But if You can do anything, have compassion on us and help us.”
9.kjv: And ofttimes it hath cast him into the fire, and into the waters, to destroy him: but if thou canst do any thing, have compassion on us, and help us.
9.blb: And often it also cast him into the fire and into the waters, so that it might destroy him. But if You are able to do anything, help us, having compassion on us.”
9.bbe: And frequently it has sent him into the fire and into the water, for his destruction; but if you are able to do anything, have pity on us, and give us help.

9.msb: “If you can believe!” said Jesus. “All things are possible to him who believes!”
9.kjv: Jesus said unto him, If thou canst believe, all things are possible to him that believeth.
9.blb: And Jesus said to him, “‘If You are able’? All things are possible to the one believing!”
9.bbe: And Jesus said to him, If you are able! All things are possible to him who has faith.

9.msb: Immediately the boy’s father cried out with tears, “Lord, I do believe; help my unbelief!”
9.kjv: And straightway the father of the child cried out, and said with tears, Lord, I believe; help thou mine unbelief.
9.blb: Immediately, having cried out, the father of the child was saying, “I believe; help my unbelief!”
9.bbe: Straight away the father of the child gave a cry, saying, I have faith; make my feeble faith stronger.

9.msb: When Jesus saw that a crowd had come running, He rebuked the unclean spirit. “You mute and deaf spirit,” He said, “I command you to come out and never enter him again.”
9.kjv: When Jesus saw that the people came running together, he rebuked the foul spirit, saying unto him, Thou dumb and deaf spirit, I charge thee, come out of him, and enter no more into him.
9.blb: And Jesus, having seen that a crowd is running together, rebuked the unclean spirit, saying to it, “Mute and deaf spirit, I command you, come out of him, and no more may you enter into him.”
9.bbe: And when Jesus saw that the people came running together, he gave orders to the unclean spirit, saying to him, You, spirit, who are the cause of his loss of voice and hearing, I say to you, come out of him, and never again go into him.

9.msb: After shrieking and convulsing him violently, the spirit came out. The boy became like a corpse, so that many said, “He is dead.”
9.kjv: And the spirit cried, and rent him sore, and came out of him: and he was as one dead; insomuch that many said, He is dead.
9.blb: And having cried out, and having thrown him into many convulsions, it came out. And he became as if dead, so as for many to say that he was dead.
9.bbe: And after crying out and shaking him violently, it came out: and the child became like one dead; so that most of them said, He is dead.

9.msb: But Jesus took him by the hand and helped him to his feet, and he stood up.
9.kjv: But Jesus took him by the hand, and lifted him up; and he arose.
9.blb: But Jesus, having taken him by the hand, raised him up, and he arose.
9.bbe: But Jesus took him by the hand, lifting him up; and he got up.

9.msb: After Jesus had gone into the house, His disciples asked Him privately, “Why couldn’t we drive it out?”
9.kjv: And when he was come into the house, his disciples asked him privately, Why could not we cast him out?
9.blb: And on His having entered into the house, His disciples were questioning Him by Himself, “Why were we not able to cast it out?”
9.bbe: And when he had gone into the house, his disciples said to him privately, Why were we unable to send it out?

9.msb: Jesus answered, “This kind cannot come out, except by prayer and fasting.”
9.kjv: And he said unto them, This kind can come forth by nothing, but by prayer and fasting.
9.blb: And He said to them, “This kind is able to come out by nothing except by prayer.”
9.bbe: And he said to them, Nothing will make this sort come out but prayer.

9.msb: Going on from there, they passed through Galilee. But Jesus did not want anyone to know,
9.kjv: And they departed thence, and passed through Galilee; and he would not that any man should know it.
9.blb: Having gone out from there, they were passing through Galilee. And He did not wish that anyone should know,
9.bbe: And they went out from there, through Galilee; and it was his desire that no man might have knowledge of it;
9.heading: The Second Prediction of the Passion

9.msb: because He was teaching His disciples. He told them, “The Son of Man will be delivered into the hands of men. They will kill Him, and on the third day He will rise.”
9.kjv: For he taught his disciples, and said unto them, The Son of man is delivered into the hands of men, and they shall kill him; and after that he is killed, he shall rise the third day.
9.blb: for He was teaching His disciples. And He was saying to them, “The Son of Man is delivered into the hands of men, and they will kill Him; and having been killed, after three days He will rise.”
9.bbe: For he was giving his disciples teaching, and saying to them, The Son of man is given up into the hands of men, and they will put him to death; and when he is dead, after three days he will come back from the dead.

9.msb: But they did not understand this statement, and they were afraid to ask Him about it.
9.kjv: But they understood not that saying, and were afraid to ask him.
9.blb: But they were not understanding the saying, and they were afraid to question Him.
9.bbe: But the saying was not clear to them, and they were in fear of questioning him about it.

9.msb: Then Jesus came to Capernaum. While He was in the house, He asked them, “What were you discussing among yourselves on the way?”
9.kjv: And he came to Capernaum: and being in the house he asked them, What was it that ye disputed among yourselves by the way?
9.blb: And they came to Capernaum. And being in the house, He was questioning them, “What were you reasoning on the way?”
9.bbe: And they came to Capernaum: and when he was in the house, he put the question to them, What were you talking about on the way?
9.heading: The Greatest in the Kingdom

9.msb: But they were silent, for on the way they had been arguing about which of them was the greatest.
9.kjv: But they held their peace: for by the way they had disputed among themselves, who should be the greatest.
9.blb: But they were silent, for they discussed with one another on the way who was greater.
9.bbe: But they said nothing: because they had had an argument between themselves on the way, about who was the greatest.

9.msb: Sitting down, Jesus called the Twelve and said, “If anyone wants to be first, he must be the last of all and the servant of all.”
9.kjv: And he sat down, and called the twelve, and saith unto them, If any man desire to be first, the same shall be last of all, and servant of all.
9.blb: And having sat down, He called the Twelve, and He says to them, “If anyone wants to be first, he will be last of all and servant of all.”
9.bbe: And seating himself, he made the twelve come to him; and he said to them, If any man has the desire to be first, he will be last of all and servant of all.

9.msb: Then He had a little child stand among them. Taking the child in His arms, He said to them,
9.kjv: And he took a child, and set him in the midst of them: and when he had taken him in his arms, he said unto them,
9.blb: And having taken a little child, He set him in their midst. And having taken him in His arms, He said to them,
9.bbe: And he took a little child, and put him in the middle of them; and taking him in his arms, he said to them,

9.msb: “Whoever welcomes one of these little children in My name welcomes Me, and whoever welcomes Me welcomes not only Me, but the One who sent Me.”
9.kjv: Whosoever shall receive one of such children in my name, receiveth me: and whosoever shall receive me, receiveth not me, but him that sent me.
9.blb: “Whoever shall receive one of such little children in My name receives Me; and whoever shall receive Me does not receive Me but the One having sent Me.”
9.bbe: Whoever will give honour to one such little child in my name, gives honour to me: and whoever gives honour to me, gives honour not to me, but to him who sent me.

9.msb: John said to Him, “Teacher, we saw someone who does not follow us driving out demons in Your name, and we forbade him, because he does not accompany us.”
9.kjv: And John answered him, saying, Master, we saw one casting out devils in thy name, and he followeth not us: and we forbad him, because he followeth not us.
9.blb: John said to Him, “Teacher, we saw someone casting out demons in Your name who does not follow us, and we were forbidding him, because he was not following us.”
9.bbe: John said to him, Master, we saw one driving out evil spirits in your name: and we said that he might not, because he is not one of us.

9.msb: “Do not stop him,” Jesus replied. “For no one who performs a miracle in My name can turn around and speak evil of Me.
9.kjv: But Jesus said, Forbid him not: for there is no man which shall do a miracle in my name, that can lightly speak evil of me.
9.blb: And Jesus said, “Do not forbid him. For there is no one who will do a mighty work in My name and will be able quickly to speak evil of Me.
9.bbe: But Jesus said, Say not so: for there is no man who will do a great work in my name, and be able at the same time to say evil of me.

9.msb: For whoever is not against you is for you.
9.kjv: For he that is not against us is on our part.
9.blb: For whoever is not against us is for us.
9.bbe: He who is not against us is for us.

9.msb: Indeed, if anyone gives you even a cup of water in My name because you are Christ’s, truly I tell you, he will never lose his reward.
9.kjv: For whosoever shall give you a cup of water to drink in my name, because ye belong to Christ, verily I say unto you, he shall not lose his reward.
9.blb: For whoever shall give you to drink a cup of water because you are Christ’s in name, truly I say to you that he shall never lose his reward.
9.bbe: Whoever gives you a cup of water, because you are Christ's, truly I say to you, he will in no way be without his reward.

9.msb: But if anyone causes one of these little ones who believe in Me to stumble, it would be better for him to have a millstone hung around his neck and to be thrown into the sea.
9.kjv: And whosoever shall offend one of these little ones that believe in me, it is better for him that a millstone were hanged about his neck, and he were cast into the sea.
9.blb: And whoever might cause to stumble one of these little ones believing in Me, it is better for him rather if a heavy millstone is put around his neck and he has been cast into the sea.
9.bbe: And whoever is a cause of trouble to one of these little ones who have faith in me, it would be better for him if a great stone was put round his neck and he was dropped into the sea.
9.heading: Temptations and Trespasses

9.msb: If your hand causes you to sin, cut it off. It is better for you to enter life crippled than to have two hands and go into hell, into the unquenchable fire,
9.kjv: And if thy hand offend thee, cut it off: it is better for thee to enter into life maimed, than having two hands to go into hell, into the fire that never shall be quenched:
9.blb: And if your hand may cause you to stumble, cut it off; it is better for you to enter into life crippled than, having two hands, to go away into Gehenna, into the unquenchable fire.
9.bbe: And if your hand is a cause of trouble to you, let it be cut off; it is better for you to go into life with one hand than to have two hands and go into hell, into the eternal fire.

9.msb: where ‘their worm never dies, and the fire is never quenched.’
9.kjv: Where their worm dieth not, and the fire is not quenched.

9.msb: If your foot causes you to sin, cut it off. It is better for you to enter life lame than to have two feet and be thrown into hell, into the unquenchable fire,
9.kjv: And if thy foot offend thee, cut it off: it is better for thee to enter halt into life, than having two feet to be cast into hell, into the fire that never shall be quenched:
9.blb: And if your foot may cause you to stumble, cut it off. It is better for you to enter into life lame than, having the two feet, to be cast into Gehenna.
9.bbe: And if your foot is a cause of trouble to you, let it be cut off: it is better for you to go into life with one foot than to have two feet and go into hell.

9.msb: where ‘their worm never dies, and the fire is never quenched.’
9.kjv: Where their worm dieth not, and the fire is not quenched.

9.msb: And if your eye causes you to sin, pluck it out. It is better for you to enter the kingdom of God with one eye than to have two eyes and be thrown into the fire of hell,
9.kjv: And if thine eye offend thee, pluck it out: it is better for thee to enter into the kingdom of God with one eye, than having two eyes to be cast into hell fire:
9.blb: And if your eye may cause you to stumble, cast it out. It is better for you to enter into the kingdom of God one-eyed than, having two eyes, to be cast into Gehenna,
9.bbe: And if your eye is a cause of trouble to you, take it out: it is better for you to go into the kingdom of God with one eye than, having two eyes, to go into hell,

9.msb: where ‘their worm never dies, and the fire is never quenched.’
9.kjv: Where their worm dieth not, and the fire is not quenched.
9.blb: where ‘their worm does not die, and the fire is not quenched.’
9.bbe: Where their worm is ever living and the fire is not put out.

9.msb: For everyone will be salted with fire, and every sacrifice will be salted with salt.
9.kjv: For every one shall be salted with fire, and every sacrifice shall be salted with salt.
9.blb: For everyone will be salted with fire.
9.bbe: Everyone will be salted with fire.
9.heading: Good Salt

9.msb: Salt is good, but if the salt loses its saltiness, with what will you season it? Have salt among yourselves, and be at peace with one another.”
9.kjv: Salt is good: but if the salt have lost his saltness, wherewith will ye season it? Have salt in yourselves, and have peace one with another.
9.blb: The salt is good, but if the salt should become unsalty, with what will you season it? Have salt among yourselves, and be at peace with one another.”
9.bbe: Salt is good; but if the taste goes from it, how will you make it salt again? Have salt in yourselves, and be at peace one with another.

10.msb: Then Jesus left that place and went into the region of Judea, beyond the Jordan. Again the crowds came to Him and He taught them, as was His custom.
10.kjv: And he arose from thence, and cometh into the coasts of Judæa by the farther side of Jordan: and the people resort unto him again; and, as he was wont, he taught them again.
10.blb: And from there, having risen up, He comes into the borders of Judea, and beyond the Jordan. And again crowds come together to Him, and as He had been accustomed, again He was teaching them.
10.bbe: And he got up, and went into the country of Judaea on the other side of Jordan: and great numbers of people came together to him again; and, as was his way, he gave them teaching.
10.heading: Teachings about Divorce

10.msb: Some Pharisees came to test Him. “Is it lawful for a man to divorce his wife?” they inquired.
10.kjv: And the Pharisees came to him, and asked him, Is it lawful for a man to put away his wife? tempting him.
10.blb: And having come, the Pharisees were questioning Him whether it is lawful for a husband to send away a wife—testing Him.
10.bbe: And Pharisees came to him, testing him with the question, Is it right for a man to put away his wife?

10.msb: “What did Moses command you?” He replied.
10.kjv: And he answered and said unto them, What did Moses command you?
10.blb: And answering, He said to them, “What did Moses command you?”
10.bbe: And he said to them in answer, What did Moses say you were to do?

10.msb: They answered, “Moses permitted a man to write his wife a certificate of divorce and send her away.”
10.kjv: And they said, Moses suffered to write a bill of divorcement, and to put her away.
10.blb: And they said, “Moses allowed us to write a roll of divorce and to send her away.”
10.bbe: And they said to him, Moses let us give her a statement in writing, and be free from her.

10.msb: But Jesus told them, “Moses wrote this commandment for you because of your hardness of heart.
10.kjv: And Jesus answered and said unto them, For the hardness of your heart he wrote you this precept.
10.blb: But Jesus said to them, “For your hardness of heart he wrote you this commandment;
10.bbe: But Jesus said to them, Because of your hard hearts he gave you this law.
