13.bbe: Even so, when you see these things taking place, you may be certain that he is near, even at the doors.

13.msb: Truly I tell you, this generation will not pass away until all these things have happened.
13.kjv: Verily I say unto you, that this generation shall not pass, till all these things be done.
13.blb: Truly I say to you that this generation shall not have passed away until all these things shall have come to pass.
13.bbe: Truly, I say to you, This generation will not come to an end till all these things are complete.

13.msb: Heaven and earth will pass away, but My words will never pass away.
13.kjv: Heaven and earth shall pass away: but my words shall not pass away.
13.blb: The heaven and the earth will pass away, but My words will never pass away.
13.bbe: Heaven and earth will come to an end, but my words will not come to an end.

13.msb: No one knows about that day or hour, not even the angels in heaven, nor the Son, but only the Father.
13.kjv: But of that day and that hour knoweth no man, no, not the angels which are in heaven, neither the Son, but the Father.
13.blb: But concerning that day or hour no one knows, not even the angels in heaven, nor the Son, except the Father.
13.bbe: But of that day or that hour no one has knowledge, not even the angels in heaven, or the Son, but the Father.
13.heading: Readiness at Any Hour

13.msb: Be on your guard, stay alert, and pray! For you do not know when the appointed time will come.
13.kjv: Take ye heed, watch and pray: for ye know not when the time is.
13.blb: Take heed; stay awake! For you do not know when the time is.
13.bbe: Take care, keep watch with prayer: for you are not certain when the time will be.

13.msb: It is like a man going on a journey who left his house, put each servant in charge of his own task, and instructed the doorkeeper to keep watch.
13.kjv: For the Son of man is as a man taking a far journey, who left his house, and gave authority to his servants, and to every man his work, and commanded the porter to watch.
13.blb: It is like a man going on a journey, having left his house and having given his servants authority, to each his work. And he commanded the doorkeeper that he should watch.
13.bbe: It is as when a man who is in another country for a time, having gone away from his house, and given authority to his servants and to everyone his work, gives the porter an order to keep watch.

13.msb: Therefore keep watch, because you do not know when the master of the house will return—whether in the evening, at midnight, when the rooster crows, or in the morning.
13.kjv: Watch ye therefore: for ye know not when the master of the house cometh, at even, or at midnight, or at the cockcrowing, or in the morning:
13.blb: Therefore watch, for you do not know when the master of the house comes—either at evening, or at midnight, or when the rooster crows, or morning—
13.bbe: So you are to keep watch: because you are not certain when the master of the house is coming, in the evening, or in the middle of the night, or at the cock's cry, or in the morning;

13.msb: Otherwise, he may arrive without notice and find you sleeping.
13.kjv: Lest coming suddenly he find you sleeping.
13.blb: lest, having come suddenly, he should find you sleeping.
13.bbe: For fear that, coming suddenly, he sees you sleeping.

13.msb: And what I say to you, I say to everyone: Keep watch!”
13.kjv: And what I say unto you I say unto all, Watch.
13.blb: And what I say to you, I say to all: Watch!”
13.bbe: And what I say to you, I say to all, Keep watch.

14.msb: Now the Passover and the Feast of Unleavened Bread were two days away, and the chief priests and scribes were looking for a covert way to arrest Jesus and kill Him.
14.kjv: After two days was the feast of the passover, and of unleavened bread: and the chief priests and the scribes sought how they might take him by craft, and put him to death.
14.blb: And after two days it would be the Passover and the Unleavened. And the chief priests and the scribes were seeking how, having taken Him by stealth, they might kill Him.
14.bbe: It was now two days before the feast of the Passover and the unleavened bread: and the chief priests and the scribes made designs how they might take him by deceit and put him to death:
14.heading: The Plot to Kill Jesus

14.msb: “But not during the feast,” they said, “or there may be a riot among the people.”
14.kjv: But they said, Not on the feast day, lest there be an uproar of the people.
14.blb: For they were saying, “Not during the feast, lest there will be an uproar of the people.”
14.bbe: But they said, Not while the feast is going on, for fear there may be trouble among the people.

14.msb: While Jesus was in Bethany reclining at the table in the home of Simon the Leper, a woman came with an alabaster jar of expensive perfume, made of pure nard. She broke open the jar and poured it on Jesus’ head.
14.kjv: And being in Bethany in the house of Simon the leper, as he sat at meat, there came a woman having an alabaster box of ointment of spikenard very precious; and she brake the box, and poured it on his head.
14.blb: And of Him being in Bethany in the house of Simon the Leper, at His having reclined, a woman came, having an alabaster flask of fragrant oil of pure nard of great price. Having broken the alabaster flask, she poured it on His head.
14.bbe: And while he was in Bethany in the house of Simon the leper, seated at table, there came a woman with a bottle of perfumed oil of great price; and when the bottle was broken she put the perfume on his head.
14.heading: Jesus Anointed at Bethany

14.msb: Some of those present, however, expressed their indignation to one another and said, “Why this waste of perfume?
14.kjv: And there were some that had indignation within themselves, and said, Why was this waste of the ointment made?
14.blb: And some were indignant within themselves: “Why has this waste of the fragrant oil come to pass?
14.bbe: But some of them were angry among themselves, saying, For what purpose has this oil been wasted?

14.msb: It could have been sold for over three hundred denarii and the money given to the poor.” And they scolded her.
14.kjv: For it might have been sold for more than three hundred pence, and have been given to the poor. And they murmured against her.
14.blb: For this fragrant oil could have been sold for more than three hundred denarii and given to the poor.” And they were grumbling at her.
14.bbe: We might have got more than three hundred pence for it, and given the money to the poor. And they said things against her among themselves.

14.msb: But Jesus said, “Leave her alone; why are you bothering her? She has done a beautiful deed to Me.
14.kjv: And Jesus said, Let her alone; why trouble ye her? she hath wrought a good work on me.
14.blb: And Jesus said, “Leave her alone; why do you cause trouble to her? She did a good work toward Me.
14.bbe: But Jesus said, Let her be; why are you troubling her? she has done a kind act to me.

14.msb: The poor you will always have with you, and you can help them whenever you want. But you will not always have Me.
14.kjv: For ye have the poor with you always, and whensoever ye will ye may do them good: but me ye have not always.
14.blb: For the poor you always have with you, and you are able to do them good whenever you desire; but not always do you have Me.
14.bbe: The poor you have ever with you, and whenever you have the desire you may do them good: but me you have not for ever.

14.msb: She has done what she could to anoint My body in advance of My burial.
14.kjv: She hath done what she could: she is come aforehand to anoint my body to the burying.
14.blb: She did what she could. She came beforehand to anoint My body for the burial.
14.bbe: She has done what she was able: she has put oil on my body to make it ready for its last resting-place.

14.msb: And truly I tell you, wherever this gospel is preached in all the world, what she has done will also be told in memory of her.”
14.kjv: Verily I say unto you, Wheresoever this gospel shall be preached throughout the whole world, this also that she hath done shall be spoken of for a memorial of her.
14.blb: And truly I say to you, wherever the gospel shall be proclaimed in the whole world, what this woman did also will be spoken of, for a memorial of her.”
14.bbe: And truly I say to you, Wherever the good news goes out through all the earth, what this woman has done will be talked of in memory of her.

14.msb: Then Judas Iscariot, one of the Twelve, went to the chief priests to betray Jesus to them.
14.kjv: And Judas Iscariot, one of the twelve, went unto the chief priests, to betray him unto them.
14.blb: And Judas Iscariot, one of the Twelve, went away to the chief priests, so that he might betray Him to them.
14.bbe: And Judas Iscariot, who was one of the twelve, went away to the chief priests, so that he might give him up to them.
14.heading: Judas Agrees to Betray Jesus

14.msb: They were delighted to hear this, and they promised to give him money. So Judas began to look for an opportunity to betray Jesus.
14.kjv: And when they heard it, they were glad, and promised to give him money. And he sought how he might conveniently betray him.
14.blb: And having heard, they rejoiced and promised to give him silver. And he was seeking how he might deliver Him up opportunely.
14.bbe: And hearing what he said, they were glad, and gave him their word to make him a payment of money. And he took thought how he might best give him up to them.

14.msb: On the first day of the Feast of Unleavened Bread, when the Passover lamb was to be sacrificed, Jesus’ disciples asked Him, “Where do You want us to prepare for You to eat the Passover?”
14.kjv: And the first day of unleavened bread, when they killed the passover, his disciples said unto him, Where wilt thou that we go and prepare that thou mayest eat the passover?
14.blb: And on the first day of the Unleavened, when they were to sacrifice the Passover, His disciples say to Him, “Where do You desire that, having gone, we should prepare so that You may eat the Passover?”
14.bbe: And on the first day of unleavened bread, when the Passover lamb is put to death, his disciples said to him, Where are we to go and make ready for you to take the Passover meal?
14.heading: Preparing the Passover

14.msb: So He sent two of His disciples and told them, “Go into the city, and a man carrying a jug of water will meet you. Follow him,
14.kjv: And he sendeth forth two of his disciples, and saith unto them, Go ye into the city, and there shall meet you a man bearing a pitcher of water: follow him.
14.blb: And He sends forth two of His disciples and says to them, “Go into the city, and a man carrying a pitcher of water will meet you. Follow him.
14.bbe: And he sent two of his disciples, and said to them, Go into the town, and there will come to you a man with a vessel of water: go after him;

14.msb: and whichever house he enters, say to the owner, ‘The Teacher asks: Where is the guest room, where I may eat the Passover with My disciples?’
14.kjv: And wheresoever he shall go in, say ye to the goodman of the house, The Master saith, Where is the guestchamber, where I shall eat the passover with my disciples?
14.blb: And wherever he might enter, say to the master of the house that the Teacher says, ‘Where is My guest room, where I may eat the Passover with My disciples?’
14.bbe: And wherever he goes in, say to the owner of the house, The Master says, Where is my guest-room, where I may take the Passover with my disciples?

14.msb: And he will show you a large upper room, furnished and ready. Make preparations for us there.”
14.kjv: And he will shew you a large upper room furnished and prepared: there make ready for us.
14.blb: And he will show you a large upper room, having been furnished, prepared. And prepare for us there.”
14.bbe: And he will take you up himself to a great room with a table and seats: there make ready for us.

14.msb: So His disciples left and went into the city, where they found everything as Jesus had described. And they prepared the Passover.
14.kjv: And his disciples went forth, and came into the city, and found as he had said unto them: and they made ready the passover.
14.blb: And the disciples went away, and they came into the city, and they found it as He said to them, and they prepared the Passover.
14.bbe: And the disciples went out and came into the town, and saw that it was as he had said: and they made ready the Passover.

14.msb: When evening came, Jesus arrived with the Twelve.
14.kjv: And in the evening he cometh with the twelve.
14.blb: And evening having come, He comes with the Twelve.
14.bbe: And when it was evening he came with the twelve.
14.heading: The Last Supper

14.msb: And while they were reclining and eating, Jesus said, “Truly I tell you, one of you who is eating with Me will betray Me.”
14.kjv: And as they sat and did eat, Jesus said, Verily I say unto you, One of you which eateth with me shall betray me.
14.blb: And in their reclining and eating, Jesus said, “Truly I say to you that one of you who is eating with Me will betray Me.”
14.bbe: And while they were seated taking food, Jesus said, Truly I say to you, One of you will be false to me, one who is taking food with me.

14.msb: They began to be grieved and to ask Him one after another, “Surely not I?” And another said, “Is it I?”
14.kjv: And they began to be sorrowful, and to say unto him one by one, Is it I? and another said, Is it I?
14.blb: They began to be grieved and to say to Him one by one, “Surely not I?”
14.bbe: They were sad, and said to him one by one, Is it I?

14.msb: He answered, “It is one of the Twelve—the one who is dipping his hand into the bowl with Me.
14.kjv: And he answered and said unto them, It is one of the twelve, that dippeth with me in the dish.
14.blb: And He said to them, “One of the Twelve, the one dipping into the bowl with Me.
14.bbe: And he said to them, It is one of the twelve, one who is putting his bread with me into the same plate.

14.msb: The Son of Man will go just as it is written about Him, but woe to that man by whom He is betrayed! It would be better for him if he had not been born.”
14.kjv: The Son of man indeed goeth, as it is written of him: but woe to that man by whom the Son of man is betrayed! good were it for that man if he had never been born.
14.blb: For indeed, the Son of Man goes as it has been written concerning Him; but woe to that man by whom the Son of Man is betrayed! It were better for him if that man had not been born.”
14.bbe: The Son of man goes, even as the Writings say of him: but cursed is that man through whom the Son of man is given up! It would have been well for that man if he had never been given birth.

14.msb: While they were eating, Jesus took bread, spoke a blessing and broke it, and gave it to the disciples, saying, “Take and eat; this is My body.”
14.kjv: And as they did eat, Jesus took bread, and blessed, and brake it, and gave to them, and said, Take, eat: this is my body.
14.blb: And in their eating, having taken bread, having spoken a blessing, He broke it and gave to them and said, “Take; this is My body.”
14.bbe: And while they were taking food, he took bread, and after blessing it, he gave the broken bread to them, and said, Take it: this is my body.

14.msb: Then He took the cup, gave thanks, and gave it to them, and they all drank from it.
14.kjv: And he took the cup, and when he had given thanks, he gave it to them: and they all drank of it.
14.blb: And having taken the cup, having given thanks, He gave to them, and they all drank of it.
14.bbe: And he took a cup, and when he had given praise, he gave it to them: and they all had a drink from it.

14.msb: He said to them, “This is My blood of the new covenant, which is poured out for many.
14.kjv: And he said unto them, This is my blood of the new testament, which is shed for many.
14.blb: And He said to them, “This is My blood of the covenant, which is being poured out for many.
14.bbe: And he said to them, This is my blood of the testament, which is given for men.

14.msb: Truly I tell you, I will no longer drink of the fruit of the vine until that day when I drink it anew in the kingdom of God.”
14.kjv: Verily I say unto you, I will drink no more of the fruit of the vine, until that day that I drink it new in the kingdom of God.
14.blb: Truly I say to you that I will never again drink of the fruit of the vine until that day when I drink it anew in the kingdom of God.”
14.bbe: Truly I say to you, I will take no more of the fruit of the vine till the day when I take it new in the kingdom of God.

14.msb: And when they had sung a hymn, they went out to the Mount of Olives.
14.kjv: And when they had sung an hymn, they went out into the mount of Olives.
14.blb: And having sung a hymn, they went out to the Mount of Olives.
14.bbe: And after a song of praise to God they went out to the Mountain of Olives.

14.msb: Then Jesus said to them, “You will all fall away on account of Me this night, for it is written: ‘I will strike the Shepherd, and the sheep will be scattered.’
14.kjv: And Jesus saith unto them, All ye shall be offended because of me this night: for it is written, I will smite the shepherd, and the sheep shall be scattered.
14.blb: And Jesus says to them, “You will all fall away, for it has been written: ‘I will strike the shepherd, and the sheep will be scattered.’
14.bbe: And Jesus said to them, You will all be turned away from me: for it is in the Writings, I will put the keeper of the sheep to death, and the sheep will be put to flight.
14.heading: Jesus Predicts Peter’s Denial

14.msb: But after I have risen, I will go ahead of you into Galilee.”
14.kjv: But after that I am risen, I will go before you into Galilee.
14.blb: But after having arisen, I will go before you into Galilee.”
14.bbe: But after I have come back from the dead, I will go before you into Galilee.

14.msb: Peter declared, “Even if all fall away, I never will.”
14.kjv: But Peter said unto him, Although all shall be offended, yet will not I.
14.blb: But Peter was saying to Him, “Even if all will fall away, yet not I.”
14.bbe: But Peter said to him, Though the others may be turned away from you, I will not.

14.msb: “Truly I tell you,” Jesus replied, “this very night, before the rooster crows twice, you will deny Me three times.”
14.kjv: And Jesus saith unto him, Verily I say unto thee, That this day, even in this night, before the cock crow twice, thou shalt deny me thrice.
14.blb: And Jesus says to him, “Truly I say to you that now, this night, before the rooster crows twice, you will deny Me three times.”
14.bbe: And Jesus said to him, Truly, I say to you that you, today, even this night, before the cock's second cry, will say three times that you have no knowledge of me.

14.msb: But Peter kept insisting all the more, “Even if I have to die with You, I will never deny You.” And all the others said the same thing.
14.kjv: But he spake the more vehemently, If I should die with thee, I will not deny thee in any wise. Likewise also said they all.
14.blb: But he kept saying emphatically, “If it is needful of me to die with You, never will I deny You.” And all of them were saying likewise also.
14.bbe: But he said with passion, If I have to be put to death with you, I will not be false to you. And they all said the same.

14.msb: Then they came to a place called Gethsemane, and Jesus told His disciples, “Sit here while I pray.”
14.kjv: And they came to a place which was named Gethsemane: and he saith to his disciples, Sit ye here, while I shall pray.
14.blb: And they come to a place, the name of which is Gethsemane; and He says to His disciples, “Sit here until I may pray.”
14.bbe: And they came to a place which was named Gethsemane: and he said to his disciples, Be seated here while I say a prayer.
14.heading: Jesus Prays at Gethsemane

14.msb: He took with Him Peter, James, and John, and began to be deeply troubled and distressed.
14.kjv: And he taketh with him Peter and James and John, and began to be sore amazed, and to be very heavy;
14.blb: And He takes Peter and James and John with Him, and He began to be greatly awestruck and deeply distressed.
14.bbe: And he took with him Peter and James and John, and grief and great trouble came on him.

14.msb: Then He said to them, “My soul is consumed with sorrow to the point of death. Stay here and keep watch.”
14.kjv: And saith unto them, My soul is exceeding sorrowful unto death: tarry ye here, and watch.
14.blb: And He says to them, “My soul is very sorrowful, even to death. Remain here and watch.”
14.bbe: And he said to them, My soul is very sad, even to death: be here a little time, and keep watch.

14.msb: Going a little farther, He fell to the ground and prayed that, if it were possible, the hour would pass from Him.
14.kjv: And he went forward a little, and fell on the ground, and prayed that, if it were possible, the hour might pass from him.
14.blb: And having gone forward a little, He fell upon the ground and was praying that, if it is possible, the hour might pass from Him.
14.bbe: And he went forward a little, and falling down on the earth, made request that, if possible, the hour might go from him.

14.msb: “Abba, Father,” He said, “all things are possible for You. Take this cup from Me. Yet not what I will, but what You will.”
14.kjv: And he said, Abba, Father, all things are possible unto thee; take away this cup from me: nevertheless not what I will, but what thou wilt.
14.blb: And He was saying, “Abba, Father, all things are possible to You. Take away this cup from Me. But not what I will, but what You will.”
14.bbe: And he said, Abba, Father, all things are possible to you; take away this cup from me: but even so let not my pleasure, but yours be done.

14.msb: Then Jesus returned and found them sleeping. “Simon, are you asleep?” He asked. “Were you not able to keep watch for one hour?
14.kjv: And he cometh, and findeth them sleeping, and saith unto Peter, Simon, sleepest thou? couldest not thou watch one hour?
14.blb: And He comes and finds them sleeping, and He says to Peter, “Simon, are you asleep? Were you not able to watch one hour?
14.bbe: And he came, and saw them sleeping, and said to Peter, Simon, are you sleeping? were you not able to keep watch one hour?

14.msb: Watch and pray so that you will not enter into temptation. For the spirit is willing, but the body is weak.”
14.kjv: Watch ye and pray, lest ye enter into temptation. The spirit truly is ready, but the flesh is weak.
14.blb: Watch and pray, so that you may not enter into temptation. For the spirit is willing, but the flesh weak.”
14.bbe: Keep watch with prayer, so that you may not be put to the test; the spirit truly is ready, but the flesh is feeble.

14.msb: Again He went away and prayed, saying the same thing.
14.kjv: And again he went away, and prayed, and spake the same words.
14.blb: And again, having gone away, He prayed, having said the same thing.
14.bbe: And again he went away, and said a prayer, using the same words.

14.msb: And again Jesus returned and found them sleeping—for their eyes were heavy. And they did not know what to answer Him.
14.kjv: And when he returned, he found them asleep again, (for their eyes were heavy,) neither wist they what to answer him.
14.blb: And again having come, He found them sleeping. For their eyes were heavy, and they did not know what they should answer Him.
14.bbe: And again he came and saw them sleeping, because their eyes were very tired; and they had nothing to say in answer.

14.msb: When Jesus returned the third time, He said, “Are you still sleeping and resting? That is enough! The hour has come. Look, the Son of Man is betrayed into the hands of sinners.
14.kjv: And he cometh the third time, and saith unto them, Sleep on now, and take your rest: it is enough, the hour is come; behold, the Son of man is betrayed into the hands of sinners.
14.blb: And He comes the third time and says to them, “Are you still sleeping and resting? It is enough! The hour came. Behold, the Son of Man is delivered up into the hands of the sinful.
14.bbe: And he came the third time, and said to them, Go on sleeping now and take your rest: it is enough; the hour has come; see, the Son of man is given up into the hands of evil men.

14.msb: Rise, let us go. See, My betrayer is approaching!”
14.kjv: Rise up, let us go; lo, he that betrayeth me is at hand.
14.blb: Rise, let us go. Behold, the one betraying Me has drawn near!”
14.bbe: Get up, let us be going; see, he who gives me up is near.

14.msb: While Jesus was still speaking, Judas, one of the Twelve, arrived, accompanied by a large crowd armed with swords and clubs, sent from the chief priests, scribes, and elders.
14.kjv: And immediately, while he yet spake, cometh Judas, one of the twelve, and with him a great multitude with swords and staves, from the chief priests and the scribes and the elders.
14.blb: And immediately, in His still speaking, Judas, one of the Twelve, comes up, and with Him a crowd with swords and clubs, from the chief priests and the scribes and the elders.
14.bbe: And straight away, while he was still talking, Judas, one of the twelve, came, and with him a great band with swords and sticks, from the chief priests and the scribes and those in authority.
14.heading: The Betrayal of Jesus

14.msb: Now the betrayer had arranged a signal with them: “The One I kiss is the man; arrest Him and lead Him away securely.”
14.kjv: And he that betrayed him had given them a token, saying, Whomsoever I shall kiss, that same is he; take him, and lead him away safely.
14.blb: Now the one delivering Him up had given to them a sign, saying, “Whomever I shall kiss is He; seize Him and lead Him away securely.”
14.bbe: Now he who had been false to him had given them a sign, saying, The one to whom I give a kiss, that is he; take him, and get him away safely.

14.msb: Going directly to Jesus, he said, “Rabbi, Rabbi!” and kissed Him.
14.kjv: And as soon as he was come, he goeth straightway to him, and saith, Master, master; and kissed him.
14.blb: And having come, immediately having come near to Him, he says, “Rabbi!” And he kissed Him.
14.bbe: And when he had come, he went straight to him and said, Master; and gave him a kiss.

14.msb: Then the men seized Jesus and arrested Him.
14.kjv: And they laid their hands on him, and took him.
14.blb: And they laid the hands on Him and seized Him.
14.bbe: And they put their hands on him, and took him.

14.msb: And one of the bystanders drew his sword and struck the servant of the high priest, cutting off his ear.
14.kjv: And one of them that stood by drew a sword, and smote a servant of the high priest, and cut off his ear.
14.blb: And a certain one of those standing by, having drawn the sword, struck the servant of the high priest and cut off his ear.
14.bbe: But a certain one of those who were near took out his sword, and gave the servant of the high priest a blow, cutting off his ear.

14.msb: Jesus asked the crowd, “Have you come out with swords and clubs to arrest Me as you would an outlaw?
14.kjv: And Jesus answered and said unto them, Are ye come out, as against a thief, with swords and with staves to take me?
14.blb: And Jesus, answering, said to them, “Did you come out with swords and clubs, as against a robber, to capture Me?
14.bbe: And Jesus said to them, Have you come out as against a thief, with swords and sticks to take me?

14.msb: Every day I was with you, teaching in the temple courts, and you did not arrest Me. But this has happened that the Scriptures would be fulfilled.”
14.kjv: I was daily with you in the temple teaching, and ye took me not: but the scriptures must be fulfilled.
14.blb: Every day I was with you in the temple, teaching, and you did not seize Me. But it is so that the Scriptures may be fulfilled.”
14.bbe: I was with you every day in the Temple teaching, and you did not take me; but this is done so that the Writings may come true.

14.msb: Then everyone deserted Him and fled.
14.kjv: And they all forsook him, and fled.
14.blb: And all, having left Him, fled.
14.bbe: And they all went away from him in fear.

14.msb: One young man who had been following Jesus was wearing a linen cloth around his body. The young men caught hold of him,
14.kjv: And there followed him a certain young man, having a linen cloth cast about his naked body; and the young men laid hold on him:
14.blb: And a certain young man was following Him, having cast a linen cloth about his naked body. And they seize him,
14.bbe: And a certain young man went after him, with only a linen cloth about his body; and they put their hands on him;

14.msb: but he pulled free of the linen cloth and ran away from them naked.
14.kjv: And he left the linen cloth, and fled from them naked.
14.blb: and having left behind the linen cloth, he fled naked.
14.bbe: But he got away unclothed, without the linen cloth.

14.msb: They led Jesus away to the high priest, and all the chief priests, elders, and scribes assembled with him.
14.kjv: And they led Jesus away to the high priest: and with him were assembled all the chief priests and the elders and the scribes.
14.blb: And they led away Jesus to the high priest, and all the chief priests and the elders and the scribes come together.
14.bbe: And they took Jesus away to the high priest; and there came together with him all the chief priests and those in authority and the scribes.
14.heading: Jesus before the Sanhedrin

14.msb: Peter followed Him at a distance, right into the courtyard of the high priest. And he sat with the officers and warmed himself by the fire.
14.kjv: And Peter followed him afar off, even into the palace of the high priest: and he sat with the servants, and warmed himself at the fire.
14.blb: And Peter followed Him from afar off, as far as to within the court of the high priest. And he was sitting with the officers and warming himself at the fire.
14.bbe: And Peter had come after him at a distance, even into the house of the high priest; and he was seated with the captains, warming himself in the light of the fire.

14.msb: Now the chief priests and the whole Sanhedrin were seeking testimony against Jesus to put Him to death, but they did not find any.
14.kjv: And the chief priests and all the council sought for witness against Jesus to put him to death; and found none.
14.blb: And the chief priests and all the Council were seeking testimony against Jesus to put Him to death, but they were not finding it.
14.bbe: Now the chief priests and all the Sanhedrin were looking for witness against Jesus so that they might put him to death; and they were unable to get any.

14.msb: For many bore false witness against Jesus, but their testimony was inconsistent.
14.kjv: For many bare false witness against him, but their witness agreed not together.
14.blb: For many were bearing false testimony against Him, but their testimonies were not alike.
14.bbe: For a number gave false witness against him and their witness was not in agreement.

14.msb: Then some men stood up and testified falsely against Him:
14.kjv: And there arose certain, and bare false witness against him, saying,
14.blb: And some, having risen up, were bearing false testimony against Him, saying,
14.bbe: Then some got up and gave false witness against him, saying,

14.msb: “We heard Him say, ‘I will destroy this man-made temple, and in three days I will build another that is made without hands.’”
14.kjv: We heard him say, I will destroy this temple that is made with hands, and within three days I will build another made without hands.
14.blb: “We heard Him saying, ‘I will demolish this temple made with hands, and in three days I will build another, not made with hands.’”
14.bbe: He said in our hearing, I will put an end to this Temple which is made with hands, and in three days I will make another without hands.

14.msb: But even their testimony was inconsistent.
14.kjv: But neither so did their witness agree together.
14.blb: And not even in this matter was their testimony alike.
14.bbe: And even so their witness was not in agreement.

14.msb: So the high priest stood up before them and questioned Jesus, “Have You no answer? What are these men testifying against You?”
14.kjv: And the high priest stood up in the midst, and asked Jesus, saying, Answerest thou nothing? what is it which these witness against thee?
14.blb: And the high priest, having risen up in the midst, questioned Jesus, saying, “Do You not answer? What do these testify against You?”
14.bbe: And the high priest got up in the middle of them, and said to Jesus, Do you say nothing in answer? what is it which these say against you?

14.msb: But Jesus remained silent and made no reply. Again the high priest questioned Him, “Are You the Christ, the Son of the Blessed One?”
14.kjv: But he held his peace, and answered nothing. Again the high priest asked him, and said unto him, Art thou the Christ, the Son of the Blessed?
14.blb: But He was silent and did not answer. Again the high priest was questioning Him and says to Him, “Are You the Christ, the Son of the Blessed One?”
14.bbe: But he kept quiet and said nothing. Again the high priest questioning him said, Are you the Christ, the son of the Holy One?

14.msb: “I am,” said Jesus, “and you will see the Son of Man sitting at the right hand of Power and coming with the clouds of heaven.”
14.kjv: And Jesus said, I am: and ye shall see the Son of man sitting on the right hand of power, and coming in the clouds of heaven.
14.blb: And Jesus said, “I am. And you will see the Son of Man sitting at the right hand of Power and coming with the clouds of heaven.”
14.bbe: And Jesus said, I am: and you will see the Son of man seated at the right hand of power, and coming with the clouds of heaven.

14.msb: At this, the high priest tore his clothes and declared, “Why do we need any more witnesses?
14.kjv: Then the high priest rent his clothes, and saith, What need we any further witnesses?
14.blb: And the high priest, having torn his garments, says, “What more need do we have of witnesses?
14.bbe: And the high priest, violently parting his robes, said, What more need have we of witnesses?

14.msb: You have heard the blasphemy. What is your verdict?” And they all condemned Him as deserving of death.
14.kjv: Ye have heard the blasphemy: what think ye? And they all condemned him to be guilty of death.
14.blb: You heard the blasphemy. What does it appear to you?” And all condemned Him to be deserving of death.
14.bbe: His words against God have come to your ears: what is your opinion? And they all said it was right for him to be put to death.

14.msb: Then some of them began to spit on Him. They blindfolded Him, struck Him with their fists, and said to Him, “Prophesy!” And the officers kept striking Him with the palms of their hands.
14.kjv: And some began to spit on him, and to cover his face, and to buffet him, and to say unto him, Prophesy: and the servants did strike him with the palms of their hands.
14.blb: And some began to spit upon Him and to cover up His face and to strike Him and to say to Him, “Prophesy!” And the officers received Him with slaps.
14.bbe: And some put shame on him and, covering his face, gave him blows and said to him, Now say what is to come: and the captains took him and gave him blows with their hands.

14.msb: While Peter was in the courtyard below, one of the servant girls of the high priest came down
14.kjv: And as Peter was beneath in the palace, there cometh one of the maids of the high priest:
14.blb: And of Peter being below in the courtyard, one of the servant girls of the high priest comes,
14.bbe: And while Peter was down in the open square of the building, one of the servant-girls of the high priest came;
14.heading: Peter Denies Jesus

14.msb: and saw him warming himself there. She looked at Peter and said, “You also were with Jesus the Nazarene.”
14.kjv: And when she saw Peter warming himself, she looked upon him, and said, And thou also wast with Jesus of Nazareth.
14.blb: and having seen Peter warming himself, having looked at him, she says, “You also were with the Nazarene, Jesus.”
14.bbe: And seeing Peter warming himself by the fire, she gave him a look, and said, You were with this Nazarene, even Jesus.

14.msb: But he denied it. “I do not know or even understand what you are talking about,” he said. Then he went out to the gateway, and the rooster crowed.
14.kjv: But he denied, saying, I know not, neither understand I what thou sayest. And he went out into the porch; and the cock crew.
14.blb: But he denied it, saying, “I neither know nor understand what you say.” And he went forth out into the gateway, and the rooster crowed.
14.bbe: But he said, I have no knowledge of him, or of what you are saying: and he went out into the doorway; and there came the cry of a cock.

14.msb: There the servant girl saw him again and said to those standing nearby, “This man is one of them.”
14.kjv: And a maid saw him again, and began to say to them that stood by, This is one of them.
14.blb: And the servant girl, having seen him, began to say again to those standing by, “This is one of them.”
14.bbe: And the girl saw him, and said again to those who were near, This is one of them.

14.msb: But he denied it again. After a little while, those standing nearby said once more to Peter, “Surely you are one of them, for you too are a Galilean and your speech is similar.”
14.kjv: And he denied it again. And a little after, they that stood by said again to Peter, Surely thou art one of them: for thou art a Galilaean, and thy speech agreeth thereto.
14.blb: But he denied it again. And after a little while, again those standing by were saying to Peter, “Truly you are of them, for you also are a Galilean.”
14.bbe: But again he said it was not so. And after a little time, again those who were near said to Peter, Truly you are one of them; for you are a Galilaean.

14.msb: But he began to curse and swear, “I do not know this man of whom you speak!”
14.kjv: But he began to curse and to swear, saying, I know not this man of whom ye speak.
14.blb: But he began to curse and to swear, “I do not know this man of whom you speak!”
14.bbe: But, with curses and oaths, he said, I have no knowledge of the man about whom you are talking.

14.msb: And the rooster crowed a second time. Then Peter remembered the word that Jesus had spoken to him: “Before the rooster crows twice, you will deny Me three times.” And he broke down and wept.
14.kjv: And the second time the cock crew. And Peter called to mind the word that Jesus said unto him, Before the cock crow twice, thou shalt deny me thrice. And when he thought thereon, he wept.
14.blb: And immediately a rooster crowed for the second time. And Peter remembered the word that Jesus said to him: “Before the rooster crows twice, you will deny Me three times.” And having broken down, he began to weep.
14.bbe: And in the same minute, the cock gave a second cry. And it came to Peter's mind how Jesus had said to him, Before the cock's second cry, you will say three times that you have no knowledge of me. And at this thought he was overcome with weeping.

15.msb: Early in the morning, the chief priests, elders, scribes, and the whole Sanhedrin devised a plan. They bound Jesus, led Him away, and handed Him over to Pilate.
15.kjv: And straightway in the morning the chief priests held a consultation with the elders and scribes and the whole council, and bound Jesus, and carried him away, and delivered him to Pilate.
15.blb: And early in the morning, having formed a counsel, the chief priests, with the elders and scribes and the whole Council, having bound Jesus, led Him away and delivered Him to Pilate.
15.bbe: And the first thing in the morning the chief priests, with those in authority and the scribes and all the Sanhedrin, had a meeting, and put cords round Jesus, and took him away, and gave him up to Pilate.
15.heading: Jesus Delivered to Pilate

15.msb: So Pilate questioned Him, “Are You the King of the Jews?” “You have said so,” Jesus replied.
15.kjv: And Pilate asked him, Art thou the King of the Jews? And he answering said unto him, Thou sayest it.
15.blb: And Pilate questioned Him, “Are You the King of the Jews?” And answering, He says to him, “You say.”
15.bbe: And Pilate put a question to him, Are you the King of the Jews? And he, answering, said to him, You say so.

15.msb: And the chief priests began to accuse Him of many things.
15.kjv: And the chief priests accused him of many things: but he answered nothing.
15.blb: And the chief priests were accusing Him harshly.
15.bbe: And the chief priests said a number of things against him.

15.msb: Then Pilate questioned Him again, “Have You no answer? Look how many charges they are testifying against You!”
15.kjv: And Pilate asked him again, saying, Answerest thou nothing? behold how many things they witness against thee.
15.blb: And Pilate began to question Him again, saying, “Do You not answer? See how many things they are accusing You of!”
15.bbe: And Pilate again put a question, Do you say nothing in answer? see how much evil they say you have done.

15.msb: But to Pilate’s amazement, Jesus made no further reply.
15.kjv: But Jesus yet answered nothing; so that Pilate marvelled.
15.blb: But Jesus answered no more, so as to amaze Pilate.
15.bbe: But Jesus gave no more answers, so that Pilate was full of wonder.

15.msb: Now it was Pilate’s custom at the feast to release to the people a prisoner of their choosing.
15.kjv: Now at that feast he released unto them one prisoner, whomsoever they desired.
15.blb: Now at the feast he would release to them one prisoner whom they requested.
15.bbe: Now at the feast every year he let one prisoner go free at their request.
15.heading: The Crowd Chooses Barabbas

15.msb: And a man named Barabbas was imprisoned with his fellow rebels who had committed murder during the insurrection.
15.kjv: And there was one named Barabbas, which lay bound with them that had made insurrection with him, who had committed murder in the insurrection.
15.blb: And the one called Barabbas was there, having been bound with the rebels who had committed murder in the insurrection.
15.bbe: And there was one named Barabbas, in prison with those who had gone against the government and in the fight had taken life.

15.msb: So the crowd cried out and began asking Pilate to keep his custom.
15.kjv: And the multitude crying aloud began to desire him to do as he had ever done unto them.
15.blb: And the crowd, having gone up, began to request that which he usually did for them.
15.bbe: And the people went up, requesting him to do as he had done for them in other years.

15.msb: “Do you want me to release to you the King of the Jews?” Pilate asked.
15.kjv: But Pilate answered them, saying, Will ye that I release unto you the King of the Jews?
15.blb: But Pilate answered them, saying, “Do you desire that I should release to you the King of the Jews?”
15.bbe: And Pilate said in answer to them, Is it your desire that I let the King of the Jews go free?

15.msb: For he knew it was out of envy that the chief priests had handed Jesus over.
15.kjv: For he knew that the chief priests had delivered him for envy.
15.blb: For he was aware that the chief priests had delivered Him up because of envy.
15.bbe: For he saw that the chief priests had given him up through envy.

15.msb: But the chief priests stirred up the crowd to have him release Barabbas to them instead.
15.kjv: But the chief priests moved the people, that he should rather release Barabbas unto them.
15.blb: But the chief priests stirred up the crowd so that he might release to them Barabbas instead.
15.bbe: But the people were moved by the chief priests to make him let Barabbas go free.

15.msb: So Pilate asked them again, “What then do you want me to do with the One you call the King of the Jews?”
15.kjv: And Pilate answered and said again unto them, What will ye then that I shall do unto him whom ye call the King of the Jews?
15.blb: And Pilate, answering, was saying to them again, “Then what do you desire that I should do with the One whom you call the King of the Jews?”
15.bbe: And Pilate again said in answer to them, What then am I to do to him to whom you give the name of the King of the Jews?
15.heading: Pilate Delivers Up Jesus

15.msb: And they shouted back, “Crucify Him!”
15.kjv: And they cried out again, Crucify him.
15.blb: And they cried out again, “Crucify Him!”
15.bbe: And they said again loudly, To the cross with him!

15.msb: “Why?” asked Pilate. “What evil has He done?” But they shouted all the louder, “Crucify Him!”
15.kjv: Then Pilate said unto them, Why, what evil hath he done? And they cried out the more exceedingly, Crucify him.
15.blb: And Pilate was saying to them, “Why? What evil did He commit?” But they shouted much more, “Crucify Him!”
15.bbe: And Pilate said to them, Why, what evil has he done? But their cry was the louder, To the cross!

15.msb: And wishing to satisfy the crowd, Pilate released Barabbas to them. But he had Jesus flogged, and handed Him over to be crucified.
15.kjv: And so Pilate, willing to content the people, released Barabbas unto them, and delivered Jesus, when he had scourged him, to be crucified.
15.blb: And Pilate, desiring to do that which was satisfactory to the crowd, released Barabbas to them. And having flogged Him, he delivered up Jesus so that He might be crucified.
15.bbe: And Pilate, desiring to do what was pleasing to the people, let Barabbas go free, and gave up Jesus, when he had been whipped, to be put to death on the cross.

15.msb: Then the soldiers led Jesus away into the palace (that is, the Praetorium) and called the whole company together.
15.kjv: And the soldiers led him away into the hall, called Prætorium; and they call together the whole band.
15.blb: And the soldiers led Him away into the palace (that is, the Praetorium), and they call together the whole cohort.
15.bbe: And the men of the army took him away into the square in front of the building which is the Praetorium, and they got together all the band.
15.heading: The Soldiers Mock Jesus

15.msb: They dressed Him in a purple robe, twisted together a crown of thorns, and set it on His head.
15.kjv: And they clothed him with purple, and platted a crown of thorns, and put it about his head,
15.blb: And they put on Him purple, and having twisted together a crown of thorns, they placed it on Him.
15.bbe: And they put a purple robe on him, and twisting a crown of thorns, they put it on him;

15.msb: And they began to salute Him: “Hail, King of the Jews!”
15.kjv: And began to salute him, Hail, King of the Jews!
15.blb: And they began to salute Him: “Hail, King of the Jews!”
15.bbe: And, as if honouring him, they said, Long life to the King of the Jews!

15.msb: They kept striking His head with a staff and spitting on Him. And they knelt down and bowed before Him.
15.kjv: And they smote him on the head with a reed, and did spit upon him, and bowing their knees worshipped him.
15.blb: And they kept striking His head with a reed and spitting on Him. And bending the knees, they were kneeling down to Him.
15.bbe: And they gave him blows on the head with a stick and put shame on him and, going down on their knees, gave him worship.

15.msb: After they had mocked Him, they removed the purple robe and put His own clothes back on Him. Then they led Him out to crucify Him.
15.kjv: And when they had mocked him, they took off the purple from him, and put his own clothes on him, and led him out to crucify him.
15.blb: And when they had mocked Him, they took off of Him the purple and put on Him His own garments. And they are leading Him out so that they might crucify Him.
15.bbe: And when they had made sport of him, they took the purple robe off him and put his clothing on him. And they took him out to put him to death on the cross.

15.msb: Now Simon of Cyrene, the father of Alexander and Rufus, was passing by on his way in from the country, and the soldiers forced him to carry the cross of Jesus.
15.kjv: And they compel one Simon a Cyrenian, who passed by, coming out of the country, the father of Alexander and Rufus, to bear his cross.
15.blb: And they compel one passing by, Simon of Cyrene, the father of Alexander and Rufus, coming from the country, that he might carry His cross.
15.bbe: And they made one, Simon of Cyrene, the father of Alexander and Rufus, who was going by, coming from the country, go with them, so that he might take his cross.
15.heading: The Crucifixion

15.msb: They brought Jesus to a place called Golgotha, which means The Place of the Skull.
15.kjv: And they bring him unto the place Golgotha, which is, being interpreted, The place of a skull.
15.blb: And they bring Him to a place, Golgotha, which is translated, Place of a Skull.
15.bbe: And they took him to the place named Golgotha, which is, Dead Man's Head.

15.msb: There they offered Him wine to drink mixed with myrrh, but He did not take it.
15.kjv: And they gave him to drink wine mingled with myrrh: but he received it not.
15.blb: And they were offering Him wine having been mixed with gall, but He did not take it.
15.bbe: And they gave him wine mixed with myrrh; but he did not take it.

15.msb: And they crucified Him. They also divided His garments by casting lots to decide what each of them would take.
15.kjv: And when they had crucified him, they parted his garments, casting lots upon them, what every man should take.
15.blb: And they crucify Him. And they divide His garments, casting a lot for them, who should take what.
15.bbe: And he was nailed to the cross; and they made a division of his clothing among them, putting to the decision of chance what everyone was to take.

15.msb: It was the third hour when they crucified Him.
15.kjv: And it was the third hour, and they crucified him.
15.blb: And it was the third hour, and they crucified Him.
15.bbe: And it was the third hour when they put him on the cross.

15.msb: And the charge inscribed against Him read: THE KING OF THE JEWS.
15.kjv: And the superscription of his accusation was written over, THE KING OF THE JEWS.
15.blb: And there was the inscription of the accusation against Him, having been written: THE KING OF THE JEWS.
15.bbe: And the statement of his crime was put in writing on the cross, THE KING OF THE JEWS.

15.msb: Along with Jesus, they crucified two robbers, one on His right and one on His left.
15.kjv: And with him they crucify two thieves; the one on his right hand, and the other on his left.
15.blb: And with Him they crucify two robbers, one at His right hand and one at His left.
15.bbe: And they put two thieves on crosses with him, one on his right side, and one on his left.

15.msb: So the Scripture was fulfilled that says, “And He was numbered with the transgressors.”
15.kjv: And the scripture was fulfilled, which saith, And he was numbered with the transgressors.

15.msb: And those who passed by heaped abuse on Him, shaking their heads and saying, “Aha! You who are going to destroy the temple and rebuild it in three days,
15.kjv: And they that passed by railed on him, wagging their heads, and saying, Ah, thou that destroyest the temple, and buildest it in three days,
15.blb: And those passing by were railing at Him, shaking their heads and saying, “Aha! The One demolishing the temple and building it in three days,
15.bbe: And those who went by made sport of him, shaking their heads, and saying, Ha! you who give the Temple to destruction, and put it up again in three days,

15.msb: come down from the cross and save Yourself!”
15.kjv: Save thyself, and come down from the cross.
15.blb: save Yourself, having come down from the cross!”
15.bbe: Keep yourself from death, and come down from the cross.

15.msb: In the same way, the chief priests and scribes mocked Him among themselves, saying, “He saved others, but He cannot save Himself!
15.kjv: Likewise also the chief priests mocking said among themselves with the scribes, He saved others; himself he cannot save.
15.blb: Likewise also the chief priests, with the scribes, mocking among one another, were saying, “He saved others; Himself He is not able to save!
15.bbe: In the same way the chief priests, laughing at him among themselves with the scribes, said, A saviour of others, he has no salvation for himself.

15.msb: Let the Christ, the King of Israel, come down now from the cross, so that we may see and believe Him!” And even those who were crucified with Him berated Him.
15.kjv: Let Christ the King of Israel descend now from the cross, that we may see and believe. And they that were crucified with him reviled him.
15.blb: The Christ, the King of Israel, let Him come down now from the cross, that we might see and believe!” And those being crucified with Him were upbraiding Him.
15.bbe: Let the Christ, the King of Israel, come down now from the cross, so that we may see and have belief. And those who were put on crosses with him said evil things against him.

15.msb: From the sixth hour until the ninth hour darkness came over all the land.
15.kjv: And when the sixth hour was come, there was darkness over the whole land until the ninth hour.
15.blb: And the sixth hour having come, darkness came over all the land until the ninth hour.
15.bbe: And when the sixth hour had come, it was dark over all the land till the ninth hour.
15.heading: The Death of Jesus

15.msb: At the ninth hour, Jesus cried out in a loud voice, “Eloi, Eloi, lima sabachthani?” which means, “My God, My God, why have You forsaken Me?”
15.kjv: And at the ninth hour Jesus cried with a loud voice, saying, Eloi, Eloi, lama sabachthani? which is, being interpreted, My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?
15.blb: And at the ninth hour, Jesus cried out in a loud voice, “Eloi, Eloi, lema sabachthani?” which is translated, “My God, My God, why did You forsake Me?”
15.bbe: And at the ninth hour, Jesus said in a loud voice, Eloi, Eloi, lama sabachthani? which is, My God, my God, why are you turned away from me?

15.msb: When some of those standing nearby heard this, they said, “Behold, He is calling Elijah.”
15.kjv: And some of them that stood by, when they heard it, said, Behold, he calleth Elias.
15.blb: And some of those standing by, having heard, were saying, “Behold, He calls Elijah.”
15.bbe: And some of those who were near, hearing it, said, See, he is crying to Elijah.

15.msb: And someone ran and filled a sponge with sour wine. He put it on a reed and held it up for Jesus to drink, saying, “Leave Him alone. Let us see if Elijah comes to take Him down.”
15.kjv: And one ran and filled a spunge full of vinegar, and put it on a reed, and gave him to drink, saying, Let alone; let us see whether Elias will come to take him down.
15.blb: And one, having run and having filled a sponge with vinegar, having put it on a reed, gave Him to drink, saying, “Let Him be; let us see if Elijah comes to take Him down.”
15.bbe: And one of them went quickly and, getting a sponge full of bitter wine, put it on a rod, and gave it to him for drink, saying, Let be; let us see if Elijah will come to take him down.

15.msb: But Jesus let out a loud cry and breathed His last.
15.kjv: And Jesus cried with a loud voice, and gave up the ghost.
15.blb: But Jesus, having uttered a great cry, breathed His last.
15.bbe: And Jesus gave a loud cry, and gave up his spirit.

15.msb: And the veil of the temple was torn in two from top to bottom.
15.kjv: And the veil of the temple was rent in twain from the top to the bottom.
15.blb: And the veil of the temple was torn into two from top to bottom.
15.bbe: And the curtain of the Temple was parted in two from end to end.

15.msb: When the centurion standing there in front of Jesus saw how He had cried out and breathed His last, he said, “Truly this man was the Son of God!”
15.kjv: And when the centurion, which stood over against him, saw that he so cried out, and gave up the ghost, he said, Truly this man was the Son of God.
15.blb: And the centurion standing opposite of Him, having seen that in this way He breathed His last, said, “Truly this man was the Son of God!”
15.bbe: And when the captain, who was near, saw how he gave up his spirit, he said, Truly this man was a son of God.

15.msb: And there were also women watching from a distance. Among them were Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James the younger and of Joses, and Salome.
15.kjv: There were also women looking on afar off: among whom was Mary Magdalene, and Mary the mother of James the less and of Joses, and Salome;
15.blb: And there were also women looking on from afar off, among whom also were Mary Magdalene, and Mary the mother of James the less and of Joses, and Salome,
15.bbe: And there were women watching from a distance: among them were Mary Magdalene, and Mary, the mother of James the less and of Joses, and Salome,

15.msb: These women had followed Jesus and ministered to Him while He was in Galilee, and there were many other women who had come up to Jerusalem with Him.
15.kjv: (Who also, when he was in Galilee, followed him, and ministered unto him;) and many other women which came up with him unto Jerusalem.
15.blb: who had been following Him and had been ministering to Him when He was in Galilee, and many others, those having come up with Him to Jerusalem.
15.bbe: Who went with him when he was in Galilee and took care of him; and a number of other women who came up with him to Jerusalem.

15.msb: Now it was already evening. Since it was Preparation Day (that is, the day before the Sabbath),
15.kjv: And now when the even was come, because it was the preparation, that is, the day before the sabbath,
15.blb: And evening already having come, since it was the Preparation (that is, the day before the Sabbath),
15.bbe: And when it was evening, because it was the time of getting ready, that is, the day before the Sabbath,
15.heading: The Burial of Jesus

15.msb: Joseph of Arimathea, a prominent Council member who himself was waiting for the kingdom of God, boldly went to Pilate to ask for the body of Jesus.
15.kjv: Joseph of Arimathaea, an honourable counsellor, which also waited for the kingdom of God, came, and went in boldly unto Pilate, and craved the body of Jesus.
15.blb: having come, Joseph from Arimathea, a prominent Council member who was also himself waiting for the kingdom of God, having boldness, went in to Pilate and asked for the body of Jesus.
15.bbe: There came Joseph of Arimathaea, a responsible man in high honour, who was himself waiting for the kingdom of God; and he went in to Pilate without fear, and made a request for the body of Jesus.

15.msb: Pilate was surprised to hear that Jesus was already dead, so he summoned the centurion to ask if this was so.
15.kjv: And Pilate marvelled if he were already dead: and calling unto him the centurion, he asked him whether he had been any while dead.
15.blb: And Pilate wondered if already He was dead. And having summoned the centurion, he inquired of him whether He was dead already.
15.bbe: And Pilate was surprised that he was dead; and, sending for the captain, he put a question to see if he had been dead for long.

15.msb: When Pilate had confirmed it with the centurion, he granted the body to Joseph.
15.kjv: And when he knew it of the centurion, he gave the body to Joseph.
15.blb: And having known from the centurion, he granted the body to Joseph.
15.bbe: And when he had news of it from the captain, he let Joseph have the body.

15.msb: So Joseph bought a linen cloth, took down the body of Jesus, wrapped it in the cloth, and placed it in a tomb that had been cut out of the rock. Then he rolled a stone against the entrance to the tomb.
15.kjv: And he bought fine linen, and took him down, and wrapped him in the linen, and laid him in a sepulchre which was hewn out of a rock, and rolled a stone unto the door of the sepulchre.
15.blb: And having bought a linen cloth, having taken Him down, he wrapped Him in the linen cloth and laid Him in a tomb that was cut out of a rock. And he rolled a stone to the door of the tomb.
15.bbe: And he got a linen cloth and, taking him down, put the linen cloth round him, and put him in a place for the dead which had been cut out of a rock; and a stone was rolled against the door.

15.msb: Mary Magdalene and Mary the mother of Joses saw where His body was placed.
15.kjv: And Mary Magdalene and Mary the mother of Joses beheld where he was laid.
15.blb: And Mary Magdalene and Mary the mother of Joses were watching where He was laid.
15.bbe: And Mary Magdalene and Mary, the mother of Joses, saw where he was put.

16.msb: When the Sabbath was over, Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James, and Salome bought spices so they could go and anoint the body of Jesus.
16.kjv: And when the sabbath was past, Mary Magdalene, and Mary the mother of James, and Salome, had bought sweet spices, that they might come and anoint him.
16.blb: And on the Sabbath having passed, Mary Magdalene and Mary the mother of James and Salome bought spices so that, having come, they might anoint Him.
16.bbe: And when the Sabbath was past, Mary Magdalene and Mary, the mother of James, and Salome, got spices, so that they might come and put them on him.
16.heading: The Resurrection

16.msb: Very early on the first day of the week, just after sunrise, they went to the tomb.
16.kjv: And very early in the morning the first day of the week, they came unto the sepulchre at the rising of the sun.
16.blb: And very early on the first of the Sabbaths, they come to the tomb at the sun having arisen.
16.bbe: And very early after dawn on the first day of the week, they came at the time of the coming up of the sun to the place where the body had been put.

16.msb: They were asking one another, “Who will roll away the stone from the entrance of the tomb?”
16.kjv: And they said among themselves, Who shall roll us away the stone from the door of the sepulchre?
16.blb: And they were saying among themselves, “Who will roll away the stone for us out from the door of the tomb?”
16.bbe: And they were saying among themselves, Who will get the stone rolled away from the door for us?

16.msb: But when they looked up, they saw that the stone had been rolled away, even though it was extremely large.
16.kjv: And when they looked, they saw that the stone was rolled away: for it was very great.
16.blb: And having looked up, they see that the stone has been rolled away—for it was exceedingly large.
16.bbe: And looking up, they saw that the stone was rolled back; and it was of great size.

16.msb: When they entered the tomb, they saw a young man dressed in a white robe sitting on the right side, and they were alarmed.
16.kjv: And entering into the sepulchre, they saw a young man sitting on the right side, clothed in a long white garment; and they were affrighted.
16.blb: And having entered into the tomb, they saw a young man clothed in a white robe sitting on the right, and they were greatly amazed.
16.bbe: And when they went in, they saw a young man seated on the right side, dressed in a white robe; and they were full of wonder.

16.msb: But he said to them, “Do not be alarmed. You are looking for Jesus the Nazarene, who was crucified. He has risen! He is not here! See the place where they put Him.
16.kjv: And he saith unto them, Be not affrighted: Ye seek Jesus of Nazareth, which was crucified: he is risen; he is not here: behold the place where they laid him.
16.blb: Now he says to them, “Do not be amazed. You seek Jesus the Nazarene, the One having been crucified. He is risen! He is not here! Behold the place where they laid Him.
16.bbe: And he said to them, Do not be troubled: you are looking for Jesus, the Nazarene, who has been put to death on the cross; he has come back from the dead; he is not here: see, the place where they put him!

16.msb: But go, tell His disciples and Peter, ‘He is going ahead of you into Galilee. There you will see Him, just as He told you.’”
16.kjv: But go your way, tell his disciples and Peter that he goeth before you into Galilee: there shall ye see him, as he said unto you.
16.blb: But go, say to His disciples and to Peter, ‘He goes before you into Galilee. There you will see Him, as He said to you.’”
16.bbe: But go, say to his disciples and to Peter, He goes before you into Galilee: there you will see him, as he said to you.

16.msb: So the women left the tomb and ran away, trembling and bewildered. And in their fear they did not say a word to anyone.
16.kjv: And they went out quickly, and fled from the sepulchre; for they trembled and were amazed: neither said they any thing to any man; for they were afraid.
16.blb: And having gone out, they fled from the tomb, for trembling and amazement had seized them. And they spoke nothing to anyone, for they were afraid.
16.bbe: And they went out quickly from the place, because fear and great wonder had come on them: and they said nothing to anyone, because they were full of fear that...

16.msb: Early on the first day of the week, after Jesus had risen, He appeared first to Mary Magdalene, from whom He had driven out seven demons.
16.kjv: Now when Jesus was risen early the first day of the week, he appeared first to Mary Magdalene, out of whom he had cast seven devils.
16.blb: And having risen early on the first of the week, He appeared first to Mary Magdalene, from whom He had cast out seven demons.
16.bbe: Now when he came back from the dead early on the first day of the week, he went first to Mary Magdalene, from whom he had sent out seven evil spirits.
16.heading: Jesus Appears to Mary Magdalene

16.msb: She went and told those who had been with Him, who were mourning and weeping.
16.kjv: And she went and told them that had been with him, as they mourned and wept.
16.blb: She, having gone, reported to those having been with Him, mourning and weeping.
16.bbe: She went and gave news of it to those who had been with him, while they were sorrowing and weeping.

16.msb: And when they heard that Jesus was alive and she had seen Him, they did not believe it.
16.kjv: And they, when they had heard that he was alive, and had been seen of her, believed not.
16.blb: And they, having heard that He is alive and was seen by her, disbelieved.
16.bbe: And they, when it came to their ears that he was living, and had been seen by her, had no belief in it.

16.msb: After this, Jesus appeared in a different form to two of them as they walked along in the country.
16.kjv: After that he appeared in another form unto two of them, as they walked, and went into the country.
16.blb: And after these things, He appeared in another form to two of them as they are walking, going into the country.
16.bbe: And after these things he was seen in another form by two of them, while they were walking on their way into the country.
16.heading: Jesus Appears to Two Disciples

16.msb: And they went back and reported it to the rest, but they did not believe them either.
16.kjv: And they went and told it unto the residue: neither believed they them.
16.blb: And they, having gone, reported to the rest; neither did they believe them.
16.bbe: And they went away and gave news of it to the rest; and they had no belief in what was said.

16.msb: Later, as they were eating, Jesus appeared to the Eleven and rebuked them for their unbelief and hardness of heart, because they did not believe those who had seen Him after He had risen.
16.kjv: Afterward he appeared unto the eleven as they sat at meat, and upbraided them with their unbelief and hardness of heart, because they believed not them which had seen him after he was risen.
16.blb: And afterward, in their reclining, He appeared to the Eleven and rebuked their unbelief and hardness of heart, because they did not believe those having seen Him arisen.
16.bbe: And later he was seen by the eleven themselves while they were taking food; and he said sharp words to them because they had no faith and their hearts were hard, and because they had no belief in those who had seen him after he had come back from the dead.
16.heading: The Great Commission

16.msb: And He said to them, “Go into all the world and preach the gospel to every creature.
16.kjv: And he said unto them, Go ye into all the world, and preach the gospel to every creature.
16.blb: And He said to them, “Having gone into all the world, proclaim the gospel to all the creation.
16.bbe: And he said to them, Go into all the world, and give the good news to everyone.

16.msb: Whoever believes and is baptized will be saved, but whoever does not believe will be condemned.
16.kjv: He that believeth and is baptized shall be saved; but he that believeth not shall be damned.
16.blb: The one having believed and having been baptized will be saved, but the one having disbelieved will be condemned.
16.bbe: He who has faith and is given baptism will get salvation; but he who has not faith will be judged.

16.msb: And these signs will accompany those who believe: In My name they will drive out demons; they will speak in new tongues;
16.kjv: And these signs shall follow them that believe; In my name shall they cast out devils; they shall speak with new tongues;
16.blb: And these signs will accompany those having believed: In My name they will cast out demons; they will speak with new tongues;
16.bbe: And these signs will be with those who have faith: in my name they will send out evil spirits; and they will make use of new languages;

16.msb: they will pick up snakes, and if they drink any deadly poison, it will not harm them; they will lay their hands on the sick, and they will be made well.”
16.kjv: They shall take up serpents; and if they drink any deadly thing, it shall not hurt them; they shall lay hands on the sick, and they shall recover.
16.blb: and with their hands they will take up serpents; and if they drink anything deadly, it shall never hurt them; they will lay hands upon the sick, and they will be well.”
16.bbe: They will take up snakes, and if there is poison in their drink, it will do them no evil; they will put their hands on those who are ill, and they will get well.

16.msb: After the Lord had spoken to them, He was taken up into heaven and sat down at the right hand of God.
16.kjv: So then after the Lord had spoken unto them, he was received up into heaven, and sat on the right hand of God.
16.blb: Therefore indeed the Lord Jesus, after speaking to them, was taken up into heaven and sat at the right hand of God.
16.bbe: So then the Lord Jesus, after he had said these words to them, was taken up into heaven and took his seat at the right hand of God.
16.heading: The Ascension

16.msb: And they went out and preached everywhere, and the Lord worked through them, confirming His word by the signs that accompanied it. Amen.
16.kjv: And they went forth, and preached every where, the Lord working with them, and confirming the word with signs following. Amen.
16.blb: And they, having gone out, preached everywhere, the Lord working with them and confirming the word by the accompanying signs.
16.bbe: And they went out, preaching everywhere, the Lord working with them, and giving witness to the word by the signs which came after. So be it.

1.msb: Many have undertaken to compose an account of the things that have been fulfilled among us,
1.kjv: Forasmuch as many have taken in hand to set forth in order a declaration of those things which are most surely believed among us,
1.blb: Inasmuch as many took in hand to draw up a narration concerning the things having been fully carried out among us,
1.bbe: As a number of attempts have been made to put together in order an account of those events which took place among us,
1.heading: Dedication to Theophilus

1.msb: just as they were handed down to us by the initial eyewitnesses and servants of the word.
1.kjv: Even as they delivered them unto us, which from the beginning were eyewitnesses, and ministers of the word;
1.blb: just as they delivered them to us—those from the beginning having been eyewitnesses and servants of the word—
1.bbe: As they were handed down to us by those who saw them from the first and were preachers of the word,

1.msb: Therefore, having carefully investigated everything from the beginning, it seemed good also to me to write an orderly account for you, most excellent Theophilus,
1.kjv: It seemed good to me also, having had perfect understanding of all things from the very first, to write unto thee in order, most excellent Theophilus,
1.blb: it seemed good also to me, having followed closely from the first all things carefully, to write in consecutive order to you, most excellent Theophilus,
1.bbe: It seemed good to me, having made observation, with great care, of the direction of events in their order, to put the facts in writing for you, most noble Theophilus;

1.msb: so that you may know the certainty of the things you have been taught.
1.kjv: That thou mightest know the certainty of those things, wherein thou hast been instructed.
1.blb: so that you may know the certainty of the things that you were instructed.
1.bbe: So that you might have certain knowledge of those things about which you were given teaching.

1.msb: In the time of Herod king of Judea there was a priest named Zechariah, who belonged to the priestly division of Abijah, and whose wife Elizabeth was a descendant of Aaron.
1.kjv: There was in the days of Herod, the king of Judæa, a certain priest named Zacharias, of the course of Abia: and his wife was of the daughters of Aaron, and her name was Elisabeth.
1.blb: There was in the days of Herod king of Judea a certain priest, by name Zechariah, of the division of Abijah, and his wife of the daughters of Aaron, and her name Elizabeth.
1.bbe: In the days of Herod, king of Judaea, there was a certain priest, by name Zacharias, of the order of Abijah; and he had a wife of the family of Aaron, and her name was Elisabeth.
1.heading: Gabriel Foretells John’s Birth

1.msb: Both of them were righteous in the sight of God, walking blamelessly in all the commandments and decrees of the Lord.
1.kjv: And they were both righteous before God, walking in all the commandments and ordinances of the Lord blameless.
1.blb: And they were both righteous before God, going on in all the commandments and righteous requirements of the Lord, blameless.
1.bbe: They were upright in the eyes of God, keeping all the rules and orders of God, and doing no wrong.

1.msb: But they had no children, because Elizabeth was barren, and they were both well along in years.
1.kjv: And they had no child, because that Elisabeth was barren, and they both were now well stricken in years.
1.blb: And unto them was no child, as Elizabeth was barren and both were advanced in their days.
1.bbe: And they were without children, because Elisabeth had never given birth, and they were at that time very old.

1.msb: One day while Zechariah’s division was on duty and he was serving as priest before God,
1.kjv: And it came to pass, that while he executed the priest’s office before God in the order of his course,
1.blb: Now it came to pass in his serving as priest in the order of his division before God,
1.bbe: Now it came about that in his turn he was acting as priest before God,

1.msb: he was chosen by lot, according to the custom of the priesthood, to enter the temple of the Lord and burn incense.
1.kjv: According to the custom of the priest’s office, his lot was to burn incense when he went into the temple of the Lord.
1.blb: according to the custom of the priesthood, that it fell to him by lot to burn incense, having entered into the temple of the Lord.
1.bbe: And as was the way of the priests, he had to go into the Temple to see to the burning of perfumes.

1.msb: And at the hour of the incense offering, the whole congregation was praying outside.
1.kjv: And the whole multitude of the people were praying without at the time of incense.
1.blb: And all the multitude of the people was praying outside at the hour of the incense.
1.bbe: And all the people were offering prayers outside, at the time of the burning of perfumes.

1.msb: Just then an angel of the Lord appeared to Zechariah, standing at the right side of the altar of incense.
1.kjv: And there appeared unto him an angel of the Lord standing on the right side of the altar of incense.
1.blb: And an angel of the Lord appeared to him, standing at the right side of the altar of the incense.
1.bbe: And he saw an angel of the Lord in his place on the right side of the altar.

1.msb: When Zechariah saw him, he was startled and gripped with fear.
1.kjv: And when Zacharias saw him, he was troubled, and fear fell upon him.
1.blb: And Zechariah was troubled having seen, and fear fell upon him.
1.bbe: And Zacharias was troubled when he saw him, and fear came on him.

1.msb: But the angel said to him, “Do not be afraid, Zechariah, because your prayer has been heard. Your wife Elizabeth will bear you a son, and you are to give him the name John.
1.kjv: But the angel said unto him, Fear not, Zacharias: for thy prayer is heard; and thy wife Elisabeth shall bear thee a son, and thou shalt call his name John.
1.blb: But the angel said to him, “Do not be afraid, Zechariah, because your petition was heard, and your wife Elizabeth will bear to you a son, and you will call his name John.
1.bbe: But the angel said, Have no fear, Zacharias, for your prayer has come to the ears of God, and your wife Elisabeth will have a son, and his name will be John.

1.msb: He will be a joy and delight to you, and many will rejoice at his birth,
1.kjv: And thou shalt have joy and gladness; and many shall rejoice at his birth.
1.blb: And he will be joy and exultation to you, and many will rejoice at his birth,
1.bbe: And you will be glad and have great delight; and numbers of people will have joy at his birth.

1.msb: for he will be great in the sight of the Lord. He shall never take wine or strong drink, and he will be filled with the Holy Spirit even from his mother’s womb.
1.kjv: For he shall be great in the sight of the Lord, and shall drink neither wine nor strong drink; and he shall be filled with the Holy Ghost, even from his mother’s womb.
1.blb: for he will be great before the Lord. And he shall never drink wine and strong drink, and he will be full of the Holy Spirit even from the womb of his mother.
1.bbe: For he will be great in the eyes of the Lord; he will not take wine or strong drink; and he will be full of the Spirit of God from his birth.

1.msb: Many of the sons of Israel he will turn back to the Lord their God.
1.kjv: And many of the children of Israel shall he turn to the Lord their God.
1.blb: And many of the sons of Israel he will turn to the Lord their God.
1.bbe: And through him great numbers of the children of Israel will be turned to the Lord their God.

1.msb: And he will go on before the Lord in the spirit and power of Elijah, to turn the hearts of the fathers to their children and the disobedient to the wisdom of the righteous—to make ready a people prepared for the Lord.”
1.kjv: And he shall go before him in the spirit and power of Elias, to turn the hearts of the fathers to the children, and the disobedient to the wisdom of the just; to make ready a people prepared for the Lord.
1.blb: And he will go on before Him in the spirit and power of Elijah, to turn the hearts of the fathers to the children, and the disobedient to the wisdom of the righteous—to make ready a people prepared for the Lord.”
