4.blb: And having rolled up the scroll, having given it back to the attendant, He sat down. And the eyes of all in the synagogue were looking intently on Him.
4.bbe: And shutting the book he gave it back to the servant and took his seat: and the eyes of all in the Synagogue were fixed on him.

4.msb: and He began by saying, “Today this Scripture is fulfilled in your hearing.”
4.kjv: And he began to say unto them, This day is this scripture fulfilled in your ears.
4.blb: And He began to say to them, “Today this Scripture has been fulfilled in your ears.”
4.bbe: Then he said to them, Today this word has come true in your hearing.

4.msb: All spoke well of Him and marveled at the gracious words that came from His lips. “Isn’t this the son of Joseph?” they asked.
4.kjv: And all bare him witness, and wondered at the gracious words which proceeded out of his mouth. And they said, Is not this Joseph’s son?
4.blb: And all were testifying to Him and were marveling at the words of grace that are proceeding out of His mouth. And they were saying, “Is this not the son of Joseph?”
4.bbe: And they were all giving witness, with wonder, to the words of grace which came from his mouth: and they said, Is not this the son of Joseph?

4.msb: Jesus said to them, “Surely you will quote this proverb to Me: ‘Physician, heal yourself! Do here in Your hometown what we have heard that You did in Capernaum.’”
4.kjv: And he said unto them, Ye will surely say unto me this proverb, Physician, heal thyself: whatsoever we have heard done in Capernaum, do also here in thy country.
4.blb: And He said to them, “Surely you will say to Me this parable: ‘Physician, heal yourself! Whatsoever we heard was done in Capernaum, do also here in Your hometown.’”
4.bbe: And he said to them, Without doubt you will say to me, Let the medical man make himself well: the things which to our knowledge were done at Capernaum, do them here in your country.

4.msb: Then He added, “Truly I tell you, no prophet is accepted in his hometown.
4.kjv: And he said, Verily I say unto you, No prophet is accepted in his own country.
4.blb: And He said, “Truly I say to you that no prophet is acceptable in his hometown.
4.bbe: And he said to them, Truly I say to you, No prophet is honoured in his country.

4.msb: But I tell you truthfully that there were many widows in Israel in the time of Elijah, when the sky was shut for three and a half years and great famine swept over all the land.
4.kjv: But I tell you of a truth, many widows were in Israel in the days of Elias, when the heaven was shut up three years and six months, when great famine was throughout all the land;
4.blb: And in truth I say to you, many widows were in Israel in the days of Elijah, when the sky was shut up for three years and six months, when a great famine came upon all the land.
4.bbe: Truly I say to you, There were a number of widows in Israel in the days of Elijah, when the heaven was shut up for three years and six months and there was no food in the land;

4.msb: Yet Elijah was not sent to any of them, but to the widow of Zarephath in Sidon.
4.kjv: But unto none of them was Elias sent, save unto Sarepta, a city of Sidon, unto a woman that was a widow.
4.blb: And Elijah was sent to none of them, except to Zarephath of the Sidonians, to a woman, a widow.
4.bbe: But Elijah was not sent to one of them, but only to Zarephath, in the land of Sidon, to a woman who was a widow.

4.msb: And there were many lepers in Israel in the time of Elisha the prophet. Yet not one of them was cleansed—only Naaman the Syrian.”
4.kjv: And many lepers were in Israel in the time of Eliseus the prophet; and none of them was cleansed, saving Naaman the Syrian.
4.blb: And many lepers were in Israel in the time of Elisha the prophet, and none of them was cleansed, except Naaman the Syrian.”
4.bbe: And there were a number of lepers in Israel in the time of Elisha the prophet, and not one of them was made clean, but only Naaman the Syrian.

4.msb: On hearing this, all the people in the synagogue were enraged.
4.kjv: And all they in the synagogue, when they heard these things, were filled with wrath,
4.blb: And all in the synagogue were filled with anger, hearing these things.
4.bbe: And all who were in the Synagogue were very angry when these things were said to them.

4.msb: They got up, drove Him out of the town, and led Him to the brow of the hill on which the town was built, in order to throw Him over the cliff.
4.kjv: And rose up, and thrust him out of the city, and led him unto the brow of the hill whereon their city was built, that they might cast him down headlong.
4.blb: And having risen up, they cast Him out of the city and led Him unto the brow of the hill upon which their city had been built, so as to throw Him over.
4.bbe: And they got up and took him out of the town to the edge of the mountain on which their town was, so that they might send him down to his death.

4.msb: But Jesus passed through the crowd and went on His way.
4.kjv: But he passing through the midst of them went his way,
4.blb: But He, having passed through their midst, went away.
4.bbe: But he came through them and went on his way.

4.msb: Then He went down to Capernaum, a town in Galilee, and on the Sabbath He began to teach the people.
4.kjv: And came down to Capernaum, a city of Galilee, and taught them on the sabbath days.
4.blb: And He went down to Capernaum, a city of Galilee, and He was teaching them on the Sabbaths.
4.bbe: And he came down to Capernaum, a town of Galilee; and he was giving them teaching on the Sabbath.
4.heading: Jesus Expels an Unclean Spirit

4.msb: They were astonished at His teaching, because His message had authority.
4.kjv: And they were astonished at his doctrine: for his word was with power.
4.blb: And they were astonished at His teaching, because His word was with authority.
4.bbe: And they were surprised at his teaching, for his word was with authority.

4.msb: In the synagogue there was a man possessed by the spirit of an unclean demon. He cried out in a loud voice,
4.kjv: And in the synagogue there was a man, which had a spirit of an unclean devil, and cried out with a loud voice,
4.blb: And in the synagogue was a man having a spirit of an unclean demon. And he cried out in a loud voice,
4.bbe: And there was a man in the Synagogue who had an unclean spirit; and he gave a loud cry and said,

4.msb: “Ha! What do You want with us, Jesus of Nazareth? Have You come to destroy us? I know who You are—the Holy One of God!”
4.kjv: Saying, Let us alone; what have we to do with thee, thou Jesus of Nazareth? art thou come to destroy us? I know thee who thou art; the Holy One of God.
4.blb: “Ha! What to us and to You, Jesus the Nazarene? Did You come to destroy us? I know who You are—the Holy One of God!”
4.bbe: Let us be! what have we to do with you, Jesus of Nazareth? have you come to put an end to us? I have knowledge who you are, the Holy One of God.

4.msb: But Jesus rebuked the demon. “Be silent!” He said. “Come out of him!” At this, the demon threw the man down before them all and came out without harming him.
4.kjv: And Jesus rebuked him, saying, Hold thy peace, and come out of him. And when the devil had thrown him in the midst, he came out of him, and hurt him not.
4.blb: And Jesus rebuked him, saying, “Be silenced, and come out from him!” And having thrown him into the midst, the demon came out from him, in nothing having hurt him.
4.bbe: And Jesus said to him, Be quiet, and come out of him. And when the evil spirit had put him down on the earth in the middle of them, he came out of him, having done him no damage.

4.msb: All the people were overcome with amazement and asked one another, “What is this message? With authority and power He commands the unclean spirits, and they come out!”
4.kjv: And they were all amazed, and spake among themselves, saying, What a word is this! for with authority and power he commandeth the unclean spirits, and they come out.
4.blb: And amazement came upon all, and they were speaking together with one another, saying, “What word is this, that with authority and power He commands the unclean spirits, and they come out?”
4.bbe: And wonder came on them all and they said to one another, What are these words? for with authority and power he gives orders to the evil spirits and they come out.

4.msb: And the news about Jesus spread throughout the surrounding region.
4.kjv: And the fame of him went out into every place of the country round about.
4.blb: And the report concerning Him was going out into every place of the surrounding region.
4.bbe: And there was much talk about him in all the places round about.

4.msb: After Jesus had left the synagogue, He went to the home of Simon, whose mother-in-law was suffering from a high fever. So they appealed to Jesus on her behalf,
4.kjv: And he arose out of the synagogue, and entered into Simon’s house. And Simon’s wife’s mother was taken with a great fever; and they besought him for her.
4.blb: And having arisen out of the synagogue, He entered into the house of Simon. And Simon’s mother-in-law was oppressed with a great fever, and they asked Him concerning her.
4.bbe: And he got up and went out of the Synagogue and went into the house of Simon. And Simon's wife's mother was very ill with a burning heat; and in answer to their prayers for her
4.heading: Jesus Heals at Peter’s House

4.msb: and He stood over her and rebuked the fever, and it left her. And she got up at once and began to serve them.
4.kjv: And he stood over her, and rebuked the fever; and it left her: and immediately she arose and ministered unto them.
4.blb: And having stood over her, He rebuked the fever, and it left her. And immediately, having arisen, she was serving them.
4.bbe: He went near her, and with a sharp word he gave orders to the disease and it went away from her; and straight away she got up and took care of their needs.

4.msb: At sunset, all who were ill with various diseases were brought to Jesus, and laying His hands on each one, He healed them.
4.kjv: Now when the sun was setting, all they that had any sick with divers diseases brought them unto him; and he laid his hands on every one of them, and healed them.
4.blb: And at the setting of the sun, all, as many as had any ailing with various diseases, brought them to Him. And He, having laid the hands on each one of them, was healing them.
4.bbe: And at sundown all those who had anyone ill with any sort of disease, took them to him, and he put his hands on every one of them and made them well.

4.msb: Demons also came out of many people, crying out, “You are the Christ, the Son of God!” But He rebuked the demons and would not allow them to speak, because they knew He was the Christ.
4.kjv: And devils also came out of many, crying out, and saying, Thou art Christ the Son of God. And he rebuking them suffered them not to speak: for they knew that he was Christ.
4.blb: Now demons also were going out from many, crying out and saying, “You are the Son of God!” And rebuking them, He was not allowing them to speak, because they knew Him to be the Christ.
4.bbe: And evil spirits came out of a number of them, crying out and saying, You are the Son of God. But he gave them sharp orders not to say a word, because they had knowledge that he was the Christ.

4.msb: At daybreak, Jesus went out to a solitary place, and the crowds were looking for Him. They came to Him and tried to keep Him from leaving.
4.kjv: And when it was day, he departed and went into a desert place: and the people sought him, and came unto him, and stayed him, that he should not depart from them.
4.blb: And day having come, having gone out, He went into a solitary place. And the crowds were seeking Him, and they came up to Him and were detaining Him not to go from them.
4.bbe: And when it was day, he came out and went to a waste place; and great numbers of people came looking for him, and they came to him and would have kept him from going away.
4.heading: Jesus Preaches in Judea

4.msb: But Jesus told them, “I must preach the good news of the kingdom of God to the other towns as well, because that is why I was sent.”
4.kjv: And he said unto them, I must preach the kingdom of God to other cities also: for therefore am I sent.
4.blb: But He said to them, “It is necessary for Me to preach the good news of the kingdom of God to the other cities also, because for this I was sent.”
4.bbe: But he said to them, I have to give the good news of the kingdom of God in other towns, because that is why I was sent.

4.msb: And He continued to preach in the synagogues of Galilee.
4.kjv: And he preached in the synagogues of Galilee.
4.blb: And He was preaching in the synagogues of Judea.
4.bbe: And he was teaching in the Synagogues of Galilee.

5.msb: On one occasion, while Jesus was standing by the Lake of Gennesaret with the crowd pressing in on Him to hear the word of God,
5.kjv: And it came to pass, that, as the people pressed upon him to hear the word of God, he stood by the lake of Gennesaret,
5.blb: Now it came to pass, in the crowd also pressing on Him to hear the word of God, that He was standing by the lake of Gennesaret.
5.bbe: Now it came about that while the people came pushing to be near him, and to have knowledge of the word of God, he was by a wide stretch of water named Gennesaret;
5.heading: The First Disciples

5.msb: He saw two boats at the edge of the lake. The fishermen had left them and were washing their nets.
5.kjv: And saw two ships standing by the lake: but the fishermen were gone out of them, and were washing their nets.
5.blb: And He saw two boats standing by the lake; but the fishermen, having gone away from them, were washing the nets.
5.bbe: And he saw two boats by the edge of the water, but the fishermen had gone out of them and were washing their nets.

5.msb: Jesus got into the boat belonging to Simon and asked him to put out a little from shore. And sitting down, He taught the people from the boat.
5.kjv: And he entered into one of the ships, which was Simon’s, and prayed him that he would thrust out a little from the land. And he sat down, and taught the people out of the ship.
5.blb: And having entered into one of the boats, which was Simon’s, He asked him to put out a little from the land. And having sat down, out of the boat He was teaching the crowds.
5.bbe: And he got into one of the boats, the property of Simon, and made a request to him to go a little way out from the land. And being seated he gave the people teaching from the boat.

5.msb: When Jesus had finished speaking, He said to Simon, “Put out into deep water and let down your nets for a catch.”
5.kjv: Now when he had left speaking, he said unto Simon, Launch out into the deep, and let down your nets for a draught.
5.blb: And when He ceased speaking, He said to Simon, “Put out into the deep and let down your nets for a catch.”
5.bbe: And when his talk was ended, he said to Simon, Go out into deep water, and let down your nets for fish.

5.msb: “Master,” Simon replied, “we have worked hard all night without catching anything. But because You say so, I will let down the net.”
5.kjv: And Simon answering said unto him, Master, we have toiled all the night, and have taken nothing: nevertheless at thy word I will let down the net.
5.blb: And answering, Simon said, “Master, having toiled through the whole night, we took nothing. But upon Your word, I will let down the nets.”
5.bbe: And Simon, answering, said, Master, we were working all night and we took nothing: but at your word I will let down the nets.

5.msb: When they had done so, they caught such a large number of fish that their net began to tear.
5.kjv: And when they had this done, they inclosed a great multitude of fishes: and their net brake.
5.blb: And having done this, they enclosed a great multitude of fish, and their nets were tearing.
5.bbe: And when they had done this, they got such a great number of fish that it seemed as if their nets would be broken;

5.msb: So they signaled to their partners in the other boat to come and help them, and they came and filled both boats so full that they began to sink.
5.kjv: And they beckoned unto their partners, which were in the other ship, that they should come and help them. And they came, and filled both the ships, so that they began to sink.
5.blb: And they beckoned to the partners in the other boat, having come, to help them, and they came and filled both boats so that they were sinking.
5.bbe: And they made signs to their friends in the other boat to come to their help. And they came, and the two boats were so full that they were going down.

5.msb: When Simon Peter saw this, he fell at Jesus’ knees. “Go away from me, Lord,” he said, “for I am a sinful man.”
5.kjv: When Simon Peter saw it, he fell down at Jesus’ knees, saying, Depart from me; for I am a sinful man, O Lord.
5.blb: And having seen, Simon Peter fell at the knees of Jesus, saying, “Go out from me, Lord, because I am a sinful man.”
5.bbe: But Simon, when he saw it, went down at the knees of Jesus and said, Go away from me, O Lord, for I am a sinner.

5.msb: For he and his companions were astonished at the catch of fish they had taken,
5.kjv: For he was astonished, and all that were with him, at the draught of the fishes which they had taken:
5.blb: For amazement laid hold on him and on all those with him at the catch of the fish that they took,
5.bbe: For he was full of wonder and so were all those who were with him, at the number of fish which they had taken;

5.msb: and so were his partners James and John, the sons of Zebedee. “Do not be afraid,” Jesus said to Simon. “From now on you will catch men.”
5.kjv: And so was also James, and John, the sons of Zebedee, which were partners with Simon. And Jesus said unto Simon, Fear not; from henceforth thou shalt catch men.
5.blb: and likewise also James and John, the sons of Zebedee, who were partners with Simon. And Jesus said to Simon, “Do not be afraid; from now on you will be catching men.”
5.bbe: And so were James and John, the sons of Zebedee, who were working with Simon. And Jesus said to Simon, Have no fear; from this time forward you will be a fisher of men.

5.msb: And when they had brought their boats ashore, they left everything and followed Him.
5.kjv: And when they had brought their ships to land, they forsook all, and followed him.
5.blb: And having brought down the boats upon the land, having left all, they followed Him.
5.bbe: And when they had got their boats to the land, they gave up everything and went after him.

5.msb: While Jesus was in one of the towns, a man came along who was covered with leprosy. When he saw Jesus, he fell facedown and begged Him, “Lord, if You are willing, You can make me clean.”
5.kjv: And it came to pass, when he was in a certain city, behold a man full of leprosy: who seeing Jesus fell on his face, and besought him, saying, Lord, if thou wilt, thou canst make me clean.
5.blb: And it came to pass, in His being in one of the cities, that behold, a man full of leprosy, and having seen Jesus, having fallen upon his face, begged Him, saying, “Lord, if You are willing, You are able to cleanse me.”
5.bbe: And it came about that while he was in one of the towns, there was a leper there: and when he saw Jesus he went down on his face in prayer to him, saying, Lord, if it is your pleasure, you have power to make me clean.
5.heading: The Leper’s Prayer

5.msb: Jesus reached out His hand and touched the man. “I am willing,” He said. “Be clean!” And immediately the leprosy left him.
5.kjv: And he put forth his hand, and touched him, saying, I will: be thou clean. And immediately the leprosy departed from him.
5.blb: And having stretched out the hand, He touched him, “saying, I am willing; be cleansed!” And immediately the leprosy went away from him.
5.bbe: And he put out his hand to him and said, It is my pleasure; be clean. And straight away his disease went from him.

5.msb: “Do not tell anyone,” Jesus instructed him. “But go, show yourself to the priest and present the offering Moses prescribed for your cleansing, as a testimony to them.”
5.kjv: And he charged him to tell no man: but go, and shew thyself to the priest, and offer for thy cleansing, according as Moses commanded, for a testimony unto them.
5.blb: And He instructed him to tell no one: “But, having gone, show yourself to the priest, and offer concerning your cleansing, just as Moses commanded, for a testimony to them.”
5.bbe: And he gave him orders: Say nothing to any man, but let the priest see you and give an offering so that you may be made clean, as the law of Moses says, and for a witness to them.

5.msb: But the news about Jesus spread all the more, and great crowds came to hear Him and to be healed by Him of their sicknesses.
5.kjv: But so much the more went there a fame abroad of him: and great multitudes came together to hear, and to be healed by him of their infirmities.
5.blb: But the word concerning Him was spreading still more, and many crowds were coming to hear and to be healed from their infirmities.
5.bbe: But news of him went out all the more, in every direction, and great numbers of people came together to give hearing to his words and to be made well from their diseases.

5.msb: Yet He frequently withdrew to the wilderness to pray.
5.kjv: And he withdrew himself into the wilderness, and prayed.
5.blb: And He Himself was withdrawing into the wilderness and praying.
5.bbe: But he went away by himself to a waste place for prayer.

5.msb: One day Jesus was teaching, and the Pharisees and teachers of the law were sitting there. People had come from Jerusalem and from every village of Galilee and Judea, and the power of the Lord was present for Him to heal the sick.
5.kjv: And it came to pass on a certain day, as he was teaching, that there were Pharisees and doctors of the law sitting by, which were come out of every town of Galilee, and Judæa, and Jerusalem: and the power of the Lord was present to heal them.
5.blb: And it came to pass, on one of the days, that He was teaching, and Pharisees and teachers of the law were sitting, who were come out of every village of Galilee, and of Judea, and of Jerusalem. And the power of the Lord was there for Him to heal.
5.bbe: And it came about that on one of these days he was teaching; and some Pharisees and teachers of the law were seated there, who had come from every town of Galilee and Judaea and from Jerusalem; and the power of the Lord was with him, to make those who were ill free from their diseases.
5.heading: Jesus Heals a Paralytic

5.msb: Just then some men came carrying a paralyzed man on a mat. They tried to bring him inside to set him before Jesus,
5.kjv: And, behold, men brought in a bed a man which was taken with a palsy: and they sought means to bring him in, and to lay him before him.
5.blb: And behold, men bringing upon a bed a man who was paralyzed, and they were seeking to bring him in and to place him before Him.
5.bbe: And some men had with them, on a bed, a man who was ill, without power of moving; and they made attempts to get him in and put him before Jesus.

5.msb: but they could not find a way through the crowd. So they went up on the roof and lowered him on his mat through the tiles into the middle of the crowd, right in front of Jesus.
5.kjv: And when they could not find by what way they might bring him in because of the multitude, they went upon the housetop, and let him down through the tiling with his couch into the midst before Jesus.
5.blb: And not having found what way they might bring him in through the crowd, having gone up on the housetop, they let him down with the little bed through the tiles into the midst before Jesus.
5.bbe: And because of the mass of people, there was no way to get him in; so they went up on the top of the house and let him down through the roof, on his bed, into the middle in front of Jesus.

5.msb: When Jesus saw their faith, He said to the man, “Friend, your sins are forgiven.”
5.kjv: And when he saw their faith, he said unto him, Man, thy sins are forgiven thee.
5.blb: And having seen their faith, He said, “Man, your sins have been forgiven you.”
5.bbe: And seeing their faith he said, Man, you have forgiveness for your sins.

5.msb: But the scribes and Pharisees began thinking to themselves, “Who is this man who speaks blasphemy? Who can forgive sins but God alone?”
5.kjv: And the scribes and the Pharisees began to reason, saying, Who is this which speaketh blasphemies? Who can forgive sins, but God alone?
5.blb: And the scribes and the Pharisees began to reason, saying, “Who is this who speaks blasphemies? Who is able to forgive sins except God alone?”
5.bbe: And the scribes and Pharisees were having an argument, saying, Who is this, who has no respect for God? who is able to give forgiveness for sins, but God only?

5.msb: Knowing what they were thinking, Jesus replied, “Why are you thinking these things in your hearts?
5.kjv: But when Jesus perceived their thoughts, he answering said unto them, What reason ye in your hearts?
5.blb: And Jesus, having known their reasonings, answering, said to them, “Why do you reason in your hearts?
5.bbe: But Jesus, who had knowledge of their thoughts, said to them, Why are you reasoning in your hearts?

5.msb: Which is easier: to say, ‘Your sins are forgiven,’ or to say, ‘Get up and walk’?
5.kjv: Whether is easier, to say, Thy sins be forgiven thee; or to say, Rise up and walk?
5.blb: Which is easier: to say, ‘Your sins have been forgiven you,’ or to say, ‘Arise and walk’?
5.bbe: Which is the simpler: to say, You have forgiveness for your sins; or to say, Get up and go?

5.msb: But so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on the earth to forgive sins …” He said to the paralytic, “I tell you, get up, pick up your mat, and go home.”
5.kjv: But that ye may know that the Son of man hath power upon earth to forgive sins, (he said unto the sick of the palsy,) I say unto thee, Arise, and take up thy couch, and go into thine house.
5.blb: But so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on the earth to forgive sins...” He said to the paralyzed one, “I say to you, arise, and having taken up your mat, go to your house.”
5.bbe: But so that you may see that on earth the Son of man has authority for the forgiveness of sins, (he said to the man who was ill,) I say to you, Get up, and take up your bed, and go into your house.

5.msb: And immediately the man stood up before them, took what he had been lying on, and went home glorifying God.
5.kjv: And immediately he rose up before them, and took up that whereon he lay, and departed to his own house, glorifying God.
5.blb: And immediately, having risen up before them, having taken up that on which he was lying, he went away to his house, glorifying God.
5.bbe: And straight away he got up before them, and took up his bed and went away to his house giving praise to God.

5.msb: Everyone was taken with amazement and glorified God. They were filled with awe and said, “We have seen remarkable things today.”
5.kjv: And they were all amazed, and they glorified God, and were filled with fear, saying, We have seen strange things to day.
5.blb: And amazement took all, and they were glorifying God. And they were filled with fear, saying, “We saw remarkable things today.”
5.bbe: And wonder overcame them all, and they gave glory to God; and they were full of fear, saying, We have seen strange things today.

5.msb: After this, Jesus went out and saw a tax collector named Levi sitting at the tax booth. “Follow Me,” He told him,
5.kjv: And after these things he went forth, and saw a publican, named Levi, sitting at the receipt of custom: and he said unto him, Follow me.
5.blb: And after these things, He went out and saw a tax collector named Levi sitting at the tax booth. And He said to him, “Follow Me.”
5.bbe: And after these things he went out, and saw Levi, a tax-farmer, seated at the place where taxes were taken, and said to him, Come after me.
5.heading: Jesus Calls Levi

5.msb: and Levi got up, left everything, and followed Him.
5.kjv: And he left all, rose up, and followed him.
5.blb: And having left all, having arisen, he began to follow Him.
5.bbe: And giving up his business, he got up and went after him.

5.msb: Then Levi hosted a great banquet for Jesus at his house. A large crowd of tax collectors was there, along with others who were eating with them.
5.kjv: And Levi made him a great feast in his own house: and there was a great company of publicans and of others that sat down with them.
5.blb: And Levi made a great banquet for Him in his house, and there was a great crowd of tax collectors and others who were reclining with them.
5.bbe: And Levi made a great feast for him in his house: and a great number of tax-farmers and others were seated at table with them.

5.msb: But their scribes and the Pharisees complained to Jesus’ disciples, “Why do you eat and drink with tax collectors and sinners?”
5.kjv: But their scribes and Pharisees murmured against his disciples, saying, Why do ye eat and drink with publicans and sinners?
5.blb: And the Pharisees and their scribes were grumbling at His disciples, saying, “Why do you eat and drink with the tax collectors and sinners?”
5.bbe: And the Pharisees and their scribes made protests against his disciples, saying, Why do you take food and drink with tax-farmers and sinners?

5.msb: Jesus answered, “It is not the healthy who need a doctor, but the sick.
5.kjv: And Jesus answering said unto them, They that are whole need not a physician; but they that are sick.
5.blb: And answering, Jesus said to them, “Those being in good health have no need of a physician, but those being ill.
5.bbe: And Jesus, answering, said to them, Those who are well have no need of a medical man, but those who are ill.

5.msb: I have not come to call the righteous, but sinners, to repentance.”
5.kjv: I came not to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.
5.blb: I have not come to call righteous ones, but sinners, to repentance.”
5.bbe: I have come, not to get the upright, but sinners, so that they may be turned from their sins.

5.msb: Then they said to Him, “Why do John’s disciples and those of the Pharisees frequently fast and pray, but Yours keep on eating and drinking?”
5.kjv: And they said unto him, Why do the disciples of John fast often, and make prayers, and likewise the disciples of the Pharisees; but thine eat and drink?
5.blb: And they said to Him, “The disciples of John fast often and make petitions; likewise also those of the Pharisees; but Yours eat and drink.”
5.bbe: And they said to him, The disciples of John frequently go without food, and make prayers, and so do the disciples of the Pharisees; but your disciples take food and drink.
5.heading: Questions about Fasting

5.msb: Jesus replied, “Can you make the guests of the bridegroom fast while He is with them?
5.kjv: And he said unto them, Can ye make the children of the bridechamber fast, while the bridegroom is with them?
5.blb: And Jesus said to them, “Are you able to make the sons of the bridechamber fast while the bridegroom is with them?
5.bbe: And Jesus said, Are you able to make the friends of the newly-married man go without food when he is with them?

5.msb: But the time will come when the bridegroom will be taken from them; then they will fast.”
5.kjv: But the days will come, when the bridegroom shall be taken away from them, and then shall they fast in those days.
5.blb: But days will come also when the bridegroom shall have been taken away from them; then they will fast in those days.”
5.bbe: But the days will come when he will be taken away from them, and then they will go without food.

5.msb: He also told them a parable: “No one sews a piece of cloth from a new garment onto an old one. If he does, he will tear the new garment as well, and the patch from the new will not match the old.
5.kjv: And he spake also a parable unto them; No man putteth a piece of a new garment upon an old; if otherwise, then both the new maketh a rent, and the piece that was taken out of the new agreeth not with the old.
5.blb: And He was speaking also a parable to them: “No one having torn a patch from a new garment puts it on an old garment. and if otherwise, he will tear the new also, and the old will not match the patch from the new.
5.bbe: And he said to them, in a story, No man takes a bit of cloth from a new coat and puts it on to an old coat, for so the new coat would be damaged and the bit from the new would not go well with the old.
5.heading: The Patches and the Wineskins

5.msb: And no one pours new wine into old wineskins. If he does, the new wine will burst the wineskins, the wine will spill, and the wineskins will be ruined.
5.kjv: And no man putteth new wine into old bottles; else the new wine will burst the bottles, and be spilled, and the bottles shall perish.
5.blb: And no one puts new wine into old wineskins. and if otherwise, the new wine will burst the wineskins, and it will be poured out, and the wineskins will be destroyed.
5.bbe: And no man puts new wine into old wine-skins, for fear that the skins will be burst by the new wine, and the wine be let out, and the skins come to destruction.

5.msb: Instead, new wine is poured into new wineskins, and both are preserved.
5.kjv: But new wine must be put into new bottles; and both are preserved.
5.blb: But new wine must be put into fresh wineskins.
5.bbe: But new wine has to be put into new wine-skins.

5.msb: And no one after drinking old wine immediately wants new, for he says, ‘The old is better.’”
5.kjv: No man also having drunk old wine straightway desireth new: for he saith, The old is better.
5.blb: And no one having drunk old wine wants new; for he says, ‘The old is good.’”
5.bbe: And no man, having had old wine, has any desire for new, for he says, The old is better.

6.msb: On the second chief Sabbath, Jesus was passing through the grainfields, and His disciples began to pick the heads of grain, rub them in their hands, and eat them.
6.kjv: And it came to pass on the second sabbath after the first, that he went through the corn fields; and his disciples plucked the ears of corn, and did eat, rubbing them in their hands.
6.blb: And it came to pass on a Sabbath that He is passing through grainfields, and His disciples were plucking and were eating the heads of grain, rubbing them in the hands.
6.bbe: Now it came about that on the Sabbath he was going through the fields of grain, and his disciples took the heads of the grain for food, crushing them in their hands.
6.heading: The Lord of the Sabbath

6.msb: But some of the Pharisees asked, “Why are you doing what is unlawful to do on the Sabbath?”
6.kjv: And certain of the Pharisees said unto them, Why do ye that which is not lawful to do on the sabbath days?
6.blb: But some of the Pharisees said, “Why do you do what is not lawful on the Sabbaths?”
6.bbe: But some of the Pharisees said, Why do you do what it is not right to do on the Sabbath?

6.msb: Jesus replied, “Have you not read what David did when he and his companions were hungry?
6.kjv: And Jesus answering them said, Have ye not read so much as this, what David did, when himself was an hungred, and they which were with him;
6.blb: And answering, Jesus said to them, “Did you not even read this, what David did when he was hungry—he and those being with him:
6.bbe: And Jesus said, Have you not seen in the Writings what David did when he was in need of food, he, and those who were with him;

6.msb: He entered the house of God, took the consecrated bread and also gave it to his companions, and ate what is lawful only for the priests to eat.”
6.kjv: How he went into the house of God, and did take and eat the shewbread, and gave also to them that were with him; which it is not lawful to eat but for the priests alone?
6.blb: how he entered into the house of God and, having taken the loaves of the presentation, he ate and gave to those with him—which it is not lawful to eat, except only for the priests?”
6.bbe: How he went into the house of God and took for food the holy bread, which only the priests may take, and gave it to those who were with him?

6.msb: Then Jesus declared, “The Son of Man is Lord even of the Sabbath.”
6.kjv: And he said unto them, That the Son of man is Lord also of the sabbath.
6.blb: And He was saying to them, “The Son of Man is Lord of the Sabbath.”
6.bbe: And he said, The Son of man is lord even of the Sabbath.

6.msb: On another Sabbath Jesus entered the synagogue and was teaching, and a man was there whose right hand was withered.
6.kjv: And it came to pass also on another sabbath, that he entered into the synagogue and taught: and there was a man whose right hand was withered.
6.blb: And it came to pass on another Sabbath that He entered into the synagogue and taught, and there was a man there, and his right hand was withered.
6.bbe: And it came about, on another Sabbath, that he went into the Synagogue and was teaching there. And a man was there whose right hand was dead.
6.heading: Jesus Heals on the Sabbath

6.msb: Looking for an accusation against Jesus, the scribes and Pharisees were watching Him closely to see if He would heal on the Sabbath.
6.kjv: And the scribes and Pharisees watched him, whether he would heal on the sabbath day; that they might find an accusation against him.
6.blb: And the scribes and the Pharisees were closely watching Him, whether He heals on the Sabbath, so that they might find reason to accuse Him.
6.bbe: And the scribes and Pharisees were watching him to see if he would make him well on the Sabbath, so that they might be able to say something against him.

6.msb: But Jesus knew their thoughts and said to the man with the withered hand, “Get up and stand among us.” So he got up and stood there.
6.kjv: But he knew their thoughts, and said to the man which had the withered hand, Rise up, and stand forth in the midst. And he arose and stood forth.
6.blb: And He had known their reasonings, and He said to the man having the withered hand, “Arise and stand in the midst.” And having risen up, he stood.
6.bbe: But he had knowledge of their thoughts; and he said to the man whose hand was dead, Get up and come into the middle. And he got up and came forward.

6.msb: Then Jesus said to them, “I ask you one thing: Is it lawful on the Sabbath to do good or to do evil, to save life or to destroy it?”
6.kjv: Then said Jesus unto them, I will ask you one thing; Is it lawful on the sabbath days to do good, or to do evil? to save life, or to destroy it?
6.blb: Then Jesus said to them, “I ask you, is it lawful on the Sabbath to do good or to do evil, to save life or to destroy?”
6.bbe: And Jesus said, I put the question to you, Is it right to do good on the Sabbath or to do evil? to give life or to take it away?

6.msb: And after looking around at all of them, He said to the man, “Stretch out your hand.” He did so, and it was restored as sound as the other.
6.kjv: And looking round about upon them all, he said unto the man, Stretch forth thy hand. And he did so: and his hand was restored whole as the other.
6.blb: And having looked around at them all, He said to him, “Stretch out your hand.” And he did, and his hand was restored.
6.bbe: And looking round on all of them, he said to him, Put out your hand. And he did so: and his hand was made well.

6.msb: But the scribes and Pharisees were filled with rage and began to discuss with one another what they might do to Jesus.
6.kjv: And they were filled with madness; and communed one with another what they might do to Jesus.
6.blb: And they were filled with madness, and they were discussing with one another what they might do to Jesus.
6.bbe: But they were full of wrath, and were talking together about what they might do to Jesus.

6.msb: In those days Jesus went out to the mountain to pray, and He spent the night in prayer to God.
6.kjv: And it came to pass in those days, that he went out into a mountain to pray, and continued all night in prayer to God.
6.blb: And it came to pass in those days that He went out to the mountain to pray, and He was spending the night in prayer to God.
6.bbe: And it came about in those days that he went out to the mountain for prayer; and he was all night in prayer to God.
6.heading: The Twelve Apostles

6.msb: When daylight came, He called His disciples to Him and chose twelve of them, whom He also designated as apostles:
6.kjv: And when it was day, he called unto him his disciples: and of them he chose twelve, whom also he named apostles;
6.blb: And when it became day, He summoned His disciples, also having chosen out from them twelve, whom He also named apostles:
6.bbe: And the day came and, turning to his disciples, he made a selection from among them of twelve, to whom he gave the name of Apostles;

6.msb: Simon, whom He named Peter, and his brother Andrew; James and John; Philip and Bartholomew;
6.kjv: Simon, (whom he also named Peter,) and Andrew his brother, James and John, Philip and Bartholomew,
6.blb: Simon, whom He also named Peter, and his brother Andrew, and James and John, and Philip and Bartholomew,
6.bbe: Simon, to whom he gave the name of Peter, and Andrew, his brother, and James and John and Philip and Bartholomew

6.msb: Matthew and Thomas; James son of Alphaeus and Simon called the Zealot;
6.kjv: Matthew and Thomas, James the son of Alphæus, and Simon called Zelotes,
6.blb: and Matthew and Thomas, and James son of Alphaeus, and Simon called Zealot,
6.bbe: And Matthew and Thomas and James, the son of Alphaeus, and Simon, who was named the Zealot,

6.msb: Judas son of James, and Judas Iscariot, who became a traitor.
6.kjv: And Judas the brother of James, and Judas Iscariot, which also was the traitor.
6.blb: and Judas son of James, and Judas Iscariot, who became a betrayer.
6.bbe: And Judas, the son of James, and Judas Iscariot, he who was false to him.

6.msb: Then Jesus came down with them and stood on a level place. A crowd of His disciples was there, along with a great number of people from all over Judea, Jerusalem, and the seacoast of Tyre and Sidon.
6.kjv: And he came down with them, and stood in the plain, and the company of his disciples, and a great multitude of people out of all Judæa and Jerusalem, and from the sea coast of Tyre and Sidon, which came to hear him, and to be healed of their diseases;
6.blb: And having come down with them, He stood on a level place, and a great crowd of His disciples, and a great multitude of the people from all Judea and Jerusalem and the sea coast of Tyre and Sidon,
6.bbe: And he came down with them to a level place, and a great band of his disciples, and a very great number of people from all Judaea and Jerusalem and from the parts of Tyre and Sidon by the sea, came to give hearing to him, and to be made well from their diseases;
6.heading: Jesus Heals the Multitudes

6.msb: They had come to hear Him and to be healed of their diseases, along with those troubled by unclean spirits. And they were healed.
6.kjv: And they that were vexed with unclean spirits: and they were healed.
6.blb: who came to hear Him and to be healed from their diseases. And those troubled from unclean spirits were healed.
6.bbe: And those who were troubled with unclean spirits were made well.

6.msb: The entire crowd was trying to touch Him, because power was coming from Him and healing them all.
6.kjv: And the whole multitude sought to touch him: for there went virtue out of him, and healed them all.
6.blb: And all the crowd was seeking to touch Him, because power was going out from Him and was healing all.
6.bbe: And all the people were desiring to be touched by him, for power came from him and made them all well.

6.msb: Looking up at His disciples, Jesus said: “Blessed are you who are poor, for yours is the kingdom of God.
6.kjv: And he lifted up his eyes on his disciples, and said, Blessed be ye poor: for yours is the kingdom of God.
6.blb: And He, having lifted up His eyes to His disciples, was saying: “Blessed are the poor, because yours is the kingdom of God.
6.bbe: And turning his eyes to his disciples he said, Happy are you who are poor: for the kingdom of God is yours.
6.heading: The Beatitudes

6.msb: Blessed are you who hunger now, for you will be filled. Blessed are you who weep now, for you will laugh.
6.kjv: Blessed are ye that hunger now: for ye shall be filled. Blessed are ye that weep now: for ye shall laugh.
6.blb: Blessed are those hungering now, because you will be filled. Blessed are those weeping now, because you will laugh.
6.bbe: Happy are you who are in need of food now: for you will be made full. Happy are you who are weeping now; for you will be glad.

6.msb: Blessed are you when people hate you, and when they exclude you and insult you and reject your name as evil because of the Son of Man.
6.kjv: Blessed are ye, when men shall hate you, and when they shall separate you from their company, and shall reproach you, and cast out your name as evil, for the Son of man’s sake.
6.blb: Blessed are you when men may hate you, and when they may exclude you and may reproach you and may cast out your name as evil, on account of the Son of Man.
6.bbe: Happy are you, when men have hate for you, and put you away from among them and say angry words to you, turning away in disgust at your name, because of the Son of man.

6.msb: Rejoice in that day and leap for joy, because great is your reward in heaven. For their fathers treated the prophets in the same way.
6.kjv: Rejoice ye in that day, and leap for joy: for, behold, your reward is great in heaven: for in the like manner did their fathers unto the prophets.
6.blb: Rejoice in that day and leap, for behold, your reward is great in heaven. For according to the same their fathers were doing to the prophets.
6.bbe: Be glad in that day, and be lifted up for joy, for your reward in heaven will be great: for their fathers did these same things to the prophets.

6.msb: But woe to you who are rich, for you have already received your comfort.
6.kjv: But woe unto you that are rich! for ye have received your consolation.
6.blb: But woe to you who are rich, because you have your comfort in full.
6.bbe: But unhappy are you who have wealth: for you have been comforted now.
6.heading: Woes to the Satisfied

6.msb: Woe to you who are well fed, for you will hunger. Woe to you who laugh now, for you will mourn and weep.
6.kjv: Woe unto you that are full! for ye shall hunger. Woe unto you that laugh now! for ye shall mourn and weep.
6.blb: Woe to you who have been filled now, because you will hunger. Woe to those laughing now, because you will mourn and weep.
6.bbe: Unhappy are you who are full of food now: for you will be in need. Unhappy are you who are laughing now: for you will be crying in sorrow.

6.msb: Woe to you when men speak well of you, for their fathers treated the false prophets in the same way.
6.kjv: Woe unto you, when all men shall speak well of you! for so did their fathers to the false prophets.
6.blb: Woe when all men may speak well of you, for according to the same their fathers were doing to the false prophets.
6.bbe: Unhappy are you when all men give you their approval: for so their fathers did to the false prophets.

6.msb: But to those of you who will listen, I say: Love your enemies, do good to those who hate you,
6.kjv: But I say unto you which hear, Love your enemies, do good to them which hate you,
6.blb: But to you who are hearing I say: Love your enemies, do good to those hating you,
6.bbe: But I say to you who give ear to me, Have love for those who are against you, do good to those who have hate for you,
6.heading: Love Your Enemies

6.msb: bless those who curse you, pray for those who mistreat you.
6.kjv: Bless them that curse you, and pray for them which despitefully use you.
6.blb: bless those cursing you, pray for those mistreating you.
6.bbe: Give blessing to those who give you curses, say prayers for those who are cruel to you.

6.msb: If someone strikes you on one cheek, turn to him the other also. And if someone takes your cloak, do not withhold your tunic as well.
6.kjv: And unto him that smiteth thee on the one cheek offer also the other; and him that taketh away thy cloke forbid not to take thy coat also.
6.blb: To the one striking you on the cheek, offer the other also; and from the one taking away your cloak, do not withhold also your tunic.
6.bbe: If a man gives you a blow on one side of your face, then let the other side be turned to him; from him who takes away your coat, do not keep back your robe.

6.msb: Give to everyone who asks you, and if anyone takes what is yours, do not demand it back.
6.kjv: Give to every man that asketh of thee; and of him that taketh away thy goods ask them not again.
6.blb: To everyone asking you, give, and from the one taking away what is yours, do not demand it back.
6.bbe: Give to everyone who comes with a request, and if a man takes away your property, make no attempt to get it back again.

6.msb: Do to others as you would have them do to you.
6.kjv: And as ye would that men should do to you, do ye also to them likewise.
6.blb: And just as you want that men may do to you, do to them likewise.
6.bbe: Do to others as you would have them do to you.

6.msb: If you love those who love you, what credit is that to you? Even sinners love those who love them.
6.kjv: For if ye love them which love you, what thank have ye? for sinners also love those that love them.
6.blb: And if you love those loving you, what grace is it to you? For even the sinners love those loving them.
6.bbe: If you have love for those who have love for you, what credit is it to you? for even sinners have love for those who have love for them.

6.msb: If you do good to those who do good to you, what credit is that to you? For even sinners do the same.
6.kjv: And if ye do good to them which do good to you, what thank have ye? for sinners also do even the same.
6.blb: For even if you do good to those doing good to you, what grace is it to you? Even the sinners do the same.
6.bbe: And if you do good to those who do good to you, what credit is it to you? for even sinners do the same.

6.msb: And if you lend to those from whom you expect repayment, what credit is that to you? For even sinners lend to sinners, expecting to be repaid in full.
6.kjv: And if ye lend to them of whom ye hope to receive, what thank have ye? for sinners also lend to sinners, to receive as much again.
6.blb: And if you lend to those from whom you expect to receive back, what grace is it to you? Even sinners lend to sinners, that they might receive back the equivalent.
6.bbe: And if you let those have the use of your money, from whom you are hoping to get it back, what credit is it to you? even sinners do so to sinners, hoping to get back as much as they gave.

6.msb: But love your enemies, do good to them, and lend to them, expecting nothing in return. Then your reward will be great, and you will be sons of the Most High; for He is kind to the ungrateful and wicked.
6.kjv: But love ye your enemies, and do good, and lend, hoping for nothing again; and your reward shall be great, and ye shall be the children of the Highest: for he is kind unto the unthankful and to the evil.
6.blb: But love your enemies, and do good, and lend expecting nothing back. And your reward will be great, and you will be sons of the Most High, because He is kind to the ungrateful and evil.
6.bbe: But be loving to those who are against you and do them good, and give them your money, not giving up hope, and your reward will be great and you will be the sons of the Most High: for he is kind to evil men, and to those who have hard hearts.

6.msb: Therefore be merciful, just as your Father is merciful.
6.kjv: Be ye therefore merciful, as your Father also is merciful.
6.blb: Be merciful, as also your Father is merciful.
6.bbe: Be full of pity, even as your Father is full of pity.

6.msb: Do not judge, and you will not be judged. Do not condemn, and you will not be condemned. Forgive, and you will be forgiven.
6.kjv: Judge not, and ye shall not be judged: condemn not, and ye shall not be condemned: forgive, and ye shall be forgiven:
6.blb: And do not judge, and you shall not be judged; and do not condemn, and you shall not be condemned; release, and you will be released.
6.bbe: Be not judges of others, and you will not be judged: do not give punishment to others, and you will not get punishment yourselves: make others free, and you will be made free:
6.heading: Judging Others

6.msb: Give, and it will be given to you. A good measure, pressed down, shaken together, and running over will be poured into your lap. For with the same measure you use, it will be measured back to you.”
6.kjv: Give, and it shall be given unto you; good measure, pressed down, and shaken together, and running over, shall men give into your bosom. For with the same measure that ye mete withal it shall be measured to you again.
6.blb: Give, and it will be given to you. A good measure, pressed down, shaken, running over, they will give into your bosom. For with what measure you measure, it will be measured back to you.”
6.bbe: Give, and it will be given to you; good measure, crushed down, full and running over, they will give to you. For in the same measure as you give, it will be given to you again.

6.msb: Jesus also told them a parable: “Can a blind man lead a blind man? Will they not both fall into a pit?
6.kjv: And he spake a parable unto them, Can the blind lead the blind? shall they not both fall into the ditch?
6.blb: And He also spoke a parable to them: “Is a blind man able to guide a blind man? Will they not both fall into a pit?
6.bbe: And he gave them teaching in the form of a story, saying, Is it possible for one blind man to be guide to another? will they not go falling together into a hole?

6.msb: A disciple is not above his teacher, but everyone who is fully trained will be like his teacher.
6.kjv: The disciple is not above his master: but every one that is perfect shall be as his master.
6.blb: A disciple is not above his teacher, but everyone fully trained will be like his teacher.
6.bbe: The disciple is not greater than his master, but everyone whose learning is complete will be like his master.

6.msb: Why do you look at the speck in your brother’s eye but fail to notice the beam in your own eye?
6.kjv: And why beholdest thou the mote that is in thy brother’s eye, but perceivest not the beam that is in thine own eye?
6.blb: And why do you look at the splinter that is in the eye of your brother, but not notice the beam that is in your own eye?
6.bbe: And why do you take note of the grain of dust in your brother's eye, but take no note of the bit of wood which is in your eye?

6.msb: Or how can you say, ‘Brother, let me take the speck out of your eye,’ while you yourself fail to see the beam in your own eye? You hypocrite! First take the beam out of your own eye, and then you will see clearly to remove the speck from your brother’s eye.
6.kjv: Either how canst thou say to thy brother, Brother, let me pull out the mote that is in thine eye, when thou thyself beholdest not the beam that is in thine own eye? Thou hypocrite, cast out first the beam out of thine own eye, and then shalt thou see clearly to pull out the mote that is in thy brother’s eye.
6.blb: How are you able to say to your brother, ‘Brother, permit that I might cast out the splinter that is in your eye,’ yourself not seeing the beam in your eye? Hypocrite! First cast out the beam from your eye, and then you will see clearly to cast out the splinter that is in the eye of your brother.
6.bbe: How will you say to your brother, Brother, let me take the grain of dust out of your eye, when you yourself do not see the bit of wood in your eye? O false one! first take the wood out of your eye and then you will see clearly to take the dust out of your brother's eye.

6.msb: No good tree bears bad fruit, nor does a bad tree bear good fruit.
6.kjv: For a good tree bringeth not forth corrupt fruit; neither doth a corrupt tree bring forth good fruit.
6.blb: For there is no good tree producing rotten fruit, nor again a rotten tree producing good fruit.
6.bbe: For no good tree gives bad fruit, and no bad tree gives good fruit.
6.heading: A Tree and Its Fruit

6.msb: For each tree is known by its own fruit. Indeed, figs are not gathered from thornbushes, nor grapes from brambles.
6.kjv: For every tree is known by his own fruit. For of thorns men do not gather figs, nor of a bramble bush gather they grapes.
6.blb: For each tree is known by its own fruit. For they do not gather figs from thorns, nor do they pick grapes from a bramble bush.
6.bbe: For every tree is judged by its fruit. Men do not get figs from thorns, or grapes from blackberry plants.

6.msb: The good man brings good things out of the good treasure of his heart, and the evil man brings evil things out of the evil treasure of his heart. For out of the overflow of the heart, the mouth speaks.
6.kjv: A good man out of the good treasure of his heart bringeth forth that which is good; and an evil man out of the evil treasure of his heart bringeth forth that which is evil: for of the abundance of the heart his mouth speaketh.
6.blb: The good man out of the good treasure of his heart brings forth what is good, and the evil out of the evil brings forth what is evil. For out of the abundance of the heart, his mouth speaks.
6.bbe: The good man, out of the good store of his heart, gives good things; and the evil man, out of his evil store, gives evil: for out of the full store of the heart come the words of the mouth.

6.msb: Why do you call Me ‘Lord, Lord,’ but do not do what I say?
6.kjv: And why call ye me, Lord, Lord, and do not the things which I say?
6.blb: And why do you call Me ‘Lord, Lord,’ and not do what I say?
6.bbe: Why do you say to me, Lord, Lord, and do not the things which I say?
6.heading: The House on the Rock

6.msb: I will show you what he is like who comes to Me and hears My words and acts on them:
6.kjv: Whosoever cometh to me, and heareth my sayings, and doeth them, I will shew you to whom he is like:
6.blb: Everyone who is coming to Me and hearing My words and doing them, I will show you whom he is like.
6.bbe: Everyone who comes to me and gives ear to my words and does them, I will make clear to you what he is like:

6.msb: He is like a man building a house, who dug down deep and laid his foundation on the rock. When the flood came, the torrent crashed against that house but could not shake it, because its foundation was on the rock.
6.kjv: He is like a man which built an house, and digged deep, and laid the foundation on a rock: and when the flood arose, the stream beat vehemently upon that house, and could not shake it: for it was founded upon a rock.
6.blb: He is like a man building a house, who dug and deepened and laid a foundation on the rock. And a flood having come, the river burst upon that house, and it was not able to shake it, because it was well built.
6.bbe: He is like a man building a house, who went deep and put the base of it on a rock; and when the water came up and the river was driving against that house, it was not moved, because the building was good.

6.msb: But the one who hears My words and does not act on them is like a man who built his house on ground without a foundation. The torrent crashed against that house, and immediately it fell—and great was its destruction!”
6.kjv: But he that heareth, and doeth not, is like a man that without a foundation built an house upon the earth; against which the stream did beat vehemently, and immediately it fell; and the ruin of that house was great.
6.blb: But the one having heard and not having done is like a man having built a house on the ground without a foundation, on which the river burst, and immediately it fell—and the ruin of that house was great!”
6.bbe: But he who gives hearing, without doing, is like a man building a house on the earth without a base for it; and when the force of the river came against it, straight away it came down; and the destruction of that house was great.

7.msb: When Jesus had concluded His discourse in the hearing of the people, He went to Capernaum.
7.kjv: Now when he had ended all his sayings in the audience of the people, he entered into Capernaum.
7.blb: And when He completed all His words in the hearing of the people, He entered into Capernaum.
7.bbe: After he had come to the end of all his words in the hearing of the people, he went into Capernaum.
7.heading: The Faith of the Centurion

7.msb: There a highly valued servant of a centurion was sick and about to die.
7.kjv: And a certain centurion’s servant, who was dear unto him, was sick, and ready to die.
7.blb: And a certain servant of a centurion, who was valued highly to him, being ill, was about to die.
7.bbe: And a certain captain had a servant who was very dear to him; this servant was ill and near to death.

7.msb: When the centurion heard about Jesus, he sent some Jewish elders to ask Him to come and heal his servant.
7.kjv: And when he heard of Jesus, he sent unto him the elders of the Jews, beseeching him that he would come and heal his servant.
7.blb: And having heard about Jesus, he sent elders of the Jews to Him, asking Him that, having come, He might save his servant.
7.bbe: And when news of Jesus came to his ears, he sent to him rulers of the Jews, requesting that he would come and make his servant well.

7.msb: They came to Jesus and pleaded with Him earnestly, “This man is worthy to have You grant this,
7.kjv: And when they came to Jesus, they besought him instantly, saying, That he was worthy for whom he should do this:
7.blb: And having come to Jesus, they were imploring Him earnestly, saying, “He is worthy to whom You will grant this,
7.bbe: And they, when they came to Jesus, made their request warmly, saying,

7.msb: for he loves our nation and has built our synagogue.”
7.kjv: For he loveth our nation, and he hath built us a synagogue.
7.blb: for he loves our nation, and he built the synagogue for us.”
7.bbe: It is right for you to do this for him, because he is a friend to our nation, and himself has put up a Synagogue for us.

7.msb: So Jesus went with them. But when He was not far from the house, the centurion sent friends with the message: “Lord, do not trouble Yourself, for I am not worthy to have You come under my roof.
7.kjv: Then Jesus went with them. And when he was now not far from the house, the centurion sent friends to him, saying unto him, Lord, trouble not thyself: for I am not worthy that thou shouldest enter under my roof:
7.blb: And Jesus was going with them, and now in His being not far away from the house, the centurion sent friends, saying to Him, “Lord, do not trouble Yourself, for I am not fit that You should enter under my roof.
7.bbe: And Jesus went with them. And when he was not far from the house, the man sent friends to him, saying, Lord, do not give yourself trouble: for I am not important enough for you to come into my house:

7.msb: That is why I did not consider myself worthy to come to You. But just say the word, and my servant will be healed.
7.kjv: Wherefore neither thought I myself worthy to come unto thee: but say in a word, and my servant shall be healed.
7.blb: Therefore neither did I count myself worthy to come to You. But say a word, and let my servant be healed.
7.bbe: And I had the feeling that I was not even good enough to come to you: but say the word only, and my servant will be well.

7.msb: For I myself am a man under authority, with soldiers under me. I tell one to go, and he goes, and another to come, and he comes. I tell my servant to do something, and he does it.”
7.kjv: For I also am a man set under authority, having under me soldiers, and I say unto one, Go, and he goeth; and to another, Come, and he cometh; and to my servant, Do this, and he doeth it.
7.blb: For I also am a man appointed under authority, having soldiers under me. And I say to this one, ‘Go,’ and he goes; and to another, ‘Come,’ and he comes; and to my servant, ‘Do this,’ and he does.”
7.bbe: For I, myself, am a man under authority, having men under me; and I say to this one, Go, and he goes; and to another, Come, and he comes; and to my servant, Do this, and he does it.

7.msb: When Jesus heard this, He marveled at the centurion. Turning to the crowd following Him, He said, “I tell you, not even in Israel have I found such great faith.”
7.kjv: When Jesus heard these things, he marvelled at him, and turned him about, and said unto the people that followed him, I say unto you, I have not found so great faith, no, not in Israel.
7.blb: And having heard these things, Jesus marveled at him. And having turned to the crowd following Him, He said, “I say to you, not even in Israel did I find such great faith.”
7.bbe: And when these things were said to Jesus, he was surprised, and, turning to the mass of people coming after him, said, I have not seen such great faith, no, not in Israel.

7.msb: And when the messengers returned to the house, they found the ailing servant in good health.
7.kjv: And they that were sent, returning to the house, found the servant whole that had been sick.
7.blb: And having returned to the house, those having been sent found the servant in good health.
7.bbe: And when those who were sent came back to the house they saw that the servant was well.

7.msb: Soon afterward, Jesus went to a town called Nain. Many of His disciples went with Him, accompanied by a large crowd.
7.kjv: And it came to pass the day after, that he went into a city called Nain; and many of his disciples went with him, and much people.
7.blb: And it came to pass on the next day that He went into a city called Nain, and His disciples were going with Him, and a great crowd.
7.bbe: And it came about, after a little time, that he went to a town named Nain; and his disciples went with him, and a great number of people.
7.heading: Jesus Raises a Widow’s Son

7.msb: As He approached the town gate, He saw a dead man being carried out, the only son of his mother, and she was a widow. And a large crowd from the town was with her.
7.kjv: Now when he came nigh to the gate of the city, behold, there was a dead man carried out, the only son of his mother, and she was a widow: and much people of the city was with her.
7.blb: And as He drew near to the gate of the city, then, behold, a dead man was being carried out, the only begotten son of his mother; and she was a widow. And a large crowd of the city was with her.
7.bbe: Now when he came near the door of the town, a dead man was being taken out, the only son of his mother, who was a widow: and a great number of people from the town were with her.

7.msb: When the Lord saw her, He had compassion on her and said, “Do not weep.”
7.kjv: And when the Lord saw her, he had compassion on her, and said unto her, Weep not.
7.blb: And having seen her, the Lord was moved with compassion toward her and said to her, “Do not weep.”
7.bbe: And when the Lord saw her, he had pity on her and said to her, Be not sad.

7.msb: Then He went up and touched the coffin, and those carrying it stood still. “Young man,” He said, “I tell you, get up!”
7.kjv: And he came and touched the bier: and they that bare him stood still. And he said, Young man, I say unto thee, Arise.
7.blb: And having come up, He touched the bier; and those bearing it stood still. And He said, “Young man, I say to you, arise!”
7.bbe: And he came near, and put his hand on the stretcher where the dead man was: and those who were moving it came to a stop. And he said, Young man, I say to you, Get up.

7.msb: And the dead man sat up and began to speak! Then Jesus gave him back to his mother.
7.kjv: And he that was dead sat up, and began to speak. And he delivered him to his mother.
7.blb: And the dead man sat up and began to speak, and He gave him to his mother.
7.bbe: And the dead man got up, and words came from his lips. And he gave him to his mother.

7.msb: A sense of awe swept over all of them, and they glorified God. “A great prophet has appeared among us!” they said. “God has visited His people!”
7.kjv: And there came a fear on all: and they glorified God, saying, That a great prophet is risen up among us; and, That God hath visited his people.
7.blb: And fear took all, and they were glorifying God, saying, “A great prophet arose among us!” and, “God visited His people!”
7.bbe: And fear came on all, and they gave praise to God, saying, A great prophet is among us: and, God has given thought to his people.

7.msb: And the news about Jesus spread throughout Judea and all the surrounding region.
7.kjv: And this rumour of him went forth throughout all Judæa, and throughout all the region round about.
7.blb: And the word of this went forth in all Judea about Him—and in all the surrounding region.
7.bbe: And this story about him went through all Judaea and the places round about.

7.msb: Then John’s disciples informed him about all these things.
7.kjv: And the disciples of John shewed him of all these things.
7.blb: And his disciples reported to John about all these things.
7.bbe: And the disciples of John gave him an account of all these things.
7.heading: John’s Inquiry

7.msb: So John called two of his disciples and sent them to ask Jesus, “Are You the One who was to come, or should we look for someone else?”
7.kjv: And John calling unto him two of his disciples sent them to Jesus, saying, Art thou he that should come? or look we for another?
7.blb: And having summoned a certain two of his disciples, John sent to the Lord, saying, “Are You the coming One, or do we look for another?”
7.bbe: Then John sent two of his disciples to the Lord, saying, Are you he who is to come, or are we waiting for another?

7.msb: When the men came to Jesus, they said, “John the Baptist sent us to ask, ‘Are You the One who was to come, or should we look for someone else?’”
7.kjv: When the men were come unto him, they said, John Baptist hath sent us unto thee, saying, Art thou he that should come? or look we for another?
7.blb: And having come to Him, the men said, “John the Baptist sent us to You, saying, ‘Are You the coming One, or do we look for another?’”
7.bbe: And when the men came to him they said, John the Baptist has sent us to you, saying, Are you he who is to come, or are we waiting for another?

7.msb: Now at that very hour Jesus healed many people of their diseases, afflictions, and evil spirits, and He gave sight to many who were blind.
7.kjv: And in that same hour he cured many of their infirmities and plagues, and of evil spirits; and unto many that were blind he gave sight.
7.blb: In that very hour, He healed many of diseases and afflictions and evil spirits, and to many blind He granted to see.
7.bbe: At that time, he made a number of people free from their diseases and their pains, and from evil spirits; and to others who were blind he gave back the use of their eyes.

7.msb: So Jesus replied, “Go back and report to John what you have seen and heard: The blind receive sight, the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead are raised, and the good news is preached to the poor.
7.kjv: Then Jesus answering said unto them, Go your way, and tell John what things ye have seen and heard; how that the blind see, the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead are raised, to the poor the gospel is preached.
7.blb: And answering, He said to them, “Having gone, report to John what you saw and heard: The blind receive sight, the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, and the deaf hear, the dead are raised, the poor have good news proclaimed.
7.bbe: And answering them he said, Go back and give news to John of what you have seen, and the things which have come to your ears; the blind now see, those who had no power in their legs are walking, lepers are made clean, those who had no hearing now have their ears open, dead men come to life again, and the poor have the good news given to them.

7.msb: Blessed is the one who does not fall away on account of Me.”
7.kjv: And blessed is he, whosoever shall not be offended in me.
7.blb: And blessed is the one who shall not be caused to stumble in Me.”
7.bbe: And a blessing will be on him who has no doubts about me.

7.msb: After John’s messengers had left, Jesus began to speak to the crowds about John: “What did you go out into the wilderness to see? A reed swaying in the wind?
7.kjv: And when the messengers of John were departed, he began to speak unto the people concerning John, What went ye out into the wilderness for to see? A reed shaken with the wind?
7.blb: And the messengers of John having gone away, He began to speak to the crowds about John: “What did you go out into the wilderness to see? A reed shaken by the wind?
7.bbe: And when the men who were sent by John had gone away, he said to the people, about John, What did you go out into the waste land to see? a tall stem moving in the wind?
7.heading: Jesus Testifies about John

7.msb: Otherwise, what did you go out to see? A man dressed in fine clothes? Look, those who wear elegant clothing and live in luxury are found in palaces.
7.kjv: But what went ye out for to see? A man clothed in soft raiment? Behold, they which are gorgeously apparelled, and live delicately, are in kings’ courts.
7.blb: But what did you go out to see? A man arrayed in soft garments? Behold, those in splendid clothing and living in luxury are in the palaces.
7.bbe: But what did you go out to see? a man in soft clothing? See now, those who have beautiful clothing and delicate food are in kings' houses.

7.msb: What then did you go out to see? A prophet? Yes, I tell you, and more than a prophet.
7.kjv: But what went ye out for to see? A prophet? Yea, I say unto you, and much more than a prophet.
7.blb: But what did you go out to see? A prophet? Yes, I say to you, and more than a prophet.
7.bbe: But what did you go out to see? a prophet? Yes, I say to you, and more than a prophet.

7.msb: This is the one about whom it is written: ‘Behold, I will send My messenger ahead of You, who will prepare Your way before You.’
7.kjv: This is he, of whom it is written, Behold, I send my messenger before thy face, which shall prepare thy way before thee.
7.blb: This is he about whom it has been written: ‘Behold, I send My messenger before Your face, who will prepare Your way before You.’
7.bbe: This is he of whom it has been said, See, I send my servant before your face, who will make ready your way before you.

7.msb: For I tell you, among those born of women there is no one greater prophet than John the Baptist, yet even the least in the kingdom of God is greater than he.”
7.kjv: For I say unto you, Among those that are born of women there is not a greater prophet than John the Baptist: but he that is least in the kingdom of God is greater than he.
7.blb: I say to you, no one among those born of women is greater than John; yet the least in the kingdom of God is greater than he.”
7.bbe: I say to you, Among all the sons of women, not one is greater than John: but he who is least in the kingdom of God is greater than he.

7.msb: All the people who heard this, even the tax collectors, acknowledged God’s justice. For they had received the baptism of John.
7.kjv: And all the people that heard him, and the publicans, justified God, being baptized with the baptism of John.
7.blb: And all the people having heard, even the tax collectors, declared God righteous, having been baptized with the baptism of John.
7.bbe: (And all the people, and the tax-farmers, to whom John had given baptism, when they had knowledge of these things, gave glory to God.

7.msb: But the Pharisees and experts in the law rejected God’s purpose for themselves, because they had not been baptized by John.
7.kjv: But the Pharisees and lawyers rejected the counsel of God against themselves, being not baptized of him.
7.blb: But the Pharisees and the lawyers set aside the counsel of God for themselves, not having been baptized by him.
7.bbe: But the Pharisees and the teachers of the law were against the purpose of God for themselves, not having had his baptism.)

7.msb: “To what, then, can I compare the men of this generation? What are they like?
7.kjv: And the Lord said, Whereunto then shall I liken the men of this generation? and to what are they like?
7.blb: “To what, therefore, will I liken the men of this generation? And to what are they like?
7.bbe: What comparison am I to make of the men of this generation? what are they like?

7.msb: They are like children sitting in the marketplace and calling out to one another: ‘We played the flute for you, and you did not dance; we sang a dirge for you, and you did not weep.’
7.kjv: They are like unto children sitting in the marketplace, and calling one to another, and saying, We have piped unto you, and ye have not danced; we have mourned to you, and ye have not wept.
7.blb: They are like children sitting in the marketplace and calling to one another, saying: ‘We played the flute for you, and you did not dance; we sang a dirge, and you did not weep.’
7.bbe: They are like children who are seated in the market-place, crying out to one another, and saying, We made music for you, but you did not take part in the dance; we gave cries of sorrow, but you were not sad.

7.msb: For John the Baptist came neither eating bread nor drinking wine, and you say, ‘He has a demon!’
7.kjv: For John the Baptist came neither eating bread nor drinking wine; and ye say, He hath a devil.
7.blb: For John the Baptist has come neither eating bread nor drinking wine, and you say, ‘He has a demon!’
7.bbe: For John the Baptist came, taking no food or drink, and you say, He has an evil spirit.

7.msb: The Son of Man came eating and drinking, and you say, ‘Look at this glutton and drunkard, a friend of tax collectors and sinners!’
7.kjv: The Son of man is come eating and drinking; and ye say, Behold a gluttonous man, and a winebibber, a friend of publicans and sinners!
7.blb: The Son of Man has come eating and drinking, and you say, ‘Behold, a man, a glutton and a drunkard, a friend of tax collectors and of sinners!’
7.bbe: The Son of man came feasting, and you say, Here is a lover of food and wine, a friend of tax-farmers and sinners.

7.msb: But wisdom is vindicated by all her children.”
7.kjv: But wisdom is justified of all her children.
7.blb: And wisdom was justified from all her children.”
7.bbe: But wisdom is judged to be right by all her children.

7.msb: Then one of the Pharisees invited Jesus to eat with him, and He entered the Pharisee’s house and reclined at the table.
7.kjv: And one of the Pharisees desired him that he would eat with him. And he went into the Pharisee’s house, and sat down to meat.
7.blb: And one of the Pharisees was requesting of Him that He should eat with him, and having entered into the house of the Pharisee, He reclined.
7.bbe: And one of the Pharisees made a request that he would take a meal with him. And he went into the Pharisee's house and took his seat at the table.
7.heading: A Sinful Woman Anoints Jesus

7.msb: When a sinful woman from that town learned that Jesus was dining there, she brought an alabaster jar of perfume.
7.kjv: And, behold, a woman in the city, which was a sinner, when she knew that Jesus sat at meat in the Pharisee’s house, brought an alabaster box of ointment,
7.blb: And behold, a woman in the city who was a sinner. And having known that He is reclining in the house of the Pharisee, having taken an alabaster flask of fragrant oil,
