13.blb: And having seen her, Jesus called her near and said to her, “Woman, you have been freed from your infirmity.”
13.bbe: And when Jesus saw her, he said to her, Woman, you are made free from your disease.

13.msb: Then He placed His hands on her, and immediately she straightened up and began to glorify God.
13.kjv: And he laid his hands on her: and immediately she was made straight, and glorified God.
13.blb: And He laid the hands on her, and immediately she was set upright and was glorifying God.
13.bbe: And he put his hands on her, and she was made straight, and gave praise to God.

13.msb: But the synagogue leader was indignant that Jesus had healed on the Sabbath. “There are six days for work,” he told the crowd. “So come and be healed on those days and not on the Sabbath.”
13.kjv: And the ruler of the synagogue answered with indignation, because that Jesus had healed on the sabbath day, and said unto the people, There are six days in which men ought to work: in them therefore come and be healed, and not on the sabbath day.
13.blb: And answering, the synagogue ruler, indignant because Jesus healed on the Sabbath, was saying to the crowd, “There are six days in which it is necessary to work. Therefore, coming, be healed in these, and not on the day of the Sabbath.”
13.bbe: And the ruler of the Synagogue was angry because Jesus had made her well on the Sabbath, and he said to the people, There are six days in which men may do work: so come on those days to be made well, and not on the Sabbath.

13.msb: “You hypocrites!” the Lord replied. “Does not each of you on the Sabbath untie his ox or donkey from the stall and lead it to water?
13.kjv: The Lord then answered him, and said, Thou hypocrite, doth not each one of you on the sabbath loose his ox or his ass from the stall, and lead him away to watering?
13.blb: But the Lord answered him and said, “Hypocrites! Does not each one of you loose his ox or donkey from the stall on the Sabbath, and having led it away, give to it to drink?
13.bbe: But the Lord gave him an answer and said, O you false men! do you not, every one of you, on the Sabbath, let loose his ox and his ass and take it to the water?

13.msb: Then should not this daughter of Abraham, whom Satan has kept bound for eighteen long years, be released from her bondage on the Sabbath day?”
13.kjv: And ought not this woman, being a daughter of Abraham, whom Satan hath bound, lo, these eighteen years, be loosed from this bond on the sabbath day?
13.blb: And this one, being a daughter of Abraham whom Satan bound, behold, eighteen years, was it not necessary for her to be loosed from this bond on the day of the Sabbath?”
13.bbe: And is it not right for this daughter of Abraham, who has been in the power of Satan for eighteen years, to be made free on the Sabbath?

13.msb: When Jesus said this, all His adversaries were humiliated. And the whole crowd rejoiced at all the glorious things He was doing.
13.kjv: And when he had said these things, all his adversaries were ashamed: and all the people rejoiced for all the glorious things that were done by him.
13.blb: And on His saying these things, all those opposed to Him were ashamed; and all the crowd was rejoicing at all the glorious things that were being done by Him.
13.bbe: And when he said these things, those who were against him were shamed, and all the people were full of joy because of the great things which were done by him.

13.msb: Then Jesus asked, “What is the kingdom of God like? To what can I compare it?
13.kjv: Then said he, Unto what is the kingdom of God like? and whereunto shall I resemble it?
13.blb: And He was saying, “What is the kingdom of God like? And to what will I liken it?
13.bbe: Then he said, What is the kingdom of God like? what comparison may I make of it?
13.heading: The Parable of the Mustard Seed

13.msb: It is like a mustard seed that a man tossed into his garden. It grew and became a great tree, and the birds of the air nested in its branches.”
13.kjv: It is like a grain of mustard seed, which a man took, and cast into his garden; and it grew, and waxed a great tree; and the fowls of the air lodged in the branches of it.
13.blb: It is like a grain of mustard that a man, having taken, cast into his garden; and it grew and became a tree, and the birds of the sky lodged in its branches.”
13.bbe: It is like a grain of mustard seed which a man took and put in his garden, and it became a tree, and the birds of heaven made their resting-places in its branches.

13.msb: Again He asked, “To what can I compare the kingdom of God?
13.kjv: And again he said, Whereunto shall I liken the kingdom of God?
13.blb: And again, He said, “To what shall I liken the kingdom of God?
13.bbe: And again he said, What is the kingdom of God like?
13.heading: The Parable of the Leaven

13.msb: It is like leaven that a woman took and mixed into three measures of flour, until all of it was leavened.”
13.kjv: It is like leaven, which a woman took and hid in three measures of meal, till the whole was leavened.
13.blb: It is like leaven that a woman, having taken it, hid in three measures of flour, until it all was leavened.”
13.bbe: It is like leaven, which a woman put into three measures of meal, and it was all leavened.

13.msb: Then Jesus traveled throughout the towns and villages, teaching as He made His way toward Jerusalem.
13.kjv: And he went through the cities and villages, teaching, and journeying toward Jerusalem.
13.blb: And He was going through by towns and villages, teaching and making progress toward Jerusalem.
13.bbe: And he went on his way, through towns and country places, teaching and journeying to Jerusalem.
13.heading: The Narrow Door

13.msb: “Lord,” someone asked Him, “will only a few people be saved?” Jesus answered,
13.kjv: Then said one unto him, Lord, are there few that be saved? And he said unto them,
13.blb: And someone said to Him, “Lord, are those being saved few?” And He said to them,
13.bbe: And someone said to him, Lord, will only a small number have salvation? And he said to them,

13.msb: “Make every effort to enter through the narrow gate. For many, I tell you, will try to enter and will not be able.
13.kjv: Strive to enter in at the strait gate: for many, I say unto you, will seek to enter in, and shall not be able.
13.blb: “Strive to enter through the narrow door, because many, I say to you, will seek to enter and will not be able.
13.bbe: Do your best to go in by the narrow door, for I say to you, A number will make the attempt to go in, but will not be able to do so.

13.msb: After the master of the house gets up and shuts the door, you will stand outside knocking and saying, ‘Lord, Lord, open the door for us.’ But he will reply, ‘I do not know where you are from.’
13.kjv: When once the master of the house is risen up, and hath shut to the door, and ye begin to stand without, and to knock at the door, saying, Lord, Lord, open unto us; and he shall answer and say unto you, I know you not whence ye are:
13.blb: From that time the master of the house shall have risen up and shall have shut the door, then you shall begin to stand outside and to knock at the door, saying, ‘Lord, open to us.’ And answering, he will say to you, ‘I do not know from where you are.’
13.bbe: When the master of the house has got up, and the door has been shut, and you, still outside, give blows on the door, saying, Lord, let us in; he will make answer and say, I have no knowledge of where you come from.

13.msb: Then you will say, ‘We ate and drank with you, and you taught in our streets.’
13.kjv: Then shall ye begin to say, We have eaten and drunk in thy presence, and thou hast taught in our streets.
13.blb: Then you will begin to say, ‘We ate in your presence, and we drank, and you taught in our streets.’
13.bbe: Then you will say, We have taken food and drink with you, and you were teaching in our streets.

13.msb: And he will answer, ‘I tell you, I do not know where you are from. Depart from me, all you evildoers.’
13.kjv: But he shall say, I tell you, I know you not whence ye are; depart from me, all ye workers of iniquity.
13.blb: And he will say, ‘I am saying to you, I do not know from where you are; depart from me, all you workers of unrighteousness.’
13.bbe: But he will say, Truly, I have no knowledge of you or where you come from; go away from me, you workers of evil.

13.msb: There will be weeping and gnashing of teeth when you see Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, and all the prophets in the kingdom of God, but you yourselves are thrown out.
13.kjv: There shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth, when ye shall see Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob, and all the prophets, in the kingdom of God, and you yourselves thrust out.
13.blb: There will be weeping and gnashing of the teeth when you shall see Abraham and Isaac and Jacob and all the prophets in the kingdom of God, but you are being cast outside.
13.bbe: There will be weeping and cries of sorrow when you see Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and all the prophets, in the kingdom of God, but you yourselves are shut outside.

13.msb: People will come from east and west and north and south, and will recline at the table in the kingdom of God.
13.kjv: And they shall come from the east, and from the west, and from the north, and from the south, and shall sit down in the kingdom of God.
13.blb: And they will come from east and west and from north and south and will recline in the kingdom of God.
13.bbe: And they will come from the east and from the west, from the north and from the south, and take their places in the kingdom of God.

13.msb: And indeed, some who are last will be first, and some who are first will be last.”
13.kjv: And, behold, there are last which shall be first, and there are first which shall be last.
13.blb: And behold, there are last who will be first, and there are first who will be last.”
13.bbe: And the last will be first, and the first will be last.

13.msb: On that very day, some Pharisees came to Jesus and told Him, “Leave this place and get away, because Herod wants to kill You.”
13.kjv: The same day there came certain of the Pharisees, saying unto him, Get thee out, and depart hence: for Herod will kill thee.
13.blb: In the same hour, some Pharisees came near, saying to Him, “Go out and proceed from here, because Herod wants to kill You.”
13.bbe: At that time, certain Pharisees came to him and said, Go away from this place, because Herod's purpose is to put you to death.
13.heading: Lament over Jerusalem

13.msb: But Jesus replied, “Go tell that fox, ‘Look, I will keep driving out demons and healing people today and tomorrow, and on the third day I will reach My goal.’
13.kjv: And he said unto them, Go ye, and tell that fox, Behold, I cast out devils, and I do cures to day and to morrow, and the third day I shall be perfected.
13.blb: And He said to them, “Having gone, say to this fox, ‘Behold, I cast out demons and I complete cures today and tomorrow, and the third day, I am accomplished.’
13.bbe: And he said, Go and say to that fox, I send out evil spirits and do works of mercy today and tomorrow, and on the third day my work will be complete.

13.msb: Nevertheless, I must keep going today and tomorrow and the next day, for it is not admissible for a prophet to perish outside of Jerusalem.
13.kjv: Nevertheless I must walk to day, and to morrow, and the day following: for it cannot be that a prophet perish out of Jerusalem.
13.blb: But it is necessary for Me to proceed today and tomorrow and the following day, because it is not permissible for a prophet to perish outside of Jerusalem.
13.bbe: But I have to go on my way today and tomorrow and the third day, for it is not right for a prophet to come to his death outside Jerusalem.

13.msb: O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, who kills the prophets and stones those sent to her, how often I have longed to gather your children together as a hen gathers her chicks under her wings, but you were unwilling!
13.kjv: O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, which killest the prophets, and stonest them that are sent unto thee; how often would I have gathered thy children together, as a hen doth gather her brood under her wings, and ye would not!
13.blb: O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, killing the prophets and stoning those sent to her, how often I willed to gather your children, the way that a hen does her brood under the wings, and you were not willing.
13.bbe: O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, putting to death the prophets, and stoning those who were sent to her! again and again would I have taken your children to myself, as a bird takes her young ones under her wings, but you would not!

13.msb: Look, your house is left to you desolate. And I tell you that you will not see Me again until you say, ‘Blessed is He who comes in the name of the Lord.’”
13.kjv: Behold, your house is left unto you desolate: and verily I say unto you, Ye shall not see me, until the time come when ye shall say, Blessed is he that cometh in the name of the Lord.
13.blb: Behold, your house is left to you. And I say to you, you shall not see Me until it will come when you say, ‘Blessed is the One coming in the name of the Lord.’”
13.bbe: Now see, your house is waste, and I say to you, You will not see me again till you say, A blessing on him who comes in the name of the Lord.

14.msb: One Sabbath, Jesus went to eat in the home of a leading Pharisee, and those in attendance were watching Him closely.
14.kjv: And it came to pass, as he went into the house of one of the chief Pharisees to eat bread on the sabbath day, that they watched him.
14.blb: And it came to pass, in His going into the house of one of the rulers of the Pharisees on a Sabbath to eat bread, that they were watching Him.
14.bbe: And it came about that when he went into the house of one of the chief Pharisees on the Sabbath, to have a meal, they were watching him.
14.heading: Jesus Heals a Man with Dropsy

14.msb: Right there before Him was a man with dropsy.
14.kjv: And, behold, there was a certain man before him which had the dropsy.
14.blb: And behold, there was a certain man with dropsy before Him.
14.bbe: And a certain man was there who had a disease.

14.msb: So Jesus asked the experts in the law and the Pharisees, “Is it lawful to heal on the Sabbath?”
14.kjv: And Jesus answering spake unto the lawyers and Pharisees, saying, Is it lawful to heal on the sabbath day?
14.blb: And answering, Jesus spoke to the lawyers and to the Pharisees, saying, “Is it lawful to heal on the Sabbath or not?”
14.bbe: And Jesus, answering, said to the scribes and Pharisees, Is it right to make people well on the Sabbath or not?

14.msb: But they remained silent. Then Jesus took hold of the man, healed him, and sent him on his way.
14.kjv: And they held their peace. And he took him, and healed him, and let him go;
14.blb: But they were silent. And having taken hold of him, He healed him and let him go.
14.bbe: But they said nothing. And he made him well and sent him away.

14.msb: And He asked them, “Which of you whose son or ox falls into a pit on the Sabbath day will not immediately pull him out?”
14.kjv: And answered them, saying, Which of you shall have an ass or an ox fallen into a pit, and will not straightway pull him out on the sabbath day?
14.blb: And He said to them, “Which of you whose son or ox will fall into a well will not also immediately pull him up on the day of the Sabbath?”
14.bbe: And he said to them, Which of you, whose ox or ass has got into a water-hole, will not straight away get him out on the Sabbath?

14.msb: And they were unable to answer these questions.
14.kjv: And they could not answer him again to these things.
14.blb: And they were not able to reply to these things.
14.bbe: And they had no answer to that question.

14.msb: When Jesus noticed how the guests chose the places of honor, He told them a parable:
14.kjv: And he put forth a parable to those which were bidden, when he marked how they chose out the chief rooms; saying unto them,
14.blb: And He was speaking a parable to those invited, remarking how they were choosing out the first places, saying to them,
14.bbe: And he gave teaching in the form of a story to the guests who came to the feast, when he saw how they took the best seats; saying to them,
14.heading: The Parable of the Guests

14.msb: “When you are invited to a wedding banquet, do not sit in the place of honor, in case someone more distinguished than you has been invited.
14.kjv: When thou art bidden of any man to a wedding, sit not down in the highest room; lest a more honourable man than thou be bidden of him;
14.blb: “When you are invited by anyone to the wedding feasts, do not recline in the first place, lest ever one more honorable than you may have been invited by him.
14.bbe: When you get a request to come to a feast, do not take the best seat, for a more important man than you may be coming,

14.msb: Then the host who invited both of you will come and tell you, ‘Give this man your seat.’ And in humiliation, you will have to take the last place.
14.kjv: And he that bade thee and him come and say to thee, Give this man place; and thou begin with shame to take the lowest room.
14.blb: And the one having invited you and him, having come, will say to you, ‘Give to this one the place,’ and then you should begin with shame to take the last place.
14.bbe: And then the giver of the feast will come to you and say, Give your place to this man; and you, with shame, will have to take the lowest seat.

14.msb: But when you are invited, go and sit in the last place, so that your host will come and tell you, ‘Friend, move up to a better place.’ Then you will be honored in front of those at the table with you.
14.kjv: But when thou art bidden, go and sit down in the lowest room; that when he that bade thee cometh, he may say unto thee, Friend, go up higher: then shalt thou have worship in the presence of them that sit at meat with thee.
14.blb: But when you are invited, having gone, recline in the last place, so that when the one having invited you might come, he will say to you, ‘Friend, come up higher.’ Then glory will be to you before all those reclining with you.
14.bbe: But when you come, go and take the lowest seat, so that when the giver of the feast comes, he may say to you, Friend, come up higher; and then you will have honour in the eyes of all the others who are there.

14.msb: For everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, and the one who humbles himself will be exalted.”
14.kjv: For whosoever exalteth himself shall be abased; and he that humbleth himself shall be exalted.
14.blb: For everyone exalting himself will be humbled, and the one humbling himself will be exalted.”
14.bbe: For every man who gives himself a high place will be put down, but he who takes a low place will be lifted up.

14.msb: Then Jesus said to the man who had invited Him, “When you host a dinner or a banquet, do not invite your friends or brothers or relatives or rich neighbors. Otherwise, they may invite you in return, and you will be repaid.
14.kjv: Then said he also to him that bade him, When thou makest a dinner or a supper, call not thy friends, nor thy brethren, neither thy kinsmen, nor thy rich neighbours; lest they also bid thee again, and a recompence be made thee.
14.blb: And also He was saying to the one having invited Him, “When you may make a dinner or a supper, do not call your friends, nor your brothers, nor your relatives nor rich neighbors, lest ever they should also invite you in return, and repayment be made to you.
14.bbe: And he said to the master of the house, When you give a feast, do not send for your friends and your brothers and your family or your neighbours who have wealth, for they may give a feast for you, and so you will get a reward.

14.msb: But when you host a banquet, invite the poor, the crippled, the lame, and the blind,
14.kjv: But when thou makest a feast, call the poor, the maimed, the lame, the blind:
14.blb: But when you may make a feast, call the poor, the crippled, the lame, the blind,
14.bbe: But when you give a feast, send for the poor and the blind and those who are broken in body:

14.msb: and you will be blessed. Since they cannot repay you, you will be repaid at the resurrection of the righteous.”
14.kjv: And thou shalt be blessed; for they cannot recompense thee: for thou shalt be recompensed at the resurrection of the just.
14.blb: and you will be blessed, because they have nothing to repay you. For it will be repaid to you in the resurrection of the righteous.”
14.bbe: And you will have a blessing, because they will not be able to give you any payment, and you will get your reward when the upright come back from the dead.

14.msb: When one of those reclining with Him heard this, he said to Jesus, “Blessed is he who will eat at the feast in the kingdom of God.”
14.kjv: And when one of them that sat at meat with him heard these things, he said unto him, Blessed is he that shall eat bread in the kingdom of God.
14.blb: And one of those reclining with Him, having heard these things, said to Him, “Blessed is anyone who will eat bread in the kingdom of God.”
14.bbe: And, hearing these words, one of those who were at table with him said to him, Happy is the man who will be a guest in the kingdom of God.
14.heading: The Parable of the Banquet

14.msb: But Jesus replied, “A certain man prepared a great banquet and invited many guests.
14.kjv: Then said he unto him, A certain man made a great supper, and bade many:
14.blb: But He said to him, “A certain man was preparing a great supper, and he called many.
14.bbe: And he said to them, A certain man gave a great feast, and sent word of it to a number of people.

14.msb: When it was time for the banquet, he sent his servant to tell those who had been invited, ‘Come, for everything is now ready.’
14.kjv: And sent his servant at supper time to say to them that were bidden, Come; for all things are now ready.
14.blb: And he sent his servant at the hour of the supper to say to those having been called, ‘Come, because now it is ready.’
14.bbe: And when the time had come, he sent his servants to say to them, Come, for all things are now ready.

14.msb: But one after another they all began to make excuses. The first one said, ‘I have bought a field, and I need to go and see it. Please excuse me.’
14.kjv: And they all with one consent began to make excuse. The first said unto him, I have bought a piece of ground, and I must needs go and see it: I pray thee have me excused.
14.blb: And all with one voice began to excuse themselves. The first said to him, ‘I bought a field, and I have need of going out to see it. I ask you, have me excused.’
14.bbe: And they all gave reasons why they were not able to come. The first said to him, I have got a new field, and it is necessary for me to go and see it: I am full of regret that I am unable to come.

14.msb: Another said, ‘I have bought five yoke of oxen, and I am going to try them out. Please excuse me.’
14.kjv: And another said, I have bought five yoke of oxen, and I go to prove them: I pray thee have me excused.
14.blb: And another said, ‘I bought five yoke of oxen, and I am going to examine them. I request of you, have me excused.’
14.bbe: And another said, I have got some cattle, and I am going to make a test of them: I am full of regret that I am unable to come.

14.msb: Still another said, ‘I have married a wife, so I cannot come.’
14.kjv: And another said, I have married a wife, and therefore I cannot come.
14.blb: And another said, ‘I married a wife, and because of this I am not able to come.’
14.bbe: And another said, I have been married, and so I am not able to come.

14.msb: That servant returned and reported all this to his master. Then the owner of the house became angry and said to his servant, ‘Go out quickly into the streets and alleys of the city, and bring in the poor, the crippled, the lame, and the blind.’
14.kjv: So that servant came, and shewed his lord these things. Then the master of the house being angry said to his servant, Go out quickly into the streets and lanes of the city, and bring in hither the poor, and the maimed, and the halt, and the blind.
14.blb: And having come, the servant reported these things to his master. Then, having become angry, the master of the house said to his servant, ‘Go out quickly into the streets and lanes of the city, and bring in here the poor and crippled and blind and lame.’
14.bbe: And the servant came back and gave his master an account of these things. Then the master of the house was angry and said to the servant, Go out quickly into the streets of the town and get the poor, the blind, and those who are broken in body.

14.msb: ‘Sir,’ the servant replied, ‘it has been done as you ordered, and there is still room.’
14.kjv: And the servant said, Lord, it is done as thou hast commanded, and yet there is room.
14.blb: And the servant said, ‘Lord, what you commanded has been done, and there is still room.’
14.bbe: And the servant said, Lord, your orders have been done, and still there is room.

14.msb: So the master told his servant, ‘Go out to the highways and hedges and compel them to come in, so that my house will be full.
14.kjv: And the lord said unto the servant, Go out into the highways and hedges, and compel them to come in, that my house may be filled.
14.blb: And the master said to the servant, ‘Go out into the roads and hedges and compel them to enter, so that my house may be filled.
14.bbe: And the lord said to the servant, Go out into the roads and the fields, and make them come in, so that my house may be full.

14.msb: For I tell you, not one of those men who were invited will taste my banquet. For many are called, but few are chosen.’”
14.kjv: For I say unto you, That none of those men which were bidden shall taste of my supper.
14.blb: For I say to you that not one of those men having been called will taste my supper.’”
14.bbe: For I say to you that not one of those who were requested to come will have a taste of my feast.

14.msb: Now large crowds were traveling with Jesus, and He turned and said to them,
14.kjv: And there went great multitudes with him: and he turned, and said unto them,
14.blb: And great crowds were going with Him, and having turned, He said to them,
14.bbe: Now a great number of people went with him.
14.heading: The Cost of Discipleship

14.msb: “If anyone comes to Me and does not hate his father and mother and wife and children and brothers and sisters—yes, even his own life—he cannot be My disciple.
14.kjv: If any man come to me, and hate not his father, and mother, and wife, and children, and brethren, and sisters, yea, and his own life also, he cannot be my disciple.
14.blb: “If anyone comes to Me and does not hate his father and mother and wife and children and brothers and sisters, and yes, even his life, he is not able to be My disciple.
14.bbe: And turning round, he said to them, If any man comes to me, and has not hate for his father and mother and wife and children and brothers and sisters, and even for his life, he may not be my disciple.

14.msb: And whoever does not carry his cross and follow Me cannot be My disciple.
14.kjv: And whosoever doth not bear his cross, and come after me, cannot be my disciple.
14.blb: Whoever does not carry his cross and come after Me is not able to be My disciple.
14.bbe: Whoever does not take up his cross and come after me may not be my disciple.

14.msb: Which of you, wishing to build a tower, does not first sit down and count the cost to see if he has the resources to complete it?
14.kjv: For which of you, intending to build a tower, sitteth not down first, and counteth the cost, whether he have sufficient to finish it?
14.blb: For which of you, wanting to build a tower, does not first, having sat down, count the cost, whether he has the things for its completion,
14.bbe: For which of you, desiring to put up a tower, does not first give much thought to the price, if he will have enough to make it complete?

14.msb: Otherwise, if he lays the foundation and is unable to finish the work, everyone who sees it will ridicule him,
14.kjv: Lest haply, after he hath laid the foundation, and is not able to finish it, all that behold it begin to mock him,
14.blb: lest ever, of him having laid its foundation and not being able to finish, all seeing it may begin to mock him,
14.bbe: For fear that if he makes a start and is not able to go on with it to the end, all who see it will be laughing at him,

14.msb: saying, ‘This man could not finish what he started to build.’
14.kjv: Saying, This man began to build, and was not able to finish.
14.blb: saying, ‘This man began to build and was not able to finish’?
14.bbe: And saying, This man made a start at building and is not able to make it complete.

14.msb: Or what king on his way to war with another king does not first sit down and consider whether he can engage with ten thousand men the one coming against him with twenty thousand?
14.kjv: Or what king, going to make war against another king, sitteth not down first, and consulteth whether he be able with ten thousand to meet him that cometh against him with twenty thousand?
14.blb: Or what king proceeding to engage with another king in war will not, having sat down, first take counsel, whether he is able with ten thousand to meet the one coming against him with twenty thousand?
14.bbe: Or what king, going to war with another king, will not first take thought if he will be strong enough, with ten thousand men, to keep off him who comes against him with twenty thousand?

14.msb: And if he is unable, he will send a delegation while the other king is still far off, to ask for terms of peace.
14.kjv: Or else, while the other is yet a great way off, he sendeth an ambassage, and desireth conditions of peace.
14.blb: And if not, in his being still far off, having sent a delegation, he asks for peace.
14.bbe: Or while the other is still a great distance away, he sends representatives requesting conditions of peace.

14.msb: In the same way, any one of you who does not give up everything he has cannot be My disciple.
14.kjv: So likewise, whosoever he be of you that forsaketh not all that he hath, he cannot be my disciple.
14.blb: So therefore, every one of you who does not take leave of all that he himself possesses is not able to be My disciple.
14.bbe: And so whoever is not ready to give up all he has may not be my disciple.

14.msb: Salt is good, but if the salt loses its savor, with what will it be seasoned?
14.kjv: Salt is good: but if the salt have lost his savour, wherewith shall it be seasoned?
14.blb: Therefore the salt is good, but if even the salt should become tasteless, with what will it be seasoned?
14.bbe: For salt is good, but if the taste goes from it, of what use is it?
14.heading: Good Salt

14.msb: It is fit neither for the soil nor for the manure pile, and it is thrown out. He who has ears to hear, let him hear.”
14.kjv: It is neither fit for the land, nor yet for the dunghill; but men cast it out. He that hath ears to hear, let him hear.
14.blb: It is fit neither for soil nor for manure; they cast it out. The one having ears to hear, let him hear.”
14.bbe: It is no good for the land or for the place of waste; no one has a use for it. He who has ears, let him give ear.

15.msb: Now all the tax collectors and sinners were gathering around to listen to Jesus.
15.kjv: Then drew near unto him all the publicans and sinners for to hear him.
15.blb: Now all the tax collectors and the sinners were drawing near to Him to hear Him.
15.bbe: Now all the tax-farmers and sinners came near to give ear to him.
15.heading: The Parable of the Lost Sheep

15.msb: So the Pharisees and scribes began to grumble: “This man welcomes sinners and eats with them.”
15.kjv: And the Pharisees and scribes murmured, saying, This man receiveth sinners, and eateth with them.
15.blb: And both the Pharisees and the scribes were grumbling, saying, “This man receives sinners and eats with them.”
15.bbe: And the Pharisees and scribes were angry, saying, This man gives approval to sinners, and takes food with them.

15.msb: Then Jesus told them this parable:
15.kjv: And he spake this parable unto them, saying,
15.blb: And He spoke to them this parable, saying,
15.bbe: And he made a story for them, saying,

15.msb: “What man among you, if he has a hundred sheep and loses one of them, does not leave the ninety-nine in the pasture and go after the one that is lost, until he finds it?
15.kjv: What man of you, having an hundred sheep, if he lose one of them, doth not leave the ninety and nine in the wilderness, and go after that which is lost, until he find it?
15.blb: “What man of you, having a hundred sheep and having lost one of them, does not leave the ninety-nine in the wilderness and go after the lost one until he should find it?
15.bbe: What man of you, having a hundred sheep, if one of them gets loose and goes away, will not let the ninety-nine be in the waste land by themselves, and go after the wandering one, till he sees where it is?

15.msb: And when he finds it, he joyfully puts it on his shoulders,
15.kjv: And when he hath found it, he layeth it on his shoulders, rejoicing.
15.blb: And having found it, he lays it on his shoulders, rejoicing.
15.bbe: And when he has got it again, he takes it in his arms with joy.

15.msb: comes home, and calls together his friends and neighbors to tell them, ‘Rejoice with me, for I have found my lost sheep!’
15.kjv: And when he cometh home, he calleth together his friends and neighbours, saying unto them, Rejoice with me; for I have found my sheep which was lost.
15.blb: And having come to the house, he calls together the friends and the neighbors, saying to them, ‘Rejoice with me, because I found my sheep, the lost one!’
15.bbe: And when he gets back to his house, he sends for his neighbours and friends, saying to them, Be glad with me, for I have got back my sheep which had gone away.

15.msb: I tell you that in the same way there will be more joy in heaven over one sinner who repents than over ninety-nine righteous ones who do not need to repent.
15.kjv: I say unto you, that likewise joy shall be in heaven over one sinner that repenteth, more than over ninety and nine just persons, which need no repentance.
15.blb: I say to you that thus there will be joy in heaven over one sinner repenting, rather than over ninety-nine righteous ones who have no need of repentance.
15.bbe: I say to you that even so there will be more joy in heaven when one sinner is turned away from his wrongdoing, than for ninety-nine good men, who have no need of a change of heart.

15.msb: Or what woman who has ten silver coins and loses one of them does not light a lamp, sweep her house, and search carefully until she finds it?
15.kjv: Either what woman having ten pieces of silver, if she lose one piece, doth not light a candle, and sweep the house, and seek diligently till she find it?
15.blb: Or what woman having ten drachmas, if she should lose one drachma, does not light a lamp and sweep the house and seek carefully until she should find it?
15.bbe: Or what woman, having ten bits of silver, if one bit has gone from her hands, will not get a light, and go through her house, searching with care till she sees it?
15.heading: The Parable of the Lost Coin

15.msb: And when she finds it, she calls together her friends and neighbors to say, ‘Rejoice with me, for I have found my lost coin.’
15.kjv: And when she hath found it, she calleth her friends and her neighbours together, saying, Rejoice with me; for I have found the piece which I had lost.
15.blb: And having found it, she calls together the friends and neighbors, saying, ‘Rejoice with me, for I found the drachma that I lost.’
15.bbe: And when she has it again, she gets her friends and neighbours together, saying, Be glad with me, for I have got back the bit of silver which had gone from me.

15.msb: In the same way, I tell you, there is joy in the presence of God’s angels over one sinner who repents.”
15.kjv: Likewise, I say unto you, there is joy in the presence of the angels of God over one sinner that repenteth.
15.blb: Thus, I say to you, there is joy before the angels of God over one sinner repenting.”
15.bbe: Even so, I say to you, There is joy among the angels of God, when one sinner is turned away from his wrongdoing.

15.msb: Then Jesus said, “There was a man who had two sons.
15.kjv: And he said, A certain man had two sons:
15.blb: And He said, “A certain man had two sons.
15.bbe: And he said, A certain man had two sons:
15.heading: The Parable of the Prodigal Son

15.msb: The younger son said to him, ‘Father, give me my share of the estate.’ So he divided his property between them.
15.kjv: And the younger of them said to his father, Father, give me the portion of goods that falleth to me. And he divided unto them his living.
15.blb: And the younger of them said to the father, ‘Father, give to me the portion of the substance falling to me.’ And he divided the livelihood between them.
15.bbe: And the younger of them said to his father, Father, give me that part of your property which will be mine. And he made division of his goods between them.

15.msb: After a few days, the younger son got everything together and journeyed to a distant country, where he squandered his wealth in wild living.
15.kjv: And not many days after the younger son gathered all together, and took his journey into a far country, and there wasted his substance with riotous living.
15.blb: And after not many days, the younger son, having gathered together all, went away into a far country, and there he scattered his substance living prodigally.
15.bbe: And not long after, the younger son got together everything which was his and took a journey into a far-away country, and there all his money went in foolish living.

15.msb: After he had spent all he had, a severe famine swept through that country, and he began to be in need.
15.kjv: And when he had spent all, there arose a mighty famine in that land; and he began to be in want.
15.blb: But on his having spent all, there was a strong famine throughout that country, and he began to lack.
15.bbe: And when everything was gone, there was no food to be had in that country, and he was in need.

15.msb: So he went and hired himself out to a citizen of that country, who sent him into his fields to feed the pigs.
15.kjv: And he went and joined himself to a citizen of that country; and he sent him into his fields to feed swine.
15.blb: And having gone, he joined himself to one of the citizens of that country, and he sent him into his fields to feed pigs.
15.bbe: And he went and put himself into the hands of one of the people of that country, and he sent him into his fields to give the pigs their food.

15.msb: He longed to fill his belly with the pods the pigs were eating, but no one would give him a thing.
15.kjv: And he would fain have filled his belly with the husks that the swine did eat: and no man gave unto him.
15.blb: And he was desiring to fill his belly from the pods that the pigs were eating, and no one was giving to him.
15.bbe: And so great was his need that he would have been glad to take the pigs' food, and no one gave him anything.

15.msb: Finally he came to his senses and said, ‘How many of my father’s hired servants have plenty of food, but I am starving to death!
15.kjv: And when he came to himself, he said, How many hired servants of my father’s have bread enough and to spare, and I perish with hunger!
15.blb: But having come to himself, he was saying, ‘How many hired men of my father have an abundance of loaves, but here I am perishing with hunger?
15.bbe: But when he came to his senses, he said, What numbers of my father's servants have bread enough, and more, while I am near to death here through need of food!

15.msb: I will get up and go back to my father and say to him, “Father, I have sinned against heaven and against you.
15.kjv: I will arise and go to my father, and will say unto him, Father, I have sinned against heaven, and before thee,
15.blb: Having risen up, I will go to my father and I will say to him, “Father, I sinned against heaven and before you;
15.bbe: I will get up and go to my father, and will say to him, Father, I have done wrong, against heaven and in your eyes:

15.msb: I am no longer worthy to be called your son. Make me like one of your hired servants.”’
15.kjv: And am no more worthy to be called thy son: make me as one of thy hired servants.
15.blb: no longer am I worthy to be called your son. Make me like one of your hired men.”’
15.bbe: I am no longer good enough to be named your son: make me like one of your servants.

15.msb: So he got up and went to his father. But while he was still in the distance, his father saw him and was filled with compassion. He ran to his son, embraced him, and kissed him.
15.kjv: And he arose, and came to his father. But when he was yet a great way off, his father saw him, and had compassion, and ran, and fell on his neck, and kissed him.
15.blb: And having risen up, he went to his father. But on his still being distant, his father saw him and was moved with compassion, and having run, he fell upon his neck and kissed him.
15.bbe: And he got up and went to his father. But while he was still far away, his father saw him and was moved with pity for him and went quickly and took him in his arms and gave him a kiss.

15.msb: The son declared, ‘Father, I have sinned against heaven and against you. I am no longer worthy to be called your son.’
15.kjv: And the son said unto him, Father, I have sinned against heaven, and in thy sight, and am no more worthy to be called thy son.
15.blb: And the son said to him, ‘Father, I sinned against heaven and before you; no longer am I worthy to be called your son.’
15.bbe: And his son said to him, Father, I have done wrong, against heaven and in your eyes: I am no longer good enough to be named your son.

15.msb: But the father said to his servants, ‘Bring the best robe and put it on him. Put a ring on his finger and sandals on his feet.
15.kjv: But the father said to his servants, Bring forth the best robe, and put it on him; and put a ring on his hand, and shoes on his feet:
15.blb: And the father said to his servants, ‘Quickly bring out the best robe and clothe him, and give a ring for his hand and sandals for his feet;
15.bbe: But the father said to his servants, Get out the first robe quickly, and put it on him, and put a ring on his hand and shoes on his feet:

15.msb: Bring the fattened calf and kill it. Let us feast and celebrate.
15.kjv: And bring hither the fatted calf, and kill it; and let us eat, and be merry:
15.blb: and having brought the fattened calf, kill it, and having eaten, let us be merry,
15.bbe: And get the fat young ox and put it to death, and let us have a feast, and be glad.

15.msb: For this son of mine was dead and is alive again! He was lost and is found!’ So they began to celebrate.
15.kjv: For this my son was dead, and is alive again; he was lost, and is found. And they began to be merry.
15.blb: because this son of mine was dead and lived again! He was lost and was found!’ And they began to be merry.
15.bbe: For this, my son, who was dead, is living again; he had gone away from me, and has come back. And they were full of joy.

15.msb: Meanwhile the older son was in the field, and as he approached the house, he heard music and dancing.
15.kjv: Now his elder son was in the field: and as he came and drew nigh to the house, he heard musick and dancing.
15.blb: And his elder son was in the field; and as, coming, he drew near to the house, he heard music and dancing.
15.bbe: Now the older son was in the field: and when he came near the house, the sounds of music and dancing came to his ears.

15.msb: So he called one of the servants and asked what was going on.
15.kjv: And he called one of the servants, and asked what these things meant.
15.blb: And having summoned one of the servants, he was inquiring what these things might be.
15.bbe: And he sent for one of the servants, questioning him about what it might be.

15.msb: ‘Your brother has returned,’ he said, ‘and your father has killed the fattened calf, because he has him back safe and sound.’
15.kjv: And he said unto him, Thy brother is come; and thy father hath killed the fatted calf, because he hath received him safe and sound.
15.blb: And he said to him, ‘Your brother has come, and your father killed the fattened calf, because he received him back in good health.’
15.bbe: And he said to him, Your brother has come; and your father has had the young ox put to death because he has come back safely.

15.msb: The older son became angry and refused to go in. So his father came out and pleaded with him.
15.kjv: And he was angry, and would not go in: therefore came his father out, and intreated him.
15.blb: But he was angry and was not willing to go in. And his father, having gone, was imploring him.
15.bbe: But he was angry and would not go in; and his father came out and made a request to him to come in.

15.msb: But he answered his father, ‘Look, all these years I have served you and never disobeyed a commandment of yours. Yet you never gave me even a young goat so I could celebrate with my friends.
15.kjv: And he answering said to his father, Lo, these many years do I serve thee, neither transgressed I at any time thy commandment: and yet thou never gavest me a kid, that I might make merry with my friends:
15.blb: But answering, he said to his father, ‘Behold, so many years I serve you, and never did I transgress a commandment of yours, and never did you give to me a young goat so that I might be merry with my friends.
15.bbe: But he made answer and said to his father, See, all these years I have been your servant, doing your orders in everything: and you never gave me even a young goat so that I might have a feast with my friends:

15.msb: But when this son of yours returns from squandering your wealth with prostitutes, you kill the fattened calf for him!’
15.kjv: But as soon as this thy son was come, which hath devoured thy living with harlots, thou hast killed for him the fatted calf.
15.blb: But when this son of yours came, the one having devoured your living with prostitutes, you killed the fattened calf for him!’
15.bbe: But when this your son came, who has been wasting your property with bad women, you put to death the fat young ox for him.

15.msb: ‘Son, you are always with me,’ the father said, ‘and all that is mine is yours.
15.kjv: And he said unto him, Son, thou art ever with me, and all that I have is thine.
15.blb: And he said to him, ‘Child, you are always with me, and all that is mine is yours.
15.bbe: And he said to him, Son, you are with me at all times, and all I have is yours.

15.msb: But it was fitting to celebrate and be glad, because this brother of yours was dead and is alive again; he was lost and is found.’”
15.kjv: It was meet that we should make merry, and be glad: for this thy brother was dead, and is alive again; and was lost, and is found.
15.blb: But it was fitting to be merry and to rejoice, because this brother of yours was dead and lived again; and he was lost and was found.’”
15.bbe: But it was right to be glad and to have a feast; for this your brother, who was dead, is living again; he had gone away and has come back.

16.msb: Jesus also said to His disciples, “There was a rich man whose manager was accused of wasting his possessions.
16.kjv: And he said also unto his disciples, There was a certain rich man, which had a steward; and the same was accused unto him that he had wasted his goods.
16.blb: Now He was also saying to the disciples, “There was a certain rich man who had a manager, and this one was accused to him as wasting his possessions.
16.bbe: And another time he said to the disciples, There was a certain man of great wealth who had a servant; and it was said to him that this servant was wasting his goods.
16.heading: The Parable of the Shrewd Manager

16.msb: So he called him in to ask, ‘What is this I hear about you? Turn in an account of your management, for you cannot be manager any longer.’
16.kjv: And he called him, and said unto him, How is it that I hear this of thee? give an account of thy stewardship; for thou mayest be no longer steward.
16.blb: And having called him, he said to him, ‘What is this I hear about you? Give the account of your management, for you are not able to manage any longer.’
16.bbe: And he sent for him and said, What is this which is said about you? give me an account of all you have done, for you will no longer be the manager of my property.

16.msb: The manager said to himself, ‘What shall I do, now that my master is taking away my position? I am too weak to dig and too ashamed to beg.
16.kjv: Then the steward said within himself, What shall I do? for my lord taketh away from me the stewardship: I cannot dig; to beg I am ashamed.
16.blb: And the manager said in himself, ‘What shall I do, because my master is taking away the management from me? I have no strength to dig; I am ashamed to beg.
16.bbe: And the servant said to himself, What am I to do now that my lord takes away my position? I have not enough strength for working in the fields, and I would be shamed if I made requests for money from people in the streets.

16.msb: I know what I will do so that after my removal from management, people will welcome me into their homes.’
16.kjv: I am resolved what to do, that, when I am put out of the stewardship, they may receive me into their houses.
16.blb: I have known what I shall do, so that when I shall have been removed from the management, they might receive me into their houses.’
16.bbe: I have come to a decision what to do, so that when I am put out of my position they will take me into their houses.

16.msb: And he called in each one of his master’s debtors. ‘How much do you owe my master?’ he asked the first.
16.kjv: So he called every one of his lord’s debtors unto him, and said unto the first, How much owest thou unto my lord?
16.blb: And having summoned each one of the debtors of his master, he was saying to the first, ‘How much do you owe to my master?’
16.bbe: And sending for every one who was in debt to his lord he said to the first, What is the amount of your debt to my lord?

16.msb: ‘A hundred measures of olive oil,’ he answered. ‘Take your bill,’ said the manager, ‘sit down quickly, and write fifty.’
16.kjv: And he said, An hundred measures of oil. And he said unto him, Take thy bill, and sit down quickly, and write fifty.
16.blb: And he said, ‘A hundred baths of oil.’ And he said to him, ‘Take your bill, and having sat down quickly, write fifty.’
16.bbe: And he said, A hundred measures of oil. And he said, Take your account straight away and put down fifty.

16.msb: Then he asked another, ‘And how much do you owe?’ ‘A hundred measures of wheat,’ he replied. ‘Take your bill and write eighty,’ he told him.
16.kjv: Then said he to another, And how much owest thou? And he said, An hundred measures of wheat. And he said unto him, Take thy bill, and write fourscore.
16.blb: Then he said to another, ‘And how much do you owe?’ And he said, ‘A hundred cors of wheat.’ He says to him, ‘Take your bill and write eighty.’
16.bbe: Then he said to another, What is the amount of your debt? And he said, A hundred measures of grain. And he said to him, Take your account and put down eighty.

16.msb: The master commended the dishonest manager because he had acted shrewdly. For the sons of this age are more shrewd in dealing with their own kind than are the sons of light.
16.kjv: And the lord commended the unjust steward, because he had done wisely: for the children of this world are in their generation wiser than the children of light.
16.blb: And the master praised the unrighteous manager because he acted shrewdly, because the sons of this age are more shrewd than the sons of the light in their own generation.
16.bbe: And his lord was pleased with the false servant, because he had been wise; for the sons of this world are wiser in relation to their generation than the sons of light.

16.msb: I tell you, use worldly wealth to make friends for yourselves so that when you fail, they will welcome you into eternal dwellings.
16.kjv: And I say unto you, Make to yourselves friends of the mammon of unrighteousness; that, when ye fail, they may receive you into everlasting habitations.
16.blb: And I say to you, make friends for yourselves by the mammon of unrighteousness, so that when it fails, they might receive you into the eternal dwellings.
16.bbe: And I say to you, Make friends for yourselves through the wealth of this life, so that when it comes to an end, you may be taken into the eternal resting-places.

16.msb: Whoever is faithful with very little will also be faithful with much, and whoever is dishonest with very little will also be dishonest with much.
16.kjv: He that is faithful in that which is least is faithful also in much: and he that is unjust in the least is unjust also in much.
16.blb: The one faithful in very little is also faithful in much, and the one unrighteous in very little is also unrighteous in much.
16.bbe: He who is true in a little, is true in much; he who is false in small things, is false in great.

16.msb: So if you have not been faithful with worldly wealth, who will entrust you with true riches?
16.kjv: If therefore ye have not been faithful in the unrighteous mammon, who will commit to your trust the true riches?
16.blb: If, therefore, you were not faithful in the unrighteous mammon, who will entrust to you the true?
16.bbe: If, then, you have not been true in your use of the wealth of this life, who will give into your care the true wealth?

16.msb: And if you have not been faithful with the belongings of another, who will give you belongings of your own?
16.kjv: And if ye have not been faithful in that which is another man’s, who shall give you that which is your own?
16.blb: And if you were not faithful in that which is of another, who will give to you that which is your own?
16.bbe: And if you have not been true in your care of the property of other people, who will give you that which is yours?

16.msb: No servant can serve two masters. Either he will hate the one and love the other, or he will be devoted to the one and despise the other. You cannot serve both God and money.”
16.kjv: No servant can serve two masters: for either he will hate the one, and love the other; or else he will hold to the one, and despise the other. Ye cannot serve God and mammon.
16.blb: No servant is able to serve two masters. For either he will hate the one and he will love the other, or he will hold to the one and he will despise the other. You are not able to serve God and mammon.”
16.bbe: No man may be a servant to two masters: for he will have hate for the one and love for the other; or he will keep to the one and have no respect for the other. You may not be servants of God and of wealth.

16.msb: The Pharisees, who were lovers of money, heard all of this and were scoffing at Jesus.
16.kjv: And the Pharisees also, who were covetous, heard all these things: and they derided him.
16.blb: Now the Pharisees, being lovers of money, were hearing all these things, and they were ridiculing Him.
16.bbe: And the Pharisees, who had a great love of money, hearing these things, were making sport of him.
16.heading: The Law and the Prophets

16.msb: So He said to them, “You are the ones who justify yourselves before men, but God knows your hearts. For what is prized among men is detestable before God.
16.kjv: And he said unto them, Ye are they which justify yourselves before men; but God knoweth your hearts: for that which is highly esteemed among men is abomination in the sight of God.
16.blb: And He said to them, “You are the ones justifying themselves before men, but God knows your hearts, because that which is high among men is an abomination before God.
16.bbe: And he said, You take care to seem right in the eyes of men, but God sees your hearts: and those things which are important in the opinion of men, are evil in the eyes of God.

16.msb: The Law and the Prophets were proclaimed until John. Since that time, the gospel of the kingdom of God is being preached, and everyone is forcing his way into it.
16.kjv: The law and the prophets were until John: since that time the kingdom of God is preached, and every man presseth into it.
16.blb: The Law and the Prophets were until John. From then, the kingdom of God is proclaimed as good news, and everyone presses into it.
16.bbe: The law and the prophets were till John: but then came the preaching of the kingdom of God, and everyone makes his way into it by force.

16.msb: But it is easier for heaven and earth to pass away than for a single stroke of a pen to drop out of the Law.
16.kjv: And it is easier for heaven and earth to pass, than one tittle of the law to fail.
16.blb: But it is easier for the heaven and the earth to pass away than one stroke of a letter of the Law to fall.
16.bbe: But heaven and earth will come to an end before the smallest letter of the law may be dropped out.

16.msb: Anyone who divorces his wife and marries another woman commits adultery, and everyone who marries a divorced woman commits adultery.
16.kjv: Whosoever putteth away his wife, and marrieth another, committeth adultery: and whosoever marrieth her that is put away from her husband committeth adultery.
16.blb: Everyone sending away his wife and marrying another commits adultery. And the one marrying her sent away from a husband, he commits adultery.
16.bbe: Everyone who puts away his wife and takes another, is a false husband: and he who is married to a woman whose husband has put her away, is no true husband to her.

16.msb: Now there was a rich man dressed in purple and fine linen, who lived each day in joyous splendor.
16.kjv: There was a certain rich man, which was clothed in purple and fine linen, and fared sumptuously every day:
16.blb: And there was a certain rich man, and he was clothed in purple and fine linen, being merry in splendor every day.
16.bbe: Now there was a certain man of great wealth, who was dressed in fair clothing of purple and delicate linen, and was shining and glad every day.
16.heading: The Rich Man and Lazarus

16.msb: And a beggar named Lazarus lay at his gate, covered with sores
16.kjv: And there was a certain beggar named Lazarus, which was laid at his gate, full of sores,
16.blb: And a certain poor man named Lazarus was laid at his gate, being full of sores
16.bbe: And a certain poor man, named Lazarus, was stretched out at his door, full of wounds,

16.msb: and longing to be fed with the crumbs that fell from the rich man’s table. Even the dogs came and licked his sores.
16.kjv: And desiring to be fed with the crumbs which fell from the rich man’s table: moreover the dogs came and licked his sores.
16.blb: and desiring to be fed from that falling from the table of the rich man; but even the dogs, coming, were licking his sores.
16.bbe: Desiring the broken bits of food which came from the table of the man of wealth; and even the dogs came and put their tongues on his wounds.

16.msb: One day the beggar died and was carried by the angels to Abraham’s side. And the rich man also died and was buried.
16.kjv: And it came to pass, that the beggar died, and was carried by the angels into Abraham’s bosom: the rich man also died, and was buried;
16.blb: And it came to pass that the poor man died, and he was carried away by the angels into the bosom of Abraham. And the rich man also died and was buried.
16.bbe: And in time the poor man came to his end, and angels took him to Abraham's breast. And the man of wealth came to his end, and was put in the earth.

16.msb: In Hades, where he was in torment, he looked up and saw Abraham from afar, with Lazarus by his side.
16.kjv: And in hell he lift up his eyes, being in torments, and seeth Abraham afar off, and Lazarus in his bosom.
16.blb: And in Hades, having lifted up his eyes, being in torment, he sees Abraham from afar and Lazarus in his bosom.
16.bbe: And in hell, being in great pain, lifting up his eyes he saw Abraham, far away, and Lazarus on his breast.

16.msb: So he cried out, ‘Father Abraham, have mercy on me and send Lazarus to dip the tip of his finger in water and cool my tongue. For I am in agony in this fire.’
16.kjv: And he cried and said, Father Abraham, have mercy on me, and send Lazarus, that he may dip the tip of his finger in water, and cool my tongue; for I am tormented in this flame.
16.blb: And having cried out, he said, ‘Father Abraham, have mercy on me and send Lazarus so that he might dip the tip of his finger in water and cool my tongue, because I am suffering in this flame.’
16.bbe: And he gave a cry and said, Father Abraham, have mercy on me and send Lazarus, so that he may put the end of his finger in water and put it on my tongue, for I am cruelly burning in this flame.

16.msb: But Abraham answered, ‘Child, remember that during your lifetime you received your good things, while Lazarus received bad things. But now he is comforted here, while you are in agony.
16.kjv: But Abraham said, Son, remember that thou in thy lifetime receivedst thy good things, and likewise Lazarus evil things: but now he is comforted, and thou art tormented.
16.blb: But Abraham said, ‘Child, remember that you fully received your good things in your life, and Lazarus likewise the evil things. But now he is comforted here, and you are suffering.
16.bbe: But Abraham said, Keep in mind, my son, that when you were living, you had your good things, while Lazarus had evil things: but now, he is comforted and you are in pain.

16.msb: And besides all this, a great chasm has been fixed between us and you, so that even those who wish cannot cross from here to you, nor can anyone cross from there to us.’
16.kjv: And beside all this, between us and you there is a great gulf fixed: so that they which would pass from hence to you cannot; neither can they pass to us, that would come from thence.
16.blb: And besides all these things, a great chasm has been fixed between us and you, so that those desiring to go over from here to you are not able, nor may they cross over from there to us.’
16.bbe: And in addition, there is a deep division fixed between us and you, so that those who might go from here to you are not able to do so, and no one may come from you to us.

16.msb: ‘Then I beg you, father,’ he said, ‘send Lazarus to my father’s house,
16.kjv: Then he said, I pray thee therefore, father, that thou wouldest send him to my father’s house:
16.blb: And he said, ‘Then I ask you, father, that you might send him to the house of my father—
16.bbe: And he said, Father, it is my request that you will send him to my father's house;

16.msb: for I have five brothers. Let him warn them, so that they will not also end up in this place of torment.’
16.kjv: For I have five brethren; that he may testify unto them, lest they also come into this place of torment.
16.blb: for I have five brothers—that he might warn them so that they might not also come to this place of torment.’
16.bbe: For I have five brothers; and let him give them an account of these things, so that they may not come to this place of pain.

16.msb: But Abraham replied, ‘They have Moses and the Prophets; let your brothers listen to them.’
16.kjv: Abraham saith unto him, They have Moses and the prophets; let them hear them.
16.blb: But Abraham says, ‘They have Moses and the prophets; let them hear them.’
16.bbe: But Abraham said, They have Moses and the prophets; let them give ear to what they say.

16.msb: ‘No, father Abraham,’ he said, ‘but if someone is sent to them from the dead, they will repent.’
16.kjv: And he said, Nay, father Abraham: but if one went unto them from the dead, they will repent.
16.blb: But he said, ‘No, father Abraham, but if one from the dead should go to them, they will repent.’
16.bbe: And he said, No, father Abraham, but if someone went to them from the dead, their hearts would be changed.

16.msb: Then Abraham said to him, ‘If they do not listen to Moses and the Prophets, they will not be persuaded even if someone rises from the dead.’”
16.kjv: And he said unto him, If they hear not Moses and the prophets, neither will they be persuaded, though one rose from the dead.
16.blb: But he said to him, ‘If they do not hear Moses and the prophets, not even will they be persuaded if one should rise out from the dead.’”
16.bbe: And he said to him, If they will not give attention to Moses and the prophets, they will not be moved even if someone comes back from the dead.

17.msb: Jesus said to the disciples, “It is inevitable that stumbling blocks will come, but woe to the one through whom they come!
17.kjv: Then said he unto the disciples, It is impossible but that offences will come: but woe unto him, through whom they come!
17.blb: And He said to His disciples, “It is impossible for the stumbling blocks not to come, but woe to him through whom they come!
17.bbe: And he said to his disciples, It is necessary for causes of trouble to come about, but unhappy is he by whom they come.
17.heading: Temptations and Trespasses

17.msb: It would be better for him to have a large millstone hung around his neck and to be thrown into the sea than to cause one of these little ones to stumble.
17.kjv: It were better for him that a millstone were hanged about his neck, and he cast into the sea, than that he should offend one of these little ones.
17.blb: It is better for him if a millstone is put around his neck and he is thrown into the sea than that he might cause to stumble one of these little ones.
17.bbe: It would be well for him if a great stone was put round his neck and he was dropped into the sea, before he made trouble for any of these little ones.

17.msb: Watch yourselves. If your brother sins against you, rebuke him; and if he repents, forgive him.
17.kjv: Take heed to yourselves: If thy brother trespass against thee, rebuke him; and if he repent, forgive him.
17.blb: Take heed to yourselves: If your brother should sin, rebuke him; and if he should repent, forgive him.
17.bbe: Give attention to yourselves: if your brother does wrong, say a sharp word to him; and if he has sorrow for his sin, let him have forgiveness.

17.msb: Even if he sins against you seven times in a day, and returns seven times in that day to say, ‘I repent,’ you must forgive him.”
17.kjv: And if he trespass against thee seven times in a day, and seven times in a day turn again to thee, saying, I repent; thou shalt forgive him.
17.blb: And if he should sin against you seven times in the day, and seven times he should return to you, saying, ‘I repent,’ you will forgive him.”
17.bbe: And if he does you wrong seven times in a day, and seven times comes to you and says, I have regret for what I have done; let him have forgiveness.

17.msb: The apostles said to the Lord, “Increase our faith!”
17.kjv: And the apostles said unto the Lord, Increase our faith.
17.blb: And the apostles said to the Lord, “Add to our faith!”
17.bbe: And the twelve said to the Lord, Make our faith greater.
17.heading: The Power of Faith

17.msb: And the Lord answered, “If you have faith the size of a mustard seed, you can say to this mulberry tree, ‘Be uprooted and planted in the sea,’ and it will obey you.
17.kjv: And the Lord said, If ye had faith as a grain of mustard seed, ye might say unto this sycamine tree, Be thou plucked up by the root, and be thou planted in the sea; and it should obey you.
17.blb: And the Lord said, “If you have faith as a grain of mustard, you would have said to this mulberry tree, ‘Be uprooted and be planted in the sea,’ and it would have obeyed you.
17.bbe: And the Lord said, If your faith was only as great as a grain of mustard seed, you might say to this tree, Be rooted up and planted in the sea; and it would be done.

17.msb: Which of you whose servant comes in from plowing or shepherding in the field will say, ‘Come at once and sit down to eat’?
17.kjv: But which of you, having a servant plowing or feeding cattle, will say unto him by and by, when he is come from the field, Go and sit down to meat?
17.blb: And which of you having a servant plowing or shepherding, the one having come in out of the field, will say to him, ‘Having come, immediately recline’?
17.bbe: But which of you, having a servant who is ploughing or keeping sheep, will say to him, when he comes in from the field, Come now and be seated and have a meal,

17.msb: Instead, won’t he tell him, ‘Prepare my meal and dress yourself to serve me while I eat and drink, and afterward you may eat and drink’?
17.kjv: And will not rather say unto him, Make ready wherewith I may sup, and gird thyself, and serve me, till I have eaten and drunken; and afterward thou shalt eat and drink?
17.blb: But will he not say to him, ‘Prepare what I may eat, and having girded yourself about, serve me while I eat and drink; and after these things you will eat and drink’?
17.bbe: Will he not say, Get a meal for me, and make yourself ready and see to my needs till I have had my food and drink; and after that you may have yours?

17.msb: Does he thank the servant because he did what he was told? I think not.
17.kjv: Doth he thank that servant because he did the things that were commanded him? I trow not.
17.blb: Does he have favor to the servant because he did the things having been directed?
17.bbe: Does he give praise to the servant because he did what was ordered?

17.msb: So you also, when you have done everything commanded of you, should say, ‘We are unworthy servants; we have only done our duty.’”
17.kjv: So likewise ye, when ye shall have done all those things which are commanded you, say, We are unprofitable servants: we have done that which was our duty to do.
17.blb: Thus also you, when you may have done all the things having been directed you, say, ‘We are unworthy servants; we have done that which we were obligated to do.’”
17.bbe: In the same way, when you have done all the things which are given you to do, say, There is no profit in us, for we have only done what we were ordered to do.

17.msb: While Jesus was on His way to Jerusalem, He was passing between Samaria and Galilee.
17.kjv: And it came to pass, as he went to Jerusalem, that he passed through the midst of Samaria and Galilee.
17.blb: And it came to pass, in His going to Jerusalem, that He was passing through the midst of Samaria and Galilee.
17.bbe: And it came about that when they were on the way to Jerusalem he went through Samaria and Galilee.
17.heading: The Ten Lepers

17.msb: As He entered one of the villages, He was met by ten lepers. They stood at a distance
17.kjv: And as he entered into a certain village, there met him ten men that were lepers, which stood afar off:
17.blb: And on His entering into a certain village, ten leprous men met Him, who stood afar off.
17.bbe: And when he went into a certain small town he came across ten men who were lepers, and they, keeping themselves at a distance,

17.msb: and raised their voices, shouting, “Jesus, Master, have mercy on us!”
17.kjv: And they lifted up their voices, and said, Jesus, Master, have mercy on us.
17.blb: And they lifted up their voice, saying, “Jesus, Master, have mercy on us!”
17.bbe: Said, in loud voices, Jesus, Master, have mercy on us.

17.msb: When Jesus saw them, He said, “Go, show yourselves to the priests.” And as they were on their way, they were cleansed.
17.kjv: And when he saw them, he said unto them, Go shew yourselves unto the priests. And it came to pass, that, as they went, they were cleansed.
17.blb: And having seen, He said to them, “Having gone, show yourselves to the priests.” And it came to pass, in their going, that they were cleansed.
17.bbe: And when he saw them he said, Go, and let the priests see you. And, while they were going, they were made clean.

17.msb: When one of them saw that he was healed, he came back, praising God in a loud voice.
17.kjv: And one of them, when he saw that he was healed, turned back, and with a loud voice glorified God,
17.blb: And one of them, having seen that he was healed, turned back, glorifying God with a loud voice,
17.bbe: And one of them, when he saw that he was clean, turning back, gave praise to God in a loud voice;

17.msb: He fell facedown at Jesus’ feet in thanksgiving to Him—and he was a Samaritan.
17.kjv: And fell down on his face at his feet, giving him thanks: and he was a Samaritan.
17.blb: and he fell on his face at His feet, giving thanks to Him. And he was a Samaritan.
17.bbe: And, falling down on his face at the feet of Jesus, he gave the credit to him; and he was a man of Samaria.

17.msb: “Were not all ten cleansed?” Jesus asked. “Where then are the other nine?
17.kjv: And Jesus answering said, Were there not ten cleansed? but where are the nine?
17.blb: And having answered, Jesus said, “Were not the ten cleansed? But where are the nine?
17.bbe: And Jesus said, Were there not ten men who were made clean? where are the nine?

17.msb: Was no one found except this foreigner to return and give glory to God?”
17.kjv: There are not found that returned to give glory to God, save this stranger.
17.blb: Was there found none having returned to give glory to God except this foreigner?”
17.bbe: Have not any of them come back to give glory to God, but only this one from a strange land?

17.msb: Then Jesus said to him, “Rise and go; your faith has made you well!”
17.kjv: And he said unto him, Arise, go thy way: thy faith hath made thee whole.
17.blb: And He said to him, “Having risen up, go; your faith has saved you!”
17.bbe: And he said to him, Get up, and go on your way; your faith has made you well.

17.msb: When asked by the Pharisees when the kingdom of God would come, Jesus replied, “The kingdom of God will not come with observable signs.
17.kjv: And when he was demanded of the Pharisees, when the kingdom of God should come, he answered them and said, The kingdom of God cometh not with observation:
17.blb: And having been questioned by the Pharisees as to when the kingdom of God is coming, He answered them and said, “The kingdom of God does not come with observation,
17.bbe: And when the Pharisees put questions to him about when the kingdom of God would come, he gave them an answer and said, The kingdom of God will not come through observation:
17.heading: The Coming of the Kingdom

17.msb: Nor will people say, ‘Look, here it is,’ or ‘There it is.’ For you see, the kingdom of God is in your midst.”
17.kjv: Neither shall they say, Lo here! or, lo there! for, behold, the kingdom of God is within you.
17.blb: nor will they say, ‘Behold, here,’ or, ‘There.’ For behold, the kingdom of God is in your midst.”
17.bbe: And men will not say, See, it is here! or, There! for the kingdom of God is among you.

17.msb: Then He said to the disciples, “The time is coming when you will long to see one of the days of the Son of Man, but you will not see it.
17.kjv: And he said unto the disciples, The days will come, when ye shall desire to see one of the days of the Son of man, and ye shall not see it.
17.blb: And He said to the disciples, “The days will come when you will desire to see one of the days of the Son of Man, and you will not see it.
17.bbe: And he said to his disciples, The time will come when you will have a great desire to see one of the days of the Son of man, but you will not see it.

17.msb: People will tell you, ‘Look, there He is!’ or ‘Look, here He is!’ Do not go out or chase after them.
17.kjv: And they shall say to you, See here; or, see there: go not after them, nor follow them.
17.blb: And they will say to you, ‘Behold, there,’ or, ‘Behold, here.’ you should not go away, nor should you pursue.
17.bbe: And if they say to you, See, it is there! or, It is here! do not go away, or go after them.

17.msb: For just as the lightning flashes and lights up the sky from one end to the other, so will be the Son of Man in His day.
17.kjv: For as the lightning, that lighteneth out of the one part under heaven, shineth unto the other part under heaven; so shall also the Son of man be in his day.
17.blb: For just as the lightning shines, flashing from the one end of the sky to the other end of the sky, so will be the Son of Man in His day.
17.bbe: For as in a thunderstorm the bright light is seen from one end of the sky to the other, so will the Son of man be when his time comes.

17.msb: But first He must suffer many things and be rejected by this generation.
17.kjv: But first must he suffer many things, and be rejected of this generation.
17.blb: But first it is necessary for Him to suffer many things and to be rejected by this generation.
17.bbe: But first, he will have to undergo much and be put on one side by this generation.

17.msb: Just as it was in the days of Noah, so also will it be in the days of the Son of Man:
17.kjv: And as it was in the days of Noe, so shall it be also in the days of the Son of man.
17.blb: And just as it came to pass in the days of Noah, so also will it be in the days of the Son of Man:
17.bbe: And as it was in the days of Noah, so will it be in the day of the Son of man.

17.msb: People were eating and drinking, marrying and being given in marriage, up to the day Noah entered the ark. Then the flood came and destroyed them all.
17.kjv: They did eat, they drank, they married wives, they were given in marriage, until the day that Noe entered into the ark, and the flood came, and destroyed them all.
17.blb: They were eating, they were drinking, they were marrying, they were being given in marriage, until that day Noah entered into the ark, and the flood came and destroyed them all.
17.bbe: They were feasting and taking wives and getting married, till the day of the overflowing of the waters, when Noah went into the ark, and they all came to destruction.

17.msb: It was the same in the days of Lot: People were eating and drinking, buying and selling, planting and building.
17.kjv: Likewise also as it was in the days of Lot; they did eat, they drank, they bought, they sold, they planted, they builded;
17.blb: Likewise, just as it came to pass in the days of Lot: They were eating, they were drinking, they were buying, they were selling, they were planting, they were building,
17.bbe: In the same way, in the days of Lot; they were feasting and trading, they were planting and building;

17.msb: But on the day Lot left Sodom, fire and sulfur rained down from heaven and destroyed them all.
17.kjv: But the same day that Lot went out of Sodom it rained fire and brimstone from heaven, and destroyed them all.
17.blb: and in that day Lot went out from Sodom, it rained fire and sulfur from heaven and destroyed all.
17.bbe: But on the day when Lot went out of Sodom, fire came down from heaven and destruction came on them all.

17.msb: It will be just like that on the day the Son of Man is revealed.
17.kjv: Even thus shall it be in the day when the Son of man is revealed.
17.blb: According to the same things it will be in that day the Son of Man is revealed.
17.bbe: So will it be in the day of the revelation of the Son of man.

17.msb: On that day, let no one on the housetop come down to retrieve his possessions. Likewise, let no one in the field return for anything he has left behind.
17.kjv: In that day, he which shall be upon the housetop, and his stuff in the house, let him not come down to take it away: and he that is in the field, let him likewise not return back.
