17.blb: In that day, the one who will be on the housetop, and his goods in the house, let him not come down to take them away; and likewise the one in the field, let him not return to the things behind.
17.bbe: On that day, if anyone is on the roof of the house, and his goods are in the house, let him not go down to take them away; and let him who is in the field not go back to his house.

17.msb: Remember Lot’s wife!
17.kjv: Remember Lot’s wife.
17.blb: Remember the wife of Lot!
17.bbe: Keep in mind Lot's wife.

17.msb: Whoever tries to save his life will lose it, but whoever loses his life will preserve it.
17.kjv: Whosoever shall seek to save his life shall lose it; and whosoever shall lose his life shall preserve it.
17.blb: Whoever may seek to keep his life will lose it; but whoever may lose it will preserve it.
17.bbe: If anyone makes an attempt to keep his life, it will be taken from him, but if anyone gives up his life, he will keep it.

17.msb: I tell you, on that night two people will be in one bed: one will be taken and the other left.
17.kjv: I tell you, in that night there shall be two men in one bed; the one shall be taken, and the other shall be left.
17.blb: I say to you, in that night there will be two upon one bed: The one will be taken, and the other will be left.
17.bbe: I say to you, In that night there will be two men sleeping in one bed, and one will be taken away and the other let go.

17.msb: Two women will be grinding grain together: one will be taken and the other left.”
17.kjv: Two women shall be grinding together; the one shall be taken, and the other left.
17.blb: There will be two women grinding at the same place: The one will be taken, and the other will be left.”
17.bbe: Two women will be crushing grain together; one will be taken away and the other let go.

17.kjv: Two men shall be in the field; the one shall be taken, and the other left.

17.msb: “Where, Lord?” they asked. Jesus answered, “Wherever there is a carcass, there the vultures will gather.”
17.kjv: And they answered and said unto him, Where, Lord? And he said unto them, Wheresoever the body is, thither will the eagles be gathered together.
17.blb: And answering, they say to Him, “Where, Lord?” And He said to them, “Where the body is, there also the vultures will be gathered together.”
17.bbe: And they, answering him, said, Where, Lord? And he said to them, Where the body is, there will the eagles come together.

18.msb: Then Jesus told them a parable about the need to pray at all times and not lose heart:
18.kjv: And he spake a parable unto them to this end, that men ought always to pray, and not to faint;
18.blb: And He was speaking a parable to them that it is necessary for them always to pray and not to grow fainthearted,
18.bbe: And he made a story for them, the point of which was that men were to go on making prayer and not get tired;
18.heading: The Parable of the Persistent Widow

18.msb: “In a certain town there was a judge who neither feared God nor respected men.
18.kjv: Saying, There was in a city a judge, which feared not God, neither regarded man:
18.blb: saying, “There was a certain judge in a certain city, not fearing God and not respecting man.
18.bbe: Saying, There was a judge in a certain town, who had no fear of God or respect for man:

18.msb: And there was a widow in that town who kept appealing to him, ‘Give me justice against my adversary.’
18.kjv: And there was a widow in that city; and she came unto him, saying, Avenge me of mine adversary.
18.blb: And there was a widow in that city, and she was coming to him, saying, ‘Avenge me from my adversary.’
18.bbe: And there was a widow in that town, and she kept on coming to him and saying, Give me my right against the man who has done me wrong.

18.msb: For a while he refused, but later he said to himself, ‘Though I neither fear God nor respect men,
18.kjv: And he would not for a while: but afterward he said within himself, Though I fear not God, nor regard man;
18.blb: And he was not willing for a time, but after these things he said in himself, ‘Even if I do not fear God nor respect man,
18.bbe: And for a time he would not: but later, he said to himself, Though I have no fear of God or respect for man,

18.msb: yet because this widow keeps pestering me, I will give her justice. Otherwise, she will wear me out with her perpetual requests.’”
18.kjv: Yet because this widow troubleth me, I will avenge her, lest by her continual coming she weary me.
18.blb: yet because this widow causes me trouble, I will avenge her, so that coming until the end, she does not exhaust me.’”
18.bbe: Because this widow is a trouble to me, I will give her her right; for if not, I will be completely tired out by her frequent coming.

18.msb: And the Lord said, “Listen to the words of the unjust judge.
18.kjv: And the Lord said, Hear what the unjust judge saith.
18.blb: And the Lord said, “Hear what the unrighteous judge says.
18.bbe: And the Lord said, Give ear to the words of the evil judge.

18.msb: Will not God bring about justice for His elect who cry out to Him day and night? Will He delay in helping them?
18.kjv: And shall not God avenge his own elect, which cry day and night unto him, though he bear long with them?
18.blb: And shall not God execute the avenging of His chosen—the ones crying out to Him day and night—and be deferring in regard to them?
18.bbe: And will not God do right in the cause of his saints, whose cries come day and night to his ears, though he is long in doing it?

18.msb: I tell you, He will promptly carry out justice on their behalf. Nevertheless, when the Son of Man comes, will He find faith on earth?”
18.kjv: I tell you that he will avenge them speedily. Nevertheless when the Son of man cometh, shall he find faith on the earth?
18.blb: I say to you that He will execute their avenging in quickness. Nevertheless, the Son of Man having come, will He find the faith on the earth?”
18.bbe: I say to you that he will quickly do right in their cause. But when the Son of man comes, will there be any faith on earth?

18.msb: To some who trusted in their own righteousness and viewed others with contempt, He also told this parable:
18.kjv: And he spake this parable unto certain which trusted in themselves that they were righteous, and despised others:
18.blb: And He also spoke this parable to some trusting in themselves that they are righteous, and despising others:
18.bbe: And he made this story for some people who were certain that they were good, and had a low opinion of others:
18.heading: The Pharisee and the Tax Collector

18.msb: “Two men went up to the temple to pray. One was a Pharisee and the other a tax collector.
18.kjv: Two men went up into the temple to pray; the one a Pharisee, and the other a publican.
18.blb: “Two men went up into the temple to pray, the one a Pharisee and the other a tax collector.
18.bbe: Two men went up to the Temple for prayer; one a Pharisee, and the other a tax-farmer.

18.msb: The Pharisee stood by himself and prayed, ‘God, I thank You that I am not like other men—swindlers, evildoers, adulterers—or even like this tax collector.
18.kjv: The Pharisee stood and prayed thus with himself, God, I thank thee, that I am not as other men are, extortioners, unjust, adulterers, or even as this publican.
18.blb: The Pharisee, having stood, was praying toward himself thus: ‘God, I thank You that I am not like the rest of the men—swindlers, unrighteous, adulterers—or even like this tax collector.
18.bbe: The Pharisee, taking up his position, said to himself these words: God, I give you praise because I am not like other men, who take more than their right, who are evil-doers, who are untrue to their wives, or even like this tax-farmer.

18.msb: I fast twice a week and pay tithes of all that I acquire.’
18.kjv: I fast twice in the week, I give tithes of all that I possess.
18.blb: I fast twice in the week; I tithe all things, as many as I gain.’
18.bbe: Twice in the week I go without food; I give a tenth of all I have.

18.msb: But the tax collector stood at a distance, unwilling even to lift up his eyes to heaven. Instead, he beat his breast and said, ‘God, have mercy on me, a sinner!’
18.kjv: And the publican, standing afar off, would not lift up so much as his eyes unto heaven, but smote upon his breast, saying, God be merciful to me a sinner.
18.blb: But the tax collector, standing afar off, was not even willing to lift up the eyes to heaven, but was striking his breast, saying, ‘God, be merciful to me, the sinner!’
18.bbe: The tax-farmer, on the other hand, keeping far away, and not lifting up even his eyes to heaven, made signs of grief and said, God, have mercy on me, a sinner.

18.msb: I tell you, this man, rather than the Pharisee, went home justified. For everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, but the one who humbles himself will be exalted.”
18.kjv: I tell you, this man went down to his house justified rather than the other: for every one that exalteth himself shall be abased; and he that humbleth himself shall be exalted.
18.blb: I say to you, this one went down to his house justified, rather than that one. For everyone exalting himself will be humbled, but the one humbling himself will be exalted.”
18.bbe: I say to you, This man went back to his house with God's approval, and not the other: for everyone who makes himself high will be made low and whoever makes himself low will be made high.

18.msb: Now people were even bringing their babies to Jesus for Him to place His hands on them. And when the disciples saw this, they rebuked those who brought them.
18.kjv: And they brought unto him also infants, that he would touch them: but when his disciples saw it, they rebuked them.
18.blb: And they were bringing the infants also to Him so that He might touch them; but having seen, the disciples were rebuking them.
18.bbe: And they took their children to him, so that he might put his hands on them: but when the disciples saw it, they said sharp words to them
18.heading: Jesus Blesses the Children

18.msb: But Jesus called the children to Him and said, “Let the little children come to Me, and do not hinder them! For the kingdom of God belongs to such as these.
18.kjv: But Jesus called them unto him, and said, Suffer little children to come unto me, and forbid them not: for of such is the kingdom of God.
18.blb: But Jesus summoned them, saying, “Permit the little children to come to Me, and do not forbid them; for of the such is the kingdom of God.
18.bbe: But Jesus sent for them, saying, Let the children come to me, and do not keep them away, for of such is the kingdom of heaven.

18.msb: Truly I tell you, anyone who does not receive the kingdom of God like a little child will never enter it.”
18.kjv: Verily I say unto you, Whosoever shall not receive the kingdom of God as a little child shall in no wise enter therein.
18.blb: Truly I say to you, whoever shall not receive the kingdom of God as a little child, he shall never enter into it.”
18.bbe: Truly I say to you, Whoever does not put himself under the kingdom of God like a little child, will not come into it at all.

18.msb: Then a certain ruler asked Him, “Good Teacher, what must I do to inherit eternal life?”
18.kjv: And a certain ruler asked him, saying, Good Master, what shall I do to inherit eternal life?
18.blb: And a certain ruler asked Him, saying, “Good Teacher, having done what will I inherit eternal life?”
18.bbe: And a certain ruler put a question to him, saying, Good Master, what have I to do so that I may have eternal life?
18.heading: The Rich Young Ruler

18.msb: “Why do you call Me good?” Jesus replied. “No one is good except God alone.
18.kjv: And Jesus said unto him, Why callest thou me good? none is good, save one, that is, God.
18.blb: But Jesus said to him, “Why do you call Me good? No one is good except One—God.
18.bbe: And Jesus said to him, Why do you say that I am good? No one is good, but only God.

18.msb: You know the commandments: ‘Do not commit adultery, do not murder, do not steal, do not bear false witness, honor your father and mother.’”
18.kjv: Thou knowest the commandments, Do not commit adultery, Do not kill, Do not steal, Do not bear false witness, Honour thy father and thy mother.
18.blb: You know the commandments: ‘You shall not commit adultery, you shall not murder, you shall not steal, you shall not bear false witness, honor your father and mother.’”
18.bbe: You have knowledge of what the law says: Do not be untrue to your wife, Do not put anyone to death, Do not take what is not yours, Do not give false witness, Give honour to your father and mother.

18.msb: “All these I have kept from my youth,” he said.
18.kjv: And he said, All these have I kept from my youth up.
18.blb: And he said, “All these I kept from my youth.”
18.bbe: And he said, All these things I have done from the time when I was a boy.

18.msb: On hearing this, Jesus told him, “You still lack one thing: Sell everything you own and give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven. Then come, follow Me.”
18.kjv: Now when Jesus heard these things, he said unto him, Yet lackest thou one thing: sell all that thou hast, and distribute unto the poor, and thou shalt have treasure in heaven: and come, follow me.
18.blb: And having heard, Jesus said to him, “Still one thing to you is lacking: Sell all, as much as you have, and distribute to the poor, and you will have treasure in the heavens; and come, follow Me.”
18.bbe: And Jesus, hearing it, said to him, One thing you still have need of; get money for your goods, and give it away to the poor, and you will have wealth in heaven; and come after me.

18.msb: But when the ruler heard this, he became very sad, because he was extremely wealthy.
18.kjv: And when he heard this, he was very sorrowful: for he was very rich.
18.blb: But having heard these things, he became very sorrowful; for he was exceedingly rich.
18.bbe: But at these words he became very sad, for he had great wealth.

18.msb: Seeing the man’s sadness, Jesus said, “How hard it is for the rich to enter the kingdom of God!
18.kjv: And when Jesus saw that he was very sorrowful, he said, How hardly shall they that have riches enter into the kingdom of God!
18.blb: And Jesus, having seen him, having become sorrowful, said, “How difficultly those having riches enter into the kingdom of God!
18.bbe: And Jesus, looking at him, said, How hard it is for those who have wealth to get into the kingdom of God!

18.msb: Indeed, it is easier for a camel to pass through the eye of a needle than for a rich man to enter the kingdom of God.”
18.kjv: For it is easier for a camel to go through a needle’s eye, than for a rich man to enter into the kingdom of God.
18.blb: For it is easier for a camel to enter through the eye of a needle than for a rich man to enter into the kingdom of God.”
18.bbe: It is simpler for a camel to go through the eye of a needle, than for a man who has much money to come into the kingdom of God.

18.msb: Those who heard this asked, “Who then can be saved?”
18.kjv: And they that heard it said, Who then can be saved?
18.blb: And those having heard said, “And who is able to be saved?”
18.bbe: And those who were present said, Then who may have salvation?

18.msb: But Jesus said, “What is impossible with man is possible with God.”
18.kjv: And he said, The things which are impossible with men are possible with God.
18.blb: And He said, “The things impossible with men are possible with God.”
18.bbe: But he said, Things which are not possible with man are possible with God.

18.msb: “Look,” said Peter, “we have left all we had to follow You.”
18.kjv: Then Peter said, Lo, we have left all, and followed thee.
18.blb: And Peter said, “Behold, we, having left our own, followed You.”
18.bbe: And Peter said, See, we have given up what is ours to come after you.

18.msb: “Truly I tell you,” Jesus replied, “no one who has left home or parents or brothers or wife or children for the sake of the kingdom of God
18.kjv: And he said unto them, Verily I say unto you, There is no man that hath left house, or parents, or brethren, or wife, or children, for the kingdom of God’s sake,
18.blb: And He said to them, “Truly I say to you that there is no one who left house or wife or brothers or parents or children for the sake of the kingdom of God
18.bbe: And he said to them, Truly I say to you, There is no man who has given up house or wife or brothers or father or mother or children, because of the kingdom of God,

18.msb: will fail to receive many times more in this age—and in the age to come, eternal life.”
18.kjv: Who shall not receive manifold more in this present time, and in the world to come life everlasting.
18.blb: who shall not receive back manifold more in this time, and in the age that is coming, eternal life.”
18.bbe: Who will not get much more in this time, and in the world to come, eternal life.

18.msb: Then Jesus took the Twelve aside and said to them, “Look, we are going up to Jerusalem, and everything the prophets have written about the Son of Man will be fulfilled.
18.kjv: Then he took unto him the twelve, and said unto them, Behold, we go up to Jerusalem, and all things that are written by the prophets concerning the Son of man shall be accomplished.
18.blb: And having taken aside the Twelve, He said to them, “Behold, we are going up to Jerusalem, and all things having been written by the prophets about the Son of Man will be accomplished.
18.bbe: And he took with him the twelve and said to them, Now we are going up to Jerusalem, and all the things which were said by the prophets will be done to the Son of man.
18.heading: The Third Prediction of the Passion

18.msb: He will be delivered over to the Gentiles and will be mocked and insulted and spit upon.
18.kjv: For he shall be delivered unto the Gentiles, and shall be mocked, and spitefully entreated, and spitted on:
18.blb: For He will be betrayed to the Gentiles and will be mocked and will be insulted and will be spit upon.
18.bbe: For he will be given up to the Gentiles, and will be made sport of and put to shame:

18.msb: They will flog Him and kill Him, and on the third day He will rise again.”
18.kjv: And they shall scourge him, and put him to death: and the third day he shall rise again.
18.blb: And having flogged Him, they will kill Him; and on the third day He will rise again.”
18.bbe: And he will be given cruel blows and put to death, and on the third day he will come back to life.

18.msb: But the disciples did not understand any of these things. The meaning was hidden from them, and they did not comprehend what He was saying.
18.kjv: And they understood none of these things: and this saying was hid from them, neither knew they the things which were spoken.
18.blb: And they understood none of these things, and this saying was hidden from them, and they did not know the things being spoken.
18.bbe: But they did not take in the sense of any of these words, and what he said was not clear to them, and their minds were not able to see it.

18.msb: As Jesus drew near to Jericho, a blind man was sitting beside the road, begging.
18.kjv: And it came to pass, that as he was come nigh unto Jericho, a certain blind man sat by the way side begging:
18.blb: And it came to pass, in His drawing near to Jericho, that a certain blind man was sitting beside the road, begging.
18.bbe: And it came about that when he got near Jericho, a certain blind man was seated by the side of the road, making requests for money from those who went by.
18.heading: Jesus Heals a Blind Beggar

18.msb: When he heard the crowd going by, he asked what was happening.
18.kjv: And hearing the multitude pass by, he asked what it meant.
18.blb: And having heard a crowd going by, he was asking what this might be.
18.bbe: And hearing the sound of a great number of people going by, he said, What is this?

18.msb: “Jesus of Nazareth is passing by,” they told him.
18.kjv: And they told him, that Jesus of Nazareth passeth by.
18.blb: And they told him, “Jesus of Nazareth is passing by.”
18.bbe: And they said to him, Jesus of Nazareth is going by.

18.msb: So he called out, “Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me!”
18.kjv: And he cried, saying, Jesus, thou Son of David, have mercy on me.
18.blb: And he called out, saying, “Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me!”
18.bbe: And he said in a loud voice, Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me.

18.msb: Those who led the way admonished him to be silent, but he cried out all the louder, “Son of David, have mercy on me!”
18.kjv: And they which went before rebuked him, that he should hold his peace: but he cried so much the more, Thou Son of David, have mercy on me.
18.blb: And those going before were rebuking him, that he should be silent. But much more he was crying out, “Son of David, have mercy on me!”
18.bbe: And those who were in front made protests and said to him, Be quiet: but he said all the more, O Son of David, have mercy on me.

18.msb: Jesus stopped and directed that the man be brought to Him. When he had come near, Jesus asked him,
18.kjv: And Jesus stood, and commanded him to be brought unto him: and when he was come near, he asked him,
18.blb: And having stood, Jesus commanded him to be brought to Him. And on his having drawn near, He questioned him,
18.bbe: And Jesus, stopping, gave orders that he was to come to him, and when he came near, he said to him,

18.msb: “What do you want Me to do for you?” “Lord,” he said, “let me see again.”
18.kjv: Saying, What wilt thou that I shall do unto thee? And he said, Lord, that I may receive my sight.
18.blb: “What do you desire that I may do for you?” And he said, “Lord, that I may receive sight.”
18.bbe: What would you have me do for you? And he said, Lord, that I may be able to see again.

18.msb: “Receive your sight!” Jesus replied. “Your faith has healed you.”
18.kjv: And Jesus said unto him, Receive thy sight: thy faith hath saved thee.
18.blb: And Jesus said to him, “Receive your sight! Your faith has saved you.”
18.bbe: And Jesus said, See again: your faith has made you well.

18.msb: Immediately he received his sight and followed Jesus, glorifying God. And all the people, when they saw it, gave praise to God.
18.kjv: And immediately he received his sight, and followed him, glorifying God: and all the people, when they saw it, gave praise unto God.
18.blb: And immediately he received his sight, and he was following Him, glorifying God. And all the people, having seen it, gave praise to God.
18.bbe: And straight away he was able to see, and he went after him, giving glory to God; and all the people when they saw it gave praise to God.

19.msb: Then Jesus entered Jericho and was passing through.
19.kjv: And Jesus entered and passed through Jericho.
19.blb: And having entered, He was passing through Jericho.
19.bbe: And he went into Jericho, and when he was going through it,
19.heading: Jesus and Zacchaeus

19.msb: And there was a man named Zacchaeus, a chief tax collector, who was very wealthy.
19.kjv: And, behold, there was a man named Zacchæus, which was the chief among the publicans, and he was rich.
19.blb: And behold, a man called by the name Zacchaeus, and he was a chief tax collector, and he was rich.
19.bbe: A man, named Zacchaeus, who was the chief tax-farmer, and a man of wealth,

19.msb: He was trying to see who Jesus was, but could not see over the crowd because he was small in stature.
19.kjv: And he sought to see Jesus who he was; and could not for the press, because he was little of stature.
19.blb: And he was seeking to see Jesus, who He is. And he was not able on account of the crowd, because he was small in stature.
19.bbe: Made an attempt to get a view of Jesus, and was not able to do so, because of the people, for he was a small man.

19.msb: So he ran on ahead and climbed a sycamore tree to see Him, since Jesus was about to pass that way.
19.kjv: And he ran before, and climbed up into a sycomore tree to see him: for he was to pass that way.
19.blb: And having run ahead to the front, he went up on a sycamore-fig tree so that he might see Him, for He was about to pass through that way.
19.bbe: And he went quickly in front of them and got up into a tree to see him, for he was going that way.

19.msb: When Jesus came to that place, He looked up and saw him and said, “Zacchaeus, hurry down, for I must stay at your house today.”
19.kjv: And when Jesus came to the place, he looked up, and saw him, and said unto him, Zacchæus, make haste, and come down; for to day I must abide at thy house.
19.blb: And as He came upon the place, having looked up, Jesus said to him, “Zacchaeus, having hurried, come down, for it is necessary for Me to stay in your house today.”
19.bbe: And when Jesus came to the place, looking up, he said to him, Zacchaeus, be quick and come down, for I am coming to your house today.

19.msb: So Zacchaeus hurried down and welcomed Him joyfully.
19.kjv: And he made haste, and came down, and received him joyfully.
19.blb: And having hurried, he came down and received Him, rejoicing.
19.bbe: And he came down quickly, and took him into his house with joy.

19.msb: And all who saw this began to grumble, saying, “He has gone to be the guest of a sinful man!”
19.kjv: And when they saw it, they all murmured, saying, That he was gone to be guest with a man that is a sinner.
19.blb: And having seen it, they were all grumbling, saying, “He entered to lodge with a sinful man.”
19.bbe: And when they saw it, they were all angry, saying, He has gone into the house of a sinner.

19.msb: But Zacchaeus stood up and said to the Lord, “Look, Lord, half of my possessions I give to the poor, and if I have cheated anyone, I will repay it fourfold.”
19.kjv: And Zacchæus stood, and said unto the Lord; Behold, Lord, the half of my goods I give to the poor; and if I have taken any thing from any man by false accusation, I restore him fourfold.
19.blb: But having stood, Zacchaeus said to the Lord, “Behold, half of my possessions, Lord, I give to the poor; and if I defrauded anything of anyone, I repay it fourfold.”
19.bbe: And Zacchaeus, waiting before him, said to the Lord, See, Lord, half of my goods I give to the poor, and if I have taken anything from anyone wrongly, I give him back four times as much.

19.msb: Jesus said to him, “Today salvation has come to this house, because this man too is a son of Abraham.
19.kjv: And Jesus said unto him, This day is salvation come to this house, forsomuch as he also is a son of Abraham.
19.blb: And Jesus said to him, “Today salvation came to this house, because he also is a son of Abraham.
19.bbe: And Jesus said to him, Today salvation has come to this house, for even he is a son of Abraham.

19.msb: For the Son of Man came to seek and to save the lost.”
19.kjv: For the Son of man is come to seek and to save that which was lost.
19.blb: For the Son of Man came to seek and to save the lost.”
19.bbe: For the Son of man came to make search for those who are wandering from the way, and to be their Saviour.

19.msb: While the people were listening to this, Jesus proceeded to tell them a parable, because He was near Jerusalem and they thought the kingdom of God would appear imminently.
19.kjv: And as they heard these things, he added and spake a parable, because he was nigh to Jerusalem, and because they thought that the kingdom of God should immediately appear.
19.blb: Now in their hearing these things, having proceeded, He spoke a parable because of His being near Jerusalem and their thinking that the kingdom of God is about to appear immediately.
19.bbe: And while they were giving ear to these words, he made another story for them, because he was near Jerusalem, and because they were of the opinion that the kingdom of God was coming straight away.
19.heading: The Parable of the Ten Minas

19.msb: So He said, “A man of noble birth went to a distant country to lay claim to his kingship and then return.
19.kjv: He said therefore, A certain nobleman went into a far country to receive for himself a kingdom, and to return.
19.blb: Therefore He said, “A certain man of noble birth went to a far country to receive for himself a kingdom and to return.
19.bbe: So he said, A certain man of high birth went into a far-away country to get a kingdom for himself, and to come back.

19.msb: Beforehand, he called ten of his servants and gave them ten minas. ‘Conduct business with this until I return,’ he said.
19.kjv: And he called his ten servants, and delivered them ten pounds, and said unto them, Occupy till I come.
19.blb: And having called ten of his servants, he gave to them ten minas and said to them, ‘Do business until I come.’
19.bbe: And he sent for ten of his servants and gave them ten pounds and said to them, Do business with this till I come.

19.msb: But his subjects hated him and sent a delegation after him to say, ‘We do not want this man to rule over us.’
19.kjv: But his citizens hated him, and sent a message after him, saying, We will not have this man to reign over us.
19.blb: But his citizens hated him and sent a delegation after him, saying, ‘We are not willing for this man to reign over us.’
19.bbe: But his people had no love for him, and sent representatives after him, saying, We will not have this man for our ruler.

19.msb: When he returned from procuring his kingship, he summoned the servants to whom he had given the money, to find out what each one had earned.
19.kjv: And it came to pass, that when he was returned, having received the kingdom, then he commanded these servants to be called unto him, to whom he had given the money, that he might know how much every man had gained by trading.
19.blb: And it came to pass on his returning, having received the kingdom, that he directed these servants to whom he had given the money to be called to him, so that he might know what each had gained by doing business.
19.bbe: And when he came back again, having got his kingdom, he gave orders for those servants to whom he had given the money to come to him, so that he might have an account of what business they had done.

19.msb: The first servant came forward and said, ‘Master, your mina has produced ten more minas.’
19.kjv: Then came the first, saying, Lord, thy pound hath gained ten pounds.
19.blb: And the first came up, saying, ‘Lord, your mina produced ten minas.’
19.bbe: And the first came before him, saying, Lord, your pound has made ten pounds.

19.msb: His master replied, ‘Well done, good servant! Because you have been faithful in a very small matter, you shall have authority over ten cities.’
19.kjv: And he said unto him, Well, thou good servant: because thou hast been faithful in a very little, have thou authority over ten cities.
19.blb: And he said to him, ‘Well done, good servant! Because you were faithful in very little, be having authority over ten cities.’
19.bbe: And he said to him, You have done well, O good servant: because you have done well in a small thing you will have authority over ten towns.

19.msb: The second servant came and said, ‘Master, your mina has made five minas.’
19.kjv: And the second came, saying, Lord, thy pound hath gained five pounds.
19.blb: And the second came, saying, ‘Your mina, master, made five minas.’
19.bbe: And another came, saying, Your pound has made five pounds.

19.msb: And to this one he said, ‘You shall have authority over five cities.’
19.kjv: And he said likewise to him, Be thou also over five cities.
19.blb: And he said also to this one, ‘And you, be over five cities.’
19.bbe: And he said, You will be ruler over five towns.

19.msb: Then another servant came and said, ‘Master, here is your mina, which I have laid away in a piece of cloth.
19.kjv: And another came, saying, Lord, behold, here is thy pound, which I have kept laid up in a napkin:
19.blb: And the other came, saying, ‘Master, behold your mina, which I had lying away in a soudario.
19.bbe: And another came, saying, Lord, here is your pound, which I put away in a cloth;

19.msb: For I was afraid of you, because you are a harsh man. You withdraw what you did not deposit and reap what you did not sow.’
19.kjv: For I feared thee, because thou art an austere man: thou takest up that thou layedst not down, and reapest that thou didst not sow.
19.blb: For I was afraid of you, because you are a harsh man. You take up what you did not lay down, and you reap what you did not sow.’
19.bbe: Because I was in fear of you, for you are a hard man: you take up what you have not put down, and get in grain where you have not put seed.

19.msb: His master replied, ‘You wicked servant, I will judge you by your own words. So you knew that I am a harsh man, withdrawing what I did not deposit and reaping what I did not sow?
19.kjv: And he saith unto him, Out of thine own mouth will I judge thee, thou wicked servant. Thou knewest that I was an austere man, taking up that I laid not down, and reaping that I did not sow:
19.blb: He says to him, ‘Out of your mouth I will judge you, evil servant. You knew that I am a harsh man, taking up what I did not lay down and reaping what I did not sow?
19.bbe: He said to him, By the words of your mouth you will be judged, you bad servant. You had knowledge that I am a hard man, taking up what I have not put down and getting in grain where I have not put seed;

19.msb: Why then did you not deposit my money in the bank, and upon my return I could have collected it with interest?’
19.kjv: Wherefore then gavest not thou my money into the bank, that at my coming I might have required mine own with usury?
19.blb: And why did you not give my money to the bank, and I, having come, might have collected it with interest?’
19.bbe: Why then did you not put my money in a bank, so that when I came I would get it back with interest?

19.msb: Then he told those standing by, ‘Take the mina from him and give it to the one who has ten minas.’
19.kjv: And he said unto them that stood by, Take from him the pound, and give it to him that hath ten pounds.
19.blb: And to those standing by he said, ‘Take from him the mina and give it to the one having the ten minas.’
19.bbe: And he said to the others who were near, Take the pound away from him, and give it to the man who has ten.

19.msb: ‘Master,’ they said, ‘he already has ten!’
19.kjv: (And they said unto him, Lord, he hath ten pounds.)
19.blb: And they said to him, ‘Lord, he has ten minas!’
19.bbe: And they say to him, Lord, he has ten pounds.

19.msb: He replied, ‘I tell you that everyone who has will be given more; but the one who does not have, even what he has will be taken away from him.
19.kjv: For I say unto you, That unto every one which hath shall be given; and from him that hath not, even that he hath shall be taken away from him.
19.blb: I say to you that to everyone having, it will be given; but from the one not having, even that which he has will be taken away.
19.bbe: And I say to you that to everyone who has, more will be given, but from him who has not, even what he has will be taken away.

19.msb: And these enemies of mine who were unwilling for me to rule over them, bring them here and slay them in front of me.’”
19.kjv: But those mine enemies, which would not that I should reign over them, bring hither, and slay them before me.
19.blb: However, these enemies of mine, those not having been willing for me to reign over them, bring them here and slay them before me.’”
19.bbe: And as for those who were against me, who would not have me for their ruler, let them come here, and be put to death before me.

19.msb: After Jesus had said this, He went on ahead, going up to Jerusalem.
19.kjv: And when he had thus spoken, he went before, ascending up to Jerusalem.
19.blb: And having said these things, He was going on ahead, going up to Jerusalem.
19.bbe: And when he had said this, he went on in front of them, going up to Jerusalem.
19.heading: The Triumphal Entry

19.msb: As He approached Bethsphage and Bethany at the Mount of Olives, He sent out two of His disciples,
19.kjv: And it came to pass, when he was come nigh to Bethphage and Bethany, at the mount called the mount of Olives, he sent two of his disciples,
19.blb: And it came to pass as He drew near to Bethphage and Bethany, toward the mount called Olivet, that He sent two of the disciples,
19.bbe: And it came about that when he got near Beth-phage and Bethany by the mountain which is named the Mountain of Olives, he sent two of the disciples,

19.msb: saying, “Go into the village ahead of you, and as you enter it, you will find a colt tied there, on which no one has ever sat. Untie it and bring it here.
19.kjv: Saying, Go ye into the village over against you; in the which at your entering ye shall find a colt tied, whereon yet never man sat: loose him, and bring him hither.
19.blb: saying, “Go into the village ahead, in which, entering, you will find a colt tied, on which no one of men ever sat; and having loosed it, bring it.
19.bbe: Saying, Go into the little town in front of you, and on going in you will see a young ass fixed with a cord, on which no man has ever been seated; let him loose and take him.

19.msb: If anyone asks, ‘Why are you untying it?’ tell him, ‘The Lord needs it.’”
19.kjv: And if any man ask you, Why do ye loose him? thus shall ye say unto him, Because the Lord hath need of him.
19.blb: And if anyone may ask you, ‘Why are you loosing it?’ thus you will say, ‘Because the Lord has need of it.’”
19.bbe: And if anyone says to you, Why are you taking him? say, The Lord has need of him.

19.msb: So those who were sent went out and found it just as Jesus had told them.
19.kjv: And they that were sent went their way, and found even as he had said unto them.
19.blb: And having gone away, those sent found it just as He said to them.
19.bbe: And those whom he sent went away, and it was as he said.

19.msb: As they were untying the colt, its owners asked, “Why are you untying the colt?”
19.kjv: And as they were loosing the colt, the owners thereof said unto them, Why loose ye the colt?
19.blb: And on their loosing the colt, its masters said to them, “Why are you loosing the colt?”
19.bbe: And when they were getting the young ass, the owners of it said to them, Why are you taking the young ass?

19.msb: “The Lord needs it,” they answered.
19.kjv: And they said, The Lord hath need of him.
19.blb: And they said, “The Lord has need of it.”
19.bbe: And they said, The Lord has need of him.

19.msb: Then they led the colt to Jesus, threw their cloaks over it, and put Jesus on it.
19.kjv: And they brought him to Jesus: and they cast their garments upon the colt, and they set Jesus thereon.
19.blb: And they led it to Jesus, and having cast their garments on the colt, they put Jesus on it.
19.bbe: And they took him to Jesus, and they put their clothing on the ass, and Jesus got on to him.

19.msb: As He rode along, the people spread their cloaks on the road.
19.kjv: And as he went, they spread their clothes in the way.
19.blb: And in His going, they were spreading their garments in the road.
19.bbe: And while he went on his way they put their clothing down on the road in front of him.

19.msb: And as He approached the descent from the Mount of Olives, the whole multitude of disciples began to praise God joyfully in a loud voice for all the miracles they had seen:
19.kjv: And when he was come nigh, even now at the descent of the mount of Olives, the whole multitude of the disciples began to rejoice and praise God with a loud voice for all the mighty works that they had seen;
19.blb: And in His drawing near, already at the descent of the Mount of Olives, the whole multitude of the disciples, rejoicing, began to praise God in a loud voice for all the mighty works that they had seen,
19.bbe: And when he came near the foot of the Mountain of Olives, all the disciples with loud voices gave praise to God with joy, because of all the great works which they had seen;

19.msb: “Blessed is the King who comes in the name of the Lord!” “Peace in heaven and glory in the highest!”
19.kjv: Saying, Blessed be the King that cometh in the name of the Lord: peace in heaven, and glory in the highest.
19.blb: saying: “Blessed is the coming King in the name of the Lord!” “Peace in heaven and glory in the highest!”
19.bbe: Saying, A blessing on the King who comes in the name of the Lord; peace in heaven and glory in the highest.

19.msb: But some of the Pharisees in the crowd said to Him, “Teacher, rebuke Your disciples!”
19.kjv: And some of the Pharisees from among the multitude said unto him, Master, rebuke thy disciples.
19.blb: And some of the Pharisees from the crowd said to Him, “Teacher, rebuke Your disciples!”
19.bbe: And some of the Pharisees among the people said to him, Master, make your disciples be quiet.

19.msb: “I tell you,” He answered, “if they remain silent, the very stones will cry out.”
19.kjv: And he answered and said unto them, I tell you that, if these should hold their peace, the stones would immediately cry out.
19.blb: And answering, He said, “I say to you that if these will be silent, the stones will cry out.”
19.bbe: And he said in answer, I say to you, if these men keep quiet, the very stones will be crying out.

19.msb: As Jesus approached Jerusalem and saw the city, He wept over it
19.kjv: And when he was come near, he beheld the city, and wept over it,
19.blb: And as He drew near, having seen the city, He wept over it,
19.bbe: And when he got near and saw the town, he was overcome with weeping for it,
19.heading: Jesus Weeps over Jerusalem

19.msb: and said, “If only you, even you, had known on this day what would bring you peace! But now it is hidden from your eyes.
19.kjv: Saying, If thou hadst known, even thou, at least in this thy day, the things which belong unto thy peace! but now they are hid from thine eyes.
19.blb: saying, “If you knew in this day, even you, the things for peace! But now they were hidden from your eyes.
19.bbe: Saying, If you, even you, had knowledge today, of the things which give peace! but you are not able to see them.

19.msb: For the days will come upon you when your enemies will barricade you and surround you and hem you in on every side.
19.kjv: For the days shall come upon thee, that thine enemies shall cast a trench about thee, and compass thee round, and keep thee in on every side,
19.blb: For the days will come upon you, and your enemies will cast around you a barricade, and they will surround you and will hem you in on every side.
19.bbe: For the time will come when your attackers will put a wall round you, and come all round you and keep you in on every side,

19.msb: They will level you to the ground—you and the children within your walls. They will not leave one stone on another, because you did not recognize the time of your visitation from God.”
19.kjv: And shall lay thee even with the ground, and thy children within thee; and they shall not leave in thee one stone upon another; because thou knewest not the time of thy visitation.
19.blb: And they will level you to the ground, and your children in you, and they will not leave a stone upon a stone in you, because you did not know the season of your visitation.”
19.bbe: And will make you level with the earth, and your children with you; and there will not be one stone resting on another in you, because you did not see that it was your day of mercy.

19.msb: Then Jesus entered the temple courts and began to drive out those who were selling and buying there.
19.kjv: And he went into the temple, and began to cast out them that sold therein, and them that bought;
19.blb: And having entered into the temple, He began to cast out those selling,
19.bbe: And he went into the Temple and put out those who were trading there,
19.heading: Jesus Cleanses the Temple

19.msb: He declared to them, “It is written: ‘My house is a house of prayer.’ But you have made it ‘a den of robbers.’”
19.kjv: Saying unto them, It is written, My house is the house of prayer: but ye have made it a den of thieves.
19.blb: saying to them, “It has been written: ‘And My house will be a house of prayer.’ But you made it ‘a den of robbers.’”
19.bbe: Saying to them, It has been said, My house is to be a house of prayer, but you have made it a hole of thieves.

19.msb: Jesus was teaching at the temple every day, but the chief priests, scribes, and leaders of the people were intent on killing Him.
19.kjv: And he taught daily in the temple. But the chief priests and the scribes and the chief of the people sought to destroy him,
19.blb: And He was teaching every day in the temple. But the chief priests and the scribes and the foremost of the people were seeking to destroy Him.
19.bbe: And every day he was teaching in the Temple. But the chief priests and the scribes and the rulers of the people were attempting to put him to death;

19.msb: Yet they could not find a way to do so, because all the people hung on His words.
19.kjv: And could not find what they might do: for all the people were very attentive to hear him.
19.blb: And they were not finding what they might do; for all the people were hanging on Him, hearing.
19.bbe: But they were not able to do anything, because the people all kept near him, being greatly interested in his words.

20.msb: One day as Jesus was teaching the people in the temple courts and proclaiming the gospel, the priests and scribes, together with the elders, came up to Him.
20.kjv: And it came to pass, that on one of those days, as he taught the people in the temple, and preached the gospel, the chief priests and the scribes came upon him with the elders,
20.blb: And it came to pass on one of the days, in His teaching the people in the temple and proclaiming the gospel, that the chief priests and the scribes came up with the elders,
20.bbe: And it came about on one of those days, when he was teaching the people in the Temple and preaching the good news,
20.heading: Jesus’ Authority Challenged

20.msb: “Tell us,” they said, “by what authority are You doing these things, and who gave You this authority?”
20.kjv: And spake unto him, saying, Tell us, by what authority doest thou these things? or who is he that gave thee this authority?
20.blb: and they spoke to Him, saying, “Tell us by what authority You do these things, or who is the one having given You this authority?”
20.bbe: That the chief priests and the scribes and the rulers of the people came to him and said, Make clear to us by what authority you do these things and who gave you this authority.

20.msb: “I will also ask you one question,” Jesus replied. “Tell Me:
20.kjv: And he answered and said unto them, I will also ask you one thing; and answer me:
20.blb: And answering, He said to them, “I also will ask you a word, and you tell Me:
20.bbe: And in answer he said to them, I will put a question to you, and do you give me an answer:

20.msb: John’s baptism—was it from heaven, or from men?”
20.kjv: The baptism of John, was it from heaven, or of men?
20.blb: The baptism of John—was it from heaven or from men?”
20.bbe: The baptism of John, was it from heaven or of men?

20.msb: They deliberated among themselves and said, “If we say, ‘From heaven,’ He will ask, ‘Why did you not believe him?’
20.kjv: And they reasoned with themselves, saying, If we shall say, From heaven; he will say, Why then believed ye him not?
20.blb: And they reasoned with themselves, saying, “If we should say, ‘From heaven,’ He will say, ‘Why did you not believe him?’
20.bbe: And they said among themselves, If we say, From heaven; he will say, Why did you not have faith in him?

20.msb: But if we say, ‘From men,’ all the people will stone us, for they are convinced that John was a prophet.”
20.kjv: But and if we say, Of men; all the people will stone us: for they be persuaded that John was a prophet.
20.blb: But if we should say, ‘From men,’ all the people will stone us, for they are persuaded that John is a prophet.”
20.bbe: But if we say, Of men; we will be stoned by the people, for they are certain that John was a prophet.

20.msb: So they answered that they did not know where it was from.
20.kjv: And they answered, that they could not tell whence it was.
20.blb: And they answered that they did not know from where.
20.bbe: And they made answer that they had no idea where it came from.

20.msb: And Jesus replied, “Neither will I tell you by what authority I am doing these things.”
20.kjv: And Jesus said unto them, Neither tell I you by what authority I do these things.
20.blb: And Jesus said to them, “Neither do I tell you by what authority I do these things.”
20.bbe: And Jesus said, And I will not make clear to you by what authority I do these things.

20.msb: Then He proceeded to tell the people this parable: “A man planted a vineyard, rented it out to some tenants, and went away for a long time.
20.kjv: Then began he to speak to the people this parable; A certain man planted a vineyard, and let it forth to husbandmen, and went into a far country for a long time.
20.blb: And He began to speak to the people this parable: “A certain man planted a vineyard, and he rented it out to farmers and traveled abroad a long time.
20.bbe: And he gave the people this story: A man made a vine-garden and gave the use of it to some field-workers and went into another country for a long time.
20.heading: The Parable of the Wicked Tenants

20.msb: At harvest time, he sent a servant to the tenants to collect his share of the fruit of the vineyard. But the tenants beat the servant and sent him away empty-handed.
20.kjv: And at the season he sent a servant to the husbandmen, that they should give him of the fruit of the vineyard: but the husbandmen beat him, and sent him away empty.
20.blb: And in the season, he sent a servant to the farmers, so that they will give to him from the fruit of the vineyard. But the farmers sent him away empty-handed, having beaten him.
20.bbe: And at the right time he sent a servant to the workers to get part of the fruit from the vines; but the workmen gave him blows and sent him away with nothing.

20.msb: So he sent another servant, but they beat him and treated him shamefully, sending him away empty-handed.
20.kjv: And again he sent another servant: and they beat him also, and entreated him shamefully, and sent him away empty.
20.blb: And he proceeded to send another servant, but having beaten and having dishonored that one also, they sent him away empty-handed.
20.bbe: And he sent another servant, and they gave blows to him in the same way, and put shame on him, and sent him away with nothing.

20.msb: Then he sent a third, but they wounded him and threw him out.
20.kjv: And again he sent a third: and they wounded him also, and cast him out.
20.blb: And he proceeded to send a third, and having wounded this one also, they cast him out.
20.bbe: And he sent a third, and they gave him wounds and put him out.

20.msb: ‘What shall I do?’ asked the owner of the vineyard. ‘I will send my beloved son. Perhaps they will respect him when they see him.’
20.kjv: Then said the lord of the vineyard, What shall I do? I will send my beloved son: it may be they will reverence him when they see him.
20.blb: Then the lord of the vineyard said, ‘What shall I do? I will send my beloved son; perhaps they will respect him.’
20.bbe: And the lord of the garden said, What am I to do? I will send my dearly loved son; they may give respect to him.

20.msb: But when the tenants saw the son, they discussed it among themselves and said, ‘This is the heir. Come, let us kill him, and the inheritance will be ours.’
20.kjv: But when the husbandmen saw him, they reasoned among themselves, saying, This is the heir: come, let us kill him, that the inheritance may be ours.
20.blb: But having seen him, the farmers were reasoning with one another, saying, ‘This is the heir; let us kill him, so that the inheritance might become ours.’
20.bbe: But when the workmen saw him, they said to one another, This is he who will one day be the owner of the property: let us put him to death and the heritage will be ours.

20.msb: So they threw him out of the vineyard and killed him. What then will the owner of the vineyard do to them?
20.kjv: So they cast him out of the vineyard, and killed him. What therefore shall the lord of the vineyard do unto them?
20.blb: And having cast him out of the vineyard, they killed him. What, therefore, will the lord of the vineyard do to them?
20.bbe: And driving him out of the garden they put him to death. Now what will the lord do to these workmen?

20.msb: He will come and kill those tenants and give the vineyard to others.” And when the people heard this, they said, “May such a thing never happen!”
20.kjv: He shall come and destroy these husbandmen, and shall give the vineyard to others. And when they heard it, they said, God forbid.
20.blb: He will come and will destroy these farmers, and will give the vineyard to others.” And having heard, they said, “Never may it be!”
20.bbe: He will come and put them to destruction and give the garden to others. And when he said this, they said, May it not be so.

20.msb: But Jesus looked directly at them and said, “Then what is the meaning of that which is written: ‘The stone the builders rejected has become the cornerstone’?
20.kjv: And he beheld them, and said, What is this then that is written, The stone which the builders rejected, the same is become the head of the corner?
20.blb: But having looked at them, He said, “What then is this that has been written: ‘The stone that those building rejected, this became the head of the corner’?
20.bbe: But he, looking on them, said, Is it not in the Writings, The stone which the builders put on one side, the same has become the chief stone of the building?

20.msb: Everyone who falls on this stone will be broken to pieces, but he on whom it falls will be crushed.”
20.kjv: Whosoever shall fall upon that stone shall be broken; but on whomsoever it shall fall, it will grind him to powder.
20.blb: Everyone having fallen on that stone will be broken; but on whomever it might fall, it will grind him into powder.”
20.bbe: Everyone falling on that stone will be broken, but the man on whom the stone comes down will be crushed to dust.

20.msb: When the chief priests and scribes realized that Jesus had spoken this parable against them, they sought to arrest Him that very hour. But they were afraid.
20.kjv: And the chief priests and the scribes the same hour sought to lay hands on him; and they feared the people: for they perceived that he had spoken this parable against them.
20.blb: And the scribes and the chief priests sought to lay hands on Him in that hour, and they feared the people. For they knew that He spoke this parable against them.
20.bbe: And the chief priests and the scribes made attempts to get their hands on him in that very hour; and they were in fear of the people, for they saw that he had made up this story against them.
20.heading: Paying Taxes to Caesar

20.msb: So they watched Him closely and sent spies who pretended to be sincere. They were hoping to catch Him in His words in order to hand Him over to the rule and authority of the governor.
20.kjv: And they watched him, and sent forth spies, which should feign themselves just men, that they might take hold of his words, that so they might deliver him unto the power and authority of the governor.
20.blb: And having closely watched, they sent spies feigning themselves to be righteous, so that they might catch Him in His word, so as to deliver Him to the rule and to the authority of the governor.
20.bbe: And they kept watch on him, and sent out secret representatives, who were acting the part of good men, in order that they might get something from his words, on account of which they might give him up to the government and into the power of the ruler.

20.msb: “Teacher,” they inquired, “we know that You speak and teach correctly. You show no partiality but teach the way of God in accordance with the truth.
20.kjv: And they asked him, saying, Master, we know that thou sayest and teachest rightly, neither acceptest thou the person of any, but teachest the way of God truly:
20.blb: And they questioned Him, saying, “Teacher, we know that You speak and teach rightly and do not receive any person, but teach the way of God on the basis of truth.
20.bbe: And they put a question to him, saying, Master, we are certain that your teaching and your words are right, and that you have no respect for a man's position, but you are teaching the true way of God:

20.msb: Is it lawful for us to pay taxes to Caesar or not?”
20.kjv: Is it lawful for us to give tribute unto Cæsar, or no?
20.blb: Is it lawful for us to give tax to Caesar or not?”
20.bbe: Is it right for us to make payment of taxes to Caesar or not?

20.msb: But Jesus saw through their duplicity and said to them, “Why do you test Me?
20.kjv: But he perceived their craftiness, and said unto them, Why tempt ye me?
20.blb: But having perceived their craftiness, He said to them,
20.bbe: But he saw through their trick and said to them,

20.msb: Show Me a denarius. Whose image and inscription are on it?” “Caesar’s,” they answered.
20.kjv: Shew me a penny. Whose image and superscription hath it? They answered and said, Cæsar’s.
20.blb: “Show Me a denarius. Whose image and inscription does it have?” And they said, “Caesar’s.”
20.bbe: Let me see a penny. Whose image and name are on it? And they said, Caesar's.

20.msb: So Jesus told them, “Give to Caesar what is Caesar’s, and to God what is God’s.”
20.kjv: And he said unto them, Render therefore unto Cæsar the things which be Cæsar’s, and unto God the things which be God’s.
20.blb: And He said to them, “Therefore give back the things of Caesar to Caesar, and the things of God to God.”
20.bbe: And he said, Then give to Caesar the things which are Caesar's, and to God the things which are God's.

20.msb: And they were unable to trap Him in His words before the people. And amazed at His answer, they fell silent.
20.kjv: And they could not take hold of his words before the people: and they marvelled at his answer, and held their peace.
20.blb: And they were not able to catch Him in His saying before the people. And having marveled at His answer, they were silent.
20.bbe: And they were not able to get anything from these words before the people: but they were full of wonder at his answer, and said nothing.

20.msb: Then some of the Sadducees, who say there is no resurrection, came to question Him.
20.kjv: Then came to him certain of the Sadducees, which deny that there is any resurrection; and they asked him,
20.blb: And some of the Sadducees, the ones denying there is a resurrection, having come, questioned Him,
20.bbe: And some of the Sadducees came to him, who say that there is no coming back from the dead; and they said to him,
20.heading: The Sadducees and the Resurrection

20.msb: “Teacher,” they said, “Moses wrote for us that if a man’s brother dies and leaves a wife but no children, the man is to marry his brother’s widow and raise up offspring for him.
20.kjv: Saying, Master, Moses wrote unto us, If any man’s brother die, having a wife, and he die without children, that his brother should take his wife, and raise up seed unto his brother.
20.blb: saying, “Teacher, Moses wrote for us that if anyone’s brother should die having a wife, and he should be childless, that his brother should take the wife and should raise up seed for his brother.
20.bbe: Master, Moses said that if a man's brother comes to his end, having a wife, but no children, his brother is to take the wife, and get a family for his brother.

20.msb: Now there were seven brothers. The first one married a wife but died childless.
20.kjv: There were therefore seven brethren: and the first took a wife, and died without children.
20.blb: Therefore there were seven brothers. And the first, having taken a wife, died childless;
20.bbe: Now there were seven brothers, and the first had a wife and came to his end, having no children;

20.msb: Then the second took her as wife, and he died childless.
20.kjv: And the second took her to wife, and he died childless.
20.blb: and the second
20.bbe: And the second;

20.msb: And the third married the widow, and in the same way all seven died, leaving no children.
20.kjv: And the third took her; and in like manner the seven also: and they left no children, and died.
20.blb: and the third took her; and likewise also the seven did not leave behind children and died.
20.bbe: And the third took her; and in the same way, all the seven, without having any children, came to their end.

20.msb: And last of all, the woman died.
20.kjv: Last of all the woman died also.
20.blb: Finally the woman also died.
20.bbe: And last of all, the woman came to her end.

20.msb: So then, in the resurrection, whose wife will she be? For all seven were married to her.”
20.kjv: Therefore in the resurrection whose wife of them is she? for seven had her to wife.
20.blb: Therefore, in the resurrection, the woman, of which of them does she become wife? For the seven had her as wife.”
20.bbe: When they come back from the dead, whose wife will she be? for all the seven had her.

20.msb: Jesus answered, “The sons of this age marry and are given in marriage.
20.kjv: And Jesus answering said unto them, The children of this world marry, and are given in marriage:
20.blb: And Jesus said to them, “The sons of this age marry and are given in marriage.
20.bbe: And Jesus said to them, The sons of this world are married and have wives;

20.msb: But those who are considered worthy to share in the age to come and in the resurrection from the dead will neither marry nor be given in marriage.
20.kjv: But they which shall be accounted worthy to obtain that world, and the resurrection from the dead, neither marry, nor are given in marriage:
20.blb: But those having been considered worthy to obtain that which is to the age and the resurrection that is out from the dead, they neither marry nor are given in marriage.
20.bbe: But those to whom is given the reward of the world to come, and to come back from the dead, have no wives, and are not married;

20.msb: In fact, they can no longer die, because they are like the angels. And since they are sons of the resurrection, they are sons of God.
20.kjv: Neither can they die any more: for they are equal unto the angels; and are the children of God, being the children of the resurrection.
20.blb: For neither are they able to die anymore, for they are like angels, and they are sons of God, being sons of the resurrection.
20.bbe: And death has no more power over them, for they are equal to the angels, and are sons of God, being of those who will come back from the dead.

20.msb: Even Moses demonstrates that the dead are raised, in the passage about the burning bush. For he calls the Lord ‘the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob.’
20.kjv: Now that the dead are raised, even Moses shewed at the bush, when he calleth the Lord the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob.
20.blb: But that the dead are raised even Moses showed at the bush, as he calls the Lord ‘the God of Abraham and the God of Isaac and the God of Jacob.’
20.bbe: But even Moses made it clear that the dead come back to life, saying, in the story of the burning thorn-tree, The Lord, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob.

20.msb: He is not the God of the dead, but of the living, for to Him all are alive.”
20.kjv: For he is not a God of the dead, but of the living: for all live unto him.
20.blb: Now He is not the God of the dead but of the living, for all live to Him.”
20.bbe: Now he is not the God of the dead but of the living: for all men are living to him.

20.msb: Some of the scribes answered, “Teacher, You have spoken well!”
20.kjv: Then certain of the scribes answering said, Master, thou hast well said.
20.blb: And answering, some of the scribes said, “Teacher, You spoke well!”
20.bbe: And some of the scribes, in answer to this, said, Master, you have said well.

20.msb: And they did not dare to question Him any further.
20.kjv: And after that they durst not ask him any question at all.
20.blb: For no longer did they dare to question Him anything.
20.bbe: And they had fear of putting any more questions to him.

20.msb: Then Jesus declared, “How can it be said that the Christ is the Son of David?
20.kjv: And he said unto them, How say they that Christ is David’s son?
20.blb: And He said to them, “How do they say the Christ is Son of David?
20.bbe: And he said to them, Why do they say that the Christ is the son of David?
20.heading: Whose Son Is the Christ?

20.msb: For David himself says in the book of Psalms: ‘The Lord said to my Lord, “Sit at My right hand
20.kjv: And David himself saith in the book of Psalms, The LORD said unto my Lord, Sit thou on my right hand,
20.blb: For David himself says in the book of Psalms: ‘The Lord said to my Lord, “Sit at My right hand
20.bbe: For David himself says in the book of Psalms, The Lord said to my Lord, Take your seat at my right hand,

20.msb: until I make Your enemies a footstool for Your feet.”’
20.kjv: Till I make thine enemies thy footstool.
20.blb: until I place Your enemies as a footstool for Your feet.”’
20.bbe: Till I put under your feet all those who are against you.

20.msb: Thus David calls Him ‘Lord.’ So how can He be David’s son?”
20.kjv: David therefore calleth him Lord, how is he then his son?
20.blb: David therefore calls Him ‘Lord,’ and how is He his son?”
20.bbe: David then gives him the name of Lord, so how is it possible for him to be his son?

20.msb: In the hearing of all the people, Jesus said to His disciples,
20.kjv: Then in the audience of all the people he said unto his disciples,
20.blb: And all the people hearing, He said to His disciples,
20.bbe: And in the hearing of all the people he said to his disciples,
20.heading: Beware of the Scribes

20.msb: “Beware of the scribes. They like to walk around in long robes, and they love the greetings in the marketplaces, the chief seats in the synagogues, and the places of honor at banquets.
20.kjv: Beware of the scribes, which desire to walk in long robes, and love greetings in the markets, and the highest seats in the synagogues, and the chief rooms at feasts;
20.blb: “Beware of the scribes, who are wanting to walk in long robes, and loving greetings in the marketplaces and first seats in the synagogues and first places at the suppers,
20.bbe: Keep away from the scribes, whose pleasure it is to go about in long robes, and to have words of respect said to them in the market-places, and to take the chief seats in the Synagogues and the first places at feasts;

20.msb: They defraud widows of their houses, and for a show make lengthy prayers. These men will receive greater condemnation.”
20.kjv: Which devour widows’ houses, and for a shew make long prayers: the same shall receive greater damnation.
20.blb: who devour the houses of widows and pray at great length as a pretext. These will receive more abundant judgment.”
20.bbe: Who take the property of widows and before the eyes of men make long prayers; they will get a greater punishment.

21.msb: Then Jesus looked up and saw the rich putting their gifts into the treasury,
21.kjv: And he looked up, and saw the rich men casting their gifts into the treasury.
21.blb: And having looked up, He saw the ones casting their gifts into the treasury—the rich.
21.bbe: And looking up, he saw the men of wealth putting their offerings in the money-box.
21.heading: The Poor Widow’s Offering

21.msb: and He saw a poor widow put in two small copper coins.
21.kjv: And he saw also a certain poor widow casting in thither two mites.
21.blb: And He saw a certain poor widow casting there two lepta.
21.bbe: And he saw a certain poor widow putting in a farthing.

21.msb: “Truly I tell you,” He said, “this poor widow has put in more than all the others.
21.kjv: And he said, Of a truth I say unto you, that this poor widow hath cast in more than they all:
21.blb: “And He said, “Truly I say to you that this poor widow cast in more than all.
21.bbe: And he said, Truly I say to you, This poor widow has given more than all of them:

21.msb: For they all contributed to God out of their surplus, but she out of her poverty has put in all she had to live on.”
21.kjv: For all these have of their abundance cast in unto the offerings of God: but she of her penury hath cast in all the living that she had.
21.blb: For these all cast in the gifts out of that which is abounding to them, but she out of her lack cast in all the livelihood that she had.”
21.bbe: For they gave out of their wealth, having more than enough for themselves: but she, even out of her need, has put in all her living.

21.msb: As some of the disciples were remarking how the temple was adorned with beautiful stones and consecrated gifts, Jesus said,
21.kjv: And as some spake of the temple, how it was adorned with goodly stones and gifts, he said,
21.blb: And some speaking about the temple, that it was adorned with goodly stones and consecrated gifts, He said,
21.bbe: And some were talking about the Temple, how it was made fair with beautiful stones and with offerings, but he said,
21.heading: Temple Destruction and Other Signs

21.msb: “As for what you see here, the time will come when not one stone will be left on another; every one will be thrown down.”
21.kjv: As for these things which ye behold, the days will come, in the which there shall not be left one stone upon another, that shall not be thrown down.
21.blb: “These things that you are beholding, the days will come in which not a stone will be left upon a stone that will not be thrown down.”
21.bbe: As for these things which you see, the days will come when not one stone will be resting on another, but all will be broken down.

21.msb: “Teacher,” they asked, “when will these things happen? And what will be the sign that they are about to take place?”
21.kjv: And they asked him, saying, Master, but when shall these things be? and what sign will there be when these things shall come to pass?
21.blb: And they questioned Him, saying, “Teacher, when, then, will these things be, and what is the sign when these things are about to happen?”
21.bbe: And they said to him, Master, when will these things be? and what sign will there be when these events are to take place?

21.msb: Jesus answered, “See to it that you are not deceived. For many will come in My name, claiming, ‘I am He,’ and, ‘The time is near.’ Therefore do not follow them.
21.kjv: And he said, Take heed that ye be not deceived: for many shall come in my name, saying, I am Christ; and the time draweth near: go ye not therefore after them.
21.blb: And He said, “Take heed, lest you be led astray; for many will come in My name, saying, ‘I am He,’ and, ‘The time has drawn near.’ Do not go after them.
21.bbe: And he said, Take care that you are not tricked: for a number of people will come in my name, saying, I am he; and, The time is near: do not go after them.

21.msb: When you hear of wars and rebellions, do not be alarmed. These things must happen first, but the end is not imminent.”
21.kjv: But when ye shall hear of wars and commotions, be not terrified: for these things must first come to pass; but the end is not by and by.
21.blb: And when you may hear of wars and disturbances, do not be terrified; for it is necessary for these things to happen first, but the end is not immediately.”
21.bbe: And when news of wars and troubled times comes to your ears, have no fear; for these things have to be, but the end will not be now.

21.msb: Then He told them, “Nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom.
21.kjv: Then said he unto them, Nation shall rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom:
21.blb: Then He was saying to them, “Nation will rise up against nation, and kingdom against kingdom.
21.bbe: Then he said to them, Nation will be moved against nation and kingdom against kingdom:
21.heading: Witnessing to All Nations

21.msb: There will be great earthquakes in various places, famines and pestilences, along with fearful sights and great signs from heaven.
21.kjv: And great earthquakes shall be in divers places, and famines, and pestilences; and fearful sights and great signs shall there be from heaven.
21.blb: There will be also great earthquakes and famines and pestilences in various places. There will also be fearful sights and great signs from heaven.
21.bbe: There will be great earth-shocks and outbursts of disease in a number of places, and men will be without food; and there will be wonders and great signs from heaven.

21.msb: But before all this, they will seize you and persecute you. On account of My name they will deliver you to the synagogues and prisons, and they will bring you before kings and governors.
21.kjv: But before all these, they shall lay their hands on you, and persecute you, delivering you up to the synagogues, and into prisons, being brought before kings and rulers for my name’s sake.
21.blb: But before all these things, they will lay their hands upon you and will persecute you, delivering you up to the synagogues and prisons, leading you away before kings and governors on account of My name.
21.bbe: But before all this, they will take you and be very cruel to you, giving you up to the Synagogues and to prisons, taking you before kings and rulers, because of my name.

21.msb: This will be your opportunity to serve as witnesses.
21.kjv: And it shall turn to you for a testimony.
21.blb: It will result to you for a testimony.
21.bbe: And it will be turned to a witness for you.

21.msb: So make up your mind not to worry beforehand how to defend yourselves.
21.kjv: Settle it therefore in your hearts, not to meditate before what ye shall answer:
21.blb: Settle, therefore, in your hearts not to premeditate to make a defense.
21.bbe: So take care not to be troubled before the time comes, about what answers you will give:

21.msb: For I will give you speech and wisdom that none of your adversaries will be able to contradict or resist.
21.kjv: For I will give you a mouth and wisdom, which all your adversaries shall not be able to gainsay nor resist.
21.blb: For I will give you a mouth and wisdom, which all those opposing you will neither be able to resist nor contradict.
21.bbe: For I will give you words and wisdom, so that not one of those who are against you will be able to get the better of you, or to put you in the wrong.

21.msb: You will be betrayed even by parents and relatives and friends and brothers, and some of you will be put to death.
21.kjv: And ye shall be betrayed both by parents, and brethren, and kinsfolks, and friends; and some of you shall they cause to be put to death.
21.blb: And you will be delivered up even by parents and brothers and relatives and friends, and they will put to death some of you.
21.bbe: But you will be given up even by your fathers and mothers, your brothers and relations and friends; and some of you will be put to death.

21.msb: And you will be hated by everyone because of My name.
21.kjv: And ye shall be hated of all men for my name’s sake.
21.blb: And you will be hated by all because of My name.
21.bbe: And you will be hated by all men, because of me.

21.msb: Yet not even a hair of your head will perish.
21.kjv: But there shall not an hair of your head perish.
21.blb: And no, not a hair of your head shall perish.
21.bbe: But not a hair of your head will come to destruction.

21.msb: By your patient endurance you will gain your souls.
21.kjv: In your patience possess ye your souls.
21.blb: By your perseverance you will gain your souls.
21.bbe: By going through all these things, you will keep your lives.

21.msb: But when you see Jerusalem surrounded by armies, you will know that her desolation is near.
21.kjv: And when ye shall see Jerusalem compassed with armies, then know that the desolation thereof is nigh.
21.blb: But when you shall see Jerusalem being encircled by encampments, then know that her desolation has drawn near.
21.bbe: But when you see armies all round about Jerusalem, then be certain that her destruction is near.
21.heading: The Destruction of Jerusalem

21.msb: Then let those who are in Judea flee to the mountains, let those in the city get out, and let those in the country stay out of the city.
21.kjv: Then let them which are in Judæa flee to the mountains; and let them which are in the midst of it depart out; and let not them that are in the countries enter thereinto.
21.blb: Then those in Judea, let them flee to the mountains; and those in her midst, let them depart; and those in the country, let them not enter into her.
21.bbe: Then let those who are in Judaea go in flight to the mountains; and those who are in the middle of the town go out; and let not those who are in the country come in.

21.msb: For these are the days of vengeance, to fulfill all that is written.
21.kjv: For these be the days of vengeance, that all things which are written may be fulfilled.
21.blb: For these are the days of avenging, to fulfill all things having been written.
21.bbe: For these are the days of punishment, in which all the things in the Writings will be put into effect.

21.msb: How miserable those days will be for pregnant and nursing mothers! For there will be great distress upon the land and wrath against this people.
21.kjv: But woe unto them that are with child, and to them that give suck, in those days! for there shall be great distress in the land, and wrath upon this people.
21.blb: Woe to those having in womb and to those nursing in those days! For there will be great distress upon the land and wrath to this people.
21.bbe: It will be hard for women who are with child, and for her with a baby at the breast, in those days. For great trouble will come on the land, and wrath on this people.

21.msb: They will fall by the edge of the sword and be led captive into all the nations. And Jerusalem will be trodden down by the Gentiles, until the times of the Gentiles are fulfilled.
21.kjv: And they shall fall by the edge of the sword, and shall be led away captive into all nations: and Jerusalem shall be trodden down of the Gentiles, until the times of the Gentiles be fulfilled.
21.blb: And they will fall by the mouth of the sword and will be led captive into all the nations, and Jerusalem will be trodden down by the nations until the times of the nations are fulfilled.
21.bbe: And they will be put to death with the sword, and will be taken as prisoners into all the nations; and Jerusalem will be crushed under the feet of the Gentiles, till the times of the Gentiles are complete.

21.msb: There will be signs in the sun and moon and stars, and on the earth dismay among the nations, bewildered by the roaring of the sea and the surging of the waves.
21.kjv: And there shall be signs in the sun, and in the moon, and in the stars; and upon the earth distress of nations, with perplexity; the sea and the waves roaring;
21.blb: And there will be signs in sun and moon and stars, and upon the earth distress of nations with perplexity at the roaring of the sea and the rolling surge—
21.bbe: And there will be signs in the sun and moon and stars; and on the earth, fear among the nations and doubt because of the loud noise of the sea and the waves;
21.heading: The Return of the Son of Man

21.msb: Men will faint from fear and anxiety over what is coming upon the earth, for the powers of the heavens will be shaken.
21.kjv: Men’s hearts failing them for fear, and for looking after those things which are coming on the earth: for the powers of heaven shall be shaken.
