11.msb: This happened three times, and everything was drawn back up into heaven.
11.kjv: And this was done three times: and all were drawn up again into heaven.
11.blb: Now this happened three times, and all was drawn up into heaven again.
11.bbe: And this was done three times, and they were all taken up again into heaven.

11.msb: Just then three men sent to me from Caesarea stopped at the house where I was staying.
11.kjv: And, behold, immediately there were three men already come unto the house where I was, sent from Cæsarea unto me.
11.blb: And behold, immediately three men having been sent to me from Caesarea stood at the house in which we were.
11.bbe: And at that minute, three men, sent from Caesarea, came to the house where we were.

11.msb: The Spirit told me to accompany them without hesitation. These six brothers also went with me, and we entered the man’s home.
11.kjv: And the Spirit bade me go with them, nothing doubting. Moreover these six brethren accompanied me, and we entered into the man’s house:
11.blb: And the Spirit told me to go with them, not having doubted. And these six brothers also went with me, and we entered into the man’s house,
11.bbe: And the Spirit gave me orders to go with them, doubting nothing. And these six brothers came with me; and we went into that man's house:

11.msb: He told us how he had seen an angel standing in his house and saying, ‘Send men to Joppa for Simon who is called Peter.
11.kjv: And he shewed us how he had seen an angel in his house, which stood and said unto him, Send men to Joppa, and call for Simon, whose surname is Peter;
11.blb: and he related to us how he saw the angel having stood in his house and having said, ‘Send forth to Joppa and send for Simon who is called Peter,
11.bbe: And he gave us an account of how he had seen the angel in his house, saying, Send to Joppa, and get Simon, named Peter, to come to you;

11.msb: He will convey to you a message by which you and all your household will be saved.’
11.kjv: Who shall tell thee words, whereby thou and all thy house shall be saved.
11.blb: who will speak words to you by which you will be saved—you and all your household.’
11.bbe: Who will say words to you through which you and all your family may get salvation.

11.msb: As I began to speak, the Holy Spirit fell upon them, just as He had fallen upon us at the beginning.
11.kjv: And as I began to speak, the Holy Ghost fell on them, as on us at the beginning.
11.blb: And in my beginning to speak, the Holy Spirit fell upon them, even as also upon us in the beginning.
11.bbe: And, while I was talking to them, the Holy Spirit came on them, as on us at first.

11.msb: Then I remembered the word of the Lord, how He said, ‘John baptized with water, but you will be baptized with the Holy Spirit.’
11.kjv: Then remembered I the word of the Lord, how that he said, John indeed baptized with water; but ye shall be baptized with the Holy Ghost.
11.blb: And I remembered the word of the Lord, how He used to say, ‘John indeed baptized with water, but you will be baptized with the Holy Spirit.’
11.bbe: And the words of the Lord came into my mind, how he said, The baptism of John was with water, but you will have baptism with the Holy Spirit.

11.msb: So if God gave them the same gift He gave us who believed in the Lord Jesus Christ, who was I to hinder the work of God?”
11.kjv: Forasmuch then as God gave them the like gift as he did unto us, who believed on the Lord Jesus Christ; what was I, that I could withstand God?
11.blb: If, then, God gave to them the same gift as also to us having believed on the Lord Jesus Christ, how was I able to forbid God?”
11.bbe: If then God gave them, when they had faith in the Lord Jesus Christ, the same as he gave to us, who was I to go against God?

11.msb: When they heard this, they had no further objections, and they glorified God, saying, “So then, God has granted even the Gentiles repentance unto life.”
11.kjv: When they heard these things, they held their peace, and glorified God, saying, Then hath God also to the Gentiles granted repentance unto life.
11.blb: And having heard these things, they were silent and glorified God, saying, “Then indeed God has given also to the Gentiles repentance unto life.”
11.bbe: And hearing these things they said nothing more, but gave glory to God, saying, Then to the Gentiles as to us has God given a change of heart, so that they may have life.

11.msb: Meanwhile those scattered by the persecution that began with Stephen traveled as far as Phoenicia, Cyprus, and Antioch, speaking the message only to Jews.
11.kjv: Now they which were scattered abroad upon the persecution that arose about Stephen travelled as far as Phenice, and Cyprus, and Antioch, preaching the word to none but unto the Jews only.
11.blb: Therefore, indeed, those having been scattered by the tribulation having taken place over Stephen passed through to Phoenicia and Cyprus and Antioch, speaking the word to no one except to Jews only.
11.bbe: Then those who had gone away at the time of the trouble about Stephen, went as far as Phoenicia and Cyprus, preaching to the Jews only.
11.heading: The Church at Antioch

11.msb: But some of them, men from Cyprus and Cyrene, went to Antioch and began speaking to the Greeks, proclaiming the good news about the Lord Jesus.
11.kjv: And some of them were men of Cyprus and Cyrene, which, when they were come to Antioch, spake unto the Grecians, preaching the Lord Jesus.
11.blb: But some of them were men of Cyprus and Cyrene, who, having come into Antioch, were speaking also to the Hellenists, proclaiming the gospel—the Lord Jesus.
11.bbe: But some of them, men of Cyprus and Cyrene, when they came to Antioch, gave the good news about the Lord Jesus to the Greeks.

11.msb: The hand of the Lord was with them, and a great number of people believed and turned to the Lord.
11.kjv: And the hand of the Lord was with them: and a great number believed, and turned unto the Lord.
11.blb: And the hand of the Lord was with them, and a great number, having believed, turned to the Lord.
11.bbe: And the power of the Lord was with them, and a great number had faith and were turned to the Lord.

11.msb: When news of this reached the ears of the church in Jerusalem, they sent out Barnabas, that he should go to Antioch.
11.kjv: Then tidings of these things came unto the ears of the church which was in Jerusalem: and they sent forth Barnabas, that he should go as far as Antioch.
11.blb: Now the report was heard in the ears of the church being in Jerusalem concerning them, and they sent forth Barnabas to go as far as Antioch—
11.bbe: And news of them came to the ears of the church at Jerusalem: and they sent Barnabas as far as Antioch:

11.msb: When he arrived and saw the grace of God, he rejoiced and encouraged them all to abide in the Lord with all their hearts.
11.kjv: Who, when he came, and had seen the grace of God, was glad, and exhorted them all, that with purpose of heart they would cleave unto the Lord.
11.blb: who, having come and having seen the grace of God, rejoiced and was exhorting all to abide in the Lord with resolute purpose of heart.
11.bbe: Who, when he came and saw the grace of God, was glad; and he made clear to them the need of keeping near the Lord with all the strength of their hearts:

11.msb: Barnabas was a good man, full of the Holy Spirit and faith, and a great number of people were brought to the Lord.
11.kjv: For he was a good man, and full of the Holy Ghost and of faith: and much people was added unto the Lord.
11.blb: For he was a good man, and full of the Holy Spirit and of faith. And a great multitude was added to the Lord.
11.bbe: For he was a good man and full of the Holy Spirit and of faith: and a great number were joined to the Lord.

11.msb: Then Barnabas went to Tarsus to look for Saul,
11.kjv: Then departed Barnabas to Tarsus, for to seek Saul:
11.blb: And he went out to Tarsus to seek Saul,
11.bbe: Then he went on to Tarsus, looking for Saul;

11.msb: and when he found him, he brought him back to Antioch. So for a full year they met together with the church and taught large numbers of people. The disciples were first called Christians at Antioch.
11.kjv: And when he had found him, he brought him unto Antioch. And it came to pass, that a whole year they assembled themselves with the church, and taught much people. And the disciples were called Christians first in Antioch.
11.blb: and having found him, he brought him to Antioch. And it came to pass that they also gathered together a whole year in the church and taught a great multitude. And in Antioch the disciples were first called Christians.
11.bbe: And when he had come across him, he took him to Antioch. And they were with the church there for a year, teaching the people; and the disciples were first given the name of Christians in Antioch.

11.msb: In those days some prophets came down from Jerusalem to Antioch.
11.kjv: And in these days came prophets from Jerusalem unto Antioch.
11.blb: Now in these days, prophets came down from Jerusalem to Antioch.
11.bbe: Now in those days prophets came from Jerusalem to Antioch.

11.msb: One of them named Agabus stood up and predicted through the Spirit that a great famine would sweep across the whole world. (This happened under Claudius Caesar.)
11.kjv: And there stood up one of them named Agabus, and signified by the Spirit that there should be great dearth throughout all the world: which came to pass in the days of Claudius Cæsar.
11.blb: And one of them named Agabus, having risen up, signified by the Spirit that a great famine is about to be over the whole world—which came to pass under Claudius.
11.bbe: And one of them, named Agabus, said publicly through the Spirit that there would be serious need of food all over the earth: which came about in the time of Claudius.

11.msb: So the disciples, each according to his ability, decided to send relief to the brothers living in Judea.
11.kjv: Then the disciples, every man according to his ability, determined to send relief unto the brethren which dwelt in Judæa:
11.blb: And the disciples, as anyone was prospered, each of them determined to send for ministry to the brothers dwelling in Judea,
11.bbe: And the disciples, everyone as he was able, made a decision to send help to the brothers living in Judaea:

11.msb: This they did, sending their gifts to the elders with Barnabas and Saul.
11.kjv: Which also they did, and sent it to the elders by the hands of Barnabas and Saul.
11.blb: which also they did, having sent it to the elders by the hand of Barnabas and Saul.
11.bbe: Which they did, sending it to the rulers of the church by the hand of Barnabas and Saul.

12.msb: About that time, King Herod reached out to harm some who belonged to the church.
12.kjv: Now about that time Herod the king stretched forth his hands to vex certain of the church.
12.blb: Now at that time, Herod the king put forth the hands to mistreat some of those of the church.
12.bbe: Now, about that time, Herod the king made cruel attacks on the Christians.
12.heading: James Killed, Peter Imprisoned

12.msb: He had James, the brother of John, put to death with the sword.
12.kjv: And he killed James the brother of John with the sword.
12.blb: And he put to death James the brother of John with the sword.
12.bbe: And he put James, the brother of John, to death with the sword.

12.msb: And seeing that this pleased the Jews, Herod proceeded to seize Peter during the Feast of Unleavened Bread.
12.kjv: And because he saw it pleased the Jews, he proceeded further to take Peter also. (Then were the days of unleavened bread.)
12.blb: And having seen that it is pleasing to the Jews, he proceeded to seize Peter also—now these were the days of the Unleavened—
12.bbe: And when he saw that this was pleasing to the Jews he went on to take Peter in addition. This was at the time of the feast of unleavened bread.

12.msb: He arrested him and put him in prison, handing him over to be guarded by four squads of four soldiers each. Herod intended to bring him out to the people after the Passover.
12.kjv: And when he had apprehended him, he put him in prison, and delivered him to four quaternions of soldiers to keep him; intending after Easter to bring him forth to the people.
12.blb: whom also having arrested, he put in prison, having delivered him to four sets of four soldiers to guard him, intending to bring him out to the people after the Passover.
12.bbe: And having taken him, he put him in prison, with four bands of armed men to keep watch over him; his purpose being to take him out to the people after the Passover.

12.msb: So Peter was kept in prison, but the church was earnestly praying to God for him.
12.kjv: Peter therefore was kept in prison: but prayer was made without ceasing of the church unto God for him.
12.blb: Therefore indeed Peter was kept in the prison, but prayer was fervently being made to God by the church concerning him.
12.bbe: So Peter was kept in prison: but the church made strong prayer to God for him.
12.heading: The Rescue of Peter

12.msb: On the night before Herod was to bring him to trial, Peter was sleeping between two soldiers, bound with two chains, with sentries standing guard at the entrance to the prison.
12.kjv: And when Herod would have brought him forth, the same night Peter was sleeping between two soldiers, bound with two chains: and the keepers before the door kept the prison.
12.blb: And when Herod was about to bring him forth, on that night Peter was sleeping between two soldiers, having been bound with two chains, and guards before the door were keeping the prison.
12.bbe: And when Herod was about to take him out, the same night Peter was sleeping in chains between two armed men, and the watchmen were keeping watch before the door of the prison.

12.msb: Suddenly an angel of the Lord appeared and a light shone in the cell. He tapped Peter on the side and woke him up, saying, “Get up quickly.” And the chains fell off his wrists.
12.kjv: And, behold, the angel of the Lord came upon him, and a light shined in the prison: and he smote Peter on the side, and raised him up, saying, Arise up quickly. And his chains fell off from his hands.
12.blb: And behold, an angel of the Lord stood by, and a light shone in the cell. And having struck Peter’s side, he woke him up, saying, “Rise up in haste.” And his chains fell off the hands.
12.bbe: And a great light was seen shining in the room, and an angel of the Lord came to Peter and, touching him on his side so that he came out of his sleep, said, Get up quickly. And his chains came off his hands.

12.msb: “Get dressed and put on your sandals,” said the angel. Peter did so, and the angel told him, “Wrap your cloak around you and follow me.”
12.kjv: And the angel said unto him, Gird thyself, and bind on thy sandals. And so he did. And he saith unto him, Cast thy garment about thee, and follow me.
12.blb: And the angel said to him, “Gird yourself and put on your sandals.” And he did so. And he says to him, “Wrap around you your cloak and follow me.”
12.bbe: Then the angel said, Put on your shoes and get ready to go. And he did so. And he said, Put your coat round you and come with me.

12.msb: So Peter followed him out, but he was unaware that what the angel was doing was real. He thought he was only seeing a vision.
12.kjv: And he went out, and followed him; and wist not that it was true which was done by the angel; but thought he saw a vision.
12.blb: And having gone out, he was following, and he did not know that what is happening by means of the angel is real, but he was thinking he saw a vision.
12.bbe: And he went out after him; and he was not certain if what was done by the angel was a fact, for it seemed to him that he was seeing a vision.

12.msb: They passed the first and second guards and came to the iron gate leading to the city, which opened for them by itself. When they had gone outside and walked the length of one block, the angel suddenly left him.
12.kjv: When they were past the first and the second ward, they came unto the iron gate that leadeth unto the city; which opened to them of his own accord: and they went out, and passed on through one street; and forthwith the angel departed from him.
12.blb: And having passed through a first and a second guard, they came to the iron gate leading into the city, which opened to them by itself. And having gone out, they went on through one street, and immediately the angel departed from him.
12.bbe: And when they had gone past the first and second watchmen they came to the iron door into the town, which came open by itself: and they went out and down one street; and then the angel went away.

12.msb: Then Peter came to himself and said, “Now I know for sure that the Lord has sent His angel and rescued me from Herod’s grasp and from everything the Jewish people were anticipating.”
12.kjv: And when Peter was come to himself, he said, Now I know of a surety, that the Lord hath sent his angel, and hath delivered me out of the hand of Herod, and from all the expectation of the people of the Jews.
12.blb: And having come to himself, Peter said, “Now I know truly that the Lord sent forth His angel and delivered me out of the hand of Herod and of all the expectation of the people of the Jews.”
12.bbe: And when Peter came to his senses he said, Now, truly, I am certain that the Lord has sent his angel and taken me out of the hands of Herod, against all the hopes of the Jews.

12.msb: And when he had realized this, he went to the house of Mary the mother of John, also called Mark, where many people had gathered together and were praying.
12.kjv: And when he had considered the thing, he came to the house of Mary the mother of John, whose surname was Mark; where many were gathered together praying.
12.blb: And having considered, he came to the house of Mary the mother of John who is called Mark, where there were many gathered together and praying.
12.bbe: And when he became clear about this, he went to the house of Mary, the mother of John named Mark, where a number of them had come together for prayer.

12.msb: Peter knocked at the outer gate, and a servant girl named Rhoda came to answer it.
12.kjv: And as Peter knocked at the door of the gate, a damsel came to hearken, named Rhoda.
12.blb: And of him having knocked at the door of the gate, a girl named Rhoda came to answer.
12.bbe: And he gave a blow on the door, and a young girl came to it, named Rhoda.

12.msb: When she recognized Peter’s voice, she was so overjoyed that she forgot to open the gate, but ran inside and announced, “Peter is standing at the gate!”
12.kjv: And when she knew Peter’s voice, she opened not the gate for gladness, but ran in, and told how Peter stood before the gate.
12.blb: And having recognized Peter’s voice, from joy she did not open the gate, but having run in, she reported Peter to be standing before the gate.
12.bbe: And hearing the voice of Peter, in her joy she went running, without opening the door, to say that Peter was outside.

12.msb: “You are out of your mind,” they told her. But when she kept insisting it was so, they said, “It must be his angel.”
12.kjv: And they said unto her, Thou art mad. But she constantly affirmed that it was even so. Then said they, It is his angel.
12.blb: And they said to her, “You are out of your mind.” But she kept insisting it to be so. And they kept saying, “It is his angel.”
12.bbe: And they said to her, You are off your head. But still she said, with decision, that it was so. And they said, It is his angel.

12.msb: But Peter kept on knocking, and when they opened the door and saw him, they were astounded.
12.kjv: But Peter continued knocking: and when they had opened the door, and saw him, they were astonished.
12.blb: But Peter continued knocking. And having opened, they saw him and were amazed.
12.bbe: But Peter went on giving blows on the door: and when it was open and they saw him, they were full of wonder.

12.msb: Peter motioned with his hand for silence, and he described how the Lord had brought him out of the prison. “Send word to James and to the brothers,” he said, and he left for another place.
12.kjv: But he, beckoning unto them with the hand to hold their peace, declared unto them how the Lord had brought him out of the prison. And he said, Go shew these things unto James, and to the brethren. And he departed, and went into another place.
12.blb: And having motioned to them with the hand to be silent, he related to them how the Lord had brought him out of the prison. And he said, “Report these things to James and to the brothers.” And having gone out, he went to another place.
12.bbe: But he made a sign to them with his hand to be quiet, and gave them an account of how the Lord had taken him out of prison. And he said, Give the news to James and the brothers. And then he went away.

12.msb: At daybreak there was no small commotion among the soldiers as to what had become of Peter.
12.kjv: Now as soon as it was day, there was no small stir among the soldiers, what was become of Peter.
12.blb: Now day having come, there was no small disturbance among the soldiers as to what then was become of Peter.
12.bbe: Now when it was day, the armed men were greatly troubled about what had become of Peter.

12.msb: After Herod had searched for him unsuccessfully, he examined the guards and ordered that they be executed. Then he went down from Judea to Caesarea and spent some time there.
12.kjv: And when Herod had sought for him, and found him not, he examined the keepers, and commanded that they should be put to death. And he went down from Judæa to Cæsarea, and there abode.
12.blb: And Herod, having sought after him and not having found him, having examined the guards, commanded them to be led away. And having gone down from Judea to Caesarea, he stayed there.
12.bbe: And Herod, when he sent for him, and he was not there, after questioning the watchmen, gave orders that they were to be put to death. Then he went down from Judaea to Caesarea for a time.

12.msb: Now Herod was in a furious dispute with the people of Tyre and Sidon, and they convened before him. Having secured the support of Blastus, the king’s chamberlain, they asked for peace, because their region depended on the king’s country for food.
12.kjv: And Herod was highly displeased with them of Tyre and Sidon: but they came with one accord to him, and, having made Blastus the king’s chamberlain their friend, desired peace; because their country was nourished by the king’s country.
12.blb: Now he was furiously angry with the Tyrians and Sidonians, and they came to him with one accord. And having gained Blastus, who was over the bedchamber of the king, they were seeking peace because of their region being nourished by the king’s.
12.bbe: Now he was very angry with the people of Tyre and Sidon: and they came to him, all together, and having made friends with Blastus, the controller of the king's house, they made a request for peace, because their country was dependent on the king's country for its food.
12.heading: The Death of Herod

12.msb: On the appointed day, Herod donned his royal robes, sat on his throne, and addressed the people.
12.kjv: And upon a set day Herod, arrayed in royal apparel, sat upon his throne, and made an oration unto them.
12.blb: Now on the appointed day Herod, having put on royal apparel and having sat on the throne, was making an address to them.
12.bbe: And on the day which had been fixed, Herod, dressed in his robes and seated in his place, made a public statement to them.

12.msb: And they began to shout, “This is the voice of a god, not a man!”
12.kjv: And the people gave a shout, saying, It is the voice of a god, and not of a man.
12.blb: And the people were crying out, “The voice of a god and not of a man!”
12.bbe: And the people, with loud cries, said, It is the voice of a god, not of a man.

12.msb: Immediately, because Herod did not give glory to God, an angel of the Lord struck him down, and he was eaten by worms and died.
12.kjv: And immediately the angel of the Lord smote him, because he gave not God the glory: and he was eaten of worms, and gave up the ghost.
12.blb: And immediately an angel of the Lord struck him because he did not give the glory to God. And having been eaten by worms, he breathed his last.
12.bbe: And straight away the angel of the Lord sent a disease on him, because he did not give the glory to God: and his flesh was wasted away by worms, and so he came to his end.

12.msb: But the word of God continued to spread and multiply.
12.kjv: But the word of God grew and multiplied.
12.blb: But the word of God continued to grow and to multiply.
12.bbe: But the word of the Lord went on increasing.

12.msb: When Barnabas and Saul had fulfilled their mission to Jerusalem, they returned, bringing with them John, also called Mark.
12.kjv: And Barnabas and Saul returned from Jerusalem, when they had fulfilled their ministry, and took with them John, whose surname was Mark.
12.blb: And Barnabas and Saul returned, having fulfilled the ministry to Jerusalem, having taken with them John, the one having been called Mark.
12.bbe: And Barnabas and Saul came back from Jerusalem, when their work was ended, taking with them John named Mark.

13.msb: Now in the church at Antioch there were certain prophets and teachers: Barnabas, Simeon called Niger, Lucius of Cyrene, Manaen (who had been brought up with Herod the tetrarch), and Saul.
13.kjv: Now there were in the church that was at Antioch certain prophets and teachers; as Barnabas, and Simeon that was called Niger, and Lucius of Cyrene, and Manaen, which had been brought up with Herod the tetrarch, and Saul.
13.blb: Now there were prophets and teachers in Antioch being there in the church: Both Barnabas and Simeon who was called Niger, and Lucius the Cyrenian, and Manaen brought up with Herod the tetrarch, and Saul.
13.bbe: Now there were at Antioch, in the church there, prophets and teachers, Barnabas, and Symeon who was named Niger, and Lucius of Cyrene, and Manaen, a relation of Herod the king, and Saul.
13.heading: Paul’s First Missionary Journey Begins

13.msb: While they were worshiping the Lord and fasting, the Holy Spirit said, “Set apart for Me Barnabas and Saul for the work to which I have called them.”
13.kjv: As they ministered to the Lord, and fasted, the Holy Ghost said, Separate me Barnabas and Saul for the work whereunto I have called them.
13.blb: Now in their ministering to the Lord and fasting, the Holy Spirit said, “Now set apart unto Me Barnabas and Saul for the work to which I have summoned them.”
13.bbe: And while they were doing the Lord's work, and going without food, the Holy Spirit said, Let Barnabas and Saul be given to me for the special work for which they have been marked out by me.

13.msb: And after they had fasted and prayed, they laid their hands on them and sent them off.
13.kjv: And when they had fasted and prayed, and laid their hands on them, they sent them away.
13.blb: Then, having fasted and having prayed and having laid the hands on them, they sent them off.
13.bbe: Then, after prayer and going without food they put their hands on them, and sent them away.

13.msb: So Barnabas and Saul, sent forth by the Holy Spirit, went down to Seleucia and sailed from there to Cyprus.
13.kjv: So they, being sent forth by the Holy Ghost, departed unto Seleucia; and from thence they sailed to Cyprus.
13.blb: Indeed, therefore, having been sent forth by the Holy Spirit, they went down to Seleucia, and they sailed from there to Cyprus.
13.bbe: So, being sent out by the Holy Spirit, they went down to Seleucia; and from there they went by ship to Cyprus.
13.heading: On Cyprus

13.msb: When they arrived at Salamis, they proclaimed the word of God in the Jewish synagogues. And John was with them as their helper.
13.kjv: And when they were at Salamis, they preached the word of God in the synagogues of the Jews: and they had also John to their minister.
13.blb: And having come into Salamis, they began proclaiming the word of God in the synagogues of the Jews. And they also had John as a helper.
13.bbe: And at Salamis they were preaching the word of God in the Synagogues of the Jews: and John was with them, helping them.

13.msb: They traveled through the island as far as Paphos, where they found a Jewish sorcerer and false prophet named Bar-Jesus,
13.kjv: And when they had gone through the isle unto Paphos, they found a certain sorcerer, a false prophet, a Jew, whose name was Bar-jesus:
13.blb: Now having passed through the whole island as far as Paphos, they found a man—a certain a magician, a Jewish false prophet—whose name was Bar-Jesus,
13.bbe: And when they had gone through all the island to Paphos, they came across a certain wonder-worker and false prophet, a Jew whose name was Bar-Jesus;

13.msb: an attendant of the proconsul, Sergius Paulus. The proconsul, a man of intelligence, summoned Barnabas and Saul because he wanted to hear the word of God.
13.kjv: Which was with the deputy of the country, Sergius Paulus, a prudent man; who called for Barnabas and Saul, and desired to hear the word of God.
13.blb: who was with the proconsul, Sergius Paulus, an intelligent man. This man, having summoned Barnabas and Saul, desired to hear the word of God.
13.bbe: Who was with the ruler, Sergius Paulus, an able man. This man sent for Barnabas and Saul, desiring to have knowledge of the word of God.

13.msb: But Elymas the sorcerer (for that is what his name means) opposed them and tried to turn the proconsul from the faith.
13.kjv: But Elymas the sorcerer (for so is his name by interpretation) withstood them, seeking to turn away the deputy from the faith.
13.blb: But Elymas the magician (for his name is translated thus) was opposing them, seeking to turn away the proconsul from the faith.
13.bbe: But Elymas, the wonder-worker (for that is the sense of his name), put himself against them, with the purpose of turning the ruler from the faith.

13.msb: Then Saul, who was also called Paul, filled with the Holy Spirit, looked directly at Elymas
13.kjv: Then Saul, (who also is called Paul,) filled with the Holy Ghost, set his eyes on him,
13.blb: And Saul, the one also called Paul, having been filled with the Holy Spirit, having looked intently upon him,
13.bbe: But Saul, whose other name is Paul, being full of the Holy Spirit, looking hard at him, said,

13.msb: and said, “O child of the devil and enemy of all righteousness, you are full of all kinds of deceit and trickery! Will you never stop perverting the straight ways of the Lord?
13.kjv: And said, O full of all subtilty and all mischief, thou child of the devil, thou enemy of all righteousness, wilt thou not cease to pervert the right ways of the Lord?
13.blb: said, “O full of all deceit and all craftiness, son of the devil, enemy of all righteousness, will you not cease perverting the straight ways of the Lord?
13.bbe: O you, who are full of false tricks and evil ways, a son of the Evil One, hating all righteousness, will you for ever be turning people from the right ways of the Lord?

13.msb: Now look, the hand of the Lord is against you, and for a time you will be blind and unable to see the light of the sun.” Immediately mist and darkness fell over him, and he groped about, seeking someone to lead him by the hand.
13.kjv: And now, behold, the hand of the Lord is upon thee, and thou shalt be blind, not seeing the sun for a season. And immediately there fell on him a mist and a darkness; and he went about seeking some to lead him by the hand.
13.blb: And now behold, the hand of the Lord is upon you, and you will be blind, not seeing the sun for a season.” And immediately mist and darkness fell upon him, and going about, he was seeking someone to lead him by the hand.
13.bbe: And now, see, the hand of the Lord is on you, and you will be blind and not able to see the sun for a time. And straight away a dark mist came down on him; and he went about looking for a guide.

13.msb: When the proconsul saw what had happened, he believed, for he was astonished at the teaching about the Lord.
13.kjv: Then the deputy, when he saw what was done, believed, being astonished at the doctrine of the Lord.
13.blb: Then the proconsul, having seen that having happened, believed, being astonished at the teaching of the Lord.
13.bbe: Then the ruler, when he saw what was done, had faith, being full of wonder at the teaching of the Lord.

13.msb: After setting sail from Paphos, Paul and his companions came to Perga in Pamphylia, where John left them to return to Jerusalem.
13.kjv: Now when Paul and his company loosed from Paphos, they came to Perga in Pamphylia: and John departing from them returned to Jerusalem.
13.blb: And those around Paul, having sailed from Paphos, came to Perga of Pamphylia. But John, having departed from them, returned to Jerusalem.
13.bbe: Then Paul and those who were with him went by ship from Paphos and came to Perga in Pamphylia: and there John went away from them and came back to Jerusalem.
13.heading: In Pisidian Antioch

13.msb: And from Perga, they traveled inland to Pisidian Antioch, where they entered the synagogue on the Sabbath and sat down.
13.kjv: But when they departed from Perga, they came to Antioch in Pisidia, and went into the synagogue on the sabbath day, and sat down.
13.blb: Now having passed through from Perga, they came to Antioch of Pisidia, and having gone into the synagogue on the day of the Sabbaths, they sat down.
13.bbe: But they, going through from Perga, came to Antioch in Pisidia; and they went into the Synagogue on the Sabbath and were seated.

13.msb: After the reading from the Law and the Prophets, the synagogue leaders sent word to them: “Brothers, if you have a word of encouragement for the people, please speak.”
13.kjv: And after the reading of the law and the prophets the rulers of the synagogue sent unto them, saying, Ye men and brethren, if ye have any word of exhortation for the people, say on.
13.blb: And after the reading of the Law and of the Prophets, the synagogue rulers sent to them, saying, “Men, brothers, if there is any word of exhortation among you toward the people, speak.”
13.bbe: And after the reading of the law and the prophets, the rulers of the Synagogue sent to them, saying, Brothers, if you have a word of comfort for the people, say on.

13.msb: Paul stood up, motioned with his hand, and began to speak: “Men of Israel and you Gentiles who fear God, listen to me!
13.kjv: Then Paul stood up, and beckoning with his hand said, Men of Israel, and ye that fear God, give audience.
13.blb: And Paul, having risen up and having motioned with the hand, said, “Men, Israelites, and those fearing God, listen:
13.bbe: And Paul, getting up and making a sign with his hand, said, Men of Israel, and you who have the fear of God, give ear.

13.msb: The God of the people chose our fathers. He made them into a great people during their stay in Egypt, and with an uplifted arm He led them out of that land.
13.kjv: The God of this people of Israel chose our fathers, and exalted the people when they dwelt as strangers in the land of Egypt, and with an high arm brought he them out of it.
13.blb: The God of this people Israel chose our fathers and exalted the people in the sojourn in the land of Egypt, and with uplifted arm He brought them out of it,
13.bbe: The God of this people Israel made selection of our fathers, lifting the people up from their low condition when they were living in the land of Egypt, and with a strong arm took them out of it.

13.msb: He endured their conduct for about forty years in the wilderness.
13.kjv: And about the time of forty years suffered he their manners in the wilderness.
13.blb: and for a period of about forty years He endured their ways in the wilderness,
13.bbe: And for about forty years he put up with their ways in the waste land.

13.msb: And having vanquished seven nations in Canaan, He gave their land to His people as their inheritance.
13.kjv: And when he had destroyed seven nations in the land of Chanaan, he divided their land to them by lot.
13.blb: and having destroyed seven nations in the land of Canaan, He gave as an inheritance their land—
13.bbe: And having put to destruction seven nations in the land of Canaan, he gave them the land for their heritage for about four hundred and fifty years.

13.msb: All this took about 450 years. After this, God gave them judges until the time of Samuel the prophet.
13.kjv: And after that he gave unto them judges about the space of four hundred and fifty years, until Samuel the prophet.
13.blb: in about four hundred and fifty years. And after these things, He gave them judges until Samuel the prophet.
13.bbe: And after these things he gave them judges, till the time of Samuel the prophet.

13.msb: Then the people asked for a king, and God gave them Saul son of Kish, from the tribe of Benjamin, who ruled forty years.
13.kjv: And afterward they desired a king: and God gave unto them Saul the son of Cis, a man of the tribe of Benjamin, by the space of forty years.
13.blb: Then they asked for a king, and God gave to them Saul son of Kish, a man of the tribe of Benjamin, forty years.
13.bbe: Then at their request for a king, God gave them Saul, the son of Kish, a man of the family of Benjamin, who was their king for forty years.

13.msb: After removing Saul, He raised up David as their king and testified about him: ‘I have found David son of Jesse a man after My own heart; he will carry out My will in its entirety.’
13.kjv: And when he had removed him, he raised up unto them David to be their king; to whom also he gave testimony, and said, I have found David the son of Jesse, a man after mine own heart, which shall fulfil all my will.
13.blb: And having removed him, He raised up David to them as king, to whom He also said, having testified: ‘I have found David the son of Jesse a man according to My heart, who will do all My will.’
13.bbe: And having put him on one side, he made David their king, to whom he gave witness, saying, I have taken David, the son of Jesse, a man dear to my heart, who will do all my pleasure.

13.msb: From the descendants of this man, God has brought to Israel salvation, as He promised.
13.kjv: Of this man’s seed hath God according to his promise raised unto Israel a Saviour, Jesus:
13.blb: Of the seed of this man, according to promise, God brought to Israel a Savior, Jesus—
13.bbe: From this man's seed has God given to Israel a Saviour, even Jesus, as he gave his word;

13.msb: Before the arrival of Jesus, John preached a baptism of repentance to Israel.
13.kjv: When John had first preached before his coming the baptism of repentance to all the people of Israel.
13.blb: John having proclaimed before the face of His coming a baptism of repentance to all the people of Israel.
13.bbe: For whose coming John made ready the way by preaching to all the people of Israel the baptism which goes with a change of heart.

13.msb: As John was completing his course, he said, ‘Who do you suppose I am? I am not that One. But there is One coming after me whose sandals I am not worthy to untie.’
13.kjv: And as John fulfilled his course, he said, Whom think ye that I am? I am not he. But, behold, there cometh one after me, whose shoes of his feet I am not worthy to loose.
13.blb: And as John was fulfilling the course, he was saying, ‘Whom do you suppose me to be? I am not He, but behold, He comes after me of whom I am not worthy to untie a sandal of the feet.’
13.bbe: And when John was completing his work, he said, What do I seem to you to be? I am not he; but one is coming after me, whose shoes I am not good enough to undo.

13.msb: Brothers, children of Abraham, and you Gentiles who fear God, it is to you that this message of salvation has been sent.
13.kjv: Men and brethren, children of the stock of Abraham, and whosoever among you feareth God, to you is the word of this salvation sent.
13.blb: Men, brothers, sons of the family of Abraham, and those among you fearing God, to us the message of this salvation was sent forth.
13.bbe: My brothers, children of the family of Abraham, and those among you who have the fear of God, to us the word of this salvation is sent.

13.msb: The people of Jerusalem and their rulers did not recognize Jesus, yet in condemning Him they fulfilled the words of the prophets that are read every Sabbath.
13.kjv: For they that dwell at Jerusalem, and their rulers, because they knew him not, nor yet the voices of the prophets which are read every sabbath day, they have fulfilled them in condemning him.
13.blb: For those dwelling in Jerusalem and their rulers, not having known Him and the voices of the prophets that are being read on every Sabbath, having condemned Him, they fulfilled them.
13.bbe: For the men of Jerusalem and their rulers, having no knowledge of him, or of the sayings of the prophets which come to their ears every Sabbath day, gave effect to them by judging him.

13.msb: And though they found no ground for a death sentence, they asked Pilate to have Him executed.
13.kjv: And though they found no cause of death in him, yet desired they Pilate that he should be slain.
13.blb: And having found no cause of death, they begged Pilate to put Him to death.
13.bbe: And though no cause of death was seen in him, they made a request to Pilate that he might be put to death.

13.msb: When they had carried out all that was written about Him, they took Him down from the tree and laid Him in a tomb.
13.kjv: And when they had fulfilled all that was written of him, they took him down from the tree, and laid him in a sepulchre.
13.blb: And when they finished all the things having been written about Him, having taken Him down from the tree, they put Him in a tomb.
13.bbe: And when they had done all the things said in the Writings about him, they took him down from the tree, and put him in the place of the dead.

13.msb: But God raised Him from the dead,
13.kjv: But God raised him from the dead:
13.blb: But God raised Him out from the dead,
13.bbe: But God gave him back from the dead:

13.msb: and for many days He was seen by those who had accompanied Him from Galilee to Jerusalem. They are His witnesses to our people.
13.kjv: And he was seen many days of them which came up with him from Galilee to Jerusalem, who are his witnesses unto the people.
13.blb: who appeared for many days to those having come up with Him from Galilee to Jerusalem, who are now His witnesses to the people.
13.bbe: And for a number of days he was seen by those who came with him from Galilee to Jerusalem, who are now his witnesses before the people.

13.msb: And now we proclaim to you the good news: What God promised our fathers
13.kjv: And we declare unto you glad tidings, how that the promise which was made unto the fathers,
13.blb: And we preach the gospel to you, the promise having been made to the fathers,
13.bbe: And we are giving you the good news of the undertaking made to the fathers,

13.msb: He has fulfilled for us, their children, by raising up Jesus. As it is written in the second Psalm: ‘You are My Son; today I have become Your Father.’
13.kjv: God hath fulfilled the same unto us their children, in that he hath raised up Jesus again; as it is also written in the second psalm, Thou art my Son, this day have I begotten thee.
13.blb: that God has fulfilled this to us their children, having raised up Jesus, as it has also been written in the second psalm: ‘You are My Son; today I have begotten You.’
13.bbe: Which God has now put into effect for our children, by sending Jesus; as it says in the second Psalm, You are my Son; this day I have given you being.

13.msb: In fact, God raised Him from the dead, never to see decay. As He has said: ‘I will give you the holy and sure blessings promised to David.’
13.kjv: And as concerning that he raised him up from the dead, now no more to return to corruption, he said on this wise, I will give you the sure mercies of David.
13.blb: And that He raised Him out from the dead, no more being about to return to decay, He spoke thus: ‘I will give to you the holy blessings, the faithful ones, of David.’
13.bbe: And about his coming back from the dead, never again to go to destruction, he has said these words, I will give you the holy and certain mercies of David.

13.msb: So also, He says in another Psalm: ‘You will not let Your Holy One see decay.’
13.kjv: Wherefore he saith also in another psalm, Thou shalt not suffer thine Holy One to see corruption.
13.blb: So also, He says in another place: ‘You will not allow Your Holy One to see decay.’
13.bbe: Because he says in another Psalm, You will not let your Holy One see destruction.

13.msb: For when David had served God’s purpose in his own generation, he fell asleep. His body was buried with his fathers and saw decay.
13.kjv: For David, after he had served his own generation by the will of God, fell on sleep, and was laid unto his fathers, and saw corruption:
13.blb: For indeed David, having served the purpose of God in his own generation, fell asleep and was added to his fathers, and he saw decay.
13.bbe: Now David, having done God's work for his generation, went to sleep, and was put with his fathers, and his body came to destruction:

13.msb: But the One whom God raised from the dead did not see decay.
13.kjv: But he, whom God raised again, saw no corruption.
13.blb: But the One God raised up did not see decay.
13.bbe: But he, who was lifted up by God, did not see destruction.

13.msb: Therefore let it be known to you, brothers, that through Jesus the forgiveness of sins is proclaimed to you.
13.kjv: Be it known unto you therefore, men and brethren, that through this man is preached unto you the forgiveness of sins:
13.blb: Therefore be it known to you, men, brothers, that through this One forgiveness of sins is proclaimed to you.
13.bbe: And so, let it be clear to you, my brothers, that through this man forgiveness of sins is offered to you:

13.msb: Through Him everyone who believes is justified from everything from which you could not be justified by the law of Moses.
13.kjv: And by him all that believe are justified from all things, from which ye could not be justified by the law of Moses.
13.blb: And in Him everyone believing is justified from all things from which you were not able to be justified in the law of Moses.
13.bbe: And through him everyone who has faith is made free from all those things, from which the law of Moses was not able to make you free.

13.msb: Watch out, then, that what was spoken by the prophets does not happen to you:
13.kjv: Beware therefore, lest that come upon you, which is spoken of in the prophets;
13.blb: Take heed, therefore, lest that having been said in the prophets might come about:
13.bbe: So take care that these words of the prophets do not come true for you;

13.msb: ‘Look, you scoffers, wonder and perish! For I am doing a work in your days that you would never believe, even if someone told you.’”
13.kjv: Behold, ye despisers, and wonder, and perish: for I work a work in your days, a work which ye shall in no wise believe, though a man declare it unto you.
13.blb: ‘Behold, scoffers, and wonder and perish; for I am working a work in your days, a work that you would never believe, even if one should declare it to you.’”
13.bbe: See, you doubters, have wonder and come to your end; for I will do a thing in your days to which you will not give belief, even if it is made clear to you.

13.msb: As the Jews were leaving the synagogue, the Gentiles urged Paul and Barnabas to continue this message on the next Sabbath.
13.kjv: And when the Jews were gone out of the synagogue, the Gentiles besought that these words might be preached to them the next sabbath.
13.blb: And on their having departed, they were begging these words to be spoken to them on the next Sabbath.
13.bbe: And when they went out, they made a request that these words might be said to them again on the Sabbath after.
13.heading: A Light for the Gentiles

13.msb: After the synagogue was dismissed, many of the Jews and devout converts to Judaism followed Paul and Barnabas, who spoke to them and urged them to continue in the grace of God.
13.kjv: Now when the congregation was broken up, many of the Jews and religious proselytes followed Paul and Barnabas: who, speaking to them, persuaded them to continue in the grace of God.
13.blb: And the synagogue having been dismissed, many of the Jews and worshiping converts followed Paul and Barnabas, who, speaking to them, kept persuading them to continue in the grace of God.
13.bbe: Now when the meeting was ended, a number of the Jews and of the God-fearing Gentiles who had become Jews, went after Paul and Barnabas: who put before them how important it was to keep on in the grace of God.

13.msb: On the following Sabbath, nearly the whole city gathered to hear the word of God.
13.kjv: And the next sabbath day came almost the whole city together to hear the word of God.
13.blb: And on the coming Sabbath, almost all the city was gathered together to hear the word of the Lord.
13.bbe: And on the Sabbath after, almost all the town came together to give hearing to the word of God.

13.msb: But when the Jews saw the crowds, they were filled with jealousy, and they blasphemously opposed and contradicted what Paul was saying.
13.kjv: But when the Jews saw the multitudes, they were filled with envy, and spake against those things which were spoken by Paul, contradicting and blaspheming.
13.blb: But the Jews, having seen the crowds, were filled with jealousy, and they began contradicting the things spoken by Paul, blaspheming.
13.bbe: But when the Jews saw such a great number of people, they were full of envy and said evil words against Paul's preaching.

13.msb: Then Paul and Barnabas answered them boldly: “It was necessary to speak the word of God to you first. But since you reject it and do not consider yourselves worthy of eternal life, we now turn to the Gentiles.
13.kjv: Then Paul and Barnabas waxed bold, and said, It was necessary that the word of God should first have been spoken to you: but seeing ye put it from you, and judge yourselves unworthy of everlasting life, lo, we turn to the Gentiles.
13.blb: And Paul and Barnabas, having spoken boldly, said, “It was necessary for the word of God to be spoken first to you. But since you thrust it away and do not judge yourselves worthy of eternal life, behold, we are turning to the Gentiles.
13.bbe: Then Paul and Barnabas without fear said, It was necessary for the word of God to be given to you first; but because you will have nothing to do with it, and have no desire for eternal life, it will now be offered to the Gentiles.

13.msb: For this is what the Lord has commanded us: ‘I have made you a light for the Gentiles, to bring salvation to the ends of the earth.’”
13.kjv: For so hath the Lord commanded us, saying, I have set thee to be a light of the Gentiles, that thou shouldest be for salvation unto the ends of the earth.
13.blb: For thus the Lord has commanded us: ‘I have placed you as a light for the Gentiles, that you may be for salvation to the end of the earth.’”
13.bbe: For so the Lord has given us orders, saying, I have given you for a light to the Gentiles so that you may be for salvation to the ends of the earth.

13.msb: When the Gentiles heard this, they rejoiced and glorified the word of the Lord, and all who were appointed for eternal life believed.
13.kjv: And when the Gentiles heard this, they were glad, and glorified the word of the Lord: and as many as were ordained to eternal life believed.
13.blb: And the Gentiles hearing were rejoicing and glorifying the word of the Lord, and as many as were appointed to eternal life believed.
13.bbe: And the Gentiles, hearing this, were glad and gave glory to the word of God: and those marked out by God for eternal life had faith.

13.msb: And the word of the Lord spread throughout that region.
13.kjv: And the word of the Lord was published throughout all the region.
13.blb: And the word of the Lord was carried through the whole region.
13.bbe: And the word of the Lord went through all the country.

13.msb: The Jews, however, incited the religious women of prominence and the leading men of the city. They stirred up persecution against Paul and Barnabas and drove them out of their district.
13.kjv: But the Jews stirred up the devout and honourable women, and the chief men of the city, and raised persecution against Paul and Barnabas, and expelled them out of their coasts.
13.blb: But the Jews incited the worshiping women of honorable position and the principals of the city, and they stirred up a persecution against Paul and Barnabas and expelled them from their district.
13.bbe: But the Jews, working up the feelings of the God-fearing women of high position and of the chief men of the town, got an attack started against Paul and Barnabas, driving them out of those parts.

13.msb: So they shook the dust off their feet in protest against them and went to Iconium.
13.kjv: But they shook off the dust of their feet against them, and came unto Iconium.
13.blb: And having shaken off the dust of the feet against them, they went to Iconium.
13.bbe: But they, shaking off the dust of that place from their feet, came to Iconium.

13.msb: And the disciples were filled with joy and with the Holy Spirit.
13.kjv: And the disciples were filled with joy, and with the Holy Ghost.
13.blb: And the disciples were filled with joy and the Holy Spirit.
13.bbe: And the disciples were full of joy and of the Holy Spirit.

14.msb: At Iconium, Paul and Barnabas went as usual into the Jewish synagogue, where they spoke so well that a great number of Jews and Greeks believed.
14.kjv: And it came to pass in Iconium, that they went both together into the synagogue of the Jews, and so spake, that a great multitude both of the Jews and also of the Greeks believed.
14.blb: Now it came to pass in Iconium, according to the same, that they entered into the synagogue of the Jews and spoke so that a large number of both Jews and Greeks believed.
14.bbe: Now in Iconium they went together to the Synagogue of the Jews and gave such teaching that a great number of Jews and Greeks had faith.
14.heading: Paul and Barnabas at Iconium

14.msb: But the unbelieving Jews stirred up the Gentiles and poisoned their minds against the brothers.
14.kjv: But the unbelieving Jews stirred up the Gentiles, and made their minds evil affected against the brethren.
14.blb: But the unbelieving Jews stirred up and poisoned the minds of the Gentiles against the brothers.
14.bbe: But those Jews who had not the faith, made the minds of the Gentiles bitter against the brothers.

14.msb: So Paul and Barnabas spent considerable time there, speaking boldly for the Lord, who affirmed the message of His grace by enabling them to perform signs and wonders.
14.kjv: Long time therefore abode they speaking boldly in the Lord, which gave testimony unto the word of his grace, and granted signs and wonders to be done by their hands.
14.blb: Therefore indeed they stayed a long time, speaking boldly for the Lord, testifying to the word of His grace, granting signs and wonders to be done through their hands.
14.bbe: So they kept there for a long time, taking heart in the Lord, who gave witness to the word of his grace by causing signs and wonders to be done by their hands.

14.msb: The people of the city were divided. Some sided with the Jews, and others with the apostles.
14.kjv: But the multitude of the city was divided: and part held with the Jews, and part with the apostles.
14.blb: Now the multitude of the city was divided, and indeed some were with the Jews, but some with the apostles.
14.bbe: But there was a division among the people of the town; some were on the side of the Jews and some on the side of the Apostles.

14.msb: But when the Gentiles and Jews, together with their rulers, set out to mistreat and stone them,
14.kjv: And when there was an assault made both of the Gentiles, and also of the Jews with their rulers, to use them despitefully, and to stone them,
14.blb: And when there was a rush of both the Gentiles and Jews, with their rulers, to mistreat and to stone them,
14.bbe: And when a violent attempt was made by the Gentiles and the Jews, with their rulers, to make an attack on them and have them stoned,

14.msb: they found out about it and fled to the Lycaonian cities of Lystra and Derbe and to the surrounding region,
14.kjv: They were ware of it, and fled unto Lystra and Derbe, cities of Lycaonia, and unto the region that lieth round about:
14.blb: having become aware, they fled to the Lycaonian cities Lystra and Derbe, and the surrounding region,
14.bbe: Having got news of it, they went in flight to the towns of Lycaonia, Lystra, and Derbe, and the country round about:

14.msb: where they continued to preach the gospel.
14.kjv: And there they preached the gospel.
14.blb: and there they continued preaching the gospel.
14.bbe: And went on preaching the good news there.

14.msb: In Lystra there sat a man crippled in his feet, who was lame from birth and had never walked.
14.kjv: And there sat a certain man at Lystra, impotent in his feet, being a cripple from his mother’s womb, who never had walked:
14.blb: And in Lystra a certain man was sitting, crippled in the feet, lame from the womb of his mother, who had never walked.
14.bbe: And at Lystra there was a certain man, who from birth had been without the use of his feet, never having had the power of walking.
14.heading: The Visit to Lystra and Derbe

14.msb: This man was listening to the words of Paul, who looked intently at him and saw that he had faith to be healed.
14.kjv: The same heard Paul speak: who stedfastly beholding him, and perceiving that he had faith to be healed,
14.blb: This man heard Paul speaking, who, having looked intently at him and having seen that he has faith to be healed,
14.bbe: This man was giving ear to the preaching of Paul, who, looking at him, and seeing that he had faith to be made well,

14.msb: In a loud voice Paul called out, “Stand up on your feet!” And the man jumped up and began to walk.
14.kjv: Said with a loud voice, Stand upright on thy feet. And he leaped and walked.
14.blb: said in a loud voice, “Stand upright on your feet!” And he sprang up and began to walk.
14.bbe: Said in a loud voice, Get up on your feet. And, jumping up, he went walking about.

14.msb: When the crowds saw what Paul had done, they lifted up their voices in the Lycaonian language: “The gods have come down to us in human form!”
14.kjv: And when the people saw what Paul had done, they lifted up their voices, saying in the speech of Lycaonia, The gods are come down to us in the likeness of men.
14.blb: And the crowds, having seen what Paul had done, lifted up their voice in Lycaonian, saying, “The gods have come down to us, having become like men!”
14.bbe: And when the people saw what Paul had done, they said in a loud voice, in the language of Lycaonia, The gods have come down to us in the form of men.

14.msb: Barnabas they called Zeus, and Paul they called Hermes, because he was the chief speaker.
14.kjv: And they called Barnabas, Jupiter; and Paul, Mercurius, because he was the chief speaker.
14.blb: And Barnabas they began calling Zeus; and Paul, Hermes, because he was the leading speaker.
14.bbe: And they gave the name of Jupiter to Barnabas, and to Paul that of Mercury, because he was the chief talker.

14.msb: The priest of Zeus, whose temple was just outside their city, brought bulls and wreaths to the city gates, hoping to offer a sacrifice along with the crowds.
14.kjv: Then the priest of Jupiter, which was before their city, brought oxen and garlands unto the gates, and would have done sacrifice with the people.
14.blb: And the priest of Zeus, being just outside the city, having brought oxen and wreaths to the gates, was desiring with the crowds to sacrifice.
14.bbe: And the priest of the image of Jupiter, which was before the town, took oxen and flowers to the doors of the town, and was about to make an offering with the people.

14.msb: But when the apostles Barnabas and Paul found out about this, they tore their clothes and rushed into the crowd, shouting,
14.kjv: Which when the apostles, Barnabas and Paul, heard of, they rent their clothes, and ran in among the people, crying out,
14.blb: But the apostles Barnabas and Paul, having heard, having torn their garments, rushed out into the crowd, crying out
14.bbe: But when this came to the ears of the Apostles, Paul and Barnabas, they went running out among the people, parting their clothing, and crying out,

14.msb: “Men, why are you doing this? We too are only men, human like you. We are bringing you good news that you should turn from these worthless things to the living God, who made heaven and earth and sea and everything in them.
14.kjv: And saying, Sirs, why do ye these things? We also are men of like passions with you, and preach unto you that ye should turn from these vanities unto the living God, which made heaven, and earth, and the sea, and all things that are therein:
14.blb: and saying, “Men, why do you do these things? We also are men of like nature with you, proclaiming the gospel to you to turn from these vain things to the living God, who made the heaven and the earth and the sea and all the things in them,
14.bbe: Good people, why are you doing these things? We are men with the same feelings as you, and we give you the good news so that you may be turned away from these foolish things to the living God, who made the heaven and the earth and the sea and all things in them:

14.msb: In past generations, He let all nations go their own way.
14.kjv: Who in times past suffered all nations to walk in their own ways.
14.blb: who in the generations past allowed all the nations to go their ways.
14.bbe: Who in the past let all nations go in the ways which seemed good to them.

14.msb: Yet He has not left Himself without testimony to His goodness: He gives you rain from heaven and fruitful seasons, filling our hearts with food and gladness.”
14.kjv: Nevertheless he left not himself without witness, in that he did good, and gave us rain from heaven, and fruitful seasons, filling our hearts with food and gladness.
14.blb: And yet He did not leave Himself without witness, doing good, giving to you rains from heaven and fruitful seasons, filling your hearts with food and gladness.”
14.bbe: But he was not without witness, because he did good, and gave you rain from heaven and times of fruit, making your hearts full of food and joy.

14.msb: Even with these words, Paul and Barnabas could hardly stop the crowds from sacrificing to them.
14.kjv: And with these sayings scarce restrained they the people, that they had not done sacrifice unto them.
14.blb: Even saying these things, they hardly stopped the crowds from sacrificing to them.
14.bbe: And even with these words, it was hard for them to keep the people from making an offering to them.

14.msb: Then some Jews arrived from Antioch and Iconium and won over the crowds. They stoned Paul and dragged him outside the city, presuming he was dead.
14.kjv: And there came thither certain Jews from Antioch and Iconium, who persuaded the people, and, having stoned Paul, drew him out of the city, supposing he had been dead.
14.blb: But Jews came from Antioch and Iconium, and having persuaded the crowds, and having stoned Paul, they dragged him outside the city, supposing him to have died.
14.bbe: But some Jews came to that place from Antioch and Iconium, and got control over the people; and after stoning Paul, they had him pulled out of the town, taking him for dead.

14.msb: But after the disciples had gathered around him, he got up and went back into the city. And the next day he left with Barnabas for Derbe.
14.kjv: Howbeit, as the disciples stood round about him, he rose up, and came into the city: and the next day he departed with Barnabas to Derbe.
14.blb: But the disciples having surrounded him, having risen up, he entered into the city. And on the next day he went out with Barnabas to Derbe.
14.bbe: But when the disciples came round him, he got up and went into the town: and the day after he went away with Barnabas to Derbe.

14.msb: They preached the gospel to that city and made many disciples. Then they returned to Lystra, Iconium, and Antioch,
14.kjv: And when they had preached the gospel to that city, and had taught many, they returned again to Lystra, and to Iconium, and Antioch,
14.blb: And having proclaimed the gospel to that city and having discipled many, they returned to Lystra and to Iconium and to Antioch,
14.bbe: And having made a number of disciples through the preaching of the good news in that town, they went back to Lystra and Iconium and Antioch,
14.heading: Strengthening the Disciples

14.msb: strengthening the souls of the disciples and encouraging them to continue in the faith. “We must endure many hardships to enter the kingdom of God,” they said.
14.kjv: Confirming the souls of the disciples, and exhorting them to continue in the faith, and that we must through much tribulation enter into the kingdom of God.
14.blb: strengthening the souls of the disciples, exhorting them to continue in the faith and that “through many tribulations it is necessary for us to enter into the kingdom of God.”
14.bbe: Making strong the souls of the disciples, saying to them that they were to keep the faith, and that we have to go through troubles of all sorts to come into the kingdom of God.

14.msb: Paul and Barnabas appointed elders for them in each church, praying and fasting as they entrusted them to the Lord, in whom they had believed.
14.kjv: And when they had ordained them elders in every church, and had prayed with fasting, they commended them to the Lord, on whom they believed.
14.blb: And having appointed elders for them in every church, having prayed, with fasting they committed them to the Lord, in whom they had believed.
14.bbe: And when they had made selection of some to be rulers in every church, and had given themselves to prayer and kept themselves from food, they put them into the care of the Lord in whom they had faith.

14.msb: After passing through Pisidia, they came to Pamphylia.
14.kjv: And after they had passed throughout Pisidia, they came to Pamphylia.
14.blb: And having passed through Pisidia, they came to Pamphylia,
14.bbe: And they went through Pisidia and came to Pamphylia.

14.msb: And when they had spoken the word in Perga, they went down to Attalia.
14.kjv: And when they had preached the word in Perga, they went down into Attalia:
14.blb: and having spoken the word in Perga, they went down to Attalia.
14.bbe: And, after preaching the word in Perga, they went down to Attalia;

14.msb: From Attalia they sailed to Antioch, where they had been commended to the grace of God for the work they had just completed.
14.kjv: And thence sailed to Antioch, from whence they had been recommended to the grace of God for the work which they fulfilled.
14.blb: And from there they sailed to Antioch, from where they had been committed to the grace of God for the work that they had fulfilled.
14.bbe: And from there they went by ship to Antioch, where they had been handed over to the grace of God for the work which they had not done.

14.msb: When they arrived, they gathered the church together and reported all that God had done through them, and how He had opened the door of faith to the Gentiles.
14.kjv: And when they were come, and had gathered the church together, they rehearsed all that God had done with them, and how he had opened the door of faith unto the Gentiles.
14.blb: And having arrived and having gathered together the church, they began declaring all that God had done with them, and that He had opened a door of faith to the Gentiles.
14.bbe: And when they came there, and had got the church together, they gave them an account of all the things which God had done through them, and how he had made open a door of faith to the Gentiles.

14.msb: And they spent a long time there with the disciples.
14.kjv: And there they abode long time with the disciples.
14.blb: And they remained no little time with the disciples.
14.bbe: And they were with the disciples there for a long time.

15.msb: Then some men came down from Judea and were teaching the brothers, “Unless you are circumcised according to the custom of Moses, you cannot be saved.”
15.kjv: And certain men which came down from Judæa taught the brethren, and said, Except ye be circumcised after the manner of Moses, ye cannot be saved.
15.blb: But certain ones having come down from Judea were teaching the brothers, “Unless you are circumcised according to the custom of Moses, you are not able to be saved.”
15.bbe: Now certain men came down from Judaea, teaching the brothers and saying that without circumcision, after the rule of Moses, there is no salvation.
15.heading: The Dispute over Circumcision

15.msb: Therefore after engaging these men in sharp debate, Paul and Barnabas were appointed, along with some other believers, to go up to Jerusalem to see the apostles and elders about this question.
15.kjv: When therefore Paul and Barnabas had no small dissension and disputation with them, they determined that Paul and Barnabas, and certain other of them, should go up to Jerusalem unto the apostles and elders about this question.
15.blb: There having been, then, no small commotion and discussion by Paul and Barnabas with them, they appointed Paul and Barnabas and certain others out of them to go up to Jerusalem, to the apostles and elders, about this question.
15.bbe: And after Paul and Barnabas had had no little argument and discussion with them, the brothers made a decision to send Paul and Barnabas and certain others of them to the Apostles and the rulers of the church at Jerusalem about this question.

15.msb: Sent on their way by the church, they passed through Phoenicia and Samaria, recounting the conversion of the Gentiles and bringing great joy to all the brothers.
15.kjv: And being brought on their way by the church, they passed through Phenice and Samaria, declaring the conversion of the Gentiles: and they caused great joy unto all the brethren.
15.blb: Therefore indeed, having been sent forward by the church, they were passing through both Phoenicia and Samaria, relating in detail the conversion of the Gentiles, and they were bringing great joy to all the brothers.
15.bbe: So they, being sent on their way by the church, went through Phoenicia and Samaria, giving news of the salvation of the Gentiles, to the great joy of all the brothers.

15.msb: On their arrival in Jerusalem, they were welcomed by the church and apostles and elders, to whom they reported all that God had done through them.
15.kjv: And when they were come to Jerusalem, they were received of the church, and of the apostles and elders, and they declared all things that God had done with them.
15.blb: And having come to Jerusalem, they were welcomed by the church and the apostles and the elders. And they declared all that God had done with them.
15.bbe: And when they came to Jerusalem, they had a meeting with the church and the Apostles and the rulers, and they gave an account of all the things which God had done through them.

15.msb: But some believers from the party of the Pharisees stood up and declared, “The Gentiles must be circumcised and required to obey the law of Moses.”
15.kjv: But there rose up certain of the sect of the Pharisees which believed, saying, That it was needful to circumcise them, and to command them to keep the law of Moses.
15.blb: Now certain ones of those who believed from the sect of the Pharisees rose up, saying, “It is necessary to circumcise them, and to command them to keep the law of Moses.”
15.bbe: But some of the Pharisees, who were of the faith, got up and said, It is necessary for these to have circumcision and to keep the law of Moses.
15.heading: The Council at Jerusalem

15.msb: So the apostles and elders met to look into this matter.
15.kjv: And the apostles and elders came together for to consider of this matter.
15.blb: And the apostles and the elders were gathered together to see about this matter.
15.bbe: And the Apostles and the rulers of the church came together and gave thought to the question.

15.msb: After much debate, Peter got up and said to them, “Brothers, you know that in the early days God made a choice among us that the Gentiles would hear from my lips the message of the gospel and believe.
15.kjv: And when there had been much disputing, Peter rose up, and said unto them, Men and brethren, ye know how that a good while ago God made choice among us, that the Gentiles by my mouth should hear the word of the gospel, and believe.
15.blb: And much discussion having taken place, Peter having risen up, said to them, “Men, brothers, you know that from early days God chose among you for the Gentiles to hear by my mouth the word of the gospel, and to believe.
15.bbe: And when there had been much discussion, Peter got up and said to them, My brothers, you have knowledge that some time back it was God's pleasure that by my mouth the good news might be given to the Gentiles so that they might have faith.

15.msb: And God, who knows the heart, showed His approval by giving the Holy Spirit to them, just as He did to us.
15.kjv: And God, which knoweth the hearts, bare them witness, giving them the Holy Ghost, even as he did unto us;
15.blb: And the heart-knowing God testified to them, having given them the Holy Spirit, as also to us.
15.bbe: And God, the searcher of hearts, was a witness to them, giving them the Holy Spirit even as he did to us;

15.msb: He made no distinction between us and them, for He cleansed their hearts by faith.
15.kjv: And put no difference between us and them, purifying their hearts by faith.
15.blb: And He made no distinction between both us and them, having purified their hearts by faith.
15.bbe: Making no division between them and us, but making clean their hearts by faith.

15.msb: Now then, why do you test God by placing on the necks of the disciples a yoke that neither we nor our fathers have been able to bear?
15.kjv: Now therefore why tempt ye God, to put a yoke upon the neck of the disciples, which neither our fathers nor we were able to bear?
15.blb: Now, therefore, why are you testing God, putting upon the neck of the disciples a yoke that neither our fathers nor we have been able to bear?
15.bbe: Why then are you testing God, by putting on the neck of the disciples a yoke so hard that not even our fathers or we were strong enough for it?

15.msb: On the contrary, we believe it is through the grace of the Lord Jesus that we are saved, just as they are.”
15.kjv: But we believe that through the grace of the Lord Jesus Christ we shall be saved, even as they.
15.blb: But we believe to be saved through the grace of the Lord Jesus, in the same manner as they also.”
15.bbe: But we have faith that we will get salvation through the grace of the Lord Jesus in the same way as they.

15.msb: The whole assembly fell silent as they listened to Barnabas and Paul describing the signs and wonders God had done among the Gentiles through them.
15.kjv: Then all the multitude kept silence, and gave audience to Barnabas and Paul, declaring what miracles and wonders God had wrought among the Gentiles by them.
15.blb: Now the whole multitude kept silent and were listening to Barnabas and Paul relating what signs and wonders God had done among the Gentiles by them.
15.bbe: And all the people were quiet while Barnabas and Paul gave an account of the signs and wonders which God had done among the Gentiles by them.

15.msb: When they had finished speaking, James declared, “Brothers, listen to me!
15.kjv: And after they had held their peace, James answered, saying, Men and brethren, hearken unto me:
15.blb: And after they were silent, James answered, saying, “Men, brothers, hear me.
15.bbe: And when they had come to an end, James, answering, said, My brothers, give ear to me:

15.msb: Simon has told us how God first visited the Gentiles to take from them a people to be His own.
15.kjv: Simeon hath declared how God at the first did visit the Gentiles, to take out of them a people for his name.
15.blb: Simeon related how God first visited to take out of the Gentiles a people for His name.
15.bbe: Symeon has given an account of how God was first pleased to take from among the Gentiles a people for himself.

15.msb: The words of the prophets agree with this, as it is written:
15.kjv: And to this agree the words of the prophets; as it is written,
15.blb: And the words of the prophets agree with this, as it is written:
15.bbe: And this is in agreement with the words of the prophets, as it is said,

15.msb: ‘After this I will return and rebuild the fallen tent of David. Its ruins I will rebuild, and I will restore it,
15.kjv: After this I will return, and will build again the tabernacle of David, which is fallen down; and I will build again the ruins thereof, and I will set it up:
15.blb: ‘After these things I will return, and I will rebuild the tabernacle of David that has fallen, and its ruins I will rebuild, and I will set it upright,
15.bbe: After these things I will come back, and will put up the tent of David which has been broken down, building up again its broken parts and making it complete:

15.msb: so that the remnant of men may seek the Lord, and all the Gentiles who are called by My name, says the Lord who does all these things.’
15.kjv: That the residue of men might seek after the Lord, and all the Gentiles, upon whom my name is called, saith the Lord, who doeth all these things.
15.blb: so that the remnant of men may seek out the Lord, and all the Gentiles, upon whom has been called My name—upon them, says the Lord, doing these things
15.bbe: So that the rest of men may make search for the Lord, and all the Gentiles on whom my name is named,

15.msb: Known for ages to God are all His works.
15.kjv: Known unto God are all his works from the beginning of the world.
15.blb: known from the age.’
15.bbe: Says the Lord, who has made these things clear from the earliest times.

15.msb: It is my judgment, therefore, that we should not cause trouble for the Gentiles who are turning to God.
15.kjv: Wherefore my sentence is, that we trouble not them, which from among the Gentiles are turned to God:
15.blb: Therefore I judge not to trouble those from the Gentiles turning to God,
15.bbe: For this reason my decision is, that we do not put trouble in the way of those who from among the Gentiles are turned to God;

15.msb: Instead, we should write and tell them to abstain from food polluted by idols, from sexual immorality, from the meat of strangled animals, and from blood.
15.kjv: But that we write unto them, that they abstain from pollutions of idols, and from fornication, and from things strangled, and from blood.
15.blb: but to write to them to abstain from the pollutions of idols, and from sexual immorality, and from that which is strangled, and from blood.
15.bbe: But that we give them orders to keep themselves from things offered to false gods, and from the evil desires of the body, and from the flesh of animals put to death in ways against the law, and from blood.

15.msb: For Moses has been proclaimed in every city from ancient times and is read in the synagogues on every Sabbath.”
15.kjv: For Moses of old time hath in every city them that preach him, being read in the synagogues every sabbath day.
