15.blb: For Moses has ones proclaiming him in every city from generations of old, being read in the synagogues on every Sabbath.”
15.bbe: For Moses, from times long past, has his preachers in every town, reading his law in the Synagogues every Sabbath.

15.msb: Then the apostles and elders, with the whole church, decided to select men from among them to send to Antioch with Paul and Barnabas. They chose Judas called Barsabbas and Silas, two leaders among the brothers,
15.kjv: Then pleased it the apostles and elders, with the whole church, to send chosen men of their own company to Antioch with Paul and Barnabas; namely, Judas surnamed Barsabas, and Silas, chief men among the brethren:
15.blb: Then it seemed good to the apostles and to the elders, with the whole church, having chosen out of them to send men to Antioch with Paul and Barnabas: Judas called Barsabbas and Silas, leading men among the brothers,
15.bbe: Then it seemed good to the Apostles and the rulers and all the church, to send men from among them to Antioch with Paul and Barnabas; Judas, named Barsabbas, and Silas, chief men among the brothers:
15.heading: The Letter to the Gentile Believers

15.msb: and sent them with this letter: The apostles, elders, and brothers, To the brothers among the Gentiles in Antioch, Syria, and Cilicia: Greetings.
15.kjv: And they wrote letters by them after this manner; The apostles and elders and brethren send greeting unto the brethren which are of the Gentiles in Antioch and Syria and Cilicia:
15.blb: having written by their hand: The apostles and the elders, brothers, To those brothers among the Gentiles in Antioch and Syria and Cilicia: Greetings.
15.bbe: And they sent a letter by them, saying, The Apostles and the older brothers, to the brothers who are of the Gentiles in Antioch and Syria and Cilicia, may joy be with you:

15.msb: It has come to our attention that some went out from us without our authorization and unsettled you, troubling your minds by saying that you must be circumcised and keep the law.
15.kjv: Forasmuch as we have heard, that certain which went out from us have troubled you with words, subverting your souls, saying, Ye must be circumcised, and keep the law: to whom we gave no such commandment:
15.blb: Inasmuch as we have heard that some went out from us, to whom we gave no instructions, and that they troubled you by words, upsetting your minds,
15.bbe: Because we have knowledge that some who went from us have been troubling you with their words, putting your souls in doubt; to whom we gave no such order;

15.msb: So we all agreed to send chosen men to you along with our beloved Barnabas and Paul,
15.kjv: It seemed good unto us, being assembled with one accord, to send chosen men unto you with our beloved Barnabas and Paul,
15.blb: it seemed good to us, having come with one accord, having chosen men to send to you with our beloved Barnabas and Paul,
15.bbe: It seemed good to us, having come to an agreement together, to send these men to you, with our well loved Barnabas and Paul,

15.msb: men who have risked their lives for the name of our Lord Jesus Christ.
15.kjv: Men that have hazarded their lives for the name of our Lord Jesus Christ.
15.blb: men having handed over their lives for the name of our Lord Jesus Christ.
15.bbe: Men who have given up their lives for the name of our Lord Jesus Christ.

15.msb: Therefore we are sending Judas and Silas to tell you in person the same things we are writing.
15.kjv: We have sent therefore Judas and Silas, who shall also tell you the same things by mouth.
15.blb: Therefore we have sent Judas and Silas, and they are telling the same things by word.
15.bbe: And so we have sent Judas and Silas, who will say the same things to you themselves, by word of mouth.

15.msb: It seemed good to the Holy Spirit and to us not to burden you with anything beyond these essential requirements:
15.kjv: For it seemed good to the Holy Ghost, and to us, to lay upon you no greater burden than these necessary things;
15.blb: For it seemed good to the Holy Spirit and to us to lay upon you no further burden except these necessary things:
15.bbe: For it seemed good to the Holy Spirit and to us, to put on you nothing more than these necessary things;

15.msb: You must abstain from food sacrificed to idols, from blood, from the meat of strangled animals, and from sexual immorality. You will do well to avoid these things. Farewell.
15.kjv: That ye abstain from meats offered to idols, and from blood, and from things strangled, and from fornication: from which if ye keep yourselves, ye shall do well. Fare ye well.
15.blb: to abstain from things sacrificed to idols, and from blood, and from what is strangled, and from sexual immorality. Keeping yourselves from these, you will do well. Farewell.
15.bbe: To keep from things offered to false gods, and from blood, and from things put to death in ways which are against the law, and from the evil desires of the body; if you keep yourselves from these, you will do well. May you be happy.

15.msb: So the men were sent off and went to Antioch, where they assembled the congregation and delivered the letter.
15.kjv: So when they were dismissed, they came to Antioch: and when they had gathered the multitude together, they delivered the epistle:
15.blb: Indeed, therefore, having been sent off, they went to Antioch, and having gathered the multitude, they delivered the letter.
15.bbe: So they, being sent away, came down to Antioch, and having got the people together, they gave them the letter.
15.heading: The Believers at Antioch Rejoice

15.msb: When the people read it, they rejoiced at its encouraging message.
15.kjv: Which when they had read, they rejoiced for the consolation.
15.blb: And having read it, they rejoiced at the encouragement.
15.bbe: And after reading it, they were glad of its comfort.

15.msb: Judas and Silas, who themselves were prophets, said much to encourage and strengthen the brothers.
15.kjv: And Judas and Silas, being prophets also themselves, exhorted the brethren with many words, and confirmed them.
15.blb: Both Judas and Silas, also being prophets themselves, exhorted and strengthened the brothers by much talk.
15.bbe: And Judas and Silas, who themselves were prophets, gave teaching to the brothers and made them strong in the faith.

15.msb: After spending some time there, they were sent off by the brothers in peace to return to the apostles.
15.kjv: And after they had tarried there a space, they were let go in peace from the brethren unto the apostles.
15.blb: And having continued a time, they were sent away in peace from the brothers to those having sent them.
15.bbe: And when they had been there for some time, they were sent back in peace by the brothers to those who had sent them.

15.kjv: Notwithstanding it pleased Silas to abide there still.

15.msb: But Paul and Barnabas remained at Antioch, along with many others, teaching and preaching the word of the Lord.
15.kjv: Paul also and Barnabas continued in Antioch, teaching and preaching the word of the Lord, with many others also.
15.blb: But Paul and Barnabas stayed in Antioch, teaching and preaching the good news—with many others also—the word of the Lord.
15.bbe: But Paul and Barnabas kept on in Antioch, teaching and preaching the word of God, with a number of others.

15.msb: Some time later Paul said to Barnabas, “Let us go back and visit our brothers in every town where we proclaimed the word of the Lord, to see how they are doing.”
15.kjv: And some days after Paul said unto Barnabas, Let us go again and visit our brethren in every city where we have preached the word of the Lord, and see how they do.
15.blb: Now after some days, Paul said to Barnabas, “Indeed, having turned back, let us look after the brothers in every city in which we have proclaimed the word of the Lord—how they are.”
15.bbe: And after some days, Paul said to Barnabas, Let us go back and see the brothers in every town where we have given the word of God, and see how they are.
15.heading: Paul’s Second Missionary Journey Begins

15.msb: Barnabas wanted to take John called Mark.
15.kjv: And Barnabas determined to take with them John, whose surname was Mark.
15.blb: Now Barnabas purposed also to take along John, called Mark.
15.bbe: And Barnabas had a desire to take with them John, named Mark.

15.msb: But Paul thought it best not to take him, because he had deserted them in Pamphylia and had not accompanied them in the work.
15.kjv: But Paul thought not good to take him with them, who departed from them from Pamphylia, and went not with them to the work.
15.blb: But Paul was thinking it fit not to take him along, the one having withdrawn from them from Pamphylia and not having gone with them to the work.
15.bbe: But Paul was of the opinion that it was not right to take with them one who had gone away from them in Pamphylia, and had not gone on with the work.

15.msb: Their disagreement was so sharp that they parted company. Barnabas took Mark and sailed for Cyprus,
15.kjv: And the contention was so sharp between them, that they departed asunder one from the other: and so Barnabas took Mark, and sailed unto Cyprus;
15.blb: Therefore a sharp disagreement arose, so that they separated from one another. And Barnabas, having taken Mark, sailed to Cyprus.
15.bbe: And there was a sharp argument between them, so that they were parted from one another, and Barnabas took Mark with him and went by ship to Cyprus;

15.msb: but Paul chose Silas and left, commended by the brothers to the grace of God.
15.kjv: And Paul chose Silas, and departed, being recommended by the brethren unto the grace of God.
15.blb: But Paul, having chosen Silas, went out, having been committed to the grace of the Lord by the brothers.
15.bbe: But Paul took Silas and went away with the blessing of the brothers.

15.msb: And he traveled through Syria and Cilicia, strengthening the churches.
15.kjv: And he went through Syria and Cilicia, confirming the churches.
15.blb: And he was passing through Syria and Cilicia, strengthening the churches.
15.bbe: And he went through Syria and Cilicia, making the churches stronger in the faith.

16.msb: Paul came to Derbe and then to Lystra, where he found a disciple named Timothy, the son of a believing Jewish woman and a Greek father.
16.kjv: Then came he to Derbe and Lystra: and, behold, a certain disciple was there, named Timotheus, the son of a certain woman, which was a Jewess, and believed; but his father was a Greek:
16.blb: And he came also to Derbe and to Lystra. And behold, a certain disciple was there, named Timothy, the son of a believing Jewish woman and a Greek father,
16.bbe: And he came to Derbe and Lystra: and there was a certain disciple there named Timothy, whose mother was one of the Jews of the faith, but his father was a Greek;
16.heading: Timothy Joins Paul and Silas

16.msb: The brothers in Lystra and Iconium spoke well of him.
16.kjv: Which was well reported of by the brethren that were at Lystra and Iconium.
16.blb: who was well spoken of by the brothers in Lystra and Iconium.
16.bbe: Of whom the brothers at Lystra and Iconium had a high opinion.

16.msb: Paul wanted Timothy to accompany him, so he took him and circumcised him on account of the Jews in that area, for they all knew that his father was a Greek.
16.kjv: Him would Paul have to go forth with him; and took and circumcised him because of the Jews which were in those quarters: for they knew all that his father was a Greek.
16.blb: Paul wanted this one to go out with him, and having taken him, he circumcised him on account of the Jews being in those parts; for they all knew that his father was a Greek.
16.bbe: Paul had a desire for him to go with him, and he gave him circumcision because of the Jews who were in those parts: for they all had knowledge that his father was a Greek.

16.msb: As they went from town to town, they delivered the decisions handed down by the apostles and elders in Jerusalem for the people to obey.
16.kjv: And as they went through the cities, they delivered them the decrees for to keep, that were ordained of the apostles and elders which were at Jerusalem.
16.blb: And while they were passing through the cities, they were delivering to them the decrees to keep—the ones decided on by the apostles and elders who were in Jerusalem.
16.bbe: And on their way through the towns, they gave them the rules which had been made by the Apostles and the rulers of the church at Jerusalem, so that they might keep them.

16.msb: So the churches were strengthened in the faith and grew daily in numbers.
16.kjv: And so were the churches established in the faith, and increased in number daily.
16.blb: So indeed the churches were strengthened in the faith and were increasing in number every day.
16.bbe: So the churches were made strong in the faith and were increased in number every day.

16.msb: After the Holy Spirit had prevented them from speaking the word in the province of Asia, they traveled through the region of Phrygia and Galatia.
16.kjv: Now when they had gone throughout Phrygia and the region of Galatia, and were forbidden of the Holy Ghost to preach the word in Asia,
16.blb: And having passed through Phrygia and the Galatian region, having been forbidden by the Holy Spirit to speak the word in Asia,
16.bbe: And after they had gone through the land of Phrygia and Galatia, the Holy Spirit did not let them take the word into Asia;
16.heading: Paul’s Vision of the Macedonian

16.msb: And when they came to the border of Mysia, they tried to enter Bithynia, but the Spirit would not permit them.
16.kjv: After they were come to Mysia, they assayed to go into Bithynia: but the Spirit suffered them not.
16.blb: and having come down to Mysia, they were attempting to go into Bithynia, and the Spirit of Jesus did not allow them.
16.bbe: And having come to Mysia, they made an attempt to go into Bithynia, but the Spirit of Jesus did not let them;

16.msb: So they passed by Mysia and went down to Troas.
16.kjv: And they passing by Mysia came down to Troas.
16.blb: And having passed by Mysia, they came down to Troas.
16.bbe: And going past Mysia, they came down to Troas.

16.msb: During the night, Paul had a vision of a man of Macedonia standing and pleading with him, “Come over to Macedonia and help us.”
16.kjv: And a vision appeared to Paul in the night; There stood a man of Macedonia, and prayed him, saying, Come over into Macedonia, and help us.
16.blb: And a vision appeared to Paul during the night: A certain man of Macedonia was standing and beseeching him and saying, “Having passed over into Macedonia, help us.”
16.bbe: And Paul had a vision in the night; a man of Macedonia came, requesting him, and saying, Come over into Macedonia and give us help.

16.msb: As soon as Paul had seen the vision, we got ready to leave for Macedonia, concluding that the Lord had called us to preach the gospel to them.
16.kjv: And after he had seen the vision, immediately we endeavoured to go into Macedonia, assuredly gathering that the Lord had called us for to preach the gospel unto them.
16.blb: And when he had seen the vision, immediately we sought to go out into Macedonia, concluding that God had summoned us to preach the gospel to them.
16.bbe: And when he had seen the vision, straight away we made the decision to go into Macedonia, for it seemed certain to us that God had sent us to give the good news to them.

16.msb: Therefore we sailed from Troas straight to Samothrace, and the following day on to Neapolis.
16.kjv: Therefore loosing from Troas, we came with a straight course to Samothracia, and the next day to Neapolis;
16.blb: And having sailed from Troas, we made a straight course to Samothrace, and on the following day to Neapolis,
16.bbe: So, from Troas we went straight by ship to Samothrace and the day after to Neapolis;
16.heading: Lydia’s Conversion in Philippi

16.msb: From there we went to the Roman colony of Philippi, the leading city of that district of Macedonia. And we stayed there several days.
16.kjv: And from thence to Philippi, which is the chief city of that part of Macedonia, and a colony: and we were in that city abiding certain days.
16.blb: and from there to Philippi, which is a leading city of the district of Macedonia—a colony. Now we were staying some days in this city.
16.bbe: And from there to Philippi, which is the most important town of Macedonia and a Roman colony: and we were there for some days.

16.msb: On the Sabbath we went outside the city along the river, where it was customary to find a place of prayer. After sitting down, we spoke to the women who had gathered there.
16.kjv: And on the sabbath we went out of the city by a river side, where prayer was wont to be made; and we sat down, and spake unto the women which resorted thither.
16.blb: And on the day of the Sabbaths, we went outside the city gate, by a river, where there was customary to be prayer. And having sat down, we began speaking to the women having gathered.
16.bbe: And on the Sabbath we went outside the town, by the river, where we had an idea that there would be a place of prayer; and, being seated, we had talk with the women who had come together.

16.msb: Among those listening was a woman named Lydia, a dealer in purple cloth from the city of Thyatira, who was a worshiper of God. The Lord opened her heart to respond to Paul’s message.
16.kjv: And a certain woman named Lydia, a seller of purple, of the city of Thyatira, which worshipped God, heard us: whose heart the Lord opened, that she attended unto the things which were spoken of Paul.
16.blb: And a certain woman named Lydia, a seller of purple of the city of Thyatira, worshiping God, was listening. The Lord opened her heart to attend to the things being spoken by Paul.
16.bbe: And a certain woman named Lydia, a trader in purple cloth of the town of Thyatira, and a God-fearing woman, gave ear to us: whose heart the Lord made open to give attention to the things which Paul was saying.

16.msb: And when she and her household had been baptized, she urged us, “If you consider me a believer in the Lord, come and stay at my house.” And she persuaded us.
16.kjv: And when she was baptized, and her household, she besought us, saying, If ye have judged me to be faithful to the Lord, come into my house, and abide there. And she constrained us.
16.blb: And when she was baptized, and her house, she begged, saying, “If you have judged me to be faithful to the Lord, having entered into my house, abide.” And she persuaded us.
16.bbe: And when she and her family had had baptism, she made a request to us, saying, If it seems to you that I am true to the Lord, come into my house and be my guests. And she made us come.

16.msb: One day as we were going to the place of prayer, we were met by a slave girl with a spirit of divination, who earned a large income for her masters by fortune-telling.
16.kjv: And it came to pass, as we went to prayer, a certain damsel possessed with a spirit of divination met us, which brought her masters much gain by soothsaying:
16.blb: Now it happened in our going to the prayer that a certain girl having a spirit of Python met us, who was bringing her masters much gain by fortune-telling.
16.bbe: And when we were going to the place of prayer, we came across a girl with a spirit which gave knowledge of the future, whose masters made great profit from her power.
16.heading: Paul and Silas Imprisoned

16.msb: This girl followed Paul and the rest of us, shouting, “These men are servants of the Most High God, who are proclaiming to us the way of salvation!”
16.kjv: The same followed Paul and us, and cried, saying, These men are the servants of the most high God, which shew unto us the way of salvation.
16.blb: Having followed Paul and us, she was crying out, saying, “These men are servants of the Most High God, who proclaim to you the way of salvation!”
16.bbe: She came after Paul and us, crying out and saying, These men are the servants of the Most High God, who are giving you news of the way of salvation.

16.msb: She continued this for many days. Eventually Paul grew so aggravated that he turned and said to the spirit, “In the name of Jesus Christ I command you to come out of her!” And the spirit left her at that very moment.
16.kjv: And this did she many days. But Paul, being grieved, turned and said to the spirit, I command thee in the name of Jesus Christ to come out of her. And he came out the same hour.
16.blb: And she continued this for many days. And Paul, having been distressed and having turned, said to the spirit, “I command you in the name of Jesus Christ to come out from her!” And it came out the same hour.
16.bbe: And this she did on a number of days. But Paul was greatly troubled and, turning, said to the spirit, I give you orders in the name of Jesus Christ, to come out of her. And it came out that very hour.

16.msb: When the girl’s owners saw that their hope of making money was gone, they seized Paul and Silas and dragged them before the authorities in the marketplace.
16.kjv: And when her masters saw that the hope of their gains was gone, they caught Paul and Silas, and drew them into the marketplace unto the rulers,
16.blb: And her masters, having seen that their hope of profit was gone, having taken hold of Paul and Silas, dragged them into the marketplace before the rulers.
16.bbe: But when her masters saw that their hope of profit was gone, they took Paul and Silas, pulling them into the market-place before the rulers;

16.msb: They brought them to the magistrates and said, “These men are Jews and are throwing our city into turmoil
16.kjv: And brought them to the magistrates, saying, These men, being Jews, do exceedingly trouble our city,
16.blb: And having brought them up to the magistrates, they said, “These men, being Jews, exceedingly trouble our city
16.bbe: And when they had taken them before the authorities, they said, These men, who are Jews, are greatly troubling our town;

16.msb: by promoting customs that are unlawful for us Romans to adopt or practice.”
16.kjv: And teach customs, which are not lawful for us to receive, neither to observe, being Romans.
16.blb: and proclaim customs not lawful for us, being Romans, to accept nor to practice.”
16.bbe: Teaching rules of living which it is not right for us to have or to keep, being Romans.

16.msb: The crowd joined in the attack against Paul and Silas, and the magistrates ordered that they be stripped and beaten with rods.
16.kjv: And the multitude rose up together against them: and the magistrates rent off their clothes, and commanded to beat them.
16.blb: And the crowd rose up together against them, and the magistrates, having torn off their garments, were commanding that they be beaten with rods.
16.bbe: And the people made an attack on them all together: and the authorities took their clothing off them, and gave orders for them to be whipped.

16.msb: And after striking them with many blows, they threw them into prison and ordered the jailer to guard them securely.
16.kjv: And when they had laid many stripes upon them, they cast them into prison, charging the jailor to keep them safely:
16.blb: And having laid many blows on them, they cast them into prison, having charged the jailer to keep them securely,
16.bbe: And when they had given them a great number of blows, they put them in prison, giving orders to the keeper of the prison to keep them safely:

16.msb: On receiving this order, he placed them in the inner cell and fastened their feet in the stocks.
16.kjv: Who, having received such a charge, thrust them into the inner prison, and made their feet fast in the stocks.
16.blb: who, having received such an order, threw them into the inner prison and fastened their feet in the stocks.
16.bbe: And he, having such orders, put them into the inner prison with chains on their feet.

16.msb: About midnight Paul and Silas were praying and singing hymns to God, and the other prisoners were listening to them.
16.kjv: And at midnight Paul and Silas prayed, and sang praises unto God: and the prisoners heard them.
16.blb: Now toward midnight, Paul and Silas, praying, were singing praises to God. And the prisoners were listening to them.
16.bbe: But about the middle of the night, Paul and Silas were making prayers and songs to God in the hearing of the prisoners;
16.heading: The Conversion of the Jailer

16.msb: Suddenly a strong earthquake shook the foundations of the prison. At once all the doors flew open and everyone’s chains came loose.
16.kjv: And suddenly there was a great earthquake, so that the foundations of the prison were shaken: and immediately all the doors were opened, and every one’s bands were loosed.
16.blb: And suddenly there was a great earthquake, so that the foundations of the prison house were shaken, and immediately all the doors were opened, and the chains of all were loosed.
16.bbe: And suddenly there was an earth-shock, so that the base of the prison was moved: and all the doors came open, and everyone's chains came off.

16.msb: When the jailer woke up and saw the prison doors open, he drew his sword and was about to kill himself, presuming that the prisoners had escaped.
16.kjv: And the keeper of the prison awaking out of his sleep, and seeing the prison doors open, he drew out his sword, and would have killed himself, supposing that the prisoners had been fled.
16.blb: And the jailer, having been awoken and having seen the doors of the prison open, having drawn his sword, was about to kill himself, supposing the prisoners to have escaped.
16.bbe: And the keeper, coming out of his sleep, and seeing the prison doors open, took his sword and was about to put himself to death, fearing that the prisoners had got away.

16.msb: But Paul called out in a loud voice, “Do not harm yourself! We are all here!”
16.kjv: But Paul cried with a loud voice, saying, Do thyself no harm: for we are all here.
16.blb: But Paul called out in a loud voice, saying, “Do not harm yourself, for we are all here!”
16.bbe: But Paul said in a loud voice, Do yourself no damage, for we are all here.

16.msb: Calling for lights, the jailer rushed in and fell trembling before Paul and Silas.
16.kjv: Then he called for a light, and sprang in, and came trembling, and fell down before Paul and Silas,
16.blb: And having called for lights, he rushed in, and having become terrified, he fell down before Paul and Silas.
16.bbe: And he sent for lights and came rushing in and, shaking with fear, went down on his face before Paul and Silas,

16.msb: Then he brought them out and asked, “Sirs, what must I do to be saved?”
16.kjv: And brought them out, and said, Sirs, what must I do to be saved?
16.blb: And having brought them out, he was saying, “Sirs, what is necessary for me to do so that I may be saved?”
16.bbe: And took them out and said, Sirs, what have I to do to get salvation?

16.msb: They replied, “Believe in the Lord Jesus Christ and you will be saved, you and your household.”
16.kjv: And they said, Believe on the Lord Jesus Christ, and thou shalt be saved, and thy house.
16.blb: And they said, “Believe on the Lord Jesus and you will be saved, you and your house.”
16.bbe: And they said, Have faith in the Lord Jesus, and you and your family will have salvation.

16.msb: Then Paul and Silas spoke the word of the Lord to him and to everyone in his house.
16.kjv: And they spake unto him the word of the Lord, and to all that were in his house.
16.blb: And they spoke the word of the Lord to him, along with all those in his house.
16.bbe: And they gave the word of the Lord to him and to all who were in his house.

16.msb: At that hour of the night, the jailer took them and washed their wounds. And without delay, he and all his household were baptized.
16.kjv: And he took them the same hour of the night, and washed their stripes; and was baptized, he and all his, straightway.
16.blb: And having taken them in that hour of the night, he washed them from the wounds, and immediately he was baptized, and all his own.
16.bbe: And that same hour of the night, he took them, and when he had given attention to their wounds, he and all his family had baptism straight away.

16.msb: Then he brought them into his home and set a meal before them. So he and all his household rejoiced that they had come to believe in God.
16.kjv: And when he had brought them into his house, he set meat before them, and rejoiced, believing in God with all his house.
16.blb: And having brought them into the house, he set a table and rejoiced with all his household, having believed in God.
16.bbe: And he took them into his house and gave them food, and he was full of joy, having faith in God with all his family.

16.msb: When daylight came, the magistrates sent their officers with the order: “Release those men.”
16.kjv: And when it was day, the magistrates sent the serjeants, saying, Let those men go.
16.blb: And day having come, the magistrates sent the officers, saying, “Release those men.”
16.bbe: But when it was day, the authorities sent the police, saying, Let these men go.
16.heading: An Official Apology

16.msb: The jailer informed Paul: “The magistrates have sent orders to release you. Now you may go on your way in peace.”
16.kjv: And the keeper of the prison told this saying to Paul, The magistrates have sent to let you go: now therefore depart, and go in peace.
16.blb: And the jailer reported these words to Paul: “The captains have sent that you may be let go. Now, therefore, having gone out, depart in peace.”
16.bbe: And the keeper said to Paul, The authorities have given orders to let you go: come out now, and go in peace.

16.msb: But Paul said to the officers, “They beat us publicly without a trial and threw us into prison, even though we are Roman citizens. And now do they want to send us away secretly? Absolutely not! Let them come themselves and escort us out!”
16.kjv: But Paul said unto them, They have beaten us openly uncondemned, being Romans, and have cast us into prison; and now do they thrust us out privily? nay verily; but let them come themselves and fetch us out.
16.blb: But Paul was saying to them, “Having beaten us publicly, uncondemned men being Romans, they cast us into prison, and now do they throw us out secretly? No indeed! Rather, having come themselves, let them bring us out.”
16.bbe: But Paul said to them, They have given us who are Romans a public whipping without judging us, and have put us in prison. Will they now send us out secretly? no, truly, let them come themselves and take us out.

16.msb: So the officers relayed this message to the magistrates, who were alarmed to hear that Paul and Silas were Roman citizens.
16.kjv: And the serjeants told these words unto the magistrates: and they feared, when they heard that they were Romans.
16.blb: And the officers reported these words to the captains, and they were afraid, having heard that they are Romans.
16.bbe: And the police gave an account of these words to the authorities, and they were full of fear on hearing that they were Romans;

16.msb: They came to appease them and led them out, requesting that they leave the city.
16.kjv: And they came and besought them, and brought them out, and desired them to depart out of the city.
16.blb: And having come, they appealed to them, and having brought them out, they were asking them to go out of the city.
16.bbe: Then they came and made prayers to them, requesting them, when they had taken them out, to go away from the town.

16.msb: After Paul and Silas came out of the prison, they went to Lydia’s house to see the brothers and encourage them. Then they left the city.
16.kjv: And they went out of the prison, and entered into the house of Lydia: and when they had seen the brethren, they comforted them, and departed.
16.blb: And having gone out of the prison, they came to Lydia, and having seen them, they exhorted the brothers and went out.
16.bbe: And they came out of the prison and went to the house of Lydia: and when they had seen the brothers they gave them comfort and went away.

17.msb: When they had passed through Amphipolis and Apollonia, they came to Thessalonica, where there was a Jewish synagogue.
17.kjv: Now when they had passed through Amphipolis and Apollonia, they came to Thessalonica, where was a synagogue of the Jews:
17.blb: And having passed through Amphipolis and Apollonia, they came to Thessalonica, where there was a synagogue of the Jews.
17.bbe: Now when they had gone through Amphipolis and Apollonia they came to Thessalonica, where there was a Synagogue of the Jews:
17.heading: The Uproar in Thessalonica

17.msb: As was his custom, Paul went into the synagogue, and on three Sabbaths he reasoned with them from the Scriptures,
17.kjv: And Paul, as his manner was, went in unto them, and three sabbath days reasoned with them out of the scriptures,
17.blb: And according to the custom of Paul, he went in to them, and for three Sabbaths he reasoned with them from the Scriptures,
17.bbe: And Paul, as he generally did, went in to them, and on three Sabbath days had discussions with them from the holy Writings,

17.msb: explaining and proving that the Christ had to suffer and rise from the dead. “This Jesus I am proclaiming to you is the Christ,” he declared.
17.kjv: Opening and alleging, that Christ must needs have suffered, and risen again from the dead; and that this Jesus, whom I preach unto you, is Christ.
17.blb: opening and setting forth that it was necessary for the Christ to have suffered and to have risen out from the dead, and that “this Jesus whom I proclaim to you is the Christ.”
17.bbe: Saying to them clearly and openly that Christ had to be put to death and come back to life again; and that this Jesus, whom, he said, I am preaching to you, is the Christ.

17.msb: Some of the Jews were persuaded and joined Paul and Silas, along with a large number of God-fearing Greeks and quite a few leading women.
17.kjv: And some of them believed, and consorted with Paul and Silas; and of the devout Greeks a great multitude, and of the chief women not a few.
17.blb: And some of them were obedient and joined themselves to Paul and to Silas, along with a great multitude of the worshiping Greeks and not a few of the leading women.
17.bbe: And some of them had faith, and were joined to Paul and Silas; and a number of the God-fearing Greeks, and some of the chief women.

17.msb: The unbelieving Jews, however, brought in some troublemakers from the marketplace, formed a mob, and sent the city into an uproar. They raided Jason’s house in search of Paul and Silas, hoping to bring them out to the people.
17.kjv: But the Jews which believed not, moved with envy, took unto them certain lewd fellows of the baser sort, and gathered a company, and set all the city on an uproar, and assaulted the house of Jason, and sought to bring them out to the people.
17.blb: But the Jews, having become jealous and having taken along certain wicked men of the market-loungers, and having collected a crowd, set the city in uproar. And having assailed the house of Jason, they were seeking them to bring out to the people.
17.bbe: But the Jews, being moved with envy, took with them certain low persons from among the common people, and getting together a great number of people, made an outcry in the town, attacking the house of Jason with the purpose of taking them out to the people.

17.msb: But when they could not find them, they dragged Jason and some other brothers before the city officials, shouting, “These men who have turned the world upside down have now come here,
17.kjv: And when they found them not, they drew Jason and certain brethren unto the rulers of the city, crying, These that have turned the world upside down are come hither also;
17.blb: But not having found them, they dragged Jason and certain brothers before the city authorities, crying out, “These ones, having upset the world, have come here also,
17.bbe: And when they were not able to get them, they took Jason and some of the brothers by force before the rulers of the town, crying, These men, who have made trouble all over the world have now come here;

17.msb: and Jason has welcomed them into his home. They are all defying Caesar’s decrees, saying that there is another king, named Jesus!”
17.kjv: Whom Jason hath received: and these all do contrary to the decrees of Cæsar, saying that there is another king, one Jesus.
17.blb: whom Jason has received. And these all do contrary to the decrees of Caesar, proclaiming another to be king—Jesus!”
17.bbe: Whom Jason has taken into his house: and they are acting against the orders of Caesar, saying that there is another king, Jesus.

17.msb: On hearing this, the crowd and city officials were greatly disturbed.
17.kjv: And they troubled the people and the rulers of the city, when they heard these things.
17.blb: And they stirred up the crowd and the city authorities hearing these things.
17.bbe: And hearing these things the people and the rulers of the town were troubled.

17.msb: And they collected bond from Jason and the others and then released them.
17.kjv: And when they had taken security of Jason, and of the other, they let them go.
17.blb: And having taken security from Jason and the rest, they let them go.
17.bbe: And having made Jason and the others give an undertaking to keep the peace, they let them go.

17.msb: As soon as night had fallen, the brothers sent Paul and Silas away to Berea. On arriving there, they went into the Jewish synagogue.
17.kjv: And the brethren immediately sent away Paul and Silas by night unto Berea: who coming thither went into the synagogue of the Jews.
17.blb: And the brothers sent away both Paul and Silas immediately by night to Berea, who, having arrived, went into the synagogue of the Jews.
17.bbe: And the brothers straight away sent Paul and Silas away by night to Beroea: and they, when they came there, went to the Synagogue of the Jews.
17.heading: The Character of the Bereans

17.msb: Now the Bereans were more noble-minded than the Thessalonians, for they received the message with great eagerness and examined the Scriptures every day to see if these teachings were true.
17.kjv: These were more noble than those in Thessalonica, in that they received the word with all readiness of mind, and searched the scriptures daily, whether those things were so.
17.blb: Now these, who were more noble than those in Thessalonica, received the word with all readiness, every day examining the Scriptures, if these things were so.
17.bbe: Now these were more noble than the Jews of Thessalonica, for they gave serious attention to the word, searching in the holy Writings every day, to see if these things were so.

17.msb: As a result, many of them believed, along with quite a few prominent Greek women and men.
17.kjv: Therefore many of them believed; also of honourable women which were Greeks, and of men, not a few.
17.blb: Therefore many of them indeed believed, and not a few of the prominent Grecian women and men.
17.bbe: And a number of them had faith, and no small number of the Greek women of high position and of the men.

17.msb: But when the Jews from Thessalonica learned that Paul was also proclaiming the word of God in Berea, they went there themselves to incite the crowds.
17.kjv: But when the Jews of Thessalonica had knowledge that the word of God was preached of Paul at Berea, they came thither also, and stirred up the people.
17.blb: But when the Jews from Thessalonica knew that the word of God also was proclaimed by Paul in Berea, they came there also, stirring up and agitating the crowds.
17.bbe: But when the Jews of Thessalonica had news that Paul was preaching the word at Beroea, they came there, troubling the people and working them up.

17.msb: The brothers immediately sent Paul away as if to the coast, but Silas and Timothy remained in Berea.
17.kjv: And then immediately the brethren sent away Paul to go as it were to the sea: but Silas and Timotheus abode there still.
17.blb: And then immediately the brothers sent away Paul to go as to the sea. And both Silas and Timothy remained there.
17.bbe: So the brothers sent Paul straight away to the sea: but Silas and Timothy kept there still.

17.msb: Those who escorted Paul brought him to Athens and then returned with instructions for Silas and Timothy to join him as soon as possible.
17.kjv: And they that conducted Paul brought him unto Athens: and receiving a commandment unto Silas and Timotheus for to come to him with all speed, they departed.
17.blb: And those escorting Paul brought him unto Athens, and having received a command to Silas and Timothy that as quickly as possible they should come to him, they departed.
17.bbe: But those who went with Paul took him as far as Athens, and then went away, with orders from him to Silas and Timothy to come to him quickly.

17.msb: While Paul was waiting for them in Athens, he was deeply disturbed in his spirit to see that the city was full of idols.
17.kjv: Now while Paul waited for them at Athens, his spirit was stirred in him, when he saw the city wholly given to idolatry.
17.blb: Now Paul in Athens waiting for them, his spirit was provoked in him, seeing the city to be utterly idolatrous.
17.bbe: Now while Paul was waiting for them at Athens, his spirit was troubled, for he saw all the town full of images of the gods.
17.heading: Paul in Athens

17.msb: So he reasoned in the synagogue with the Jews and God-fearing Gentiles, and in the marketplace with those he met each day.
17.kjv: Therefore disputed he in the synagogue with the Jews, and with the devout persons, and in the market daily with them that met with him.
17.blb: So indeed he was reasoning in the synagogue with the Jews and those worshiping, and in the marketplace on every day with those meeting.
17.bbe: So he had discussions in the Synagogue with the Jews and God-fearing Gentiles, and every day in the market-place with those who were there.

17.msb: Some Epicurean and Stoic philosophers also began to debate with him. Some of them asked, “What is this babbler trying to say?” Others said, “He seems to be advocating foreign gods.” They said this because Paul was proclaiming the good news of Jesus and the resurrection.
17.kjv: Then certain philosophers of the Epicureans, and of the Stoicks, encountered him. And some said, What will this babbler say? other some, He seemeth to be a setter forth of strange gods: because he preached unto them Jesus, and the resurrection.
17.blb: And also some of the Epicureans and Stoics, philosophers, encountered him, and some were saying, “What may this babbler desire to say?” but others, “He seems to be a proclaimer of strange gods,” because he was proclaiming the gospel—Jesus and the resurrection.
17.bbe: And some of those who were supporters of the theories of the Epicureans and the Stoics, had a meeting with him. And some said, What is this talker of foolish words saying? And others, He seems to be a preacher of strange gods: because he was preaching of Jesus and his coming back from the dead.

17.msb: So they took Paul and brought him to the Areopagus, where they asked him, “May we know what this new teaching is that you are presenting?
17.kjv: And they took him, and brought him unto Areopagus, saying, May we know what this new doctrine, whereof thou speakest, is?
17.blb: And having taken hold of him, they brought him to the Areopagus, saying, “Are we able to know what this new teaching is that is spoken by you?
17.bbe: And they took him to Mars' Hill, saying, Will you make clear to us what is this new teaching of yours?

17.msb: For you are bringing some strange notions to our ears, and we want to know what they mean.”
17.kjv: For thou bringest certain strange things to our ears: we would know therefore what these things mean.
17.blb: For you are bringing some strange things to our ears. We resolve, therefore, to know what these things wish to be.”
17.bbe: For you seem to us to say strange things, and we have a desire to get the sense of them.

17.msb: Now all the Athenians and foreigners who lived there spent their time doing nothing more than hearing and articulating new ideas.
17.kjv: (For all the Athenians and strangers which were there spent their time in nothing else, but either to tell, or to hear some new thing.)
17.blb: Now all the Athenians and the visiting foreigners spent their time on nothing other than to say something and to hear something new.
17.bbe: (Now all the Athenians and the men from other lands who come there were giving all their time to talking or hearing of anything new.)

17.msb: Then Paul stood up in the meeting of the Areopagus and said, “Men of Athens, I see that in every way you are very religious.
17.kjv: Then Paul stood in the midst of Mars’ hill, and said, Ye men of Athens, I perceive that in all things ye are too superstitious.
17.blb: And Paul, having stood in the midst of the Areopagus, was saying, “Men, Athenians, in all things I perceive you as very religious.
17.bbe: And Paul got to his feet on Mars' Hill and said, O men of Athens, I see that you are overmuch given to fear of the gods.
17.heading: Paul’s Address in the Areopagus

17.msb: For as I walked around and examined your objects of worship, I even found an altar with this inscription: TO AN UNKNOWN GOD. Therefore Him whom you worship as something unknown, I now proclaim to you.
17.kjv: For as I passed by, and beheld your devotions, I found an altar with this inscription, TO THE UNKNOWN GOD. Whom therefore ye ignorantly worship, him declare I unto you.
17.blb: For passing through and examining your objects of worship, I even found an altar on which had been inscribed: TO AN UNKNOWN GOD. Therefore whom you worship without knowing, this I proclaim to you.
17.bbe: For when I came by, I was looking at the things to which you give worship, and I saw an altar with this writing on it, TO THE GOD OF WHOM THERE IS NO KNOWLEDGE. Now, what you, without knowledge, give worship to, I make clear to you.

17.msb: The God who made the world and everything in it is the Lord of heaven and earth and does not live in temples made by human hands.
17.kjv: God that made the world and all things therein, seeing that he is Lord of heaven and earth, dwelleth not in temples made with hands;
17.blb: The God having made the world and all things that are in it, He, being Lord of heaven and earth, does not dwell in hand-made temples,
17.bbe: The God who made the earth and everything in it, he, being Lord of heaven and earth, is not housed in buildings made with hands;

17.msb: Nor is He served by the hands of men, as if He needed anything, because He Himself gives everyone life and breath and everything else.
17.kjv: Neither is worshipped with men’s hands, as though he needed any thing, seeing he giveth to all life, and breath, and all things;
17.blb: nor is He served by hands of men as needing anything—He who gives to all life and breath and all things.
17.bbe: And he is not dependent on the work of men's hands, as if he had need of anything, for he himself gives to all life and breath and all things;

17.msb: From one blood He made every nation of men, that they should inhabit the whole earth; and He determined their appointed times and the boundaries of their lands.
17.kjv: And hath made of one blood all nations of men for to dwell on all the face of the earth, and hath determined the times before appointed, and the bounds of their habitation;
17.blb: And He made out of one man every nation of men to dwell upon all the face of the earth, having determined the appointed times and the boundaries of their habitation,
17.bbe: And he has made of one blood all the nations of men living on all the face of the earth, ordering their times and the limits of their lands,

17.msb: The Lord intended that they would seek Him and perhaps reach out for Him and find Him, though He is not far from each one of us.
17.kjv: That they should seek the Lord, if haply they might feel after him, and find him, though he be not far from every one of us:
17.blb: to seek God, if perhaps indeed they might feel after Him and might find Him. And indeed, He is not far from each one of us.
17.bbe: So that they might make search for God, in order, if possible, to get knowledge of him and make discovery of him, though he is not far from every one of us:

17.msb: ‘For in Him we live and move and have our being.’ As some of your own poets have said, ‘We are His offspring.’
17.kjv: For in him we live, and move, and have our being; as certain also of your own poets have said, For we are also his offspring.
17.blb: ‘For in Him we live and move and are.’ As also some of the poets among you have said, ‘For we are also His offspring.’
17.bbe: For in him we have life and motion and existence; as certain of your verse writers have said, For we are his offspring.

17.msb: Therefore, being offspring of God, we should not think that the Divine Being is like gold or silver or stone, an image formed by man’s skill and imagination.
17.kjv: Forasmuch then as we are the offspring of God, we ought not to think that the Godhead is like unto gold, or silver, or stone, graven by art and man’s device.
17.blb: Therefore, being offspring of God, we ought not to consider the Divine Being to be like gold or silver or stone, a graven thing of man’s craft and imagination.
17.bbe: If then we are the offspring of God, it is not right for us to have the idea that God is like gold or silver or stone, formed by the art or design of man.

17.msb: Although God overlooked the ignorance of earlier times, He now commands all people everywhere to repent.
17.kjv: And the times of this ignorance God winked at; but now commandeth all men every where to repent:
17.blb: Indeed, therefore, God, having overlooked the times of ignorance, now commands all men everywhere to repent,
17.bbe: Those times when men had no knowledge were overlooked by God; but now he gives orders to all men in every place to undergo a change of heart:

17.msb: For He has set a day when He will judge the world with justice by the Man He has appointed. He has given proof of this to everyone by raising Him from the dead.”
17.kjv: Because he hath appointed a day, in the which he will judge the world in righteousness by that man whom he hath ordained; whereof he hath given assurance unto all men, in that he hath raised him from the dead.
17.blb: because He set a day in which He is about to judge the world in righteousness by the Man whom He appointed, having provided a guarantee to all, having raised Him out from the dead.”
17.bbe: Because a day has been fixed in which all the world will be judged in righteousness by the man who has been marked out by him for this work; of which he has given a sign to all men by giving him back from the dead.

17.msb: When they heard about the resurrection of the dead, some began to mock him, but others said, “We want to hear you again on this topic.”
17.kjv: And when they heard of the resurrection of the dead, some mocked: and others said, We will hear thee again of this matter.
17.blb: Now having heard of a resurrection of the dead, some indeed began mocking, but some said, “We will hear you concerning this again also.”
17.bbe: Now on hearing about the coming back from death, some of them made sport of it, but others said, Let us go more fully into this another time.

17.msb: At that, Paul left the Areopagus.
17.kjv: So Paul departed from among them.
17.blb: Thus Paul went out from their midst.
17.bbe: And so Paul went away from among them.

17.msb: But some joined him and believed, including Dionysius the Areopagite, a woman named Damaris, and others who were with them.
17.kjv: Howbeit certain men clave unto him, and believed: among the which was Dionysius the Areopagite, and a woman named Damaris, and others with them.
17.blb: But some men, having joined themselves to him, believed, among whom also were Dionysius the Areopagite, and a woman named Damaris, and others with them.
17.bbe: But some men gave him their support: among whom was Dionysius the Areopagite, and a woman named Damaris, and others with them.

18.msb: After this, Paul left Athens and went to Corinth.
18.kjv: After these things Paul departed from Athens, and came to Corinth;
18.blb: And after these things, having departed from Athens, he came to Corinth.
18.bbe: After these things, he went away from Athens, and came to Corinth.
18.heading: Paul Ministers in Corinth

18.msb: There he found a Jew named Aquila, a native of Pontus, who had recently come from Italy with his wife Priscilla because Claudius had ordered all the Jews to leave Rome. Paul went to visit them,
18.kjv: And found a certain Jew named Aquila, born in Pontus, lately come from Italy, with his wife Priscilla; (because that Claudius had commanded all Jews to depart from Rome:) and came unto them.
18.blb: And having found a certain Jew named Aquila, a native of Pontus, and Priscilla his wife, recently having come from Italy because of Claudius having commanded all the Jews to depart out of Rome, he came to them,
18.bbe: And there he came across a certain Jew named Aquila, a man of Pontus by birth, who not long before had come from Italy with his wife Priscilla, because Claudius had given orders that all Jews were to go away from Rome: and he came to them;

18.msb: and he stayed and worked with them because they were tentmakers by trade, just as he was.
18.kjv: And because he was of the same craft, he abode with them, and wrought: for by their occupation they were tentmakers.
18.blb: and because of being of the same trade, he stayed with them and worked. For they were tentmakers by the trade.
18.bbe: And because he was of the same trade, he was living with them, and they did their work together; for by trade they were tent-makers.

18.msb: Every Sabbath he reasoned in the synagogue, trying to persuade Jews and Greeks alike.
18.kjv: And he reasoned in the synagogue every sabbath, and persuaded the Jews and the Greeks.
18.blb: And he was reasoning in the synagogue on every Sabbath, persuading both Jews and Greeks.
18.bbe: And every Sabbath he had discussions in the Synagogue, turning Jews and Greeks to the faith.

18.msb: And when Silas and Timothy came down from Macedonia, Paul was compelled by the Spirit, testifying to the Jews that Jesus is the Christ.
18.kjv: And when Silas and Timotheus were come from Macedonia, Paul was pressed in the spirit, and testified to the Jews that Jesus was Christ.
18.blb: Now when both Silas and Timothy came down from Macedonia, Paul was occupied with the word, earnestly testifying to the Jews Jesus to be the Christ.
18.bbe: And when Silas and Timothy came down from Macedonia, Paul was completely given up to the word, preaching to the Jews that the Christ was Jesus.

18.msb: But when they opposed and insulted him, he shook out his garments and told them, “Your blood be on your own heads! I am innocent of it. From now on I will go to the Gentiles.”
18.kjv: And when they opposed themselves, and blasphemed, he shook his raiment, and said unto them, Your blood be upon your own heads; I am clean: from henceforth I will go unto the Gentiles.
18.blb: But on their opposing and reviling him, having shaken out the garments, he said to them, “Your blood be upon your head! I am clean. From now on I will go to the Gentiles.”
18.bbe: And when they put themselves against him, and said evil words, he said, shaking his clothing, Your blood be on your heads, I am clean: from now I will go to the Gentiles.

18.msb: So Paul left the synagogue and went next door to the house of Justus, a worshiper of God.
18.kjv: And he departed thence, and entered into a certain man’s house, named Justus, one that worshipped God, whose house joined hard to the synagogue.
18.blb: And having departed from there, he came to the house of a certain one named Titus Justus, one worshiping God, whose house was adjoining the synagogue.
18.bbe: And moving from there, he went into the house of a man named Titus Justus, a God-fearing man, whose house was very near the Synagogue.

18.msb: Crispus, the synagogue leader, and his whole household believed in the Lord. And many of the Corinthians who heard the message believed and were baptized.
18.kjv: And Crispus, the chief ruler of the synagogue, believed on the Lord with all his house; and many of the Corinthians hearing believed, and were baptized.
18.blb: And Crispus, the synagogue ruler, believed in the Lord with all his house, and many of the Corinthians hearing believed and were baptized.
18.bbe: And Crispus, the ruler of the Synagogue, with all his family, had faith in the Lord; and a great number of the people of Corinth, hearing the word, had faith and were given baptism.

18.msb: One night the Lord spoke to Paul in a vision: “Do not be afraid; keep on speaking; do not be silent.
18.kjv: Then spake the Lord to Paul in the night by a vision, Be not afraid, but speak, and hold not thy peace:
18.blb: Now the Lord said to Paul through a vision in the night, “Do not be afraid, but continue speaking, and do not be silent,
18.bbe: And the Lord said to Paul in the night, in a vision, Have no fear and go on preaching:

18.msb: For I am with you and no one will lay a hand on you, because I have many people in this city.”
18.kjv: For I am with thee, and no man shall set on thee to hurt thee: for I have much people in this city.
18.blb: because I am with you, and no one will lay a hand on you to harm you, because there are many people unto Me in this city.”
18.bbe: For I am with you, and no one will make an attack on you to do you damage: for I have a number of people in this town.

18.msb: So Paul stayed for a year and a half, teaching the word of God among the Corinthians.
18.kjv: And he continued there a year and six months, teaching the word of God among them.
18.blb: And he remained a year and six months, teaching the word of God among them.
18.bbe: And he was there for a year and six months, teaching the word of God among them.

18.msb: While Gallio was proconsul of Achaia, the Jews coordinated an attack on Paul and brought him before the judgment seat.
18.kjv: And when Gallio was the deputy of Achaia, the Jews made insurrection with one accord against Paul, and brought him to the judgment seat,
18.blb: But Gallio being proconsul of Achaia, the Jews with one accord rose up against Paul and led him to the judgment seat,
18.bbe: But when Gallio was ruler of Achaia, all the Jews together made an attack on Paul, and took him to the judge's seat,
18.heading: Paul before Gallio

18.msb: “This man is persuading the people to worship God in ways contrary to the law,” they said.
18.kjv: Saying, This fellow persuadeth men to worship God contrary to the law.
18.blb: saying, “This man persuades men to worship God contrary to the law.”
18.bbe: Saying, This man is teaching the people to give worship to God in a way which is against the law.

18.msb: But just as Paul was about to speak, Gallio told the Jews, “If this matter involved a wrongdoing or vicious crime, O Jews, it would be reasonable for me to hear your complaint.
18.kjv: And when Paul was now about to open his mouth, Gallio said unto the Jews, If it were a matter of wrong or wicked lewdness, O ye Jews, reason would that I should bear with you:
18.blb: And Paul being about to open the mouth, Gallio said to the Jews, “If indeed it was some unrighteousness or wicked crime, O Jews, according to reason I would have endured with you.
18.bbe: But when Paul was about to say something, Gallio said to the Jews, If this was anything to do with wrongdoing or crime, there would be a reason for me to give you a hearing:

18.msb: But since it is a dispute about words and names and your own law, settle it yourselves. For I refuse to be a judge of such things.”
18.kjv: But if it be a question of words and names, and of your law, look ye to it; for I will be no judge of such matters.
18.blb: But if it is a question about a word and names and in reference to your law, you will see yourselves. I resolve not to be a judge of these things.”
18.bbe: But if it is a question of words or names or of your law, see to it yourselves; I will not be a judge of such things.

18.msb: And he drove them away from the judgment seat.
18.kjv: And he drave them from the judgment seat.
18.blb: And he drove them from the judgment seat.
18.bbe: And he sent them away from the judge's seat.

18.msb: At this, all the Greeks seized Sosthenes the synagogue leader and beat him in front of the judgment seat. But none of this was of concern to Gallio.
18.kjv: Then all the Greeks took Sosthenes, the chief ruler of the synagogue, and beat him before the judgment seat. And Gallio cared for none of those things.
18.blb: Then they all, having seized Sosthenes the synagogue ruler, were beating him before the judgment seat. And it mattered nothing to Gallio about these things.
18.bbe: And they all made an attack on Sosthenes, the ruler of the Synagogue, and gave him blows before the judge's seat; but Gallio gave no attention to these things.

18.msb: Paul remained in Corinth for quite some time before saying goodbye to the brothers. He had his head shaved in Cenchrea to keep a vow he had made, and then he sailed for Syria, accompanied by Priscilla and Aquila.
18.kjv: And Paul after this tarried there yet a good while, and then took his leave of the brethren, and sailed thence into Syria, and with him Priscilla and Aquila; having shorn his head in Cenchrea: for he had a vow.
18.blb: Now Paul, having remained many days more, having taken leave of the brothers, sailed away to Syria—and with him Priscilla and Aquila—having shaved the head in Cenchrea, for he had a vow.
18.bbe: And Paul, after waiting some days, went away from the brothers and went by ship to Syria, Priscilla and Aquila being with him; and he had had his hair cut off in Cenchrea, for he had taken an oath.
18.heading: Paul Returns to Antioch

18.msb: When he reached Ephesus, Paul left Priscilla and Aquila. He himself went into the synagogue there and reasoned with the Jews.
18.kjv: And he came to Ephesus, and left them there: but he himself entered into the synagogue, and reasoned with the Jews.
18.blb: And they came to Ephesus and left them there. And he himself, having entered into the synagogue, reasoned with the Jews.
18.bbe: And they came down to Ephesus and he left them there: and he himself went into the Synagogue and had a discussion with the Jews.

18.msb: When they asked him to stay with them for a while longer, he declined.
18.kjv: When they desired him to tarry longer time with them, he consented not;
18.blb: And of them asking him to remain for a longer time, he did not consent,
18.bbe: And being requested by them to be there for a longer time, he said, No;

18.msb: But as he left, he said, “I must by all means keep this coming feast in Jerusalem, but I will come back to you if God is willing.” And he set sail from Ephesus.
18.kjv: But bade them farewell, saying, I must by all means keep this feast that cometh in Jerusalem: but I will return again unto you, if God will. And he sailed from Ephesus.
18.blb: but having taken leave and having said, “I will return to you again, God willing,” he sailed from Ephesus,
18.bbe: And went from them, saying, I will come back to you if God lets me; and he took ship from Ephesus.

18.msb: When Paul had landed at Caesarea, he went up and greeted the church at Jerusalem. Then he went down to Antioch.
18.kjv: And when he had landed at Cæsarea, and gone up, and saluted the church, he went down to Antioch.
18.blb: and having landed at Caesarea, having gone up and having greeted the church, he went down to Antioch.
18.bbe: And when he had come to land at Caesarea, he went to see the church, and then went down to Antioch.

18.msb: After Paul had spent some time in Antioch, he traveled from place to place throughout the region of Galatia and Phrygia, strengthening all the disciples.
18.kjv: And after he had spent some time there, he departed, and went over all the country of Galatia and Phrygia in order, strengthening all the disciples.
18.blb: And having stayed some time, he went out, passing successively through the Galatian region and Phrygia, strengthening all the disciples.
18.bbe: And having been there for some time, he went through the country of Galatia and Phrygia in order, making the disciples strong in the faith.
18.heading: Paul’s Third Missionary Journey Begins

18.msb: Meanwhile a Jew named Apollos, a native of Alexandria, came to Ephesus. He was an eloquent man, well versed in the Scriptures.
18.kjv: And a certain Jew named Apollos, born at Alexandria, an eloquent man, and mighty in the scriptures, came to Ephesus.
18.blb: Now a certain Jew named Apollos, a native of Alexandria, came to Ephesus, being an eloquent man, mighty in the Scriptures.
18.bbe: Now a certain Jew named Apollos, an Alexandrian by birth, and a man of learning, came to Ephesus; and he had great knowledge of the holy Writings.

18.msb: He had been instructed in the way of the Lord and was fervent in spirit. He spoke and taught accurately about the Lord, though he knew only the baptism of John.
18.kjv: This man was instructed in the way of the Lord; and being fervent in the spirit, he spake and taught diligently the things of the Lord, knowing only the baptism of John.
18.blb: He was instructed in the way of the Lord. And being fervent in spirit, he was speaking and was teaching earnestly the things concerning Jesus, knowing only the baptism of John,
18.bbe: This man had been trained in the way of the Lord; and burning in spirit, he gave himself up to teaching the facts about Jesus, though he had knowledge only of John's baptism:

18.msb: And he began to speak boldly in the synagogue. When Aquila and Priscilla heard him, they took him aside and explained to him the way of God more accurately.
18.kjv: And he began to speak boldly in the synagogue: whom when Aquila and Priscilla had heard, they took him unto them, and expounded unto him the way of God more perfectly.
18.blb: and he began to speak boldly in the synagogue. But Priscilla and Aquila, having heard him, took him to them and expounded the way of God to him more accurately.
18.bbe: And he was preaching in the Synagogue without fear. But Priscilla and Aquila, hearing his words, took him in, and gave him fuller teaching about the way of God.

18.msb: When Apollos resolved to cross over to Achaia, the brothers encouraged him and wrote to the disciples there to welcome him. On his arrival, he was a great help to those who by grace had believed.
18.kjv: And when he was disposed to pass into Achaia, the brethren wrote, exhorting the disciples to receive him: who, when he was come, helped them much which had believed through grace:
18.blb: And in his resolving to pass through into Achaia, the brothers, having encouraged him, wrote to the disciples to welcome him, who, having arrived, helped greatly those having believed through grace.
18.bbe: And when he had a desire to go over into Achaia, the brothers gave him help, and sent letters to the disciples requesting them to take him in among them: and when he had come, he gave much help to those who had faith through grace:

18.msb: For he powerfully refuted the Jews in public debate, proving from the Scriptures that Jesus is the Christ.
18.kjv: For he mightily convinced the Jews, and that publickly, shewing by the scriptures that Jesus was Christ.
18.blb: For he was powerfully refuting the Jews publicly, showing by the Scriptures Jesus to be the Christ.
18.bbe: For he overcame the Jews in public discussion, making clear from the holy Writings that the Christ was Jesus.

19.msb: While Apollos was at Corinth, Paul passed through the interior and came to Ephesus. There he found some disciples
19.kjv: And it came to pass, that, while Apollos was at Corinth, Paul having passed through the upper coasts came to Ephesus: and finding certain disciples,
19.blb: And it came to pass while Apollos was in Corinth that Paul, having passed through the upper parts to come to Ephesus and having found certain disciples,
19.bbe: And it came about that while Apollos was at Corinth, Paul, having gone through the higher country, came to Ephesus, where there were certain disciples:
19.heading: The Holy Spirit Received at Ephesus

19.msb: and asked them, “Did you receive the Holy Spirit when you became believers?” “No,” they answered, “we have not even heard that there is a Holy Spirit.”
19.kjv: He said unto them, Have ye received the Holy Ghost since ye believed? And they said unto him, We have not so much as heard whether there be any Holy Ghost.
19.blb: also said to them, “Did you receive the Holy Spirit, having believed?” And they said to him, “But we did not even hear that there is a Holy Spirit.”
19.bbe: And he said to them, Did you get the Holy Spirit when you had faith? And they said to him, No, we have had no knowledge of the Holy Spirit.

19.msb: “Into what, then, were you baptized?” Paul asked. “The baptism of John,” they replied.
19.kjv: And he said unto them, Unto what then were ye baptized? And they said, Unto John’s baptism.
19.blb: And he said, “Into what, then, were you baptized?” And they said, “Into John's baptism.”
19.bbe: And he said, What sort of baptism did you have? And they said, The baptism of John.

19.msb: Paul explained: “John’s baptism was indeed a baptism of repentance. He told the people to believe in the One coming after him, that is, in Christ Jesus.”
19.kjv: Then said Paul, John verily baptized with the baptism of repentance, saying unto the people, that they should believe on him which should come after him, that is, on Christ Jesus.
19.blb: And Paul said, “John baptized a baptism of repentance, saying to the people that they should believe in the One coming after him, that is, in Jesus.”
19.bbe: And Paul said, John gave a baptism which goes with a change of heart, saying to the people that they were to have faith in him who was coming after him, that is, in Jesus.

19.msb: On hearing this, they were baptized into the name of the Lord Jesus.
19.kjv: When they heard this, they were baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus.
19.blb: And having heard, they were baptized into the name of the Lord Jesus.
19.bbe: And hearing this, they had baptism in the name of the Lord Jesus.

19.msb: And when Paul laid his hands on them, the Holy Spirit came upon them, and they spoke in tongues and prophesied.
19.kjv: And when Paul had laid his hands upon them, the Holy Ghost came on them; and they spake with tongues, and prophesied.
19.blb: And Paul having laid the hands on them, the Holy Spirit came upon them, and they were speaking in tongues and prophesying.
19.bbe: And when Paul had put his hands on them, the Holy Spirit came on them; and they had the power of talking in tongues, and acting like prophets.

19.msb: There were about twelve men in all.
19.kjv: And all the men were about twelve.
19.blb: And there were in all about twelve men.
19.bbe: And there were about twelve of these men.

19.msb: Then Paul went into the synagogue and spoke boldly there for three months, arguing persuasively about the kingdom of God.
19.kjv: And he went into the synagogue, and spake boldly for the space of three months, disputing and persuading the things concerning the kingdom of God.
19.blb: And having entered into the synagogue, he was speaking boldly for three months, reasoning and persuading concerning the kingdom of God.
19.bbe: And he went into the Synagogue, and for three months he was preaching there without fear, reasoning and teaching about the kingdom of God.
19.heading: Paul Ministers in Ephesus

19.msb: But when some of them stubbornly refused to believe and publicly maligned the Way, Paul took his disciples and left the synagogue to conduct daily discussions in the lecture hall of a man named Tyrannus.
19.kjv: But when divers were hardened, and believed not, but spake evil of that way before the multitude, he departed from them, and separated the disciples, disputing daily in the school of one Tyrannus.
19.blb: But when some were hardened and were disbelieving, speaking evil of the Way before the multitude, having departed from them, he separated the disciples, reasoning every day in the lecture hall of Tyrannus.
19.bbe: But because some of the people were hard-hearted and would not give hearing, saying evil words about the Way before the people, he went away from them, and kept the disciples separate, reasoning every day in the school of Tyrannus.

19.msb: This continued for two years, so that everyone who lived in the province of Asia, Jews and Greeks alike, heard the word of the Lord Jesus.
19.kjv: And this continued by the space of two years; so that all they which dwelt in Asia heard the word of the Lord Jesus, both Jews and Greeks.
19.blb: And this continued for two years, so that all those inhabiting Asia heard the word of the Lord, both Jews and Greeks.
19.bbe: And this went on for two years, so that all those who were living in Asia had knowledge of the word of the Lord, Greeks as well as Jews.

19.msb: God did extraordinary miracles through the hands of Paul,
19.kjv: And God wrought special miracles by the hands of Paul:
19.blb: And God was doing miracles not being ordinary through the hands of Paul,
19.bbe: And God did special works of power by the hands of Paul:

19.msb: so that even handkerchiefs and aprons that had touched him were brought to the sick, and the diseases and evil spirits left them.
19.kjv: So that from his body were brought unto the sick handkerchiefs or aprons, and the diseases departed from them, and the evil spirits went out of them.
19.blb: so that even soudaria or simikinthia from his skin were brought to the ailing, and the diseases departed from them, and the evil spirits left.
19.bbe: So that bits of linen and clothing from his body were taken to people who were ill, and their diseases went away from them and the evil spirits went out.

19.msb: Now there were some itinerant Jewish exorcists who tried to invoke the name of the Lord Jesus over those with evil spirits. They would say, “I command you by Jesus, whom Paul proclaims.”
19.kjv: Then certain of the vagabond Jews, exorcists, took upon them to call over them which had evil spirits the name of the Lord Jesus, saying, We adjure you by Jesus whom Paul preacheth.
19.blb: And some of the itinerant Jews, exorcists, also attempted to invoke the name of the Lord Jesus over those having evil spirits, saying, “I adjure you by Jesus, whom Paul proclaims.”
19.bbe: But some of the Jews who went from place to place driving out evil spirits, took it on themselves to make use of the name of the Lord Jesus over those who had evil spirits, saying, I give you orders, by Jesus, whom Paul is preaching.
19.heading: Seven Sons of Sceva

19.msb: Seven sons of Sceva, a Jewish chief priest, were doing this.
19.kjv: And there were seven sons of one Sceva, a Jew, and chief of the priests, which did so.
19.blb: Now seven sons of a certain Sceva, a Jewish high priest, were doing this.
19.bbe: And there were seven sons of a man named Sceva, a Jew and a chief priest, who did this.

19.msb: But one day the evil spirit responded, “Jesus I know, and I know about Paul, but who are you?”
19.kjv: And the evil spirit answered and said, Jesus I know, and Paul I know; but who are ye?
19.blb: But the evil spirit, answering, said to them, “Jesus I know, and Paul I know about; but you, who are you?”
19.bbe: And the evil spirit, answering, said to them, I have knowledge of Jesus, and of Paul, but who are you?

19.msb: Then the man with the evil spirit jumped on them and overpowered them. The attack was so violent that they ran out of the house naked and wounded.
19.kjv: And the man in whom the evil spirit was leaped on them, and overcame them, and prevailed against them, so that they fled out of that house naked and wounded.
19.blb: And the man in whom was the evil spirit, having leapt on them, having overpowered them all, prevailed against them so that they fled out of that house naked and wounded.
19.bbe: And the man in whom the evil spirit was, jumping on them, was stronger than the two of them, and overcame them, so that they went running from that house, wounded and without their clothing.

19.msb: This became known to all the Jews and Greeks living in Ephesus, and fear came over all of them. So the name of the Lord Jesus was held in high honor.
19.kjv: And this was known to all the Jews and Greeks also dwelling at Ephesus; and fear fell on them all, and the name of the Lord Jesus was magnified.
19.blb: Now this became known to all those inhabiting Ephesus, both Jews and Greeks. And fear fell upon them all, and the name of the Lord Jesus was being magnified.
19.bbe: And this came to the ears of all those, Jews and Greeks, who were living at Ephesus; and fear came on them all, and the name of the Lord Jesus was made great.

19.msb: Many who had believed now came forward, confessing and disclosing their deeds.
19.kjv: And many that believed came, and confessed, and shewed their deeds.
19.blb: And many of those having believed were coming, confessing and declaring their deeds,
19.bbe: And a number of those who had faith came and made a public statement of their sins and all their acts.

19.msb: And a number of those who had practiced magic arts brought their books and burned them in front of everyone. When the value of the books was calculated, the total came to fifty thousand drachmas.
19.kjv: Many of them also which used curious arts brought their books together, and burned them before all men: and they counted the price of them, and found it fifty thousand pieces of silver.
19.blb: and many of those having practiced works of magic, having brought the books, burned them before all. And they counted up the prices of them and found it five myriads of silver.
19.bbe: And a great number of those who were experts in strange arts took their books and put them on the fire in front of everyone: and when the books were valued they came to fifty thousand bits of silver.

19.msb: So the word of the Lord powerfully continued to spread and prevail.
19.kjv: So mightily grew the word of God and prevailed.
19.blb: Thus the word of the Lord continued to increase and prevail with might.
19.bbe: So the word of the Lord was increased very greatly and was full of power.

19.msb: After these things had happened, Paul resolved in the Spirit to go to Jerusalem, passing through Macedonia and Achaia. “After I have been there,” he said, “I must see Rome as well.”
19.kjv: After these things were ended, Paul purposed in the spirit, when he had passed through Macedonia and Achaia, to go to Jerusalem, saying, After I have been there, I must also see Rome.
19.blb: Now after these things were fulfilled, Paul purposed in the Spirit to go to Jerusalem, having passed through Macedonia and Achaia, having said, “After my having been there, it is necessary for me to see Rome also.”
19.bbe: Now after these things were ended, Paul came to a decision that when he had gone through Macedonia and Achaia he would go to Jerusalem, saying, After I have been there, I have a desire to see Rome.
19.heading: The Riot in Ephesus

19.msb: He sent two of his helpers, Timothy and Erastus, to Macedonia, while he stayed for a time in the province of Asia.
19.kjv: So he sent into Macedonia two of them that ministered unto him, Timotheus and Erastus; but he himself stayed in Asia for a season.
19.blb: And having sent two of those ministering to him, Timothy and Erastus, into Macedonia, he remained for a time in Asia.
