19.bbe: And having sent two of his helpers, Timothy and Erastus, into Macedonia, he himself went on living in Asia for a time.

19.msb: About that time there arose a great disturbance about the Way.
19.kjv: And the same time there arose no small stir about that way.
19.blb: And there arose at the same time no little disturbance concerning the Way.
19.bbe: And about that time a great outcry took place about the Way.

19.msb: It began with a silversmith named Demetrius who made silver shrines of Artemis, bringing much business to the craftsmen.
19.kjv: For a certain man named Demetrius, a silversmith, which made silver shrines for Diana, brought no small gain unto the craftsmen;
19.blb: For a certain silversmith named Demetrius, making silver shrines of Artemis, was bringing no little business to the craftsmen.
19.bbe: For there was a certain man named Demetrius, a silver-worker, who made silver boxes for the images of Diana, and gave no small profit to the workmen;

19.msb: Demetrius assembled the craftsmen, along with the workmen in related trades. “Men,” he said, “you know that this business is our source of prosperity.
19.kjv: Whom he called together with the workmen of like occupation, and said, Sirs, ye know that by this craft we have our wealth.
19.blb: Having brought them together along with the workmen in such things, he said, “Men, you know that out of this business is our wealth.
19.bbe: Whom he got together, with other workmen of the same trade, and said to them, Men, it is clear that from this business we get our wealth.

19.msb: And you can see and hear that not only in Ephesus, but in nearly the whole province of Asia, this Paul has persuaded a great number of people to turn away. He says that man-made gods are no gods at all.
19.kjv: Moreover ye see and hear, that not alone at Ephesus, but almost throughout all Asia, this Paul hath persuaded and turned away much people, saying that they be no gods, which are made with hands:
19.blb: And you see and hear that not only in Ephesus, but in almost all of Asia, this Paul, having persuaded them, has turned away a great many people, saying that they are not gods being made by hands.
19.bbe: And you see, for it has come to your ears, that not only at Ephesus, but almost all through Asia, this Paul has been teaching numbers of people and turning them away, saying that those are not gods who are made by men's hands:

19.msb: There is danger not only that our business will fall into disrepute, but also that the temple of the great goddess Artemis will be discredited and her majesty deposed—she who is worshiped by all the province of Asia and the whole world.”
19.kjv: So that not only this our craft is in danger to be set at nought; but also that the temple of the great goddess Diana should be despised, and her magnificence should be destroyed, whom all Asia and the world worshippeth.
19.blb: Now not only is this business of ours endangered to come into disrepute, but also for the temple of the great goddess Artemis to be reckoned for nothing, and also her majesty to be deposed, whom all Asia and the world worship.”
19.bbe: And there is danger, not only that our trade may be damaged in the opinion of men, but that the holy place of the great goddess Diana may be no longer honoured, and that she to whom all Asia and the world give worship, will be put down from her high position.

19.msb: When the men heard this, they were enraged and began shouting, “Great is Artemis of the Ephesians!”
19.kjv: And when they heard these sayings, they were full of wrath, and cried out, saying, Great is Diana of the Ephesians.
19.blb: And having heard and having become full of rage, they were crying out, saying, “Great is Artemis of the Ephesians!”
19.bbe: And hearing this, they were very angry, crying out and saying, Great is Diana of Ephesus.

19.msb: Soon the whole city was in disarray. They rushed together into the theatre, dragging with them Gaius and Aristarchus, Paul’s traveling companions from Macedonia.
19.kjv: And the whole city was filled with confusion: and having caught Gaius and Aristarchus, men of Macedonia, Paul’s companions in travel, they rushed with one accord into the theatre.
19.blb: And the city was filled with confusion, and with one accord they rushed to the theatre, having dragged off Gaius and Aristarchus, Macedonians, fellow travelers of Paul.
19.bbe: And the town was full of noise and trouble, and they all came running into the theatre, having taken by force Gaius and Aristarchus, men of Macedonia who were journeying in company with Paul.

19.msb: Paul wanted to go before the assembly, but the disciples would not allow him.
19.kjv: And when Paul would have entered in unto the people, the disciples suffered him not.
19.blb: But on Paul intending to go in to the people, the disciples were not allowing him.
19.bbe: And when Paul was about to go in to the people, the disciples did not let him.

19.msb: Even some of Paul’s friends who were officials of the province of Asia sent word to him, begging him not to venture into the theatre.
19.kjv: And certain of the chief of Asia, which were his friends, sent unto him, desiring him that he would not adventure himself into the theatre.
19.blb: And also some of the Asiarchs being friends to him, having sent to him, were urging him not to venture into the theatre.
19.bbe: And some of the rulers of Asia, being his friends, sent to him, requesting him seriously not to put himself in danger by going into the theatre.

19.msb: Meanwhile the assembly was in turmoil. Some were shouting one thing and some another, and most of them did not even know why they were there.
19.kjv: Some therefore cried one thing, and some another: for the assembly was confused; and the more part knew not wherefore they were come together.
19.blb: Some indeed therefore were crying out one thing, some another. For the assembly was confused, and most did not know for what cause they were assembled.
19.bbe: And some said one thing, and some another: for there was no order in the meeting; and most of them had no idea why they had come together.

19.msb: The Jews in the crowd pushed Alexander forward, and he motioned for silence so he could make his defense to the people.
19.kjv: And they drew Alexander out of the multitude, the Jews putting him forward. And Alexander beckoned with the hand, and would have made his defence unto the people.
19.blb: And out of the crowd they put forward Alexander, the Jews having thrust him forward. And Alexander, having motioned with the hand, was wanting to make a defense to the people.
19.bbe: Then they took Alexander out from among the people, the Jews putting him forward. And Alexander, making a sign with his hand, was about to make a statement to the people in answer:

19.msb: But when they realized that he was a Jew, they all shouted in unison for about two hours: “Great is Artemis of the Ephesians!”
19.kjv: But when they knew that he was a Jew, all with one voice about the space of two hours cried out, Great is Diana of the Ephesians.
19.blb: But having recognized that he is a Jew, there was one cry from all, ongoing about two hours, crying out, “Great is Artemis of the Ephesians!”
19.bbe: But when they saw that he was a Jew, all of them with one voice went on crying out for about two hours, Great is Diana of Ephesus.

19.msb: Finally the city clerk quieted the crowd and declared, “Men of Ephesus, doesn’t everyone know that the city of Ephesus is guardian of the temple of the great goddess Artemis and of her image, which fell from heaven?
19.kjv: And when the townclerk had appeased the people, he said, Ye men of Ephesus, what man is there that knoweth not how that the city of the Ephesians is a worshipper of the great goddess Diana, and of the image which fell down from Jupiter?
19.blb: And having calmed the crowd, the town clerk says, “Men, Ephesians, what man is there indeed who does not know the city of the Ephesians as being temple-keeper of the great Artemis and of that fallen from the sky?
19.bbe: And when the chief secretary had got the people quiet, he said, Men of Ephesus, is any man without knowledge that the town of Ephesus is the keeper of the holy place of the great Diana, who was sent down from Jupiter?

19.msb: Since these things are undeniable, you ought to be calm and not do anything rash.
19.kjv: Seeing then that these things cannot be spoken against, ye ought to be quiet, and to do nothing rashly.
19.blb: Therefore, these things being undeniable, it is necessary for you to be calm and to do nothing rash.
19.bbe: So then, because these things may not be doubted, it would be better for you to be quiet, and do nothing unwise.

19.msb: For you have brought these men here, though they have neither robbed our temple nor blasphemed your goddess.
19.kjv: For ye have brought hither these men, which are neither robbers of churches, nor yet blasphemers of your goddess.
19.blb: For you brought these men, neither temple plunderers nor blaspheming our goddess.
19.bbe: For you have taken these men, who are not doing damage to the holy place or talking against our goddess.

19.msb: So if Demetrius and his fellow craftsmen have a complaint against anyone, the courts are open and proconsuls are available. Let them bring charges against one another there.
19.kjv: Wherefore if Demetrius, and the craftsmen which are with him, have a matter against any man, the law is open, and there are deputies: let them implead one another.
19.blb: Therefore if indeed Demetrius and the craftsmen with him have a matter against anyone, courts are conducted, and there are proconsuls; let them accuse one another.
19.bbe: If, then, Demetrius and the workmen who are with him have a protest to make against any man, the law is open to them, and there are judges; let them put up a cause at law against one another.

19.msb: But if you are seeking anything concerning other matters, it must be settled in a legal assembly.
19.kjv: But if ye enquire any thing concerning other matters, it shall be determined in a lawful assembly.
19.blb: But if you inquire anything beyond this, it will be solved in the lawful assembly.
19.bbe: But if any other business is in question, let it be taken up in the regular meeting.

19.msb: For we are in jeopardy of being charged with rioting for today’s events, and we have no justification to account for this commotion.”
19.kjv: For we are in danger to be called in question for this day’s uproar, there being no cause whereby we may give an account of this concourse.
19.blb: And indeed, we are in danger of being accused of insurrection concerning this day, there existing not one cause concerning which we will be able to give a reason concerning this commotion.”
19.bbe: For, truly, we are in danger of being made responsible for this day's trouble, there being no cause for it: and we are not able to give any reason for this coming together.

19.msb: After he had said this, he dismissed the assembly.
19.kjv: And when he had thus spoken, he dismissed the assembly.
19.blb: And having said these things, he dismissed the assembly.
19.bbe: And when he had said this, he sent the meeting away.

20.msb: When the uproar had ended, Paul sent for the disciples. And he said goodbye to them and left for Macedonia.
20.kjv: And after the uproar was ceased, Paul called unto him the disciples, and embraced them, and departed for to go into Macedonia.
20.blb: Now after the uproar had ceased, Paul, having summoned the disciples and having encouraged them, having said farewell, went out to go to Macedonia.
20.bbe: And after the noise had come to an end, Paul, having sent for the disciples and given them comfort, went away from them to Macedonia.
20.heading: Paul in Macedonia and Greece

20.msb: After traveling through that area and speaking many words of encouragement, he arrived in Greece,
20.kjv: And when he had gone over those parts, and had given them much exhortation, he came into Greece,
20.blb: And having passed through those districts and having exhorted them with much talk, he came to Greece.
20.bbe: And when he had gone through those parts and given them much teaching, he came into Greece.

20.msb: where he stayed three months. And when the Jews formed a plot against him as he was about to sail for Syria, he decided to go back through Macedonia.
20.kjv: And there abode three months. And when the Jews laid wait for him, as he was about to sail into Syria, he purposed to return through Macedonia.
20.blb: And having continued three months, a plot having been made against him by the Jews, he being about to sail into Syria, a purpose arose to return through Macedonia.
20.bbe: And when he had been there three months, because the Jews had made a secret design against him when he was about to take ship for Syria, he made a decision to go back through Macedonia.

20.msb: Paul was accompanied into the province of Asia by Sopater from Berea, Aristarchus and Secundus from Thessalonica, Gaius from Derbe, Timothy, and Tychicus and Trophimus from the province of Asia.
20.kjv: And there accompanied him into Asia Sopater of Berea; and of the Thessalonians, Aristarchus and Secundus; and Gaius of Derbe, and Timotheus; and of Asia, Tychicus and Trophimus.
20.blb: And he was accompanied by Sopater son of Pyrrhus, a Berean, and Aristarchus, and Secundus of the Thessalonians, and Gaius of Derbe, and Timothy, and the Asians Tychicus and Trophimus.
20.bbe: And Sopater of Beroea, the son of Pyrrhus, and Aristarchus and Secundus of Thessalonica, and Gaius of Derbe, and Timothy, and Tychicus and Trophimus of Asia, went with him as far as Asia.

20.msb: These men went on ahead and waited for us in Troas.
20.kjv: These going before tarried for us at Troas.
20.blb: But these, having gone ahead, waited for us in Troas.
20.bbe: But these had gone before, and were waiting for us at Troas.

20.msb: And after the Feast of Unleavened Bread, we sailed from Philippi, and five days later we rejoined them in Troas, where we stayed seven days.
20.kjv: And we sailed away from Philippi after the days of unleavened bread, and came unto them to Troas in five days; where we abode seven days.
20.blb: And we sailed away from Philippi after the days of the Unleavened, and within five days we came to them at Troas, where we stayed seven days.
20.bbe: And we went away from Philippi by ship after the days of unleavened bread, and came to them at Troas in five days; and we were there for seven days.

20.msb: On the first day of the week, the disciples came together to break bread. Since Paul was ready to leave the next day, he talked to them and kept on speaking until midnight.
20.kjv: And upon the first day of the week, when the disciples came together to break bread, Paul preached unto them, ready to depart on the morrow; and continued his speech until midnight.
20.blb: And on the first of the week, we having come together to break bread, Paul, about to depart on the next day, talked to them and continued the talk until midnight.
20.bbe: And on the first day of the week, when we had come together for the holy meal, Paul gave them a talk, for it was his purpose to go away on the day after; and he went on talking till after the middle of the night.
20.heading: Eutychus Revived at Troas

20.msb: Now there were many lamps in the upper room where we were gathered.
20.kjv: And there were many lights in the upper chamber, where they were gathered together.
20.blb: Now there were many lamps in the upper room where we were assembled.
20.bbe: And there were a number of lights in the room where we had come together.

20.msb: And a certain young man named Eutychus, seated in the window, was sinking into a deep sleep as Paul talked on and on. When he was sound asleep, he fell from the third story and was picked up dead.
20.kjv: And there sat in a window a certain young man named Eutychus, being fallen into a deep sleep: and as Paul was long preaching, he sunk down with sleep, and fell down from the third loft, and was taken up dead.
20.blb: And a certain young man named Eutychus was sitting by the window, overcome by deep sleep, Paul talking on longer. Having been overcome by sleep, he fell down from the third story and was picked up dead.
20.bbe: And a certain young man named Eutychus, who was seated in the window, went into a deep sleep; and while Paul went on talking, being overcome by sleep, he had a fall from the third floor, and was taken up dead.

20.msb: But Paul went down, threw himself on the young man, and embraced him. “Do not be alarmed!” he said. “He is still alive!”
20.kjv: And Paul went down, and fell on him, and embracing him said, Trouble not yourselves; for his life is in him.
20.blb: But Paul, having descended, fell upon him, and having embraced him, he said, “Do not be alarmed, for his life is in him!”
20.bbe: And Paul went down and, falling on him, took him in his arms and said, Do not be troubled, for his life is in him.

20.msb: Then Paul went back upstairs, broke bread, and ate. And after speaking until daybreak, he departed.
20.kjv: When he therefore was come up again, and had broken bread, and eaten, and talked a long while, even till break of day, so he departed.
20.blb: And having gone up, and having broken the bread, and having eaten, and having talked for a considerable time until daybreak, so he went out.
20.bbe: And when he had gone up, and had taken the broken bread, he went on talking to them for a long time, even till dawn, and then he went away.

20.msb: And the people were greatly relieved to take the boy home alive.
20.kjv: And they brought the young man alive, and were not a little comforted.
20.blb: Then they brought the boy alive and were not just a little comforted.
20.bbe: And they took the boy in, living, and were greatly comforted.

20.msb: We went to the ship and sailed to Assos, where we were to take Paul aboard. He had arranged this because he was going there on foot.
20.kjv: And we went before to ship, and sailed unto Assos, there intending to take in Paul: for so had he appointed, minding himself to go afoot.
20.blb: But we, having gone ahead to the ship, sailed to Assos, being about to take in Paul there. For having arranged thus, he was readying himself to go on foot.
20.bbe: But we, going before him by ship, went to Assos with the purpose of taking Paul in there: for so he had given orders, because he himself was coming by land.
20.heading: From Troas to Miletus

20.msb: And when he met us at Assos, we took him aboard and went on to Mitylene.
20.kjv: And when he met with us at Assos, we took him in, and came to Mitylene.
20.blb: And when he met with us at Assos, having taken him in, we came to Mitylene.
20.bbe: And when he came up with us at Assos, we took him in the ship and went on to Mitylene.

20.msb: Sailing on from there, we arrived the next day opposite Chios. The day after that we arrived at Samos. And after remaining at Trogyllium, on the following day we came to Miletus.
20.kjv: And we sailed thence, and came the next day over against Chios; and the next day we arrived at Samos, and tarried at Trogyllium; and the next day we came to Miletus.
20.blb: And having sailed away from there, the next day we arrived opposite Chios, and the second day we arrived at Samos, and the following day we came to Miletus.
20.bbe: And going from there by sea, we came on the day after opposite Chios, and touching at Samos on the day after that, we came on the third day to Miletus.

20.msb: Paul had decided to sail past Ephesus to avoid spending time in the province of Asia, because he was in a hurry to reach Jerusalem, if possible, by the day of Pentecost.
20.kjv: For Paul had determined to sail by Ephesus, because he would not spend the time in Asia: for he hasted, if it were possible for him, to be at Jerusalem the day of Pentecost.
20.blb: For Paul had decided to sail by Ephesus, so that it might not come upon him to spend time in Asia; for he was hastening, if it was possible for him, to be in Jerusalem on the day of Pentecost.
20.bbe: For Paul's purpose was to go past Ephesus, so that he might not be kept in Asia; for he was going quickly, in order, if possible, to be at Jerusalem on the day of Pentecost.

20.msb: From Miletus, Paul sent to Ephesus for the elders of the church.
20.kjv: And from Miletus he sent to Ephesus, and called the elders of the church.
20.blb: And from Miletus, having sent to Ephesus, he called for the elders of the church.
20.bbe: And from Miletus he sent to Ephesus for the rulers of the church.
20.heading: Paul’s Farewell to the Ephesians

20.msb: When they came to him, he said, “You know how I lived the whole time I was with you, from the first day I arrived in the province of Asia.
20.kjv: And when they were come to him, he said unto them, Ye know, from the first day that I came into Asia, after what manner I have been with you at all seasons,
20.blb: And when they had come to him, he said to them, “You know from the first day on which I arrived in Asia, how I was with you the whole time,
20.bbe: And when they had come, he said to them, You yourselves have seen what my life has been like all the time from the day when I first came into Asia,

20.msb: I served the Lord with great humility and with many tears, especially in the trials that came upon me through the plots of the Jews.
20.kjv: Serving the Lord with all humility of mind, and with many tears, and temptations, which befell me by the lying in wait of the Jews:
20.blb: serving the Lord with all humility and tears, and in trials having befallen me in the plots of the Jews;
20.bbe: Doing the Lord's work without pride, through all the sorrow and troubles which came on me because of the evil designs of the Jews:

20.msb: I did not shrink back from declaring anything that was helpful to you as I taught you publicly and from house to house,
20.kjv: And how I kept back nothing that was profitable unto you, but have shewed you, and have taught you publickly, and from house to house,
20.blb: how I kept back nothing of that being profitable, to declare it to you and to teach you publicly and from house to house,
20.bbe: And how I kept back nothing which might be of profit to you, teaching you publicly and privately,

20.msb: testifying to Jews and Greeks alike about repentance to God and faith in our Lord Jesus.
20.kjv: Testifying both to the Jews, and also to the Greeks, repentance toward God, and faith toward our Lord Jesus Christ.
20.blb: earnestly testifying both to the Jews and to the Greeks repentance to God and faith in our Lord Jesus Christ.
20.bbe: Preaching to Jews and to Greeks the need for a turning of the heart to God, and faith in the Lord Jesus Christ.

20.msb: And now, compelled by the Spirit, I am going to Jerusalem, not knowing what will happen to me there.
20.kjv: And now, behold, I go bound in the spirit unto Jerusalem, not knowing the things that shall befall me there:
20.blb: And now behold, bound in the Spirit I go to Jerusalem, not knowing what will happen to me in it,
20.bbe: And now, as you see, I am going to Jerusalem, a prisoner in spirit, having no knowledge of what will come to me there:

20.msb: I only know that in town after town the Holy Spirit warns that chains and afflictions await me.
20.kjv: Save that the Holy Ghost witnesseth in every city, saying that bonds and afflictions abide me.
20.blb: except that the Holy Spirit fully testifies to me in every city, saying that chains and tribulations await me.
20.bbe: Only that the Holy Spirit makes clear to me in every town that prison and pains are waiting for me.

20.msb: But I consider my life of no value to me, if only I may finish my course with joy and complete the ministry I have received from the Lord Jesus—the ministry of testifying to the good news of God’s grace.
20.kjv: But none of these things move me, neither count I my life dear unto myself, so that I might finish my course with joy, and the ministry, which I have received of the Lord Jesus, to testify the gospel of the grace of God.
20.blb: But on no account do I make my life dear to myself, so as to finish my course and the ministry that I received from the Lord Jesus: to testify fully to the gospel of the grace of God.
20.bbe: But I put no value on my life, if only at the end of it I may see the work complete which was given to me by the Lord Jesus, to be a witness of the good news of the grace of God.

20.msb: Now I know that none of you among whom I have preached the kingdom of God will see my face again.
20.kjv: And now, behold, I know that ye all, among whom I have gone preaching the kingdom of God, shall see my face no more.
20.blb: And now, behold, I know that all of you among whom I went about proclaiming the kingdom will see my face no more.
20.bbe: And now I am conscious that you, among whom I have gone about preaching the kingdom, will not see my face again.

20.msb: Therefore I testify to you this day that I am innocent of the blood of all men.
20.kjv: Wherefore I take you to record this day, that I am pure from the blood of all men.
20.blb: Therefore I testify to you in this day that I am innocent of the blood of all.
20.bbe: And so I say to you this day that I am clean from the blood of all men.

20.msb: For I did not shrink back from declaring to you the whole will of God.
20.kjv: For I have not shunned to declare unto you all the counsel of God.
20.blb: For I did not shrink back from proclaiming to you the whole counsel of God.
20.bbe: For I have not kept back from you anything of the purpose of God.

20.msb: Therefore keep watch over yourselves and the entire flock of which the Holy Spirit has made you overseers. Be shepherds of the church of the Lord and God, which He purchased with His own blood.
20.kjv: Take heed therefore unto yourselves, and to all the flock, over the which the Holy Ghost hath made you overseers, to feed the church of God, which he hath purchased with his own blood.
20.blb: Take heed to yourselves and to all the flock among whom the Holy Spirit has set you as overseers, to shepherd the church of God, which He purchased with His own blood.
20.bbe: Give attention to yourselves, and to all the flock which the Holy Spirit has given into your care, to give food to the church of God, for which he gave his blood.

20.msb: For I know this, that after my departure, savage wolves will come in among you and will not spare the flock.
20.kjv: For I know this, that after my departing shall grievous wolves enter in among you, not sparing the flock.
20.blb: I have known that after my departure, grievous wolves will come in among you, not sparing the flock,
20.bbe: I am conscious that after I am gone, evil wolves will come in among you, doing damage to the flock;

20.msb: Even from your own number, men will rise up and distort the truth to draw away disciples after them.
20.kjv: Also of your own selves shall men arise, speaking perverse things, to draw away disciples after them.
20.blb: and out from your own selves men will rise up, speaking perverse things to draw away disciples after them.
20.bbe: And from among yourselves will come men who will give wrong teaching, turning away the disciples after them.

20.msb: Therefore be alert and remember that for three years I never stopped warning each of you night and day with tears.
20.kjv: Therefore watch, and remember, that by the space of three years I ceased not to warn every one night and day with tears.
20.blb: Therefore stay awake, remembering that three years, night and day, I did not cease admonishing each one with tears.
20.bbe: So keep watch, having in mind that for three years without resting I was teaching every one of you, day and night, with weeping.

20.msb: And now I commit you, brothers, to God and to the word of His grace, which can build you up and give you an inheritance among all who are sanctified.
20.kjv: And now, brethren, I commend you to God, and to the word of his grace, which is able to build you up, and to give you an inheritance among all them which are sanctified.
20.blb: And now I commit you to God and to the word of His grace, being able to build you up and to give you an inheritance among all those having been sanctified.
20.bbe: And now, I give you into the care of God and the word of his grace, which is able to make you strong and to give you your heritage among all the saints.

20.msb: I have not coveted anyone’s silver or gold or clothing.
20.kjv: I have coveted no man’s silver, or gold, or apparel.
20.blb: I coveted no one’s silver or gold or clothing.
20.bbe: I have had no desire for any man's silver or gold or clothing.

20.msb: You yourselves know that these hands of mine have ministered to my own needs and those of my companions.
20.kjv: Yea, ye yourselves know, that these hands have ministered unto my necessities, and to them that were with me.
20.blb: You yourselves know that these hands ministered to my needs and to those being with me.
20.bbe: You yourselves have seen that with these hands I got what was necessary for me and those who were with me.

20.msb: In everything, I showed you that by this kind of hard work we must help the weak, remembering the words of the Lord Jesus Himself: ‘It is more blessed to give than to receive.’”
20.kjv: I have shewed you all things, how that so labouring ye ought to support the weak, and to remember the words of the Lord Jesus, how he said, It is more blessed to give than to receive.
20.blb: In everything I showed you that by thus laboring, it is necessary to aid those being weak, and also to remember the words of the Lord Jesus, how He Himself said, ‘It is more blessed to give than to receive.’”
20.bbe: In all things I was an example to you of how, in your lives, you are to give help to the feeble, and keep in memory the words of the Lord Jesus, how he himself said, There is a greater blessing in giving than in getting.

20.msb: When Paul had said this, he knelt down with all of them and prayed.
20.kjv: And when he had thus spoken, he kneeled down, and prayed with them all.
20.blb: And having said these things, having bowed his knee, he prayed with them all.
20.bbe: And having said these words, he went down on his knees in prayer with them all.

20.msb: They all wept openly as they embraced Paul and kissed him.
20.kjv: And they all wept sore, and fell on Paul’s neck, and kissed him,
20.blb: Then there was much weeping among all, and having fallen upon the neck of Paul, they were kissing him,
20.bbe: And they were all weeping, falling on Paul's neck and kissing him,

20.msb: They were especially grieved by his statement that they would never see his face again. Then they accompanied him to the ship.
20.kjv: Sorrowing most of all for the words which he spake, that they should see his face no more. And they accompanied him unto the ship.
20.blb: sorrowing especially over the word that he had spoken, that they are about to see his face no more. And they accompanied him to the ship.
20.bbe: Being sad most of all because he had said that they would not see his face again. And so they went with him to the ship.

21.msb: After we had torn ourselves away from them, we sailed directly to Cos, and the next day on to Rhodes, and from there to Patara.
21.kjv: And it came to pass, that after we were gotten from them, and had launched, we came with a straight course unto Coos, and the day following unto Rhodes, and from thence unto Patara:
21.blb: And it happened that after having drawn away from them, having run directly in our sailing, we came to Cos, and the next day to Rhodes, and from there to Patara.
21.bbe: And after parting from them, we put out to sea and came straight to Cos, and the day after to Rhodes, and from there to Patara:
21.heading: Paul’s Journey to Jerusalem

21.msb: Finding a ship crossing over to Phoenicia, we boarded it and set sail.
21.kjv: And finding a ship sailing over unto Phenicia, we went aboard, and set forth.
21.blb: And having found a boat passing over into Phoenicia, having gone aboard, we set sail.
21.bbe: And as there was a ship going to Phoenicia, we went in it.

21.msb: After sighting Cyprus and passing south of it, we sailed on to Syria and landed at Tyre, where the ship was to unload its cargo.
21.kjv: Now when we had discovered Cyprus, we left it on the left hand, and sailed into Syria, and landed at Tyre: for there the ship was to unlade her burden.
21.blb: And having sighted Cyprus and having left it on the left, we kept sailing to Syria and landed at Tyre, for the ship was unloading the cargo there.
21.bbe: And when we had come in view of Cyprus, going past it on our left, we went on to Syria, and came to land at Tyre: for there the goods which were in the ship had to be taken out.

21.msb: We sought out disciples in Tyre and stayed with them seven days. Through the Spirit they kept telling Paul not to go up to Jerusalem.
21.kjv: And finding disciples, we tarried there seven days: who said to Paul through the Spirit, that he should not go up to Jerusalem.
21.blb: And we remained there seven days, having sought out the disciples, who kept saying to Paul through the Spirit not to go up to Jerusalem.
21.bbe: And meeting the disciples we were there for seven days: and they gave Paul orders through the Spirit not to go up to Jerusalem.

21.msb: But when our time there had ended, we set out on our journey. All the disciples, with their wives and children, accompanied us out of the city and knelt down on the beach to pray with us.
21.kjv: And when we had accomplished those days, we departed and went our way; and they all brought us on our way, with wives and children, till we were out of the city: and we kneeled down on the shore, and prayed.
21.blb: And it happened that when we had completed the days, having gone out, we journeyed, all accompanying us, with wives and children, as far as outside the city. And having bowed the knees on the shore, having prayed,
21.bbe: And when these days came to an end, we went on our journey; and they all, with their wives and children, came with us on our way till we were out of the town: and after going on our knees in prayer by the sea,

21.msb: And after we had said our farewells, we went aboard the ship, and they returned home.
21.kjv: And when we had taken our leave one of another, we took ship; and they returned home again.
21.blb: having said farewell to one another, we then went up into the boat, and they returned to their own.
21.bbe: We said our last words to one another, and got into the ship, and they went back to their houses.

21.msb: When we had finished our voyage from Tyre, we landed at Ptolemais, where we greeted the brothers and stayed with them for a day.
21.kjv: And when we had finished our course from Tyre, we came to Ptolemais, and saluted the brethren, and abode with them one day.
21.blb: And having completed the voyage from Tyre, we came down to Ptolemais; and having greeted the brothers, we stayed one day with them.
21.bbe: And journeying by ship from Tyre we came to Ptolemais; and there we had talk with the brothers and were with them for one day.

21.msb: Leaving the next day, Paul and his companions went on to Caesarea and stayed at the home of Philip the evangelist, who was one of the Seven.
21.kjv: And the next day we that were of Paul’s company departed, and came unto Cæsarea: and we entered into the house of Philip the evangelist, which was one of the seven; and abode with him.
21.blb: And having gone out on the next day, we came to Caesarea; and having entered into the house of Philip the evangelist, being of the Seven, we stayed with him.
21.bbe: And on the day after, we went away and came to Caesarea, where we were guests in the house of Philip, the preacher, who was one of the seven.
21.heading: Paul Visits Philip the Evangelist

21.msb: He had four unmarried daughters who prophesied.
21.kjv: And the same man had four daughters, virgins, which did prophesy.
21.blb: And with this man there were four daughters, virgins, prophesying.
21.bbe: And he had four daughters, virgins, who were prophets.

21.msb: After we had been there several days, a prophet named Agabus came down from Judea.
21.kjv: And as we tarried there many days, there came down from Judæa a certain prophet, named Agabus.
21.blb: And in our remaining many days, a certain prophet named Agabus came down from Judea.
21.bbe: And while we were waiting there for some days, a certain prophet, named Agabus, came down from Judaea.

21.msb: Coming over to us, he took Paul’s belt, bound his own feet and hands, and said, “The Holy Spirit says: ‘In this way the Jews of Jerusalem will bind the owner of this belt and hand him over to the Gentiles.’”
21.kjv: And when he was come unto us, he took Paul’s girdle, and bound his own hands and feet, and said, Thus saith the Holy Ghost, So shall the Jews at Jerusalem bind the man that owneth this girdle, and shall deliver him into the hands of the Gentiles.
21.blb: And having come to us and having taken Paul’s belt, having bound his feet and hands, he said, “Thus the Holy Spirit says, ‘In this way the Jews in Jerusalem will bind the man whose belt this is, and they will deliver him into the hands of the Gentiles.’”
21.bbe: And he came to us, and took the band of Paul's clothing, and putting it round his feet and hands, said, The Holy Spirit says these words, So will the Jews do to the man who is the owner of this band, and they will give him up into the hands of the Gentiles.

21.msb: When we heard this, we and the people there pleaded with Paul not to go up to Jerusalem.
21.kjv: And when we heard these things, both we, and they of that place, besought him not to go up to Jerusalem.
21.blb: And when we had heard these things, both we and those of that place were begging him not to go up to Jerusalem.
21.bbe: And hearing these things, we and those who were living in that place made request to him not to go to Jerusalem.

21.msb: Then Paul answered, “Why are you weeping and breaking my heart? I am ready not only to be bound, but also to die in Jerusalem for the name of the Lord Jesus.”
21.kjv: Then Paul answered, What mean ye to weep and to break mine heart? for I am ready not to be bound only, but also to die at Jerusalem for the name of the Lord Jesus.
21.blb: Then Paul answered, “What are you doing, weeping and breaking my heart? For I have readiness not only to be bound, but also to die at Jerusalem for the name of the Lord Jesus.”
21.bbe: Then Paul said, What are you doing, weeping and wounding my heart? for I am ready, not only to be a prisoner, but to be put to death at Jerusalem for the name of the Lord Jesus.

21.msb: When he would not be dissuaded, we quieted down and said, “The Lord’s will be done.”
21.kjv: And when he would not be persuaded, we ceased, saying, The will of the Lord be done.
21.blb: And he not being persuaded, we were silent, having said, “The will of the Lord be done.”
21.bbe: And as he might not be moved we did no more, saying, Let the purpose of God be done.

21.msb: After these days, we packed up and went on to Jerusalem.
21.kjv: And after those days we took up our carriages, and went up to Jerusalem.
21.blb: And after these days, having packed the baggage, we were going up to Jerusalem.
21.bbe: And after these days we got ready and went up to Jerusalem.

21.msb: Some of the disciples from Caesarea accompanied us, and they took us to stay at the home of Mnason the Cypriot, an early disciple.
21.kjv: There went with us also certain of the disciples of Cæsarea, and brought with them one Mnason of Cyprus, an old disciple, with whom we should lodge.
21.blb: And some of the disciples from Caesarea also went with us, bringing a certain Mnason, a Cypriot, an early disciple with whom we would lodge.
21.bbe: And some of the disciples from Caesarea went with us, taking a certain Mnason of Cyprus, one of the early disciples, in whose house we were to be living.

21.msb: When we arrived in Jerusalem, the brothers welcomed us joyfully.
21.kjv: And when we were come to Jerusalem, the brethren received us gladly.
21.blb: Now of us having arrived at Jerusalem, the brothers received us gladly.
21.bbe: And when we came to Jerusalem, the brothers were pleased to see us.
21.heading: Paul’s Arrival at Jerusalem

21.msb: The next day Paul went in with us to see James, and all the elders were present.
21.kjv: And the day following Paul went in with us unto James; and all the elders were present.
21.blb: And on the following day, Paul went in with us to James, and all the elders arrived.
21.bbe: And on the day after, Paul went with us to James, and all the rulers of the church were present.

21.msb: Paul greeted them and recounted one by one the things that God had done among the Gentiles through his ministry.
21.kjv: And when he had saluted them, he declared particularly what things God had wrought among the Gentiles by his ministry.
21.blb: And having greeted them, he began to relate, one by one, each of the things God had done among the Gentiles through his ministry.
21.bbe: And when he had said how glad he was to see them, he gave them a detailed account of the things which God had done through his work among the Gentiles.

21.msb: When they heard this, they glorified the Lord. Then they said to Paul, “You see, brother, how many thousands of Jews have believed, and all of them are zealous for the law.
21.kjv: And when they heard it, they glorified the Lord, and said unto him, Thou seest, brother, how many thousands of Jews there are which believe; and they are all zealous of the law:
21.blb: And those having heard were glorifying God, and they said to him, “You see, brother, how many myriads there are among the Jews having believed, and they are all zealous ones of the law.
21.bbe: And hearing it, they gave praise to God; and they said to him, You see, brother, what thousands there are among the Jews, who have the faith; and they all have a great respect for the law:

21.msb: But they are under the impression that you teach all the Jews who live among the Gentiles to forsake Moses, telling them not to circumcise their children or observe our customs.
21.kjv: And they are informed of thee, that thou teachest all the Jews which are among the Gentiles to forsake Moses, saying that they ought not to circumcise their children, neither to walk after the customs.
21.blb: Now they have been informed about you that you teach all Jews among the Gentiles apostasy from Moses, telling them not to circumcise the children nor to walk in the customs.
21.bbe: And they have had news of you, how you have been teaching all the Jews among the Gentiles to give up the law of Moses, and not to give circumcision to their children, and not to keep the old rules.

21.msb: What then should we do? Certainly a multitude will gather, for they will hear that you have come.
21.kjv: What is it therefore? the multitude must needs come together: for they will hear that thou art come.
21.blb: What then is it? Certainly they will hear that you have come.
21.bbe: What then is the position? They will certainly get news that you have come.

21.msb: Therefore do what we advise you. There are four men with us who have taken a vow.
21.kjv: Do therefore this that we say to thee: We have four men which have a vow on them;
21.blb: Therefore do this that we say to you. With us there are four men having a vow on themselves.
21.bbe: Do this, then, which we say to you: We have four men who have taken an oath;

21.msb: Take these men, purify yourself along with them, and pay their expenses so they can have their heads shaved. Then everyone will know that there is no truth to these rumors about you, but that you also live in obedience to the law.
21.kjv: Them take, and purify thyself with them, and be at charges with them, that they may shave their heads: and all may know that those things, whereof they were informed concerning thee, are nothing; but that thou thyself also walkest orderly, and keepest the law.
21.blb: Having taken these, be purified with them and bear expense for them, so that they will shave the head. And all will know that what they have been informed about you is nothing, but that you yourself also walk orderly, keeping the law.
21.bbe: Go with these, and make yourself clean with them, and make the necessary payments for them, so that they may be free from their oath: and everyone will see that the statements made about you are not true, but that you put yourself under rule, and keep the law.

21.msb: As for the Gentile believers, we have written to them our decision that they should observe no such thing, except that they must abstain from food sacrificed to idols, from blood, from the meat of strangled animals, and from sexual immorality.”
21.kjv: As touching the Gentiles which believe, we have written and concluded that they observe no such thing, save only that they keep themselves from things offered to idols, and from blood, and from strangled, and from fornication.
21.blb: Now concerning those of the Gentiles having believed, we wrote, having adjudged, to keep themselves from both the things sacrificed to idols and blood, and from what is strangled and sexual immorality.”
21.bbe: But as to the Gentiles who have the faith, we sent a letter, giving our decision that they were to keep themselves from offerings made to false gods, and from blood, and from the flesh of animals put to death in ways against the law, and from the evil desires of the body.

21.msb: So the next day Paul took the men and purified himself along with them. Then he entered the temple to give notice of the date when their purification would be complete and the offering would be made for each of them.
21.kjv: Then Paul took the men, and the next day purifying himself with them entered into the temple, to signify the accomplishment of the days of purification, until that an offering should be offered for every one of them.
21.blb: Then Paul, having taken the men on the following day, having been purified with them, entered into the temple, declaring the fulfillment of the days of the purification until the offering was offered for each one of them.
21.bbe: Then Paul took the men, and on the day after, making himself clean with them, he went into the Temple, giving out the statement that the days necessary for making them clean were complete, till the offering was made for every one of them.

21.msb: When the seven days were almost over, some Jews from the province of Asia saw Paul at the temple. They stirred up the whole crowd and seized him,
21.kjv: And when the seven days were almost ended, the Jews which were of Asia, when they saw him in the temple, stirred up all the people, and laid hands on him,
21.blb: Now when the seven days were about to be completed, the Jews from Asia, having seen him in the temple, began stirring up all the crowd, and they laid the hands upon him,
21.bbe: And when the seven days were almost ended, the Jews from Asia, seeing him in the Temple, got the people together and put their hands on him,
21.heading: Paul Seized at the Temple

21.msb: crying out, “Men of Israel, help us! This is the man who teaches everyone everywhere against our people and against our law and against this place. Furthermore, he has brought Greeks into the temple and defiled this holy place.”
21.kjv: Crying out, Men of Israel, help: This is the man, that teacheth all men every where against the people, and the law, and this place: and further brought Greeks also into the temple, and hath polluted this holy place.
21.blb: crying out, “Men, Israelites, help! This is the man who is teaching all those everywhere against the people and the law and this place. And besides, he has also brought Greeks into the temple and defiled this holy place.”
21.bbe: Crying out, Men of Israel, come to our help: this is the man who is teaching all men everywhere against the people and the law and this place: and in addition, he has taken Greeks into the Temple, and made this holy place unclean.

21.msb: For they had seen Trophimus the Ephesian with him in the city, and they assumed that Paul had brought him into the temple.
21.kjv: (For they had seen before with him in the city Trophimus an Ephesian, whom they supposed that Paul had brought into the temple.)
21.blb: For it was they having previously seen Trophimus the Ephesian in the city with him, whom they were supposing that Paul had brought into the temple.
21.bbe: For they had seen him before in the town with Trophimus of Ephesus, and had the idea that Paul had taken him with him into the Temple.

21.msb: The whole city was stirred up, and the people rushed together. They seized Paul and dragged him out of the temple, and at once the gates were shut.
21.kjv: And all the city was moved, and the people ran together: and they took Paul, and drew him out of the temple: and forthwith the doors were shut.
21.blb: And the whole city was provoked, and there was a rushing together of the people. And having laid hold of Paul, they dragged him outside the temple, and immediately the doors were shut.
21.bbe: And all the town was moved, and the people came running together and put their hands on Paul, pulling him out of the Temple: and then the doors were shut.

21.msb: While they were trying to kill him, the commander of the Roman regiment received a report that all Jerusalem was in turmoil.
21.kjv: And as they went about to kill him, tidings came unto the chief captain of the band, that all Jerusalem was in an uproar.
21.blb: And in their seeking to kill him, a report came to the commander of the cohort that all Jerusalem was in an uproar,
21.bbe: And while they were attempting to put him to death, news came to the chief captain of the band that all Jerusalem was out of control.

21.msb: Immediately he took some soldiers and centurions and ran down to the crowd. When the people saw the commander and the soldiers, they stopped beating Paul.
21.kjv: Who immediately took soldiers and centurions, and ran down unto them: and when they saw the chief captain and the soldiers, they left beating of Paul.
21.blb: who at once, having taken with him soldiers and centurions, ran down upon them. And having seen the commander and the soldiers, they stopped beating Paul.
21.bbe: And straight away he took some armed men and went quickly down to them: and the Jews, seeing them, gave no more blows to Paul.

21.msb: The commander came up and arrested Paul, ordering that he be bound with two chains. Then he asked who he was and what he had done.
21.kjv: Then the chief captain came near, and took him, and commanded him to be bound with two chains; and demanded who he was, and what he had done.
21.blb: Then having drawn near, the commander laid hold of him and commanded him to be bound with two chains, and he began inquiring who he might be and what it is he has been doing.
21.bbe: Then the chief captain came near and took him, and gave orders for him to be put in chains, questioning them as to who he was and what he had done.

21.msb: Some in the crowd were crying out one thing, and some another. And since the commander could not get at the truth because of the uproar, he ordered that Paul be brought into the barracks.
21.kjv: And some cried one thing, some another, among the multitude: and when he could not know the certainty for the tumult, he commanded him to be carried into the castle.
21.blb: They were crying out in the crowd one thing, but others another. And he, not being able to know the facts on account of the uproar, ordered him to be brought into the barracks.
21.bbe: And some said one thing and some another, among the people: and as he was not able to get a knowledge of the facts because of the noise, he gave orders for Paul to be taken into the army building.

21.msb: When Paul reached the steps, he had to be carried by the soldiers because of the violence of the mob.
21.kjv: And when he came upon the stairs, so it was, that he was borne of the soldiers for the violence of the people.
21.blb: And when he came to the stairs, it happened that he was carried by the soldiers because of the violence of the crowd.
21.bbe: And when he came on to the steps, he was lifted up by the armed men, because of the force of the people;

21.msb: For the crowd that followed him kept shouting, “Away with him!”
21.kjv: For the multitude of the people followed after, crying, Away with him.
21.blb: For the multitude of the people were following, crying out, “Away with him!”
21.bbe: For a great mass of people came after them, crying out, Away with him!

21.msb: As they were about to take Paul into the barracks, he asked the commander, “May I speak to you?” “Do you speak Greek?” he replied.
21.kjv: And as Paul was to be led into the castle, he said unto the chief captain, May I speak unto thee? Who said, Canst thou speak Greek?
21.blb: And being about to be brought into the barracks, Paul says to the commander, “Is it permitted to me to say something to you?” And he was saying, “Do you know Greek?
21.bbe: And when Paul was about to be taken into the building, he said to the chief captain, May I say something to you? And he said, Have you a knowledge of Greek?
21.heading: Paul Addresses the Crowd

21.msb: “Aren’t you the Egyptian who incited a rebellion some time ago and led four thousand members of the Assassins into the wilderness?”
21.kjv: Art not thou that Egyptian, which before these days madest an uproar, and leddest out into the wilderness four thousand men that were murderers?
21.blb: Are you not, then, the Egyptian, the one before these days having led a revolt and having led out into the wilderness the four thousand men of the Assassins?”
21.bbe: Are you by chance the Egyptian who, before this, got the people worked up against the government and took four thousand men of the Assassins out into the waste land?

21.msb: But Paul answered, “I am a Jew from Tarsus in Cilicia, a citizen of no ordinary city. Now I beg you to allow me to speak to the people.”
21.kjv: But Paul said, I am a man which am a Jew of Tarsus, a city in Cilicia, a citizen of no mean city: and, I beseech thee, suffer me to speak unto the people.
21.blb: But Paul said, “I am indeed a Jew, a man of Tarsus of Cilicia, a citizen of no insignificant city. Now I implore you, allow me to speak to the people.”
21.bbe: But Paul said, I am a Jew of Tarsus in Cilicia, which is not an unimportant town: I make a request to you to let me say a word to the people.

21.msb: Having received permission, Paul stood on the steps and motioned to the crowd. A great hush came over the crowd, and he addressed them in Hebrew:
21.kjv: And when he had given him licence, Paul stood on the stairs, and beckoned with the hand unto the people. And when there was made a great silence, he spake unto them in the Hebrew tongue, saying,
21.blb: And he having allowed him, Paul, having stood on the stairs, made a sign with the hand to the people. And a great silence having taken place, he spoke to them in the Hebrew language, saying:
21.bbe: And when he let him do so, Paul, from the steps, made a sign with his hand to the people, and when they were all quiet, he said to them in the Hebrew language,

22.msb: “Brothers and fathers, listen now to my defense before you.”
22.kjv: Men, brethren, and fathers, hear ye my defence which I make now unto you.
22.blb: “Men, brothers and fathers, hear now my defense to you.”
22.bbe: My brothers and fathers, give ear to the story of my life which I now put before you.
22.heading: Paul’s Defense to the Crowd

22.msb: When they heard him speak to them in Hebrew, they became even more quiet. Then Paul declared,
22.kjv: (And when they heard that he spake in the Hebrew tongue to them, they kept the more silence: and he saith,)
22.blb: And having heard that he was addressing them in the Hebrew language, they became even more quiet. And he says,
22.bbe: And, hearing him talking in the Hebrew language, they became the more quiet, and he said,

22.msb: “I am indeed a Jew, born in Tarsus of Cilicia, but raised in this city. I was educated at the feet of Gamaliel in strict conformity to the law of our fathers. I was just as zealous for God as any of you are today.
22.kjv: I am verily a man which am a Jew, born in Tarsus, a city in Cilicia, yet brought up in this city at the feet of Gamaliel, and taught according to the perfect manner of the law of the fathers, and was zealous toward God, as ye all are this day.
22.blb: “I am a man, a Jew, born in Tarsus of Cilicia and brought up in this city at the feet of Gamaliel, having been educated according to the exactness of the law of our fathers, being a zealous one of God, even as all of you are this day,
22.bbe: I am a Jew of Tarsus in Cilicia by birth, but I had my education in this town at the feet of Gamaliel, being trained in the keeping of every detail of the law of our fathers; given up to the cause of God with all my heart, as you are today.

22.msb: I persecuted this Way even to the death, detaining both men and women and throwing them into prison,
22.kjv: And I persecuted this way unto the death, binding and delivering into prisons both men and women.
22.blb: who persecuted this Way as far as death, binding and delivering to prisons both men and women,
22.bbe: And I made attacks on this Way, even to death, taking men and women and putting them in prison.

22.msb: as the high priest and the whole Council can testify about me. I even obtained letters from them to their brothers in Damascus, and I was on my way to apprehend these people and bring them to Jerusalem to be punished.
22.kjv: As also the high priest doth bear me witness, and all the estate of the elders: from whom also I received letters unto the brethren, and went to Damascus, to bring them which were there bound unto Jerusalem, for to be punished.
22.blb: as also the high priest—and all the elderhood—testifies to me, from whom also having received letters to the brothers, I was going to Damascus to bring also those being there bound to Jerusalem so that they might be punished.
22.bbe: Of which the high priest will be a witness, and all the rulers, from whom I had letters to the brothers; and I went into Damascus, to take those who were there as prisoners to Jerusalem for punishment.

22.msb: About noon as I was approaching Damascus, suddenly a bright light from heaven flashed around me.
22.kjv: And it came to pass, that, as I made my journey, and was come nigh unto Damascus about noon, suddenly there shone from heaven a great light round about me.
22.blb: But it happened to me, journeying and drawing near to Damascus about noon, that suddenly a great light out of heaven shone around me,
22.bbe: And it came about that while I was on my journey, coming near to Damascus, about the middle of the day, suddenly I saw a great light from heaven shining round me.

22.msb: I fell to the ground and heard a voice say to me, ‘Saul, Saul, why do you persecute Me?’
22.kjv: And I fell unto the ground, and heard a voice saying unto me, Saul, Saul, why persecutest thou me?
22.blb: and I fell to the ground and heard a voice saying to me, ‘Saul, Saul, why do you persecute Me?’
22.bbe: And when I went down on the earth, a voice came to my ears saying to me, Saul, Saul, why are you attacking me so cruelly?

22.msb: ‘Who are You, Lord?’ I asked. ‘I am Jesus of Nazareth, whom you are persecuting,’ He replied.
22.kjv: And I answered, Who art thou, Lord? And he said unto me, I am Jesus of Nazareth, whom thou persecutest.
22.blb: And I answered, ‘Who are You, Lord?’ And He said to me, ‘I am Jesus of Nazareth, whom you are persecuting.’
22.bbe: And I, answering, said, Who are you; Lord? And he said to me, I am Jesus of Nazareth, whom you are attacking.

22.msb: My companions saw the light and were terrified, but they could not understand the voice of the One speaking to me.
22.kjv: And they that were with me saw indeed the light, and were afraid; but they heard not the voice of him that spake to me.
22.blb: And those being with me indeed saw the light, but they did not hear the voice of the One speaking to me.
22.bbe: And those who were with me saw the light, but the voice of him who was talking to me came not to their ears.

22.msb: Then I asked, ‘What should I do, Lord?’ ‘Get up and go into Damascus,’ He told me. ‘There you will be told all that you have been appointed to do.’
22.kjv: And I said, What shall I do, Lord? And the Lord said unto me, Arise, and go into Damascus; and there it shall be told thee of all things which are appointed for thee to do.
22.blb: And I said, ‘What shall I do, Lord?’ And the Lord said to me, ‘Having risen up, go to Damascus, and there it will be told to you concerning all things that it has been appointed to you to do.’
22.bbe: And I said, What have I to do, Lord? And the Lord said to me, Get up, and go into Damascus; and it will be made clear to you what you have to do.

22.msb: Because the brilliance of the light had blinded me, my companions led me by the hand into Damascus.
22.kjv: And when I could not see for the glory of that light, being led by the hand of them that were with me, I came into Damascus.
22.blb: And while I could not see from the brightness of that light, I came to Damascus, being led by the hand by those being with me.
22.bbe: And because I was unable to see because of the glory of that light, those who were with me took me by the hand, and so I came to Damascus.

22.msb: There a man named Ananias, a devout observer of the law who was highly regarded by all the Jews living there,
22.kjv: And one Ananias, a devout man according to the law, having a good report of all the Jews which dwelt there,
22.blb: And a certain Ananias, a devout man according to the law, being testified to by all the Jews dwelling there,
22.bbe: And one Ananias, a God-fearing man, who kept the law, and of whom all the Jews in that place had a high opinion,

22.msb: came and stood beside me. ‘Brother Saul,’ he said, ‘receive your sight.’ And at that moment I could see him.
22.kjv: Came unto me, and stood, and said unto me, Brother Saul, receive thy sight. And the same hour I looked up upon him.
22.blb: having come to me and having stood near, said to me, ‘Brother Saul, look up.’ And the same hour I looked up at him.
22.bbe: Came to my side and said, Brother Saul, let your eyes be open. And in that very hour I was able to see him.

22.msb: Then he said, ‘The God of our fathers has appointed you to know His will and to see the Righteous One and to hear His voice.
22.kjv: And he said, The God of our fathers hath chosen thee, that thou shouldest know his will, and see that Just One, and shouldest hear the voice of his mouth.
22.blb: And he said, ‘The God of our fathers has appointed you to know His will, and to see the Righteous One, and to hear a voice out of His mouth.
22.bbe: And he said, You have been marked out by the God of our fathers to have knowledge of his purpose, and to see the Upright One and to give ear to the words of his mouth.

22.msb: You will be His witness to everyone of what you have seen and heard.
22.kjv: For thou shalt be his witness unto all men of what thou hast seen and heard.
22.blb: For you will be a witness for Him to all men of what you have seen and heard.
22.bbe: For you will be a witness for him to all men of what you have seen and of what has come to your ears.

22.msb: And now what are you waiting for? Get up, be baptized, and wash your sins away, calling on the name of the Lord.’
22.kjv: And now why tarriest thou? arise, and be baptized, and wash away thy sins, calling on the name of the Lord.
22.blb: And now, why do you delay? Having arisen, be baptized and wash away your sins, having called on His name.’
22.bbe: And now, why are you waiting? get up, and have baptism, for the washing away of your sins, giving worship to his name.

22.msb: Later, when I had returned to Jerusalem and was praying at the temple, I fell into a trance
22.kjv: And it came to pass, that, when I was come again to Jerusalem, even while I prayed in the temple, I was in a trance;
22.blb: And it happened to me, having returned to Jerusalem and in my praying in the temple, that I fell into a trance
22.bbe: And it came about that when I had come back to Jerusalem, while I was at prayer in the Temple, my senses became more than naturally clear,

22.msb: and saw the Lord saying to me, ‘Hurry! Leave Jerusalem quickly, because the people here will not accept your testimony about Me.’
22.kjv: And saw him saying unto me, Make haste, and get thee quickly out of Jerusalem: for they will not receive thy testimony concerning me.
22.blb: and saw Him saying to me, ‘Make haste and go forth with speed out of Jerusalem, because they will not accept your testimony about Me.’
22.bbe: And I saw him saying to me, Go out of Jerusalem straight away because they will not give hearing to your witness about me.

22.msb: ‘Lord,’ I answered, ‘they know very well that in one synagogue after another I imprisoned and beat those who believed in You.
22.kjv: And I said, Lord, they know that I imprisoned and beat in every synagogue them that believed on thee:
22.blb: And I said, ‘Lord, they themselves know that in each of those synagogues I was imprisoning and beating those believing on You.
22.bbe: And I said, Lord, they themselves have knowledge that I went through the Synagogues putting in prison and whipping all those who had faith in you:

22.msb: And when the blood of Your witness Stephen was shed, I stood there giving my approval to his death and watching over the garments of those who killed him.’
22.kjv: And when the blood of thy martyr Stephen was shed, I also was standing by, and consenting unto his death, and kept the raiment of them that slew him.
22.blb: And when the blood of Your witness Stephen was poured out, I myself was also standing by and consenting and watching over the garments of those killing him.’
22.bbe: And when Stephen your witness was put to death, I was there, giving approval, and looking after the clothing of those who put him to death.

22.msb: Then He said to me, ‘Go! I will send you far away to the Gentiles.’”
22.kjv: And he said unto me, Depart: for I will send thee far hence unto the Gentiles.
22.blb: And He said to me, ‘Go, because I will send you far away to the Gentiles.’”
22.bbe: And he said to me, Go, for I will send you far away to the Gentiles.

22.msb: The crowd listened to Paul until he made this statement. Then they lifted up their voices and shouted, “Rid the earth of him! He is not fit to live!”
22.kjv: And they gave him audience unto this word, and then lifted up their voices, and said, Away with such a fellow from the earth: for it is not fit that he should live.
22.blb: Now they were listening to him until this word. And they lifted up their voice, saying, “Away with such from the earth! For it is not fitting for him to live!”
22.bbe: And they gave him a hearing as far as this word; then with loud voices they said, Away with this man from the earth; it is not right for him to be living.
22.heading: Paul the Roman Citizen

22.msb: As they were crying out and throwing off their cloaks and tossing dust into the air,
22.kjv: And as they cried out, and cast off their clothes, and threw dust into the air,
22.blb: And in their crying out and casting off the garments and throwing dust into the air,
22.bbe: And while they were crying out, and pulling off their clothing, and sending dust into the air,

22.msb: the commander ordered that Paul be brought into the barracks. He directed that Paul be flogged and interrogated to determine the reason for this outcry against him.
22.kjv: The chief captain commanded him to be brought into the castle, and bade that he should be examined by scourging; that he might know wherefore they cried so against him.
22.blb: the commander ordered him to be brought into the barracks, having directed him to be examined by flogging, so that he might know for what cause they were crying out against him like this.
22.bbe: The chief captain gave orders for him to be taken into the army building, saying that he would put him to the test by whipping, so that he might have knowledge of the reason why they were crying out so violently against him.

22.msb: But as he stretched him out to strap him down, Paul said to the centurion standing there, “Is it lawful for you to flog a Roman citizen without a trial?”
22.kjv: And as they bound him with thongs, Paul said unto the centurion that stood by, Is it lawful for you to scourge a man that is a Roman, and uncondemned?
22.blb: But as they stretched him forward with the straps, Paul said to the centurion standing by, “Is it lawful to you to flog a man who is a Roman and uncondemned?”
22.bbe: And when they had put leather bands round him, Paul said to the captain who was present, Is it the law for you to give blows to a man who is a Roman and has not been judged?

22.msb: On hearing this, the centurion went and reported it to the commander. “Consider what you are about to do,” he said. “This man is a Roman citizen.”
22.kjv: When the centurion heard that, he went and told the chief captain, saying, Take heed what thou doest: for this man is a Roman.
22.blb: And the centurion, having heard, having gone to the commander, reported it, saying, “What are you about to do? For this man is a Roman.”
22.bbe: And hearing this, the man went to the chief captain and gave him an account of it, saying, What are you about to do? for this man is a Roman.

22.msb: The commander went to Paul and asked, “Tell me, are you a Roman citizen?” “Yes,” he answered.
22.kjv: Then the chief captain came, and said unto him, Tell me, art thou a Roman? He said, Yea.
22.blb: And having come near, the commander said to him, “Tell me, are you a Roman?” And he was saying, “Yes.”
22.bbe: And the chief captain came to him and said, Give me an answer, are you a Roman? And he said, Yes.

22.msb: “I paid a high price for my citizenship,” said the commander. “But I was born a citizen,” Paul replied.
22.kjv: And the chief captain answered, With a great sum obtained I this freedom. And Paul said, But I was free born.
22.blb: And the commander answered, “I bought this citizenship with a great sum.” But Paul was saying, “But I have even been born so.”
22.bbe: And the chief captain said, I got Roman rights for myself at a great price. And Paul said, But I had them by birth.

22.msb: At once those who were about to interrogate Paul stepped back, and the commander himself was alarmed when he realized that he had put a Roman citizen in chains.
22.kjv: Then straightway they departed from him which should have examined him: and the chief captain also was afraid, after he knew that he was a Roman, and because he had bound him.
22.blb: So immediately those being about to examine him departed from him, and the commander also was afraid, having ascertained that he is a Roman, and because he had bound him.
22.bbe: Then those who were about to put him to the test went away: and the chief captain was in fear, seeing that he was a Roman, and that he had put chains on him.

22.msb: The next day the commander, wanting to learn the real reason Paul was accused by the Jews, released him from the bonds and ordered the chief priests and their whole Sanhedrin to assemble. Then he brought Paul down and had him stand before them.
22.kjv: On the morrow, because he would have known the certainty wherefore he was accused of the Jews, he loosed him from his bands, and commanded the chief priests and all their council to appear, and brought Paul down, and set him before them.
22.blb: And on the next day, desiring to know for certain why he is accused by the Jews, he unbound him and he commanded the chief priests and all the Council to assemble. And having brought down Paul, he set him among them.
22.bbe: But on the day after, desiring to have certain knowledge of what the Jews had to say against him, he made him free, and gave orders for the chief priests and all the Sanhedrin to come together, and he took Paul and put him before them.

23.msb: Paul looked directly at the Sanhedrin and said, “Brothers, I have conducted myself before God in all good conscience to this day.”
23.kjv: And Paul, earnestly beholding the council, said, Men and brethren, I have lived in all good conscience before God until this day.
23.blb: And having looked intently at the Council, Paul said, “Men, brothers, I have conducted myself in all good conscience to God up to this day.”
23.bbe: And Paul, looking fixedly at the Sanhedrin, said, My brothers, my life has been upright before God till this day.
23.heading: Paul before the Sanhedrin

23.msb: At this, the high priest Ananias ordered those standing near Paul to strike him on the mouth.
23.kjv: And the high priest Ananias commanded them that stood by him to smite him on the mouth.
23.blb: And the high priest Ananias commanded those standing by him to strike him on the mouth.
23.bbe: And the high priest, Ananias, gave orders to those who were near him to give him a blow on the mouth.

23.msb: Then Paul said to him, “God will strike you, you whitewashed wall! You sit here to judge me according to the law, yet you yourself violate the law by commanding that I be struck.”
23.kjv: Then said Paul unto him, God shall smite thee, thou whited wall: for sittest thou to judge me after the law, and commandest me to be smitten contrary to the law?
23.blb: Then Paul said to him, “God is about to strike you, whitewashed wall! And you, do you sit judging me according to the law, and violating the law, command me to be struck?”
23.bbe: Then Paul said to him, God will give blows to you, you whitewashed wall: are you here to be my judge by law, and by your orders am I given blows against the law?

23.msb: But those standing nearby said, “How dare you insult the high priest of God!”
23.kjv: And they that stood by said, Revilest thou God’s high priest?
23.blb: But those who stood by said, “Do you insult the high priest of God?”
23.bbe: And those who were near said, Do you say such words against God's high priest?

23.msb: “Brothers,” Paul replied, “I was not aware that he was the high priest, for it is written: ‘Do not speak evil about the ruler of your people.’”
23.kjv: Then said Paul, I wist not, brethren, that he was the high priest: for it is written, Thou shalt not speak evil of the ruler of thy people.
23.blb: And Paul was saying, “I was not aware, brothers, that he is high priest; for it has been written: ‘You shall not speak evil of the ruler of your people.’”
23.bbe: And Paul said, Brother, I had no idea that he was the high priest: for it has been said, You may not say evil about the ruler of your people.

23.msb: Then Paul, knowing that some of them were Sadducees and others Pharisees, called out in the Sanhedrin, “Brothers, I am a Pharisee, the son of a Pharisee. It is because of my hope in the resurrection of the dead that I am on trial.”
23.kjv: But when Paul perceived that the one part were Sadducees, and the other Pharisees, he cried out in the council, Men and brethren, I am a Pharisee, the son of a Pharisee: of the hope and resurrection of the dead I am called in question.
23.blb: And Paul, having known that the one part consists of Sadducees, but the other of Pharisees, was crying out in the Council, “Men, brothers, I am a Pharisee, the son of a Pharisee; concerning hope and resurrection of the dead I am judged.”
23.bbe: But when Paul saw that half of them were Sadducees and the rest Pharisees, he said in the Sanhedrin, Brothers, I am a Pharisee, and the son of Pharisees: I am here to be judged on the question of the hope of the coming back from the dead.

23.msb: As soon as he had said this, a dispute broke out between the Pharisees and Sadducees, and the assembly was divided.
23.kjv: And when he had so said, there arose a dissension between the Pharisees and the Sadducees: and the multitude was divided.
23.blb: And on his saying this, a dissension arose between the Pharisees and Sadducees, and the multitude was divided.
23.bbe: And when he had said this, there was an argument between the Pharisees and the Sadducees, and a division in the meeting.

23.msb: For the Sadducees say that there is neither a resurrection nor angels nor spirits, but the Pharisees acknowledge them all.
23.kjv: For the Sadducees say that there is no resurrection, neither angel, nor spirit: but the Pharisees confess both.
23.blb: For indeed Sadducees say there is no resurrection nor angel nor spirit, but Pharisees confess both.
23.bbe: For the Sadducees say that there is no coming back from the dead, and no angels or spirits: but the Pharisees have belief in all these.

23.msb: A great clamor arose, and some scribes from the party of the Pharisees got up and contended sharply, “We find nothing wrong with this man. If a spirit or an angel has spoken to him, let us not fight against God.”
23.kjv: And there arose a great cry: and the scribes that were of the Pharisees’ part arose, and strove, saying, We find no evil in this man: but if a spirit or an angel hath spoken to him, let us not fight against God.
23.blb: Then a great clamor arose, and some of the scribes of the party of the Pharisees, having risen up, were contending, saying, “We find nothing evil in this man. And what if a spirit or an angel has spoken to him?”
23.bbe: And there was a great outcry: and some of the scribes on the side of the Pharisees got up and took part in the discussion, saying, We see no evil in this man: what if he has had a revelation from an angel or a spirit?

23.msb: The dispute grew so violent that the commander was afraid they would tear Paul to pieces. He ordered the soldiers to go down and remove him by force and bring him into the barracks.
23.kjv: And when there arose a great dissension, the chief captain, fearing lest Paul should have been pulled in pieces of them, commanded the soldiers to go down, and to take him by force from among them, and to bring him into the castle.
23.blb: And a great dissension arising, the commander, having feared, lest Paul should be torn to pieces by them, commanded the troop, having gone down, to take him by force from their midst and to bring him into the barracks.
23.bbe: And when the argument became very violent, the chief captain, fearing that Paul would be pulled in two by them, gave orders to the armed men to take him by force from among them, and take him into the army building.

23.msb: The following night the Lord stood near Paul and said, “Take courage, Paul! As you have testified about Me in Jerusalem, so also you must testify in Rome.”
23.kjv: And the night following the Lord stood by him, and said, Be of good cheer, Paul: for as thou hast testified of me in Jerusalem, so must thou bear witness also at Rome.
23.blb: But the following night the Lord, having stood by him, said, “Take courage, for as you have fully testified about Me at Jerusalem, so also it is necessary for you to testify at Rome.”
23.bbe: And the night after, the Lord came to his side and said, Be of good heart, for as you have been witnessing for me in Jerusalem, so will you be my witness in Rome.

23.msb: When daylight came, some of the Jews formed a conspiracy and bound themselves with an oath not to eat or drink until they had killed Paul.
23.kjv: And when it was day, certain of the Jews banded together, and bound themselves under a curse, saying that they would neither eat nor drink till they had killed Paul.
23.blb: And day having come, the Jews, having made a conspiracy, put themselves under an oath, declaring neither to eat nor to drink until they should kill Paul.
23.bbe: And when it was day, the Jews came together and put themselves under an oath that they would take no food or drink till they had put Paul to death.
23.heading: The Plot to Kill Paul
