23.msb: More than forty of them were involved in this plot.
23.kjv: And they were more than forty which had made this conspiracy.
23.blb: Now there were more than forty having made this sworn conspiracy,
23.bbe: And more than forty of them took this oath.

23.msb: They went to the chief priests and elders and said, “We have bound ourselves with a solemn oath not to eat anything until we have killed Paul.
23.kjv: And they came to the chief priests and elders, and said, We have bound ourselves under a great curse, that we will eat nothing until we have slain Paul.
23.blb: who, having come to the chief priests and the elders, said, “We have bound ourselves with an oath to eat nothing until we should kill Paul.
23.bbe: And they came to the chief priests and the rulers and said, We have taken a great oath to take no food till we have put Paul to death

23.msb: Now then, you and the Sanhedrin petition the commander to bring him down to you tomorrow on the pretext of examining his case more carefully. We are ready to kill him on the way.”
23.kjv: Now therefore ye with the council signify to the chief captain that he bring him down unto you to morrow, as though ye would enquire something more perfectly concerning him: and we, or ever he come near, are ready to kill him.
23.blb: Now therefore, you, with the Council, make a report to the commander, so that he might bring him down to you as being about to examine more accurately the things about him. And we are ready to kill him before his drawing near.”
23.bbe: So now, will you and the Sanhedrin make a request to the military authorities to have him sent down to you, as if you were desiring to go into the business in greater detail; and we, before ever he gets to you, will be waiting to put him to death.

23.msb: But when the son of Paul’s sister heard about the plot, he went into the barracks and told Paul.
23.kjv: And when Paul’s sister’s son heard of their lying in wait, he went and entered into the castle, and told Paul.
23.blb: But the son of Paul’s sister, having heard of the ambush, having come near and having entered into the barracks, reported it to Paul.
23.bbe: But Paul's sister's son had word of their design, and he came into the army building and gave news of it to Paul.

23.msb: Then Paul called one of the centurions and said, “Take this young man to the commander; he has something to tell him.”
23.kjv: Then Paul called one of the centurions unto him, and said, Bring this young man unto the chief captain: for he hath a certain thing to tell him.
23.blb: And Paul, having summoned one of the centurions, was saying, “Take this young man to the commander, for he has something to report to him.”
23.bbe: And Paul sent for a captain and said, Take this young man to your chief, for he has news for him.

23.msb: So the centurion took him to the commander and said, “Paul the prisoner sent and asked me to bring this young man to you. He has something to tell you.”
23.kjv: So he took him, and brought him to the chief captain, and said, Paul the prisoner called me unto him, and prayed me to bring this young man unto thee, who hath something to say unto thee.
23.blb: Therefore indeed the one having taken him brought him to the commander, and he says, “Paul the prisoner, having summoned me, asked me to lead this young man to you, having something to say to you.”
23.bbe: So he took him to the chief captain and said, Paul, the prisoner, made a request to me to take this young man to you, for he has something to say to you.

23.msb: The commander took the young man by the hand, drew him aside, and asked, “What do you need to tell me?”
23.kjv: Then the chief captain took him by the hand, and went with him aside privately, and asked him, What is that thou hast to tell me?
23.blb: Then the commander, having taken hold of his hand and having withdrawn in private, began to inquire, “What is it that you have to report to me?”
23.bbe: And the chief took him by the hand and, going on one side, said to him privately, What is it you have to say to me?

23.msb: He answered, “The Jews have agreed to ask you to bring Paul to the Sanhedrin tomorrow on the pretext of acquiring more information about him.
23.kjv: And he said, The Jews have agreed to desire thee that thou wouldest bring down Paul to morrow into the council, as though they would enquire somewhat of him more perfectly.
23.blb: And he said, “The Jews have agreed to ask you that you might bring down Paul into the Council tomorrow as being about to inquire something more accurately about him.
23.bbe: And he said, The Jews are in agreement together to make a request to you for Paul to be taken, on the day after this, into the Sanhedrin, to be questioned in greater detail.

23.msb: Do not let them persuade you, because more than forty men are waiting to ambush him. They have bound themselves with an oath not to eat or drink until they have killed him; they are ready now, awaiting your consent.”
23.kjv: But do not thou yield unto them: for there lie in wait for him of them more than forty men, which have bound themselves with an oath, that they will neither eat nor drink till they have killed him: and now are they ready, looking for a promise from thee.
23.blb: You, therefore, should not be persuaded by them. For more than forty of their men lie in wait for him, who have put themselves under an oath neither to eat nor to drink until they should kill him; and now they are ready, awaiting the promise from you.”
23.bbe: But do not give way to them, for more than forty of them are waiting for him, having taken an oath not to take food or drink till they have put him to death: and now they are ready, waiting for your order.

23.msb: So the commander dismissed the young man and instructed him, “Do not tell anyone that you have reported this to me.”
23.kjv: So the chief captain then let the young man depart, and charged him, See thou tell no man that thou hast shewed these things to me.
23.blb: Therefore indeed the commander dismissed the young man, having instructed him, “Tell no one that you have reported these things to me.”
23.bbe: So the chief captain let the young man go, saying to him, Do not say to anyone that you have given me word of these things.

23.msb: Then he called two of his centurions and said, “Prepare two hundred soldiers, seventy horsemen, and two hundred spearmen to go to Caesarea in the third hour of the night.
23.kjv: And he called unto him two centurions, saying, Make ready two hundred soldiers to go to Cæsarea, and horsemen threescore and ten, and spearmen two hundred, at the third hour of the night;
23.blb: And having summoned a certain two of the centurions, he said, “Prepare for the third hour of the night two hundred soldiers and seventy horsemen and two hundred spearmen, so that they might go as far as Caesarea,
23.bbe: And he sent for two captains and said, Make ready two hundred men, with seventy horsemen and two hundred spearmen, to go to Caesarea, at the third hour of the night:
23.heading: Paul Sent to Felix

23.msb: Provide mounts for Paul to take him safely to Governor Felix.”
23.kjv: And provide them beasts, that they may set Paul on, and bring him safe unto Felix the governor.
23.blb: and provide mounts so that, having set Paul upon them, they might bring him safely to Felix the governor,”
23.bbe: And get beasts so that they may put Paul on them, and take him safely to Felix, the ruler.

23.msb: And he wrote the following letter:
23.kjv: And he wrote a letter after this manner:
23.blb: having written a letter having this form:
23.bbe: And he sent a letter in these words:

23.msb: Claudius Lysias, To His Excellency, Governor Felix: Greetings.
23.kjv: Claudius Lysias unto the most excellent governor Felix sendeth greeting.
23.blb: Claudius Lysias, To the most excellent Governor Felix: Greetings.
23.bbe: Claudius Lysias, to the most noble ruler, Felix, peace be with you.

23.msb: This man was seized by the Jews, and they were about to kill him when I came with my troops to rescue him. For I had learned that he is a Roman citizen,
23.kjv: This man was taken of the Jews, and should have been killed of them: then came I with an army, and rescued him, having understood that he was a Roman.
23.blb: This man having been seized by the Jews and being about to be killed by them—having come up with the troop, I rescued him, having learned that he is a Roman.
23.bbe: This man was taken by the Jews, and was about to be put to death by them, when I came on them with the army and took him out of danger, having knowledge that he was a Roman.

23.msb: and since I wanted to know their charges against him, I brought him down to their Sanhedrin.
23.kjv: And when I would have known the cause wherefore they accused him, I brought him forth into their council:
23.blb: And resolving to know the charge on account of which they were accusing him, I brought him down to their Council,
23.bbe: And, desiring to get at the reason for their attack on him, I took him down to their Sanhedrin:

23.msb: I found that the accusation involved questions about their own law, but there was no charge worthy of death or imprisonment.
23.kjv: Whom I perceived to be accused of questions of their law, but to have nothing laid to his charge worthy of death or of bonds.
23.blb: whom I found being accused concerning questions of their law, but having no accusation worthy of death or of chains.
23.bbe: Then it became clear to me that it was a question of their law, and that nothing was said against him which might be a reason for prison or death.

23.msb: When I was informed that there was a plot by the Jews against the man, I sent him to you at once. I also instructed his accusers to present their case against him before you. Farewell.
23.kjv: And when it was told me how that the Jews laid wait for the man, I sent straightway to thee, and gave commandment to his accusers also to say before thee what they had against him. Farewell.
23.blb: And a plot having been disclosed to me to be against the man, I sent him to you at once, also having instructed the accusers to speak these things against him before you.
23.bbe: And when news was given to me that a secret design was being made against the man, I sent him straight away to you, giving orders to those who are against him to make their statements before you.

23.msb: So the soldiers followed their orders and brought Paul by night to Antipatris.
23.kjv: Then the soldiers, as it was commanded them, took Paul, and brought him by night to Antipatris.
23.blb: Therefore indeed the soldiers, according to that having been ordered them, having taken Paul, brought him to Antipatris by night.
23.bbe: So the armed men, as they were ordered, took Paul and came by night to Antipatris.

23.msb: The next day they returned to the barracks and let the horsemen go on with him.
23.kjv: On the morrow they left the horsemen to go with him, and returned to the castle:
23.blb: And on the next day, having allowed the horsemen to go with him, they returned to the barracks;
23.bbe: But on the day after, they sent the horsemen on with him, and went back to their place:

23.msb: When the horsemen arrived in Caesarea, they delivered the letter to the governor and presented Paul to him.
23.kjv: Who, when they came to Cæsarea, and delivered the epistle to the governor, presented Paul also before him.
23.blb: those having entered into Caesarea and having delivered the letter to the governor, also presented Paul to him.
23.bbe: And they, when they came to Caesarea, gave the letter to the ruler, and took Paul before him.

23.msb: The governor read the letter and asked what province Paul was from. Learning that he was from Cilicia,
23.kjv: And when the governor had read the letter, he asked of what province he was. And when he understood that he was of Cilicia;
23.blb: And having read it and having asked what province he is from, and having learned that he is from Cilicia,
23.bbe: And after reading it, he said, What part of the country do you come from? And, hearing that he was from Cilicia,

23.msb: he said, “I will hear your case when your accusers arrive.” Then he ordered that Paul be kept under guard in Herod’s Praetorium.
23.kjv: I will hear thee, said he, when thine accusers are also come. And he commanded him to be kept in Herod’s judgment hall.
23.blb: he was saying, “I will hear you fully when your accusers may have arrived also,” having commanded him to be guarded in the Praetorium of Herod.
23.bbe: I will give hearing to your cause, he said, when those who are against you have come. And he gave orders for him to be kept in Herod's Praetorium.

24.msb: Five days later the high priest Ananias came down with the elders and a lawyer named Tertullus, who presented to the governor their case against Paul.
24.kjv: And after five days Ananias the high priest descended with the elders, and with a certain orator named Tertullus, who informed the governor against Paul.
24.blb: And after five days the high priest Ananias came down with some elders and a certain orator, Tertullus, who made a presentation against Paul to the governor.
24.bbe: And after five days, the high priest, Ananias, came with certain of the rulers, and an expert talker, one Tertullus; and they made a statement to Felix against Paul.
24.heading: Tertullus Prosecutes Paul

24.msb: When Paul had been called in, Tertullus opened the prosecution: “Because of you, we have enjoyed a lasting peace, and your foresight has brought worthy reforms to this nation.
24.kjv: And when he was called forth, Tertullus began to accuse him, saying, Seeing that by thee we enjoy great quietness, and that very worthy deeds are done unto this nation by thy providence,
24.blb: And he having been called, Tertullus began to accuse him, saying, “Attaining great peace through you, and excellent measures being done to this nation through your foresight,
24.bbe: And when he had been sent for, Tertullus, starting his statement, said, Because by you we are living in peace, and through your wisdom wrongs are put right for this nation,

24.msb: In every way and everywhere, most excellent Felix, we acknowledge this with all gratitude.
24.kjv: We accept it always, and in all places, most noble Felix, with all thankfulness.
24.blb: in every way and also everywhere, we gladly accept it, most excellent Felix, with all thankfulness.
24.bbe: In all things and in all places we are conscious of our great debt to you, most noble Felix.

24.msb: But in order not to delay you any further, I beg your indulgence to hear us briefly.
24.kjv: Notwithstanding, that I be not further tedious unto thee, I pray thee that thou wouldest hear us of thy clemency a few words.
24.blb: But so that I should not be a hindrance to you any longer, I implore you to hear us briefly in your kindness.
24.bbe: But, so that I may not make you tired, I make a request to you of your mercy, to give hearing to a short statement.

24.msb: We have found this man to be a pestilence, stirring up dissension among the Jews all over the world. He is a ringleader of the sect of the Nazarenes,
24.kjv: For we have found this man a pestilent fellow, and a mover of sedition among all the Jews throughout the world, and a ringleader of the sect of the Nazarenes:
24.blb: For having found this man a pestilence and stirring dissension among all the Jews in the world—also a leader of the sect of the Nazarenes—
24.bbe: For this man, in our opinion, is a cause of trouble, a maker of attacks on the government among Jews through all the empire, and a chief mover in the society of the Nazarenes:

24.msb: and he even tried to desecrate the temple; so we seized him.
24.kjv: Who also hath gone about to profane the temple: whom we took, and would have judged according to our law.
24.blb: who even attempted to profane the temple, whom we also seized.
24.bbe: Who, in addition, was attempting to make the Temple unclean: whom we took,

24.kjv: But the chief captain Lysias came upon us, and with great violence took him away out of our hands,

24.msb: By examining him yourself, you will be able to learn the truth about all our charges against him.”
24.kjv: Commanding his accusers to come unto thee: by examining of whom thyself mayest take knowledge of all these things, whereof we accuse him.
24.blb: Having examined him yourself, you will be able to know from him concerning all these things of which we accuse him.”
24.bbe: And from whom you will be able, by questioning him yourself, to get knowledge of all the things which we say against him.

24.msb: The Jews concurred, asserting that these charges were true.
24.kjv: And the Jews also assented, saying that these things were so.
24.blb: And the Jews also agreed, declaring these things to be so.
24.bbe: And the Jews were in agreement with his statement, saying that these things were so.

24.msb: When the governor motioned for Paul to speak, he began his response: “Knowing that you have been a judge over this nation for many years, I gladly make my defense.
24.kjv: Then Paul, after that the governor had beckoned unto him to speak, answered, Forasmuch as I know that thou hast been of many years a judge unto this nation, I do the more cheerfully answer for myself:
24.blb: And the governor having motioned to him to speak, Paul answered: “Knowing you as being a judge to this nation for many years, I make a defense cheerfully to the things concerning myself,
24.bbe: Then when the ruler had given him a sign to make his answer, Paul said, Because I have knowledge that you have been a judge over this nation for a number of years, I am glad to make my answer:
24.heading: Paul’s Defense to Felix

24.msb: You can verify for yourself that no more than twelve days ago I went up to worship in Jerusalem.
24.kjv: Because that thou mayest understand, that there are yet but twelve days since I went up to Jerusalem for to worship.
24.blb: you being able to know that there are to me no more than twelve days since I went up to worship in Jerusalem.
24.bbe: Seeing that you are able to make certain of the fact that it is not more than twelve days from the time when I came up to Jerusalem for worship;

24.msb: Yet my accusers did not find me debating with anyone in the temple or riling up a crowd in the synagogues or in the city.
24.kjv: And they neither found me in the temple disputing with any man, neither raising up the people, neither in the synagogues, nor in the city:
24.blb: And neither did they find me reasoning with anyone or making a tumultuous gathering of a crowd in the temple, nor in the synagogues, nor in the city.
24.bbe: And they have not seen me in argument with any man in the Temple, or working up the feelings of the people, in the Synagogues or in the town:

24.msb: Nor can they prove any of their charges against me.
24.kjv: Neither can they prove the things whereof they now accuse me.
24.blb: Nor are they able to prove to you the things concerning which now they accuse me.
24.bbe: And they are not able to give facts in support of the things which they say against me now.

24.msb: I do confess to you, however, that I worship the God of our fathers according to the Way, which they call a sect. I believe everything that is written throughout the Law and the Prophets,
24.kjv: But this I confess unto thee, that after the way which they call heresy, so worship I the God of my fathers, believing all things which are written in the law and in the prophets:
24.blb: But I confess this to you, that according to the Way, which they call a sect, so I serve the God of our fathers, believing all things throughout the Law and that have been written in the Prophets,
24.bbe: But this I will say openly to you, that I do give worship to the God of our fathers after that Way, which to them is not the true religion: but I have belief in all the things which are in the law and in the books of the prophets:

24.msb: and I have the same hope in God that they themselves cherish, that there will be a resurrection of the dead—of both the righteous and the wicked.
24.kjv: And have hope toward God, which they themselves also allow, that there shall be a resurrection of the dead, both of the just and unjust.
24.blb: having a hope in God, which they themselves also await, that there is about to be a resurrection both of righteous and of unrighteous.
24.bbe: Hoping in God for that which they themselves are looking for, that there will be a coming back from the dead for upright men and wrongdoers.

24.msb: In this hope, I strive always to maintain a clear conscience before God and man.
24.kjv: And herein do I exercise myself, to have always a conscience void of offence toward God, and toward men.
24.blb: In this I myself also strive to have a conscience without offense toward God and men through everything.
24.bbe: And in this, I do my best at all times to have no reason for shame before God or men.

24.msb: After several years, then, I returned to Jerusalem to bring alms to my people and to present offerings.
24.kjv: Now after many years I came to bring alms to my nation, and offerings.
24.blb: Now after many years, I arrived to bring alms to my nation, and offerings,
24.bbe: Now after a number of years I came to give help and offerings to my nation:

24.msb: At the time they found me in the temple, I was ceremonially clean and was not inciting a crowd or an uproar. But there are some Jews from the province of Asia
24.kjv: Whereupon certain Jews from Asia found me purified in the temple, neither with multitude, nor with tumult.
24.blb: during which they found me purified in the temple, not with a crowd nor with an uproar. But there are some Jews from Asia
24.bbe: And having been made clean, I was in the Temple, but not with a great number of people, and not with noise: but there were certain Jews from Asia,

24.msb: who ought to appear before you and bring charges, if they have anything against me.
24.kjv: Who ought to have been here before thee, and object, if they had ought against me.
24.blb: who ought to appear before you and to make accusation if they may have anything against me.
24.bbe: And it would have been better if they had come here to make a statement, if they have anything against me.

24.msb: Otherwise, let these men state for themselves any crime they found in me when I stood before the Sanhedrin,
24.kjv: Or else let these same here say, if they have found any evil doing in me, while I stood before the council,
24.blb: Or let these say themselves any unrighteousness they found in my having stood before the Council,
24.bbe: Or let these men here present say what wrongdoing was seen in me when I was before the Sanhedrin,

24.msb: unless it was this one thing I called out as I stood in their presence: ‘It is concerning the resurrection of the dead that I am being tried by you today.’”
24.kjv: Except it be for this one voice, that I cried standing among them, Touching the resurrection of the dead I am called in question by you this day.
24.blb: other than concerning this one voice in which I cried out standing among them: ‘I am judged by you this day concerning the resurrection of the dead.’”
24.bbe: But only this one thing which I said among them in a loud voice, I am this day being judged on the question of the coming back from the dead.

24.msb: On hearing these things Felix, who was well informed about the Way, adjourned the hearing and said, “When Lysias the commander comes, I will decide your case.”
24.kjv: And when Felix heard these things, having more perfect knowledge of that way, he deferred them, and said, When Lysias the chief captain shall come down, I will know the uttermost of your matter.
24.blb: But Felix, having known more precisely the things concerning the Way, put them off, having said, “When Lysias the commander shall have come down, I will examine the things as to you,”
24.bbe: But Felix, who had a more detailed knowledge of the Way, put them off, saying, When Lysias, the chief captain, comes down, I will give attention to your business.
24.heading: The Verdict Postponed

24.msb: He ordered the centurion to keep Paul under guard, but to allow him some freedom and permit his friends to come and minister to his needs.
24.kjv: And he commanded a centurion to keep Paul, and to let him have liberty, and that he should forbid none of his acquaintance to minister or come unto him.
24.blb: having commanded the centurion to keep him and to let him have ease and not to forbid his own to minister to him.
24.bbe: And he gave orders to the captain to keep Paul under his control, and to let him have everything he had need of; and not to keep his friends from coming to see him.

24.msb: After several days, Felix returned with his wife Drusilla, who was a Jewess. He sent for Paul and listened to him speak about faith in Christ.
24.kjv: And after certain days, when Felix came with his wife Drusilla, which was a Jewess, he sent for Paul, and heard him concerning the faith in Christ.
24.blb: Then after some days Felix, having arrived with his own wife Drusilla, being a Jewess, sent for Paul and heard him concerning the faith in Christ Jesus.
24.bbe: But after some days, Felix came with Drusilla his wife, who was of the Jews by birth, and sent for Paul, and gave hearing to him about faith in Christ Jesus.

24.msb: As Paul expounded on righteousness, self-control, and the coming judgment, Felix became frightened and said, “You may go for now. When I find the time, I will call for you.”
24.kjv: And as he reasoned of righteousness, temperance, and judgment to come, Felix trembled, and answered, Go thy way for this time; when I have a convenient season, I will call for thee.
24.blb: And in his reasoning concerning righteousness and self-control and the coming judgment, Felix, having become frightened, answered, “Be going for the present, and having found opportunity, I will call for you,”
24.bbe: And while he was talking about righteousness and self-control and the judging which was to come, Felix had great fear and said, Go away for the present, and when the right time comes I will send for you.

24.msb: At the same time, he was hoping that Paul would offer him a bribe to release him. So he sent for Paul frequently and talked with him.
24.kjv: He hoped also that money should have been given him of Paul, that he might loose him: wherefore he sent for him the oftener, and communed with him.
24.blb: at the same time also hoping that riches will be given to him by Paul. Therefore also, sending for him often, he was talking with him.
24.bbe: For he was hoping that Paul would give him money: so he sent for him more frequently and had talk with him.

24.msb: After two years had passed, Felix was succeeded by Porcius Festus. And wishing to do the Jews a favor, Felix left Paul in prison.
24.kjv: But after two years Porcius Festus came into Felix’ room: and Felix, willing to shew the Jews a pleasure, left Paul bound.
24.blb: But two years having been completed, Felix received Porcius Festus as successor, and wishing to acquire for himself favor with the Jews, Felix left Paul bound.
24.bbe: But after two years Porcius Festus took the place of Felix, who, desiring to have the approval of the Jews, kept Paul in chains.

25.msb: Three days after his arrival in the province, Festus went up from Caesarea to Jerusalem,
25.kjv: Now when Festus was come into the province, after three days he ascended from Cæsarea to Jerusalem.
25.blb: Therefore Festus, having arrived in the province, after three days went up to Jerusalem from Caesarea.
25.bbe: So Festus, having come into that part of the country which was under his rule, after three days went up to Jerusalem from Caesarea.
25.heading: Paul’s Trial before Festus

25.msb: where the high priest and Jewish leaders presented their case against Paul. They urged Festus
25.kjv: Then the high priest and the chief of the Jews informed him against Paul, and besought him,
25.blb: And the chief priests and the chiefs of the Jews presented to him against Paul, and they were imploring him,
25.bbe: And the chief priests and the chief men of the Jews made statements against Paul,

25.msb: to grant them a concession against Paul by summoning him to Jerusalem, because they were preparing an ambush to kill him along the way.
25.kjv: And desired favour against him, that he would send for him to Jerusalem, laying wait in the way to kill him.
25.blb: requesting a favor against him that he would summon him to Jerusalem, forming an ambush to kill him on the way.
25.bbe: Requesting Festus to give effect to their design against him, and send him to Jerusalem, when they would be waiting to put him to death on the way.

25.msb: But Festus replied, “Paul is being held in Caesarea, and I myself am going there soon.
25.kjv: But Festus answered, that Paul should be kept at Cæsarea, and that he himself would depart shortly thither.
25.blb: Then, indeed, Festus answered that Paul is to be kept in Caesarea, and that he himself is about to go out in haste.
25.bbe: But Festus, in answer, said that Paul was being kept in prison at Caesarea, and that in a short time he himself was going there.

25.msb: So if this man has done anything wrong, let some of your leaders come down with me and accuse him there.”
25.kjv: Let them therefore, said he, which among you are able, go down with me, and accuse this man, if there be any wickedness in him.
25.blb: “Therefore those powerful among you,” he says, “having gone down together, if there is anything wrong in the man, let them accuse him.”
25.bbe: So, he said, let those who have authority among you go with me, and if there is any wrong in the man, let them make a statement against him.

25.msb: After spending more than ten days with them, Festus went down to Caesarea. The next day he sat on the judgment seat and ordered that Paul be brought in.
25.kjv: And when he had tarried among them more than ten days, he went down unto Cæsarea; and the next day sitting on the judgment seat commanded Paul to be brought.
25.blb: And having spent with them no more than eight or ten days, having gone down to Caesarea, on the next day having sat on the judgment seat, he commanded Paul to be brought.
25.bbe: And when he had been with them not more than eight or ten days, he went down to Caesarea; and on the day after, he took his place on the judge's seat, and sent for Paul.

25.msb: When Paul arrived, the Jews who had come down from Jerusalem stood around him, laying against Paul many serious charges that they could not prove.
25.kjv: And when he was come, the Jews which came down from Jerusalem stood round about, and laid many and grievous complaints against Paul, which they could not prove.
25.blb: And he having arrived, the Jews having come down from Jerusalem stood around him, bringing many and weighty charges, which they were not able to prove.
25.bbe: And when he came, the Jews who had come down from Jerusalem came round him, and made all sorts of serious statements against him, which were not supported by the facts.

25.msb: Then Paul made his defense: “I have committed no offense against the law of the Jews or against the temple or against Caesar.”
25.kjv: While he answered for himself, Neither against the law of the Jews, neither against the temple, nor yet against Cæsar, have I offended any thing at all.
25.blb: Paul made his defense: “Neither against the law of the Jews, nor against the temple, nor against Caesar, have I sinned in anything.”
25.bbe: Then Paul, in his answer to them, said, I have done no wrong against the law of the Jews, or against the Temple, or against Caesar.

25.msb: But Festus, wishing to do the Jews a favor, said to Paul, “Are you willing to go up to Jerusalem to stand trial before me on these charges?”
25.kjv: But Festus, willing to do the Jews a pleasure, answered Paul, and said, Wilt thou go up to Jerusalem, and there be judged of these things before me?
25.blb: But Festus, wishing to lay a favor on the Jews, answering, said to Paul, “Are you willing, having gone up to Jerusalem, to be judged before me there concerning these things?”
25.bbe: But Festus, desiring to get the approval of the Jews, said to Paul, Will you go up to Jerusalem, and be judged before me there in connection with these things?

25.msb: Paul replied, “I am standing before the judgment seat of Caesar, where I ought to be tried. I have done nothing wrong to the Jews, as you yourself know very well.
25.kjv: Then said Paul, I stand at Cæsar’s judgment seat, where I ought to be judged: to the Jews have I done no wrong, as thou very well knowest.
25.blb: And Paul said, “I am standing before the judgment seat of Caesar, where it is necessary for me to be judged. I did nothing wrong to the Jews, as you also know very well.
25.bbe: And Paul said, I am before the seat of Caesar's authority where it is right for me to be judged: I have done no wrong to the Jews, as you are well able to see.
25.heading: Paul Appeals to Caesar

25.msb: If, however, I am guilty of anything worthy of death, I do not refuse to die. But if there is no truth to their accusations against me, no one has the right to hand me over to them. I appeal to Caesar!”
25.kjv: For if I be an offender, or have committed any thing worthy of death, I refuse not to die: but if there be none of these things whereof these accuse me, no man may deliver me unto them. I appeal unto Cæsar.
25.blb: Therefore if indeed I am unrighteous and have done anything worthy of death, I do not refuse to die. But if there is nothing of which they can accuse me, no one can give me up to them. I appeal to Caesar!”
25.bbe: If, then, I am a wrongdoer and there is a cause of death in me, I am ready for death: if it is not as they say against me, no man may give me up to them. Let my cause come before Caesar.

25.msb: Then Festus conferred with his council and replied, “You have appealed to Caesar. To Caesar you will go!”
25.kjv: Then Festus, when he had conferred with the council, answered, Hast thou appealed unto Cæsar? unto Cæsar shalt thou go.
25.blb: Then Festus, having conferred with the council, answered, “You have appealed to Caesar; to Caesar you will go!”
25.bbe: Then Festus, having had a discussion with the Jews, made answer, You have said, Let my cause come before Caesar; to Caesar you will go.

25.msb: After several days had passed, King Agrippa and Bernice came down to Caesarea to pay their respects to Festus.
25.kjv: And after certain days king Agrippa and Bernice came unto Cæsarea to salute Festus.
25.blb: Now some days having passed, Agrippa the king and Bernice came down to Caesarea, greeting Festus.
25.bbe: Now when some days had gone by, King Agrippa and Bernice came to Caesarea and went to see Festus.
25.heading: Festus Consults Agrippa

25.msb: Since he was staying several days, Festus laid out Paul’s case before the king: “There is a certain man whom Felix left in prison.
25.kjv: And when they had been there many days, Festus declared Paul’s cause unto the king, saying, There is a certain man left in bonds by Felix:
25.blb: And as they were staying there many days, Festus laid before the king the things relating to Paul, saying, “There is a certain man left by Felix, a prisoner,
25.bbe: And as they were there for some days, Festus gave them Paul's story, saying, There is a certain man here who was put in prison by Felix:

25.msb: While I was in Jerusalem, the chief priests and elders of the Jews presented their case and requested a judgment against him.
25.kjv: About whom, when I was at Jerusalem, the chief priests and the elders of the Jews informed me, desiring to have judgment against him.
25.blb: concerning whom, in my having been in Jerusalem, the chief priests and the elders of the Jews made a presentation, requesting a judgment against him,
25.bbe: Against whom the chief priests and the rulers of the Jews made a statement when I was at Jerusalem, requesting me to give a decision against him.

25.msb: I told them that it is not the Roman custom to hand a man over to die before he has had an opportunity to face his accusers and defend himself against their charges.
25.kjv: To whom I answered, It is not the manner of the Romans to deliver any man to die, before that he which is accused have the accusers face to face, and have licence to answer for himself concerning the crime laid against him.
25.blb: to whom I answered that it is not a custom with Romans to give up any man before the one being accused may have it to face the accusers and may have a place of defense concerning the accusation.
25.bbe: To whom I gave answer that it is not the Roman way to give a man up, till he has been face to face with those who are attacking him, and has had a chance to give an answer to the statements made against him.

25.msb: So when they came here with me, I did not delay. The next day I sat on the judgment seat and ordered that the man be brought in.
25.kjv: Therefore, when they were come hither, without any delay on the morrow I sat on the judgment seat, and commanded the man to be brought forth.
25.blb: Therefore on their having come together here, having made no delay, the next day having sat on the judgment seat, I commanded the man to be brought,
25.bbe: So, when they had come together here, straight away, on the day after, I took my place on the judge's seat and sent for the man.

25.msb: But when his accusers rose to speak, they did not charge him with anything I had expected.
25.kjv: Against whom when the accusers stood up, they brought none accusation of such things as I supposed:
25.blb: concerning whom the accusers, having stood up, were bringing no charge of the evils that I was expecting.
25.bbe: But when they got up they said nothing about such crimes as I had in mind:

25.msb: They only had some contentions with him regarding their own religion and a certain Jesus who had died, but whom Paul affirmed to be alive.
25.kjv: But had certain questions against him of their own superstition, and of one Jesus, which was dead, whom Paul affirmed to be alive.
25.blb: But they had certain questions against him concerning their own religion and concerning a certain Jesus having been dead, whom Paul was affirming to be alive.
25.bbe: But had certain questions against him in connection with their religion, and about one Jesus, now dead, who, Paul said, was living.

25.msb: Since I was at a loss as to how to investigate this matter, I asked if he was willing to go to Jerusalem and be tried there on these charges.
25.kjv: And because I doubted of such manner of questions, I asked him whether he would go to Jerusalem, and there be judged of these matters.
25.blb: Now I, being perplexed concerning this inquiry, was asking if he was willing to go to Jerusalem and there to be judged concerning these things.
25.bbe: And as I had not enough knowledge for the discussion of these things, I made the suggestion to him to go to Jerusalem and be judged there.

25.msb: But when Paul appealed to be held over for the decision of the Emperor, I ordered that he be held until I could send him to Caesar.”
25.kjv: But when Paul had appealed to be reserved unto the hearing of Augustus, I commanded him to be kept till I might send him to Cæsar.
25.blb: But Paul having appealed for himself to be kept for the decision of the Emperor, I commanded him to be kept until I might send him to Caesar.”
25.bbe: But when Paul made a request that he might be judged by Caesar, I gave orders for him to be kept till I might send him to Caesar.

25.msb: Then Agrippa said to Festus, “I would like to hear this man myself.” “Tomorrow you will hear him,” Festus declared.
25.kjv: Then Agrippa said unto Festus, I would also hear the man myself. To morrow, said he, thou shalt hear him.
25.blb: And Agrippa said to Festus, “I have also been wanting to hear the man myself.” He says, “Tomorrow you will hear him.”
25.bbe: And Agrippa said to Festus, I have a desire to give the man a hearing myself. Tomorrow, he said, you may give him a hearing.

25.msb: The next day Agrippa and Bernice came with great pomp and entered the auditorium, along with the commanders and leading men of the city. And Festus ordered that Paul be brought in.
25.kjv: And on the morrow, when Agrippa was come, and Bernice, with great pomp, and was entered into the place of hearing, with the chief captains, and principal men of the city, at Festus’ commandment Paul was brought forth.
25.blb: Therefore on the next day, Agrippa and Bernice having come with great pomp and having entered into the auditorium with both the commanders and the men of prominence in the city, and Festus having commanded, Paul was brought in.
25.bbe: So on the day after, when Agrippa and Bernice in great glory had come into the public place of hearing, with the chief of the army and the chief men of the town, at the order of Festus, Paul was sent for.
25.heading: Paul before Agrippa and Bernice

25.msb: Then Festus said, “King Agrippa and all who are present with us, you see this man. The whole Jewish community has petitioned me about him, both here and in Jerusalem, crying out that he ought not to live any longer.
25.kjv: And Festus said, King Agrippa, and all men which are here present with us, ye see this man, about whom all the multitude of the Jews have dealt with me, both at Jerusalem, and also here, crying that he ought not to live any longer.
25.blb: And Festus says, “King Agrippa and all men being present with us, you see this one concerning whom all the multitude of the Jews pleaded with me, both in Jerusalem and here, crying out of him that he ought not to live any longer.
25.bbe: And Festus said, King Agrippa, and all those who are present here with us, you see this man, about whom all the Jews have made protests to me, at Jerusalem and in this place, saying that it is not right for him to be living any longer.

25.msb: But I found he had done nothing worthy of death, and since he has now appealed to the Emperor, I decided to send him.
25.kjv: But when I found that he had committed nothing worthy of death, and that he himself hath appealed to Augustus, I have determined to send him.
25.blb: But I, having understood him to have done nothing worthy of death—this one himself now having appealed to the Emperor—I determined to send him,
25.bbe: But, in my opinion, there is no cause of death in him, and as he himself has made a request to be judged by Caesar, I have said that I would send him.

25.msb: I have nothing definite to write to our sovereign about him. Therefore I have brought him before all of you, and especially before you, King Agrippa, so that after this inquiry I may have something to write.
25.kjv: Of whom I have no certain thing to write unto my lord. Wherefore I have brought him forth before you, and specially before thee, O king Agrippa, that, after examination had, I might have somewhat to write.
25.blb: concerning whom I have nothing definite to write to my lord. Therefore I have brought him before you all, and especially before you, King Agrippa, so that on the examination having taken place, I might have something to write.
25.bbe: But I have no certain account of him to send to Caesar. So I have sent for him to come before you, and specially before you, King Agrippa, so that after the business has been gone into, I may have something to put in writing.

25.msb: For it seems unreasonable to me to send on a prisoner without specifying the charges against him.”
25.kjv: For it seemeth to me unreasonable to send a prisoner, and not withal to signify the crimes laid against him.
25.blb: For it seems absurd to me, sending a prisoner, not also to specify the charges against him.”
25.bbe: For it seems to me against reason to send a prisoner without making clear what there is against him.

26.msb: Agrippa said to Paul, “You have permission to speak for yourself.” Then Paul stretched out his hand and began his defense:
26.kjv: Then Agrippa said unto Paul, Thou art permitted to speak for thyself. Then Paul stretched forth the hand, and answered for himself:
26.blb: And Agrippa was saying to Paul, “It is permitted you to speak for yourself.” Then Paul, having stretched out the hand, began his defense:
26.bbe: And Agrippa said to Paul, You may put your cause before us. Then Paul, stretching out his hand, made his answer, saying:
26.heading: Paul’s Testimony to Agrippa

26.msb: “King Agrippa, I consider myself fortunate to stand before you today to defend myself against all the accusations of the Jews,
26.kjv: I think myself happy, king Agrippa, because I shall answer for myself this day before thee touching all the things whereof I am accused of the Jews:
26.blb: “Concerning all of which I am accused by the Jews, King Agrippa, I esteem myself fortunate before you, being about to defend myself today,
26.bbe: In my opinion I am happy, King Agrippa, to be able to give my answer before you today to all these things which the Jews say against me:

26.msb: especially since you are acquainted with all the Jewish customs and controversies. I beg you, therefore, to listen to me patiently.
26.kjv: Especially because I know thee to be expert in all customs and questions which are among the Jews: wherefore I beseech thee to hear me patiently.
26.blb: you being especially acquainted with all the customs and also controversies of the Jews. Therefore I implore you to hear me patiently.
26.bbe: The more so, because you are expert in all questions to do with the Jews and their ways: so I make my request to you to give me a hearing to the end.

26.msb: Surely all the Jews know how I have lived from my earliest childhood among my own people in Jerusalem.
26.kjv: My manner of life from my youth, which was at the first among mine own nation at Jerusalem, know all the Jews;
26.blb: Then indeed my manner of life, which is from youth, having been from its beginning among my nation and in Jerusalem, all the Jews know—
26.bbe: All the Jews have knowledge of my way of life from my early years, as it was from the start among my nation, and at Jerusalem;

26.msb: They have known me for a long time and can testify, if they are willing, that I lived as a Pharisee, adhering to the strictest sect of our religion.
26.kjv: Which knew me from the beginning, if they would testify, that after the most straitest sect of our religion I lived a Pharisee.
26.blb: knowing me from the first, if they would be willing to testify—that according to the strictest sect of our religion I lived as a Pharisee.
26.bbe: And they are able to say, if they would give witness, that I was living as a Pharisee, in that division of our religion which is most regular in the keeping of the law.

26.msb: And now I stand on trial because of my hope in the promise that God made to our fathers,
26.kjv: And now I stand and am judged for the hope of the promise made of God unto our fathers:
26.blb: And now I stand, being judged for the hope of the promise having been made by God to our fathers,
26.bbe: And now I am here to be judged because of the hope given by God's word to our fathers;

26.msb: the promise our twelve tribes are hoping to see fulfilled as they earnestly serve God day and night. It is because of this hope, O King Agrippa, that I am accused by the Jews.
26.kjv: Unto which promise our twelve tribes, instantly serving God day and night, hope to come. For which hope’s sake, king Agrippa, I am accused of the Jews.
26.blb: to which our twelve tribes hope to attain, serving in earnestness night and day, the hope concerning which I am accused by the Jews, O king.
26.bbe: For the effecting of which our twelve tribes have been working and waiting night and day with all their hearts. And in connection with this hope I am attacked by the Jews, O king!

26.msb: Why would any of you consider it incredible that God raises the dead?
26.kjv: Why should it be thought a thing incredible with you, that God should raise the dead?
26.blb: Why is it judged incredible by you if God raises the dead?
26.bbe: Why, in your opinion, is it outside belief for God to make the dead come to life again?

26.msb: So then, I too was convinced that I ought to do all I could to oppose the name of Jesus of Nazareth.
26.kjv: I verily thought with myself, that I ought to do many things contrary to the name of Jesus of Nazareth.
26.blb: Therefore I indeed in myself thought it to be necessary to do many things contrary to the name of Jesus of Nazareth,
26.bbe: For I, truly, was of the opinion that it was right for me to do a number of things against the name of Jesus of Nazareth.

26.msb: And that is what I did in Jerusalem. With authority from the chief priests I put many of the saints in prison, and when they were condemned to death, I cast my vote against them.
26.kjv: Which thing I also did in Jerusalem: and many of the saints did I shut up in prison, having received authority from the chief priests; and when they were put to death, I gave my voice against them.
26.blb: which I also did in Jerusalem. And I also locked up many of the saints in prisons, having received the authority from the chief priests; and on their being put to death, I cast against them a vote.
26.bbe: And this I did in Jerusalem: and numbers of the saints I put in prison, having had authority given to me from the chief priests, and when they were put to death, I gave my decision against them.

26.msb: I frequently had them punished in the synagogues, and I tried to make them blaspheme. In my raging fury against them, I even went to foreign cities to persecute them.
26.kjv: And I punished them oft in every synagogue, and compelled them to blaspheme; and being exceedingly mad against them, I persecuted them even unto strange cities.
26.blb: And in all the synagogues, punishing them often, I was compelling them to blaspheme. And being exceedingly furious against them, I was persecuting them even as far as to foreign cities,
26.bbe: And I gave them punishment frequently, in all the Synagogues, forcing them to say things against God; and burning with passion against them, I went after them even into far-away towns.

26.msb: In this pursuit I was on my way to Damascus with the authority and commission of the chief priests.
26.kjv: Whereupon as I went to Damascus with authority and commission from the chief priests,
26.blb: during which, going to Damascus with the authority and commission of the chief priests,
26.bbe: Then, when I was journeying to Damascus with the authority and orders of the chief priests,

26.msb: About noon, O king, as I was on the road, I saw a light from heaven, brighter than the sun, shining around me and my companions.
26.kjv: At midday, O king, I saw in the way a light from heaven, above the brightness of the sun, shining round about me and them which journeyed with me.
26.blb: at midday on the road I saw, O king, a light from heaven above the brightness of the sun having shone around me and those going with me.
26.bbe: In the middle of the day, on the road I saw a light from heaven, brighter than the sun, shining round me and those who were journeying with me.

26.msb: We all fell to the ground, and I heard a voice say to me in Hebrew, ‘Saul, Saul, why do you persecute Me? It is hard for you to kick against the goads.’
26.kjv: And when we were all fallen to the earth, I heard a voice speaking unto me, and saying in the Hebrew tongue, Saul, Saul, why persecutest thou me? it is hard for thee to kick against the pricks.
26.blb: And all of us having fallen down to the ground, I heard a voice saying to me in the Hebrew language, ‘Saul, Saul, why do you persecute Me? It is hard for you to kick against the goads.’
26.bbe: And when we had all gone down on the earth, a voice came to me, saying in the Hebrew language, Saul, Saul, why are you attacking me so cruelly? It is hard for you to go against the impulse which is driving you.

26.msb: ‘Who are You, Lord?’ I asked. ‘I am Jesus, whom you are persecuting,’ He replied.
26.kjv: And I said, Who art thou, Lord? And he said, I am Jesus whom thou persecutest.
26.blb: Then I said, ‘Who are You, Lord?’ And the Lord said, ‘I am Jesus, whom you are persecuting.
26.bbe: And I said, Who are you, Lord? And the Lord said, I am Jesus, whom you are attacking.

26.msb: ‘But get up and stand on your feet. For I have appeared to you to appoint you as a servant and as a witness of what you have seen and what I will show you.
26.kjv: But rise, and stand upon thy feet: for I have appeared unto thee for this purpose, to make thee a minister and a witness both of these things which thou hast seen, and of those things in the which I will appear unto thee;
26.blb: But rise up and stand on your feet. For I have appeared to you for this, to appoint you as a servant and a witness both of that which you have seen of Me and of the things in which I will appear to you,
26.bbe: But get up on your feet: for I have come to you for this purpose, to make you a servant and a witness of the things in which you have seen me, and of those in which you will see me;

26.msb: I will rescue you from your own people and from the Gentiles. I am sending you to them
26.kjv: Delivering thee from the people, and from the Gentiles, unto whom now I send thee,
26.blb: delivering you from the people and from the Gentiles, to whom I am sending you
26.bbe: And I will keep you safe from the people, and from the Gentiles, to whom I send you,

26.msb: to open their eyes, so that they may turn from darkness to light and from the power of Satan to God, that they may receive forgiveness of sins and an inheritance among those sanctified by faith in Me.’
26.kjv: To open their eyes, and to turn them from darkness to light, and from the power of Satan unto God, that they may receive forgiveness of sins, and inheritance among them which are sanctified by faith that is in me.
26.blb: to open their eyes, so that they may turn from darkness to light and from the power of Satan to God, that they may receive forgiveness of sins and an inheritance among those having been sanctified by faith in Me.’
26.bbe: To make their eyes open, turning them from the dark to the light, and from the power of Satan to God, so that they may have forgiveness of sins and a heritage among those who are made holy by faith in me.

26.msb: So then, King Agrippa, I was not disobedient to the heavenly vision.
26.kjv: Whereupon, O king Agrippa, I was not disobedient unto the heavenly vision:
26.blb: Hence, King Agrippa, I was not disobedient to the heavenly vision,
26.bbe: So, then, King Agrippa, I did not go against the vision from heaven;

26.msb: First to those in Damascus and Jerusalem, then to everyone throughout the region of Judea, and then to the Gentiles, I declared that they should repent and turn to God, performing deeds worthy of their repentance.
26.kjv: But shewed first unto them of Damascus, and at Jerusalem, and throughout all the coasts of Judæa, and then to the Gentiles, that they should repent and turn to God, and do works meet for repentance.
26.blb: but also first to those in Damascus and Jerusalem, also to all the region of Judea, and to the Gentiles, I was declaring to repent and to turn to God, doing works worthy of repentance.
26.bbe: But I went about, first to those in Damascus and Jerusalem, and through all the country of Judaea, and then to the Gentiles, preaching a change of heart, so that they, being turned to God, might give, in their works, the fruits of a changed heart.

26.msb: For this reason the Jews seized me in the temple courts and tried to kill me.
26.kjv: For these causes the Jews caught me in the temple, and went about to kill me.
26.blb: On account of these things the Jews, having seized me (being in the temple), were attempting to kill me.
26.bbe: For this reason, the Jews took me in the Temple, and made an attempt to put me to death.

26.msb: But I have had God’s help to this day, and I stand here to testify to small and great alike. I am saying nothing beyond what the prophets and Moses said would happen:
26.kjv: Having therefore obtained help of God, I continue unto this day, witnessing both to small and great, saying none other things than those which the prophets and Moses did say should come:
26.blb: Therefore, having obtained help from God up to this day, I have stood bearing witness both to small and to great, saying nothing other than that which both the prophets and Moses said was about to happen:
26.bbe: And so, by God's help, I am here today, witnessing to small and great, saying nothing but what the prophets and Moses said would come about;

26.msb: that the Christ would suffer, and as the first to rise from the dead, would proclaim light to our people and to the Gentiles.”
26.kjv: That Christ should suffer, and that he should be the first that should rise from the dead, and should shew light unto the people, and to the Gentiles.
26.blb: that the Christ would suffer and, as first through resurrection from the dead, He is about to proclaim light both to our people and to the Gentiles.”
26.bbe: That the Christ would go through pain, and being the first to come back from the dead, would give light to the people and to the Gentiles.

26.msb: At this stage of Paul’s defense, Festus exclaimed in a loud voice, “You are insane, Paul! Your great learning is driving you to madness!”
26.kjv: And as he thus spake for himself, Festus said with a loud voice, Paul, thou art beside thyself; much learning doth make thee mad.
26.blb: Now of him making this defense, Festus said in a loud voice, “You are insane, Paul! Much learning turns you to insanity!”
26.bbe: And when he made his answer in these words, Festus said in a loud voice, Paul, you are off your head; your great learning has made you unbalanced.
26.heading: Festus Interrupts Paul’s Defense

26.msb: But he answered, “I am not insane, most excellent Festus; I am speaking words of truth and sobriety.
26.kjv: But he said, I am not mad, most noble Festus; but speak forth the words of truth and soberness.
26.blb: But Paul says, “I am not insane, most excellent Festus, but I declare forth words of truth and sobriety.
26.bbe: Then Paul said, I am not off my head, most noble Festus, but my words are true and wise.

26.msb: For the king knows about these matters, and I can speak freely to him. I am confident that none of this has escaped his notice, because it was not done in a corner.
26.kjv: For the king knoweth of these things, before whom also I speak freely: for I am persuaded that none of these things are hidden from him; for this thing was not done in a corner.
26.blb: For the king understands concerning these things, to whom also I speak, being bold. For I am persuaded that none of these things are hidden from him, for this thing is not done in a corner.
26.bbe: For the king has knowledge of these things, to whom I am talking freely; being certain that all this is common knowledge to him; for it has not been done in secret.

26.msb: King Agrippa, do you believe the prophets? I know you do.”
26.kjv: King Agrippa, believest thou the prophets? I know that thou believest.
26.blb: Do you believe the prophets, King Agrippa? I know that you believe.”
26.bbe: King Agrippa, have you faith in the prophets? I am certain that you have.

26.msb: Then Agrippa said to Paul, “Can you persuade me in such a short time to become a Christian?”
26.kjv: Then Agrippa said unto Paul, Almost thou persuadest me to be a Christian.
26.blb: Then Agrippa said to Paul, “In so little time do you persuade me to become a Christian?”
26.bbe: And Agrippa said to Paul, A little more and you will be making me a Christian.

26.msb: “Short time or long,” Paul replied, “I wish to God that not only you but all who hear me this day may become what I am, except for these chains.”
26.kjv: And Paul said, I would to God, that not only thou, but also all that hear me this day, were both almost, and altogether such as I am, except these bonds.
26.blb: And Paul said, “I would wish anyhow to God, both in a little and in much, not only you, but also all those hearing me this day, to become such as I also am, except these chains.”
26.bbe: And Paul said, It is my prayer to God that, in little or great measure, not only you, but all those hearing me today might be even as I am, but for these chains.

26.msb: When he had spoken these things, the king and the governor rose, along with Bernice and those seated with them.
26.kjv: And when he had thus spoken, the king rose up, and the governor, and Bernice, and they that sat with them:
26.blb: Then the king and the governor rose up, and Bernice and those sitting with them,
26.bbe: And the king and the ruler and Bernice and those who were seated with them got up;

26.msb: On their way out, they said to one another, “This man has done nothing worthy of death or imprisonment.”
26.kjv: And when they were gone aside, they talked between themselves, saying, This man doeth nothing worthy of death or of bonds.
26.blb: and having withdrawn, they began speaking to one another, saying, “This man is doing nothing worthy of death or of chains.”
26.bbe: And when they had gone away they said to one another, This man has done nothing which might give cause for death or prison.

26.msb: And Agrippa said to Festus, “This man could have been released if he had not appealed to Caesar.”
26.kjv: Then said Agrippa unto Festus, This man might have been set at liberty, if he had not appealed unto Cæsar.
26.blb: Then Agrippa was saying to Festus, “This man could have been released if he had not appealed to Caesar.”
26.bbe: And Agrippa said to Festus, This man might have been made free, if he had not put his cause before Caesar.

27.msb: When it was decided that we would sail for Italy, Paul and some other prisoners were handed over to a centurion named Julius, who belonged to the Imperial Regiment.
27.kjv: And when it was determined that we should sail into Italy, they delivered Paul and certain other prisoners unto one named Julius, a centurion of Augustus’ band.
27.blb: Now when our sailing to Italy was determined, they delivered up both Paul and certain other prisoners to a centurion named Julius, of the cohort of Augustus.
27.bbe: And when the decision had been made that we were to go by sea to Italy, they gave Paul and certain other prisoners into the care of a captain named Julius, of the Augustan band.
27.heading: Paul Sails for Rome

27.msb: We boarded an Adramyttian ship about to sail for ports along the coast of Asia, and we put out to sea. Aristarchus, a Macedonian from Thessalonica, was with us.
27.kjv: And entering into a ship of Adramyttium, we launched, meaning to sail by the coasts of Asia; one Aristarchus, a Macedonian of Thessalonica, being with us.
27.blb: And having boarded a ship of Adramyttium being about to sail to the places along Asia, we set sail—Aristarchus, a Macedonian of Thessalonica, being with us.
27.bbe: And we went to sea in a ship of Adramyttium which was sailing to the sea towns of Asia, Aristarchus, a Macedonian of Thessalonica, being with us.

27.msb: The next day we landed at Sidon, and Julius treated Paul with consideration, allowing him to visit his friends and receive their care.
27.kjv: And the next day we touched at Sidon. And Julius courteously entreated Paul, and gave him liberty to go unto his friends to refresh himself.
27.blb: And the next day we landed at Sidon. And Julius, having treated Paul considerately, allowed him, having gone to his friends, to receive care.
27.bbe: And on the day after, we came to Sidon; and Julius was kind to Paul, and let him go to see his friends and take a rest.

27.msb: After putting out from there, we sailed to the lee of Cyprus because the winds were against us.
27.kjv: And when we had launched from thence, we sailed under Cyprus, because the winds were contrary.
27.blb: And having set sail from there, we sailed under Cyprus because of the winds being contrary.
27.bbe: And sailing again from there, we went on under cover of Cyprus, because the wind was against us.

27.msb: And when we had sailed across the open sea off the coast of Cilicia and Pamphylia, we came to Myra in Lycia.
27.kjv: And when we had sailed over the sea of Cilicia and Pamphylia, we came to Myra, a city of Lycia.
27.blb: And having sailed across the sea along Cilicia and Pamphylia, we came to Myra of Lycia.
27.bbe: And having gone across the sea off Cilicia and Pamphylia we came to Myra, in Lycia.

27.msb: There the centurion found an Alexandrian ship sailing for Italy and put us on board.
27.kjv: And there the centurion found a ship of Alexandria sailing into Italy; and he put us therein.
27.blb: And there the centurion, having found a ship of Alexandria sailing to Italy, placed us into it.
27.bbe: And there the captain came across a ship of Alexandria, sailing for Italy, and put us in it.

27.msb: After sailing slowly for many days, we arrived off Cnidus. When the wind impeded us, we sailed to the lee of Crete, opposite Salmone.
27.kjv: And when we had sailed slowly many days, and scarce were come over against Cnidus, the wind not suffering us, we sailed under Crete, over against Salmone;
27.blb: And sailing slowly for many days, and with difficulty having arrived off Cnidus, the wind not permitting us, we sailed under Crete off Salmone.
27.bbe: And when we had gone on slowly for a long time, and had had hard work getting across to Cnidus, for the wind was against us, we went under cover of Crete, in the direction of Salmone;

27.msb: After we had moved along the coast with difficulty, we came to a place called Fair Havens, near the town of Lasea.
27.kjv: And, hardly passing it, came unto a place which is called The fair havens; nigh whereunto was the city of Lasea.
27.blb: And coasting along it with difficulty, we came to a certain place called Fair Havens, near to which was the city of Lasea.
27.bbe: And sailing down the side of it, as well as we were able, we came to a certain place named Fair Havens, near which was the town of Lasea.

27.msb: By now much time had passed, and the voyage had already become dangerous because it was after the Fast. So Paul advised them,
27.kjv: Now when much time was spent, and when sailing was now dangerous, because the fast was now already past, Paul admonished them,
27.blb: Now much time having passed and the voyage being already dangerous because of even the Fast already being over, Paul was admonishing them,
27.bbe: And as a long time had gone by, and the journey was now full of danger, because it was late in the year, Paul put the position before them,

27.msb: “Men, I can see that our voyage will be filled with disaster and great loss, not only to ship and cargo, but to our own lives as well.”
27.kjv: And said unto them, Sirs, I perceive that this voyage will be with hurt and much damage, not only of the lading and ship, but also of our lives.
27.blb: saying to them, “Men, I see that the voyage is about to be with disaster and much loss, not only of the cargo and of the ship, but also of our lives.”
27.bbe: Saying, Friends, I see that this journey will be one of great damage and loss, not only to the goods and the ship, but to ourselves.

27.msb: But contrary to Paul’s advice, the centurion was persuaded by the pilot and by the owner of the ship.
27.kjv: Nevertheless the centurion believed the master and the owner of the ship, more than those things which were spoken by Paul.
27.blb: But the centurion was persuaded by the pilot and the ship owner rather than by the things spoken by Paul.
27.bbe: But the captain gave more attention to the master and the owner of the ship than to what Paul said.

27.msb: Since the harbor was unsuitable to winter in, the majority decided to sail on, hoping that somehow they could reach Phoenix to winter there. Phoenix was a harbor in Crete facing both southwest and northwest.
27.kjv: And because the haven was not commodious to winter in, the more part advised to depart thence also, if by any means they might attain to Phenice, and there to winter; which is an haven of Crete, and lieth toward the south west and north west.
27.blb: And the harbor being unsuitable to winter in, the majority made a decision to set sail from there, if somehow they might be able, having arrived at Phoenix—a harbor of Crete looking toward the southwest and toward the northwest—to winter there.
27.bbe: And as the harbour was not a good one in which to be for the winter, the greater number of them were for going out to sea, in order, if possible, to put in for the winter at Phoenix, a harbour of Crete, looking to the north-east and south-east.

27.msb: When a gentle south wind began to blow, they thought they had their opportunity. So they weighed anchor and sailed along, hugging the coast of Crete.
27.kjv: And when the south wind blew softly, supposing that they had obtained their purpose, loosing thence, they sailed close by Crete.
27.blb: And a south wind having blown gently, having thought to have obtained their purpose, having weighed anchor, they began coasting along very near Crete.
27.bbe: And when the south wind came softly, being of the opinion that their purpose might be effected, they let the ship go and went sailing down the side of Crete, very near to the land.
27.heading: The Storm at Sea

27.msb: But it was not long before a cyclone called the Northeaster swept down across the island.
27.kjv: But not long after there arose against it a tempestuous wind, called Euroclydon.
27.blb: But not long after, there came down from it a tempestuous wind called Euroclydon.
27.bbe: But after a little time, a very violent wind, named Euraquilo, came down from it with great force.

27.msb: Unable to head into the wind, the ship was caught up. So we gave way and let ourselves be driven along.
27.kjv: And when the ship was caught, and could not bear up into the wind, we let her drive.
27.blb: And the ship having been caught and not being able to face the wind, having given way, we were driven along.
27.bbe: And when the ship got into the grip of it, and was not able to make headway into the wind, we gave way, and went before it.

27.msb: Passing to the lee of a small island called Clauda, we barely managed to secure the lifeboat.
27.kjv: And running under a certain island which is called Clauda, we had much work to come by the boat:
27.blb: And having run under a certain island called Cauda, we were able with difficulty to gain control of the lifeboat,
27.bbe: And, sailing near the side of a small island named Cauda, we were able, though it was hard work, to make the ship's boat safe:

27.msb: After hoisting it up, the crew used ropes to undergird the ship. And fearing that they would run aground on the sandbars of Syrtis, they lowered the sea anchor and were driven along.
27.kjv: Which when they had taken up, they used helps, undergirding the ship; and, fearing lest they should fall into the quicksands, strake sail, and so were driven.
27.blb: which having taken up, they began using supports, undergirding the ship. And fearing lest they might fall into the sandbars of Syrtis, having lowered the gear, thus they were driven along.
27.bbe: And having got it up, they put cords under and round the ship; but fearing that they might be pushed on to the Syrtis, they let down the sails and so went running before the wind.

27.msb: We were tossed so violently that the next day the men began to jettison the cargo.
27.kjv: And we being exceedingly tossed with a tempest, the next day they lightened the ship;
27.blb: And in our being storm-tossed violently, on the next day they began to make a jettison of cargo,
27.bbe: And, still fighting the storm with all our strength, the day after they made a start at getting the goods out of the ship;

27.msb: On the third day, we threw the ship’s tackle overboard with our own hands.
27.kjv: And the third day we cast out with our own hands the tackling of the ship.
27.blb: and on the third day they cast away the tackle of the ship with their own hands.
27.bbe: And on the third day, they let all the sailing apparatus go over the side.

27.msb: When neither sun nor stars appeared for many days and the great storm continued to batter us, we abandoned all hope of being saved.
27.kjv: And when neither sun nor stars in many days appeared, and no small tempest lay on us, all hope that we should be saved was then taken away.
27.blb: And neither sun nor stars appearing for many days, and no small storm lying on us, from then on all hope of our being saved was abandoned.
27.bbe: And as we had not seen the sun or stars for a long time, and a great storm was on us, all hope of salvation was gone.

27.msb: After the men had gone a long time without food, Paul stood up among them and said, “Men, you should have followed my advice not to sail from Crete. Then you would have averted this disaster and loss.
27.kjv: But after long abstinence Paul stood forth in the midst of them, and said, Sirs, ye should have hearkened unto me, and not have loosed from Crete, and to have gained this harm and loss.
27.blb: There being also much time without food, at that time having stood up in their midst, Paul said, “It was necessary indeed, O men, having been obedient to me, not to have set sail from Crete and to have incurred this disaster and loss.
27.bbe: And when they had been without food for a long time, Paul got up among them and said, Friends, it would have been better if you had given attention to me and not gone sailing out from Crete, to undergo this damage and loss.

27.msb: But now I urge you to keep up your courage, because you will not experience any loss of life, but only of the ship.
27.kjv: And now I exhort you to be of good cheer: for there shall be no loss of any man’s life among you, but of the ship.
27.blb: And now I exhort you to take heart, for there will be no loss of life from among you—only of the ship.
27.bbe: But now, I say to you, be of good heart, for there will be no loss of life, but only of the ship.

27.msb: For just last night an angel of the God to whom I belong and whom I serve stood beside me
27.kjv: For there stood by me this night the angel of God, whose I am, and whom I serve,
27.blb: For this night an angel of God, whose I am and whom I serve, stood by me,
27.bbe: For this night there came to my side an angel of the God who is my Master and whose servant I am,

27.msb: and said, ‘Do not be afraid, Paul; you must stand before Caesar. And look, God has granted you the lives of all who sail with you.’
27.kjv: Saying, Fear not, Paul; thou must be brought before Cæsar: and, lo, God hath given thee all them that sail with thee.
27.blb: saying, ‘Do not be afraid, Paul. It is necessary for you to stand before Caesar. And behold, God has granted to you all those sailing with you.’
27.bbe: Saying, Have no fear, Paul, for you will come before Caesar, and God has given to you all those who are sailing with you.

27.msb: So take courage, men, for I believe God that it will happen just as He told me.
27.kjv: Wherefore, sirs, be of good cheer: for I believe God, that it shall be even as it was told me.
27.blb: Therefore take heart, men, for I believe God that it will be thus, according to the way it has been said to me.
27.bbe: And so, O men, be of good heart, for I have faith in God that it will be as he said to me.

27.msb: However, we must run aground on some island.”
27.kjv: Howbeit we must be cast upon a certain island.
27.blb: But it is necessary for us to fall upon a certain island.”
27.bbe: But we will be sent on to a certain island.

27.msb: On the fourteenth night we were still being driven across the Adriatic Sea. About midnight the sailors sensed they were approaching land.
27.kjv: But when the fourteenth night was come, as we were driven up and down in Adria, about midnight the shipmen deemed that they drew near to some country;
27.blb: And when the fourteenth night had come of us being driven about in the Adriatic, toward the middle of the night the sailors began sensing some land to be drawing near to them.
27.bbe: But when the fourteenth day came, while we were going here and there in the Adriatic sea, about the middle of the night the sailors had an idea that they were getting near land;
27.heading: The Shipwreck

27.msb: They took soundings and found that the water was twenty fathoms deep. Going a little farther, they took another set of soundings that read fifteen fathoms.
27.kjv: And sounded, and found it twenty fathoms: and when they had gone a little further, they sounded again, and found it fifteen fathoms.
27.blb: And having taken soundings, they found twenty fathoms. And having gone a little farther and having taken soundings again, they found fifteen fathoms.
27.bbe: And they let down the lead, and saw that the sea was a hundred and twenty feet deep; and after a little time they did it again and it was ninety feet.

27.msb: Fearing that we would run aground on the rocks, they dropped four anchors from the stern and prayed for daybreak.
27.kjv: Then fearing lest we should have fallen upon rocks, they cast four anchors out of the stern, and wished for the day.
27.blb: And fearing, lest we might fall somewhere on rocky places, having cast four anchors out of the stern, they were praying for day to come.
27.bbe: Then, fearing that by chance we might come on to the rocks, they let down four hooks from the back of the ship, and made prayers for the coming of day.

27.msb: Meanwhile, the sailors attempted to escape from the ship. Pretending to lower anchors from the bow, they let the lifeboat down into the sea.
27.kjv: And as the shipmen were about to flee out of the ship, when they had let down the boat into the sea, under colour as though they would have cast anchors out of the foreship,
27.blb: And the sailors seeking to flee out of the ship and having let down the lifeboat into the sea under pretense as being about to cast out anchors from the bow,
27.bbe: Then the sailors made attempts secretly to get away from the ship, letting down a boat as if they were about to put down hooks from the front of the ship;

27.msb: But Paul said to the centurion and the soldiers, “Unless these men remain with the ship, you cannot be saved.”
27.kjv: Paul said to the centurion and to the soldiers, Except these abide in the ship, ye cannot be saved.
27.blb: Paul said to the centurion and to the soldiers, “Unless these remain in the ship, you are not able to be saved.”
27.bbe: But Paul said to the captain and his men, If you do not keep these men in the ship, you will not be safe.

27.msb: So the soldiers cut the ropes to the lifeboat and set it adrift.
27.kjv: Then the soldiers cut off the ropes of the boat, and let her fall off.
27.blb: Then the soldiers cut away the ropes of the lifeboat and allowed it to fall away.
27.bbe: Then the armed men, cutting the cords of the boat, let her go.

27.msb: Right up to daybreak, Paul kept urging them all to eat: “Today is your fourteenth day in constant suspense, without taking any food.
27.kjv: And while the day was coming on, Paul besought them all to take meat, saying, This day is the fourteenth day that ye have tarried and continued fasting, having taken nothing.
27.blb: And until that day was about to come, Paul kept urging all to partake of food, saying, “Today is the fourteenth day you continue waiting without eating, having taken nothing.
27.bbe: And when dawn was near, Paul gave them all orders to take food, saying, This is the fourteenth day you have been waiting and taking no food.

27.msb: So for your own preservation, I urge you to eat something, because not a single hair of your head will be lost.”
27.kjv: Wherefore I pray you to take some meat: for this is for your health: for there shall not an hair fall from the head of any of you.
