27.blb: Therefore I exhort you to take food, for this is for your preservation; for not one hair of your head will perish.”
27.bbe: So I make request to you to take food; for this is for your salvation: not a hair from the head of any of you will come to destruction.

27.msb: After he had said this, Paul took bread and gave thanks to God in front of them all. Then he broke it and began to eat.
27.kjv: And when he had thus spoken, he took bread, and gave thanks to God in presence of them all: and when he had broken it, he began to eat.
27.blb: And having said these things and having taken bread, he gave thanks to God before all; and having broken it, he began to eat.
27.bbe: And when he had said this and had taken bread, he gave praise to God before them all, and took a meal of the broken bread.

27.msb: They were all encouraged and took some food themselves.
27.kjv: Then were they all of good cheer, and they also took some meat.
27.blb: And all, having been encouraged, also took food themselves.
27.bbe: Then they all took heart and did the same.

27.msb: In all, there were 276 of us on board.
27.kjv: And we were in all in the ship two hundred threescore and sixteen souls.
27.blb: And we were altogether two hundred seventy-six souls in the ship.
27.bbe: And we were, in the ship, two hundred and seventy-six persons.

27.msb: After the men had eaten their fill, they lightened the ship by throwing the grain into the sea.
27.kjv: And when they had eaten enough, they lightened the ship, and cast out the wheat into the sea.
27.blb: And having been filled with food, they began to lighten the ship, casting out the wheat into the sea.
27.bbe: And when they had had enough food, they made the weight of the ship less, turning the grain out into the sea.

27.msb: When daylight came, they did not recognize the land, but they sighted a bay with a sandy beach, where they decided to run the ship aground if possible.
27.kjv: And when it was day, they knew not the land: but they discovered a certain creek with a shore, into the which they were minded, if it were possible, to thrust in the ship.
27.blb: And when it was day, they did not recognize the land, but they noticed a certain bay, having a shore on which they decided to drive the ship if they could.
27.bbe: And when it was day, they had no knowledge of the land, but they saw an inlet of the sea with a floor of sand, and they had the idea of driving the ship up on to it if possible.

27.msb: Cutting away the anchors, they left them in the sea as they loosened the ropes that held the rudders. Then they hoisted the foresail to the wind and made for the beach.
27.kjv: And when they had taken up the anchors, they committed themselves unto the sea, and loosed the rudder bands, and hoised up the mainsail to the wind, and made toward shore.
27.blb: And having cut away the anchors, they left them in the sea, at the same time having loosened the ropes of the rudders. And having hoisted the foresail to the blowing wind, they began making for the shore.
27.bbe: So cutting away the hooks, and letting them go into the sea, and freeing the cords of the guiding-blades, and lifting up the sail to the wind, they went in the direction of the inlet.

27.msb: But the ship struck a sandbar and ran aground. The bow stuck fast and would not move, and the stern was being broken up by the pounding of the waves.
27.kjv: And falling into a place where two seas met, they ran the ship aground; and the forepart stuck fast, and remained unmoveable, but the hinder part was broken with the violence of the waves.
27.blb: But having fallen into a place between two seas, they ran the vessel aground. And indeed the bow, having stuck fast, remained immovable, and the stern was being broken up by the violence of the waves.
27.bbe: And coming to a point between two seas, they got the ship to land; and the front part was fixed in the sand and not able to be moved, but the back part was broken by the force of the waves.

27.msb: The soldiers planned to kill the prisoners so none of them could swim to freedom.
27.kjv: And the soldiers’ counsel was to kill the prisoners, lest any of them should swim out, and escape.
27.blb: Now the plan of the soldiers was that they should kill the prisoners, lest anyone, having swum away, should escape.
27.bbe: Then the armed men were for putting the prisoners to death, so that no one would get away by swimming.

27.msb: But the centurion, wanting to spare Paul’s life, thwarted their plan. He commanded those who could swim to jump overboard first and get to land.
27.kjv: But the centurion, willing to save Paul, kept them from their purpose; and commanded that they which could swim should cast themselves first into the sea, and get to land:
27.blb: But the centurion, desiring to save Paul, hindered them of the plan; and he commanded those being able to swim, having cast themselves off first, to go out on the land,
27.bbe: But the captain, desiring to keep Paul safe, kept them from their purpose, and gave orders that those who had knowledge of swimming were to go off the ship and get first to land:

27.msb: The rest were to follow on planks and various parts of the ship. In this way everyone was brought safely to land.
27.kjv: And the rest, some on boards, and some on broken pieces of the ship. And so it came to pass, that they escaped all safe to land.
27.blb: and the rest, some indeed on boards and some on things from the ship. And thus it came to pass that all were brought safely to the land.
27.bbe: And the rest, some on boards and some on things from the ship. And so it came about that they all got safe to land.

28.msb: Once we were safely ashore, we learned that the island was called Malta.
28.kjv: And when they were escaped, then they knew that the island was called Melita.
28.blb: And having been saved, then we found out that the island is called Malta.
28.bbe: And when we were safe, we made the discovery that the island was named Melita.
28.heading: Ashore on Malta

28.msb: The islanders showed us extraordinary kindness. They kindled a fire and welcomed all of us because it was raining and cold.
28.kjv: And the barbarous people shewed us no little kindness: for they kindled a fire, and received us every one, because of the present rain, and because of the cold.
28.blb: And the natives were showing not just the ordinary kindness to us. For having kindled a fire, they received all of us because of the rain setting in and because of the cold.
28.bbe: And the simple people living there were uncommonly kind to us, for they made a fire for us, and took us in, because it was raining and cold.

28.msb: Paul gathered a bundle of sticks, and as he laid them on the fire, a viper, driven out by the heat, fastened itself to his hand.
28.kjv: And when Paul had gathered a bundle of sticks, and laid them on the fire, there came a viper out of the heat, and fastened on his hand.
28.blb: Now on Paul having gathered a multitude of sticks and having laid them on the fire, a viper, having come out from the heat, fastened itself on his hand.
28.bbe: But when Paul had got some sticks together and put them on the fire, a snake came out, because of the heat, and gave him a bite on the hand.

28.msb: When the islanders saw the creature hanging from his hand, they said to one another, “Surely this man is a murderer. Although he was saved from the sea, Justice has not allowed him to live.”
28.kjv: And when the barbarians saw the venomous beast hang on his hand, they said among themselves, No doubt this man is a murderer, whom, though he hath escaped the sea, yet vengeance suffereth not to live.
28.blb: And when the natives saw the beast hanging from his hand, they began to say to one another, “By all means this man is a murderer whom, having been saved from the sea, Dike did not permit to live.”
28.bbe: And when the people saw it hanging on his hand, they said to one another, Without doubt this man has put someone to death, and though he has got safely away from the sea, God will not let him go on living.

28.msb: But Paul shook the creature off into the fire and suffered no ill effects.
28.kjv: And he shook off the beast into the fire, and felt no harm.
28.blb: Then indeed, having shaken off the creature into the fire, he suffered no harm.
28.bbe: But shaking off the beast into the fire, he got no damage.

28.msb: The islanders were expecting him to swell up or suddenly drop dead. But after waiting a long time and seeing nothing unusual happen to him, they changed their minds and said he was a god.
28.kjv: Howbeit they looked when he should have swollen, or fallen down dead suddenly: but after they had looked a great while, and saw no harm come to him, they changed their minds, and said that he was a god.
28.blb: But they were expecting him to be about to become inflamed or suddenly to fall down dead. But on their waiting a great while and seeing nothing amiss happening to him, having changed their opinion, they began declaring him to be a god.
28.bbe: But they had the idea that they would see him becoming ill, or suddenly falling down dead; but after waiting a long time, and seeing that no damage came to him, changing their opinion, they said he was a god.

28.msb: Nearby stood an estate belonging to Publius, the chief official of the island. He welcomed us and entertained us hospitably for three days.
28.kjv: In the same quarters were possessions of the chief man of the island, whose name was Publius; who received us, and lodged us three days courteously.
28.blb: Now in the parts around that place were lands of the chief of the island, named Publius, who, having received us, entertained us hospitably for three days.
28.bbe: Now near that place there was some land, the property of the chief man of the island, who was named Publius; who very kindly took us into his house as his guests for three days.

28.msb: The father of Publius was sick in bed, suffering from fever and dysentery. Paul went in to see him, and after praying and placing his hands on him, he healed the man.
28.kjv: And it came to pass, that the father of Publius lay sick of a fever and of a bloody flux: to whom Paul entered in, and prayed, and laid his hands on him, and healed him.
28.blb: And it came to pass that the father of Publius was lying, oppressed with fevers and dysentery, toward whom Paul, having entered and having prayed, having laid the hands on him, healed him.
28.bbe: And the father of Publius was ill, with a disease of the stomach; to whom Paul went, and put his hands on him, with prayer, and made him well.

28.msb: After this had happened, the rest of the sick on the island came and were cured as well.
28.kjv: So when this was done, others also, which had diseases in the island, came, and were healed:
28.blb: And on this having taken place, also the rest in the island having infirmities were coming and were healed,
28.bbe: And when this took place, all the others in the island who had diseases came and were made well.

28.msb: The islanders honored us in many ways and supplied our needs when we were ready to sail.
28.kjv: Who also honoured us with many honours; and when we departed, they laded us with such things as were necessary.
28.blb: who also honored us with many honors, and on setting sail, they laid on us the things for our needs.
28.bbe: Then they gave us great honour, and, when we went away, they put into the ship whatever things we were in need of.

28.msb: After three months we set sail in an Alexandrian ship that had wintered in the island. It had the Twin Brothers as a figurehead.
28.kjv: And after three months we departed in a ship of Alexandria, which had wintered in the isle, whose sign was Castor and Pollux.
28.blb: And after three months, we sailed in an Alexandrian ship having wintered in the island, with a figurehead of the Dioscuri.
28.bbe: And after three months we went to sea in a ship of Alexandria sailing under the sign of the Dioscuri, which had been at the island for the winter.
28.heading: Paul Arrives in Italy

28.msb: Putting in at Syracuse, we stayed there three days.
28.kjv: And landing at Syracuse, we tarried there three days.
28.blb: And having put in at Syracuse, we stayed three days,
28.bbe: And going into the harbour at Syracuse, we were waiting there for three days.

28.msb: From there we sailed around and came to Rhegium. After one day, a south wind came up, and on the second day we arrived at Puteoli.
28.kjv: And from thence we fetched a compass, and came to Rhegium: and after one day the south wind blew, and we came the next day to Puteoli:
28.blb: from where, having cast off, we arrived at Rhegium. And after one day, a south wind having come up, on the second day we came to Puteoli,
28.bbe: And from there, going about in a curve, we came to Rhegium: and after one day a south wind came up and on the day after we came to Puteoli:

28.msb: There we found some brothers who invited us to spend the week with them. And so we came to Rome.
28.kjv: Where we found brethren, and were desired to tarry with them seven days: and so we went toward Rome.
28.blb: where having found some brothers, we were entreated to remain with them seven days. And so we came to Rome.
28.bbe: Where we came across some of the brothers, who kept us with them for seven days; and so we came to Rome.

28.msb: The brothers there had heard about us and traveled as far as the Forum of Appius and the Three Taverns to meet us. When Paul saw them, he was encouraged and gave thanks to God.
28.kjv: And from thence, when the brethren heard of us, they came to meet us as far as Appii forum, and The three taverns: whom when Paul saw, he thanked God, and took courage.
28.blb: And the brothers from there, having heard the things concerning us, came out as far as the Forum of Appius and the Three Taverns to meet us, whom Paul having seen, having given thanks to God, took courage.
28.bbe: And the brothers, when they had news of us, came out from town as far as Appii Forum and the Three Taverns to have a meeting with us: and Paul, seeing them, gave praise to God and took heart.

28.msb: When we arrived in Rome, the centurion delivered up the prisoners to the captain of the guard, but Paul was permitted to stay by himself, with a soldier to guard him.
28.kjv: And when we came to Rome, the centurion delivered the prisoners to the captain of the guard: but Paul was suffered to dwell by himself with a soldier that kept him.
28.blb: Now when we came to Rome, Paul was allowed to stay by himself with the soldier guarding him.
28.bbe: And when we came into Rome, they let Paul have a house for himself and the armed man who kept watch over him.
28.heading: Paul Preaches at Rome

28.msb: After three days, Paul called together the leaders of the Jews. When they had gathered, he said to them, “Brothers, although I have done nothing against our people or the customs of our fathers, I was taken prisoner in Jerusalem and handed over to the Romans.
28.kjv: And it came to pass, that after three days Paul called the chief of the Jews together: and when they were come together, he said unto them, Men and brethren, though I have committed nothing against the people, or customs of our fathers, yet was I delivered prisoner from Jerusalem into the hands of the Romans.
28.blb: And it came to pass after three days that he called together those being leaders of the Jews. And on their having come together, he was saying to them, “Men, brothers, having done nothing against the people or the customs of our fathers, I was delivered from Jerusalem as a prisoner into the hands of the Romans,
28.bbe: Then after three days he sent for the chief men of the Jews: and when they had come together, he said to them, My brothers, though I had done nothing against the people or the ways of our fathers, I was given, a prisoner from Jerusalem, into the hands of the Romans.

28.msb: They examined me and wanted to release me, because there was no basis for a death sentence against me.
28.kjv: Who, when they had examined me, would have let me go, because there was no cause of death in me.
28.blb: who, having examined me, were wanting to let me go on account of not one cause of death existing in me.
28.bbe: Who, when they had put questions to me, were ready to let me go free, because there was no cause of death in me.

28.msb: But when the Jews objected, I was compelled to appeal to Caesar, even though I have no charge to bring against my nation.
28.kjv: But when the Jews spake against it, I was constrained to appeal unto Cæsar; not that I had ought to accuse my nation of.
28.blb: But on the Jews objecting, I was compelled to appeal to Caesar, not as having anything to accuse my nation.
28.bbe: But when the Jews made protest against it, I had to put my cause into Caesar's hands; not because I have anything to say against my nation.

28.msb: So for this reason I have called to see you and speak with you. It is because of the hope of Israel that I am bound with this chain.”
28.kjv: For this cause therefore have I called for you, to see you, and to speak with you: because that for the hope of Israel I am bound with this chain.
28.blb: For this cause, therefore, I have called to see you and to speak to you. For because of the hope of Israel, I have around me this chain.”
28.bbe: But for this reason I sent for you, to see and have talk with you: for because of the hope of Israel I am in these chains.

28.msb: The leaders replied, “We have not received any letters about you from Judea, nor have any of the brothers from there reported or even mentioned anything bad about you.
28.kjv: And they said unto him, We neither received letters out of Judæa concerning thee, neither any of the brethren that came shewed or spake any harm of thee.
28.blb: And they said to him, “We received neither letters concerning you from Judea, nor did any of the brothers having arrived report or say anything evil concerning you.
28.bbe: And they said to him, We have not had letters from Judaea about you, and no one of the brothers has come to us here to give an account or say any evil about you.

28.msb: But we consider your views worth hearing, because we know that people everywhere are speaking against this sect.”
28.kjv: But we desire to hear of thee what thou thinkest: for as concerning this sect, we know that every where it is spoken against.
28.blb: But we count it worthy to hear from you what you think, for truly, concerning this sect, it is known to us that it is spoken against everywhere.”
28.bbe: But we have a desire to give hearing to your opinion: for as to this form of religion, we have knowledge that in all places it is attacked.

28.msb: So they set a day to meet with Paul, and many people came to the place he was staying. He expounded to them from morning to evening, testifying about the kingdom of God and persuading them about Jesus from the Law of Moses and the Prophets.
28.kjv: And when they had appointed him a day, there came many to him into his lodging; to whom he expounded and testified the kingdom of God, persuading them concerning Jesus, both out of the law of Moses, and out of the prophets, from morning till evening.
28.blb: Then, having appointed to him a day, many came to him to the lodging, to whom he expounded from morning to evening, fully testifying to the kingdom of God and persuading them concerning Jesus from both the Law of Moses and the Prophets.
28.bbe: And when a day had been fixed, they came to his house in great numbers; and he gave them teaching, giving witness to the kingdom of God, and having discussions with them about Jesus, from the law of Moses and from the prophets, from morning till evening.

28.msb: Some of them were convinced by what he said, but others refused to believe.
28.kjv: And some believed the things which were spoken, and some believed not.
28.blb: And indeed, some were persuaded of the things being said, but some refused to believe.
28.bbe: And some were in agreement with what he said, but some had doubts.

28.msb: They disagreed among themselves and began to leave after Paul had made this final statement: “The Holy Spirit was right when He spoke to our fathers through Isaiah the prophet:
28.kjv: And when they agreed not among themselves, they departed, after that Paul had spoken one word, Well spake the Holy Ghost by Esaias the prophet unto our fathers,
28.blb: And being discordant with one another they began to leave, Paul having said one word: “The Holy Spirit spoke rightly by the prophet Isaiah to your fathers,
28.bbe: And they went away, for there was a division among them after Paul had said this one thing: Well did the Holy Spirit say by the prophet Isaiah to your fathers,

28.msb: ‘Go to this people and say, “You will be ever hearing but never understanding; you will be ever seeing but never perceiving.”
28.kjv: Saying, Go unto this people, and say, Hearing ye shall hear, and shall not understand; and seeing ye shall see, and not perceive:
28.blb: saying: ‘Go to this people and say, “In hearing you will hear and never understand; and in seeing you will see and never perceive.”
28.bbe: Go to this people and say, Though you give ear, you will not get knowledge; and seeing, you will see, but the sense will not be clear to you:

28.msb: For this people’s heart has grown callous; they hardly hear with their ears, and they have closed their eyes. Otherwise they might see with their eyes, hear with their ears, understand with their hearts, and turn, and I would heal them.’
28.kjv: For the heart of this people is waxed gross, and their ears are dull of hearing, and their eyes have they closed; lest they should see with their eyes, and hear with their ears, and understand with their heart, and should be converted, and I should heal them.
28.blb: For the heart of this people grew dull, and with the ears they barely hear, and they have closed their eyes, lest ever they should see with the eyes, and should hear with the ears, and should understand with the heart, and should turn, and I will heal them.’
28.bbe: For the heart of this people has become fat and their ears are slow in hearing and their eyes are shut; for fear that they might see with their eyes and give hearing with their ears and become wise in their hearts and be turned again to me, so that I might make them well.

28.msb: Be advised, therefore, that God’s salvation has been sent to the Gentiles, and they will listen!”
28.kjv: Be it known therefore unto you, that the salvation of God is sent unto the Gentiles, and that they will hear it.
28.blb: Therefore be it known to you that this salvation of God has been sent to the Gentiles, and they will listen!”
28.bbe: Be certain, then, that the salvation of God is sent to the Gentiles, and they will give hearing.

28.msb: And when he had said these things, the Jews went away, disputing sharply among themselves.
28.kjv: And when he had said these words, the Jews departed, and had great reasoning among themselves.

28.msb: Paul stayed there two full years in his own rented house, welcoming all who came to visit him.
28.kjv: And Paul dwelt two whole years in his own hired house, and received all that came in unto him,
28.blb: And he stayed two whole years in his own rented house, and he was welcoming all those coming to him,
28.bbe: And for the space of two years, Paul was living in the house of which he had the use, and had talk with all those who went in to see him,

28.msb: Boldly and freely he proclaimed the kingdom of God and taught about the Lord Jesus Christ.
28.kjv: Preaching the kingdom of God, and teaching those things which concern the Lord Jesus Christ, with all confidence, no man forbidding him.
28.blb: proclaiming the kingdom of God and teaching the things concerning the Lord Jesus Christ with all boldness, freely.
28.bbe: Preaching the kingdom of God and teaching about the Lord Jesus Christ without fear, and no orders were given that he was not to do so.

1.msb: Paul, a servant of Jesus Christ, called to be an apostle, and set apart for the gospel of God—
1.kjv: Paul, a servant of Jesus Christ, called to be an apostle, separated unto the gospel of God,
1.blb: Paul, a servant of Christ Jesus, a called apostle having been set apart for the gospel of God,
1.bbe: Paul, a servant of Jesus Christ, an Apostle by the selection of God, given authority as a preacher of the good news,
1.heading: Paul Greets the Saints in Rome

1.msb: the gospel He promised beforehand through His prophets in the Holy Scriptures,
1.kjv: (Which he had promised afore by his prophets in the holy scriptures,)
1.blb: which He promised beforehand through His prophets in Holy Scriptures,
1.bbe: Of which God had given word before by his prophets in the holy Writings,

1.msb: regarding His Son, who was a descendant of David according to the flesh,
1.kjv: Concerning his Son Jesus Christ our Lord, which was made of the seed of David according to the flesh;
1.blb: concerning His Son, the One having come of the seed of David according to the flesh,
1.bbe: About his Son who, in the flesh, came from the family of David,

1.msb: and who through the Spirit of holiness was declared with power to be the Son of God by His resurrection from the dead: Jesus Christ our Lord.
1.kjv: And declared to be the Son of God with power, according to the spirit of holiness, by the resurrection from the dead:
1.blb: the One having been determined the Son of God in power according to the Spirit of holiness by resurrection from the dead: Jesus Christ our Lord,
1.bbe: But was marked out as Son of God in power by the Holy Spirit through the coming to life again of the dead; Jesus Christ our Lord,

1.msb: Through Him and on behalf of His name, we received grace and apostleship to call all those among the Gentiles to the obedience that comes from faith.
1.kjv: By whom we have received grace and apostleship, for obedience to the faith among all nations, for his name:
1.blb: through whom we received grace and apostleship for obedience of faith among all the Gentiles on behalf of His name,
1.bbe: Through whom grace has been given to us, sending us out to make disciples to the faith among all nations, for his name:

1.msb: And you also are among those who are called to belong to Jesus Christ.
1.kjv: Among whom are ye also the called of Jesus Christ:
1.blb: among whom are you also, called of Jesus Christ.
1.bbe: Among whom you in the same way have been marked out to be disciples of Jesus Christ:

1.msb: To all in Rome who are loved by God and called to be saints: Grace and peace to you from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
1.kjv: To all that be in Rome, beloved of God, called to be saints: Grace to you and peace from God our Father, and the Lord Jesus Christ.
1.blb: To all those being in Rome beloved of God, called saints: Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
1.bbe: To all those who are in Rome, loved by God, marked out as saints: Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.

1.msb: First, I thank my God through Jesus Christ for all of you, because your faith is being proclaimed all over the world.
1.kjv: First, I thank my God through Jesus Christ for you all, that your faith is spoken of throughout the whole world.
1.blb: First indeed, I thank my God through Jesus Christ for all of you, because your faith is being proclaimed in all the world.
1.bbe: First of all, I give praise to my God through Jesus Christ for you all, because news of your faith has gone into all the world.
1.heading: Unashamed of the Gospel

1.msb: God, whom I serve with my spirit in preaching the gospel of His Son, is my witness how constantly I remember you
1.kjv: For God is my witness, whom I serve with my spirit in the gospel of his Son, that without ceasing I make mention of you always in my prayers;
1.blb: For God, whom I serve in my spirit in the gospel of His Son, is my witness how unceasingly I make remembrance of you,
1.bbe: For God is my witness, whose servant I am in spirit in the good news of his Son, that you are at all times in my memory and in my prayers,

1.msb: in my prayers at all times, asking that now at last by God’s will I may succeed in coming to you.
1.kjv: Making request, if by any means now at length I might have a prosperous journey by the will of God to come unto you.
1.blb: always upon my prayers, imploring if somehow now at last by the will of God I will make a prosperous journey to come to you.
1.bbe: And that I am ever making prayers that God will give me a good journey to you.

1.msb: For I long to see you so that I may impart to you some spiritual gift to strengthen you,
1.kjv: For I long to see you, that I may impart unto you some spiritual gift, to the end ye may be established;
1.blb: For I long to see you so that I may impart some spiritual gift to you, to your being strengthened,
1.bbe: For I have a strong desire to see you, and to give you some grace of the spirit, so that you may be made strong;

1.msb: that is, that you and I may be mutually encouraged by each other’s faith.
1.kjv: That is, that I may be comforted together with you by the mutual faith both of you and me.
1.blb: and, that is, to be encouraged together among you through the faith among one another, both of you and of me.
1.bbe: That is to say, that all of us may be comforted together by the faith which is in you and in me.

1.msb: I do not want you to be unaware, brothers, how often I planned to come to you (but have been prevented from visiting until now), in order that I might have a harvest among you, just as I have had among the other Gentiles.
1.kjv: Now I would not have you ignorant, brethren, that oftentimes I purposed to come unto you, (but was let hitherto,) that I might have some fruit among you also, even as among other Gentiles.
1.blb: Now I do not want you to be ignorant, brothers, that many times I purposed to come to you, and was prevented until the present, so that I might have some fruit among you also, even as among the other Gentiles.
1.bbe: You may be certain, my brothers, that it has frequently been in my mind to come to you (but till now I was kept from it), so that I might have some fruit from you in the same way as I have had it from the other nations.

1.msb: I am obligated both to Greeks and non-Greeks, both to the wise and the foolish.
1.kjv: I am debtor both to the Greeks, and to the Barbarians; both to the wise, and to the unwise.
1.blb: I am a debtor both to Greeks and to barbarians, both to wise and to foolish.
1.bbe: I have a debt to Greeks and to the nations outside; to the wise and to those who have no learning.

1.msb: That is why I am so eager to preach the gospel also to you who are in Rome.
1.kjv: So, as much as in me is, I am ready to preach the gospel to you that are at Rome also.
1.blb: Thus, as to me, I am ready to preach the gospel also to you who are in Rome.
1.bbe: For which reason I have the desire, as far as I am able, to give the knowledge of the good news to you who are in Rome.

1.msb: I am not ashamed of the gospel of Christ, because it is the power of God for salvation to everyone who believes, first to the Jew, then to the Greek.
1.kjv: For I am not ashamed of the gospel of Christ: for it is the power of God unto salvation to every one that believeth; to the Jew first, and also to the Greek.
1.blb: For I am not ashamed of the gospel, for it is the power of God unto salvation to everyone believing—both to Jew first, and to Greek.
1.bbe: For I have no feeling of shame about the good news, because it is the power of God giving salvation to everyone who has faith, to the Jew first, and then to the Greek.

1.msb: For the gospel reveals the righteousness of God that comes by faith from start to finish, just as it is written: “The righteous will live by faith.”
1.kjv: For therein is the righteousness of God revealed from faith to faith: as it is written, The just shall live by faith.
1.blb: For in it the righteousness of God is revealed from faith to faith, just as it has been written: “And the righteous one will live by faith.”
1.bbe: For in it there is the revelation of the righteousness of God from faith to faith: as it is said in the holy Writings, The man who does righteousness will be living by his faith.

1.msb: The wrath of God is being revealed from heaven against all the godlessness and wickedness of men who suppress the truth by their wickedness.
1.kjv: For the wrath of God is revealed from heaven against all ungodliness and unrighteousness of men, who hold the truth in unrighteousness;
1.blb: For the wrath of God is revealed from heaven against all ungodliness and unrighteousness of men, suppressing the truth in unrighteousness,
1.bbe: For there is a revelation of the wrath of God from heaven against all the wrongdoing and evil thoughts of men who keep down what is true by wrongdoing;
1.heading: God’s Wrath against Sin

1.msb: For what may be known about God is plain to them, because God has made it plain to them.
1.kjv: Because that which may be known of God is manifest in them; for God hath shewed it unto them.
1.blb: because that which is known of God is manifest among them, for God has revealed it to them.
1.bbe: Because the knowledge of God may be seen in them, God having made it clear to them.

1.msb: For since the creation of the world God’s invisible qualities, His eternal power and divine nature, have been clearly seen, being understood from His workmanship, so that men are without excuse.
1.kjv: For the invisible things of him from the creation of the world are clearly seen, being understood by the things that are made, even his eternal power and Godhead; so that they are without excuse:
1.blb: For from the creation of the world His invisible qualities, both His eternal power and divinity, are clearly seen, being understood by the things made, for them to be without excuse.
1.bbe: For from the first making of the world, those things of God which the eye is unable to see, that is, his eternal power and existence, are fully made clear, he having given the knowledge of them through the things which he has made, so that men have no reason for wrongdoing:

1.msb: For although they knew God, they neither glorified Him as God nor gave thanks to Him, but they became futile in their thinking and darkened in their foolish hearts.
1.kjv: Because that, when they knew God, they glorified him not as God, neither were thankful; but became vain in their imaginations, and their foolish heart was darkened.
1.blb: For having known God, not as God did they glorify Him, or give thanks, but they became futile in their thoughts and their foolish heart was darkened.
1.bbe: Because, having the knowledge of God, they did not give glory to God as God, and did not give praise, but their minds were full of foolish things, and their hearts, being without sense, were made dark.

1.msb: Although they claimed to be wise, they became fools,
1.kjv: Professing themselves to be wise, they became fools,
1.blb: Professing to be wise, they became fools,
1.bbe: Seeming to be wise, they were in fact foolish,

1.msb: and exchanged the glory of the immortal God for images of mortal man and birds and animals and reptiles.
1.kjv: And changed the glory of the uncorruptible God into an image made like to corruptible man, and to birds, and fourfooted beasts, and creeping things.
1.blb: and they changed the glory of the immortal God into the likeness of an image of mortal man and birds and quadrupeds and creeping things.
1.bbe: And by them the glory of the eternal God was changed and made into the image of man who is not eternal, and of birds and beasts and things which go on the earth.

1.msb: Therefore God gave them over in the desires of their hearts to impurity for the dishonoring of their bodies with one another.
1.kjv: Wherefore God also gave them up to uncleanness through the lusts of their own hearts, to dishonour their own bodies between themselves:
1.blb: Therefore God gave them up in the sinful desires of their hearts to uncleanness to dishonor their bodies among themselves,
1.bbe: For this reason God gave them up to the evil desires of their hearts, working shame in their bodies with one another:

1.msb: They exchanged the truth of God for a lie, and worshiped and served the creature rather than the Creator, who is forever worthy of praise! Amen.
1.kjv: Who changed the truth of God into a lie, and worshipped and served the creature more than the Creator, who is blessed for ever. Amen.
1.blb: who changed the truth of God into falsehood, and worshiped and served the creature rather than the One having created, who is blessed to the ages! Amen.
1.bbe: Because by them the true word of God was changed into that which is false, and they gave worship and honour to the thing which is made, and not to him who made it, to whom be blessing for ever. So be it.

1.msb: For this reason God gave them over to dishonorable passions. Even their women exchanged natural relations for unnatural ones.
1.kjv: For this cause God gave them up unto vile affections: for even their women did change the natural use into that which is against nature:
1.blb: Because of this, God gave up them to passions of dishonor. For even their females changed the natural use into that contrary to nature.
1.bbe: For this reason God gave them up to evil passions, and their women were changing the natural use into one which is unnatural:

1.msb: Likewise, the men abandoned natural relations with women and burned with lust for one another. Men committed indecent acts with other men, and received in themselves the due penalty for their error.
1.kjv: And likewise also the men, leaving the natural use of the woman, burned in their lust one toward another; men with men working that which is unseemly, and receiving in themselves that recompence of their error which was meet.
1.blb: And likewise also the males, having left the natural use of the female, were inflamed in their lust toward one another, males with males, working out shame and receiving back in themselves the recompense that was fitting of their error.
1.bbe: And in the same way the men gave up the natural use of the woman and were burning in their desire for one another, men doing shame with men, and getting in their bodies the right reward of their evil-doing.

1.msb: Furthermore, since they did not see fit to acknowledge God, He gave them up to a depraved mind, to do what ought not to be done.
1.kjv: And even as they did not like to retain God in their knowledge, God gave them over to a reprobate mind, to do those things which are not convenient;
1.blb: And just as they did not see fit to have God in their knowledge, God gave them up to an unfit mind, to do the things not being proper;
1.bbe: And because they had not the mind to keep God in their knowledge, God gave them up to an evil mind, to do those things which are not right;

1.msb: They have become filled with every kind of wickedness, sexual immorality, evil, greed, and depravity. They are full of envy, murder, strife, deceit, and malice. They are gossips,
1.kjv: Being filled with all unrighteousness, fornication, wickedness, covetousness, maliciousness; full of envy, murder, debate, deceit, malignity; whisperers,
1.blb: being filled with all unrighteousness, wickedness, covetousness, malice; full of envy, murder, strife, deceit, malice; gossips,
1.bbe: Being full of all wrongdoing, evil, desire for the goods of others, hate, envy, putting to death, fighting, deceit, cruel ways, evil talk, and false statements about others;

1.msb: slanderers, God-haters, insolent, arrogant, and boastful. They invent new forms of evil; they disobey their parents.
1.kjv: Backbiters, haters of God, despiteful, proud, boasters, inventors of evil things, disobedient to parents,
1.blb: slanderers, hateful to God, insolent, arrogant, boasters; inventors of evil, disobedient to parents;
1.bbe: Hated by God, full of pride, without respect, full of loud talk, given to evil inventions, not honouring father or mother,

1.msb: They are senseless, faithless, heartless, unforgiving, merciless.
1.kjv: Without understanding, covenantbreakers, without natural affection, implacable, unmerciful:
1.blb: unintelligent, untrustworthy, unloving, unmerciful;
1.bbe: Without knowledge, not true to their undertakings, unkind, having no mercy:

1.msb: Although they know God’s righteous decree that those who do such things are worthy of death, they not only continue to do these things, but also approve of those who practice them.
1.kjv: Who knowing the judgment of God, that they which commit such things are worthy of death, not only do the same, but have pleasure in them that do them.
1.blb: who, having known the righteous decree of God that those practicing such things are worthy of death, not only are doing them, but also agree with those practicing them.
1.bbe: Who, though they have knowledge of the law of God, that the fate of those who do these things is death, not only go on doing these things themselves, but give approval to those who do them.

2.msb: You, therefore, have no excuse, you who pass judgment on another. For on whatever grounds you judge the other, you are condemning yourself, because you who pass judgment do the same things.
2.kjv: Therefore thou art inexcusable, O man, whosoever thou art that judgest: for wherein thou judgest another, thou condemnest thyself; for thou that judgest doest the same things.
2.blb: Therefore you are without excuse, O man, every one who is judging. For in that which you judge the other, you are condemning yourself, for you, the one judging, practice the same things.
2.bbe: So you have no reason, whoever you are, for judging: for in judging another you are judging yourself, for you do the same things.
2.heading: God’s Righteous Judgment

2.msb: And we know that God’s judgment against those who do such things is based on truth.
2.kjv: But we are sure that the judgment of God is according to truth against them which commit such things.
2.blb: But we know that the judgment of God upon those practicing such things is according to truth.
2.bbe: And we are conscious that God is a true judge against those who do such things.

2.msb: So when you, O man, pass judgment on others, yet do the same things, do you think you will escape God’s judgment?
2.kjv: And thinkest thou this, O man, that judgest them which do such things, and doest the same, that thou shalt escape the judgment of God?
2.blb: Now do you reckon this, O man, the one judging those practicing such things, and doing them yourself, that you will escape the judgment of God?
2.bbe: But you who are judging another for doing what you do yourself, are you hoping that God's decision will not take effect against you?

2.msb: Or do you disregard the riches of His kindness, tolerance, and patience, not realizing that God’s kindness leads you to repentance?
2.kjv: Or despisest thou the riches of his goodness and forbearance and longsuffering; not knowing that the goodness of God leadeth thee to repentance?
2.blb: Or do you despise the riches of His kindness and forbearance and patience, not knowing that the kindness of God leads you to repentance?
2.bbe: Or is it nothing to you that God had pity on you, waiting and putting up with you for so long, not seeing that in his pity God's desire is to give you a change of heart?

2.msb: But because of your hard and unrepentant heart, you are storing up wrath against yourself for the day of wrath, revelation, and God’s righteous judgment.
2.kjv: But after thy hardness and impenitent heart treasurest up unto thyself wrath against the day of wrath and revelation of the righteous judgment of God;
2.blb: But according to your hardness and unrepentant heart, you are storing up for yourself wrath in the day of wrath and revelation of the righteous judgment of God,
2.bbe: But by your hard and unchanged heart you are storing up wrath for yourself in the day of the revelation of God's judging in righteousness;

2.msb: God “will repay each one according to his deeds.”
2.kjv: Who will render to every man according to his deeds:
2.blb: who “will repay to each according to his works,”
2.bbe: Who will give to every man his right reward:

2.msb: To those who by perseverance in doing good seek glory, honor, and immortality, He will give eternal life.
2.kjv: To them who by patient continuance in well doing seek for glory and honour and immortality, eternal life:
2.blb: to those who indeed with perseverance in good work are seeking glory and honor and immortality, eternal life;
2.bbe: To those who go on with good works in the hope of glory and honour and salvation from death, he will give eternal life:

2.msb: But for those who are self-seeking and who reject the truth and follow wickedness, there will be anger and wrath.
2.kjv: But unto them that are contentious, and do not obey the truth, but obey unrighteousness, indignation and wrath,
2.blb: but to those of self-interest and disobeying the truth but obeying unrighteousness, wrath and anger;
2.bbe: But to those who, from a love of competition, are not guided by what is true, will come the heat of his wrath,

2.msb: There will be trouble and distress for every human being who does evil, first for the Jew, then for the Greek;
2.kjv: Tribulation and anguish, upon every soul of man that doeth evil, of the Jew first, and also of the Gentile;
2.blb: tribulation and distress upon every soul of man working evil, both of Jew first, and also of Greek;
2.bbe: Trouble and sorrow on all whose works are evil, to the Jew first and then to the Greek;

2.msb: but glory, honor, and peace for everyone who does good, first for the Jew, then for the Greek.
2.kjv: But glory, honour, and peace, to every man that worketh good, to the Jew first, and also to the Gentile:
2.blb: but glory and honor and peace to everyone working good, both to Jew first, and to Greek.
2.bbe: But glory and honour and peace to all whose works are good, to the Jew first and then to the Greek:

2.msb: For God does not show favoritism.
2.kjv: For there is no respect of persons with God.
2.blb: For there is no partiality with God.
2.bbe: For one man is not different from another before God.

2.msb: All who sin apart from the law will also perish apart from the law, and all who sin under the law will be judged by the law.
2.kjv: For as many as have sinned without law shall also perish without law: and as many as have sinned in the law shall be judged by the law;
2.blb: For as many as have sinned without the law will also perish without the law; and as many as have sinned in the law will be judged by the law,
2.bbe: All those who have done wrong without the law will get destruction without the law: and those who have done wrong under the law will have their punishment by the law;

2.msb: For it is not the hearers of the law who are righteous before God, but it is the doers of the law who will be declared righteous.
2.kjv: (For not the hearers of the law are just before God, but the doers of the law shall be justified.
2.blb: for not the hearers of the law are righteous before God; but the doers of the law will be declared righteous.
2.bbe: For it is not the hearers of the law who will be judged as having righteousness before God, but only the doers:

2.msb: Indeed, when Gentiles, who do not have the law, do by nature what the law requires, they are a law to themselves, even though they do not have the law.
2.kjv: For when the Gentiles, which have not the law, do by nature the things contained in the law, these, having not the law, are a law unto themselves:
2.blb: For when Gentiles, not having the law, may do by nature the things of the law, these not having a law are a law to themselves,
2.bbe: For when the Gentiles without the law have a natural desire to do the things in the law, they are a law to themselves;

2.msb: So they show that the work of the law is written on their hearts, their consciences also bearing witness, and their thoughts either accusing or defending them
2.kjv: Which shew the work of the law written in their hearts, their conscience also bearing witness, and their thoughts the mean while accusing or else excusing one another;)
2.blb: who show the work of the law written in their hearts, their conscience also testifying, and the thoughts between one another accusing or also defending them
2.bbe: Because the work of the law is seen in their hearts, their sense of right and wrong giving witness to it, while their minds are at one time judging them and at another giving them approval;

2.msb: on the day when God will judge men’s secrets through Jesus Christ, as proclaimed by my gospel.
2.kjv: In the day when God shall judge the secrets of men by Jesus Christ according to my gospel.
2.blb: on the day when God judges the secrets of men according to my gospel through Christ Jesus.
2.bbe: In the day when God will be a judge of the secrets of men, as it says in the good news of which I am a preacher, through Jesus Christ.

2.msb: Behold, you call yourself a Jew. You rely on the law and boast in God.
2.kjv: Behold, thou art called a Jew, and restest in the law, and makest thy boast of God,
2.blb: But if you are named a Jew and rest upon the law and boast in God,
2.bbe: But as for you who have the name of Jew, and are resting on the law, and take pride in God,
2.heading: The Jews and the Law

2.msb: And you know His will and approve of what is superior because you are instructed by the law.
2.kjv: And knowest his will, and approvest the things that are more excellent, being instructed out of the law;
2.blb: and you know the will and approve the things being superior, being instructed out of the law,
2.bbe: And have knowledge of his desires, and are a judge of the things which are different, having the learning of the law,

2.msb: And you are convinced that you are a guide for the blind, a light for those in darkness,
2.kjv: And art confident that thou thyself art a guide of the blind, a light of them which are in darkness,
2.blb: and you have persuaded yourself that you are a guide of the blind, a light to those in darkness,
2.bbe: In the belief that you are a guide to the blind, a light to those in the dark,

2.msb: an instructor of the foolish, a teacher of infants, because you have in the law the embodiment of knowledge and truth.
2.kjv: An instructor of the foolish, a teacher of babes, which hast the form of knowledge and of the truth in the law.
2.blb: an instructor of the foolish, a teacher of infants, having in the law the form of knowledge and of the truth—
2.bbe: A teacher of the foolish, having in the law the form of knowledge and of what is true;

2.msb: You, then, who teach others, do you not teach yourself? You who preach against stealing, do you steal?
2.kjv: Thou therefore which teachest another, teachest thou not thyself? thou that preachest a man should not steal, dost thou steal?
2.blb: then you who are teaching another, do you not teach yourself? You who are preaching not to steal, do you steal?
2.bbe: You who give teaching to others, do you give it to yourself? you who say that a man may not take what is not his, do you take what is not yours?

2.msb: You who forbid adultery, do you commit adultery? You who abhor idols, do you rob temples?
2.kjv: Thou that sayest a man should not commit adultery, dost thou commit adultery? thou that abhorrest idols, dost thou commit sacrilege?
2.blb: You who are saying not to commit adultery, do you commit adultery? You who are abhorring idols, do you rob temples?
2.bbe: You who say that a man may not be untrue to his wife, are you true to yours? you who are a hater of images, do you do wrong to the house of God?

2.msb: You who boast in the law, do you dishonor God by breaking the law?
2.kjv: Thou that makest thy boast of the law, through breaking the law dishonourest thou God?
2.blb: You who boast in the law, do you dishonor God through the transgression of the law?
2.bbe: You who take pride in the law, are you doing wrong to the honour of God by behaviour which is against the law?

2.msb: As it is written: “God’s name is blasphemed among the Gentiles because of you.”
2.kjv: For the name of God is blasphemed among the Gentiles through you, as it is written.
2.blb: As it has been written: “For the name of God is blasphemed among the Gentiles because of you.”
2.bbe: For the name of God is shamed among the Gentiles because of you, as it is said in the holy Writings.

2.msb: Circumcision has value if you observe the law, but if you break the law, your circumcision has become uncircumcision.
2.kjv: For circumcision verily profiteth, if thou keep the law: but if thou be a breaker of the law, thy circumcision is made uncircumcision.
2.blb: For circumcision indeed profits if you practice the law; but if you are a transgressor of the law, your circumcision has become uncircumcision.
2.bbe: It is true that circumcision is of use if you keep the law, but if you go against the law it is as if you had it not.

2.msb: If a man who is not circumcised keeps the requirements of the law, will not his uncircumcision be regarded as circumcision?
2.kjv: Therefore if the uncircumcision keep the righteousness of the law, shall not his uncircumcision be counted for circumcision?
2.blb: Therefore if the uncircumcision keeps the righteous requirements of the law, will not his uncircumcision be reckoned as circumcision?
2.bbe: If those who have not circumcision keep the rules of the law, will it not be credited to them as circumcision?

2.msb: The one who is physically uncircumcised yet keeps the law will condemn you who, even though you have the written code and circumcision, are a lawbreaker.
2.kjv: And shall not uncircumcision which is by nature, if it fulfil the law, judge thee, who by the letter and circumcision dost transgress the law?
2.blb: And the uncircumcision by nature, fulfilling the law, will judge you who through the letter and circumcision are a transgressor of the law.
2.bbe: And they, by their keeping of the law without circumcision, will be judges of you, by whom the law is broken though you have the letter of the law and circumcision.

2.msb: A man is not a Jew because he is one outwardly, nor is circumcision only outward and physical.
2.kjv: For he is not a Jew, which is one outwardly; neither is that circumcision, which is outward in the flesh:
2.blb: For it is not the one who on the outside is a Jew, nor is that on the outside in flesh circumcision.
2.bbe: The true Jew is not one who is only so publicly, and circumcision is not that which may be seen in the flesh:

2.msb: No, a man is a Jew because he is one inwardly, and circumcision is a matter of the heart, by the Spirit, not by the written code. Such a man’s praise does not come from men, but from God.
2.kjv: But he is a Jew, which is one inwardly; and circumcision is that of the heart, in the spirit, and not in the letter; whose praise is not of men, but of God.
2.blb: But a Jew is one on the inside, and circumcision is of heart, in spirit, not in letter, of whom the praise is not of men, but of God.
2.bbe: But he is a Jew who is a secret one, whose circumcision is of the heart, in the spirit and not in the letter; whose praise is not from men, but from God.

3.msb: What, then, is the advantage of being a Jew? Or what is the value of circumcision?
3.kjv: What advantage then hath the Jew? or what profit is there of circumcision?
3.blb: What then is the superiority of the Jew? Or what is the profit of the circumcision?
3.bbe: How then is the Jew better off? or what profit is there in circumcision?
3.heading: God Remains Faithful

3.msb: Much in every way. First of all, they have been entrusted with the very words of God.
3.kjv: Much every way: chiefly, because that unto them were committed the oracles of God.
3.blb: Much in every way. For first indeed, that they were entrusted with the oracles of God.
3.bbe: Much in every way: first of all because the words of God were given to them.

3.msb: What if some did not have faith? Will their lack of faith nullify God’s faithfulness?
3.kjv: For what if some did not believe? shall their unbelief make the faith of God without effect?
3.blb: For what If some disbelieved? Will their unbelief nullify the faithfulness of God?
3.bbe: And if some have no faith, will that make the faith of God without effect?

3.msb: Certainly not! Let God be true and every man a liar. As it is written: “So that You may be proved right when You speak and victorious when You judge.”
3.kjv: God forbid: yea, let God be true, but every man a liar; as it is written, That thou mightest be justified in thy sayings, and mightest overcome when thou art judged.
3.blb: Never may it be! But let God be true and every man a liar, as it has been written: “So that You may be justified in Your words, and you will be victorious in Your judging.”
3.bbe: In no way: but let God be true, though every man is seen to be untrue; as it is said in the Writings, That your words may be seen to be true, and you may be seen to be right when you are judged.

3.msb: But if our unrighteousness highlights the righteousness of God, what shall we say? That God is unjust to inflict His wrath on us? I am speaking in human terms.
3.kjv: But if our unrighteousness commend the righteousness of God, what shall we say? Is God unrighteous who taketh vengeance? (I speak as a man)
3.blb: But if our unrighteousness proves God’s righteousness, what will we say? God, inflicting the wrath, is unrighteous? I speak according to man.
3.bbe: But if the righteousness of God is supported by our wrongdoing what is to be said? is it wrong for God to be angry (as men may say)?

3.msb: Certainly not! In that case, how could God judge the world?
3.kjv: God forbid: for then how shall God judge the world?
3.blb: Never may it be! Otherwise, how will God judge the world?
3.bbe: In no way: because if it is so, how is God able to be the judge of all the world?

3.msb: For if my falsehood accentuates God’s truthfulness, to the increase of His glory, why am I still condemned as a sinner?
3.kjv: For if the truth of God hath more abounded through my lie unto his glory; why yet am I also judged as a sinner?
3.blb: But if the truth of God in my falsehood abounded to His glory, why am I also still judged as a sinner?
3.bbe: But if, because I am untrue, God being seen to be true gets more glory, why am I to be judged as a sinner?

3.msb: Why not say, as some slanderously claim that we say, “Let us do evil that good may result”? Their condemnation is deserved!
3.kjv: And not rather, (as we be slanderously reported, and as some affirm that we say,) Let us do evil, that good may come? whose damnation is just.
3.blb: And is it not, as we are slandered and as some affirm us to say, “Let us do evil so that the good may come”? Their judgment is just.
3.bbe: Let us not do evil so that good may come (a statement which we are falsely said by some to have made), because such behaviour will have its right punishment.

3.msb: What then? Are we any better? Not at all. For we have already made the charge that Jews and Greeks alike are all under sin.
3.kjv: What then? are we better than they? No, in no wise: for we have before proved both Jews and Gentiles, that they are all under sin;
3.blb: What then? Are we better? Not at all. For we charged before both Jews and Greeks with being all under sin.
3.bbe: What then? are we worse off than they? In no way: because we have before made it clear that Jews as well as Greeks are all under the power of sin;
3.heading: There Is No One Righteous

3.msb: As it is written: “There is no one righteous, not even one.
3.kjv: As it is written, There is none righteous, no, not one:
3.blb: As it has been written: “There is no one righteous, not even one;
3.bbe: As it is said in the holy Writings, There is not one who does righteousness;

3.msb: There is no one who understands, no one who seeks God.
3.kjv: There is none that understandeth, there is none that seeketh after God.
3.blb: there is no one understanding; there is no one seeking out God.
3.bbe: Not one who has the knowledge of what is right, not one who is a searcher after God;

3.msb: All have turned away, they have together become worthless; there is no one who does good, not even one.”
3.kjv: They are all gone out of the way, they are together become unprofitable; there is none that doeth good, no, not one.
3.blb: All turned away; together they became worthless; there is none who is doing kindness, there is not even one.”
3.bbe: They have all gone out of the way, there is no profit in any of them; there is not one who does good, not so much as one:

3.msb: “Their throats are open graves; their tongues practice deceit.” “The venom of vipers is on their lips.”
3.kjv: Their throat is an open sepulchre; with their tongues they have used deceit; the poison of asps is under their lips:
3.blb: “Their throat is a grave having been opened; they keep practicing deceit with their tongues;” “the poison of vipers is under their lips,”
3.bbe: Their throat is like an open place of death; with their tongues they have said what is not true: the poison of snakes is under their lips:

3.msb: “Their mouths are full of cursing and bitterness.”
3.kjv: Whose mouth is full of cursing and bitterness:
3.blb: “of whom the mouth is full of cursing and of bitterness;”
3.bbe: Whose mouth is full of curses and bitter words:

3.msb: “Their feet are swift to shed blood;
3.kjv: Their feet are swift to shed blood:
3.blb: “their feet are swift to shed blood;
3.bbe: Their feet are quick in running after blood;

3.msb: ruin and misery lie in their wake,
3.kjv: Destruction and misery are in their ways:
3.blb: ruin and misery are in their paths;
3.bbe: Destruction and trouble are in their ways;

3.msb: and the way of peace they have not known.”
3.kjv: And the way of peace have they not known:
3.blb: and a way of peace they did not know.”
3.bbe: And of the way of peace they have no knowledge:

3.msb: “There is no fear of God before their eyes.”
3.kjv: There is no fear of God before their eyes.
3.blb: “There is no fear of God before their eyes.”
3.bbe: There is no fear of God before their eyes.

3.msb: Now we know that whatever the law says, it says to those who are under the law, so that every mouth may be silenced and the whole world held accountable to God.
3.kjv: Now we know that what things soever the law saith, it saith to them who are under the law: that every mouth may be stopped, and all the world may become guilty before God.
3.blb: Now we know that as much as the law says, it speaks to those in the law, so that every mouth may be shut, and all the world may be under judgment to God.
3.bbe: Now, we have knowledge that what the law says is for those who are under the law, so that every mouth may be stopped, and all men may be judged by God:

3.msb: Therefore no one will be justified in His sight by works of the law. For the law merely brings awareness of sin.
3.kjv: Therefore by the deeds of the law there shall no flesh be justified in his sight: for by the law is the knowledge of sin.
3.blb: Therefore by works of the law, not any flesh will be justified before Him; for through the law is knowledge of sin.
3.bbe: Because by the works of the law no man is able to have righteousness in his eyes, for through the law comes the knowledge of sin.

3.msb: But now, apart from the law, the righteousness of God has been revealed, as attested by the Law and the Prophets.
3.kjv: But now the righteousness of God without the law is manifested, being witnessed by the law and the prophets;
3.blb: But now, apart from the law, the righteousness of God has been revealed, being testified to by the Law and the Prophets.
3.bbe: But now without the law there is a revelation of the righteousness of God, to which witness is given by the law and the prophets;
3.heading: Righteousness through Faith in Christ

3.msb: And this righteousness from God comes through faith in Jesus Christ to all and upon all who believe. There is no distinction,
3.kjv: Even the righteousness of God which is by faith of Jesus Christ unto all and upon all them that believe: for there is no difference:
3.blb: And the righteousness of God is through faith from Jesus Christ toward all those believing. For there is no distinction,
3.bbe: That is, the righteousness of God through faith in Jesus Christ, to all those who have faith; and one man is not different from another,

3.msb: for all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God,
3.kjv: For all have sinned, and come short of the glory of God;
3.blb: for all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God,
3.bbe: For all have done wrong and are far from the glory of God;

3.msb: and are justified freely by His grace through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus.
3.kjv: Being justified freely by his grace through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus:
3.blb: being justified freely by His grace through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus,
3.bbe: And they may have righteousness put to their credit, freely, by his grace, through the salvation which is in Christ Jesus:

3.msb: God presented Him as an atoning sacrifice in His blood through faith, in order to demonstrate His righteousness, because in His forbearance He had passed over the sins committed beforehand.
3.kjv: Whom God hath set forth to be a propitiation through faith in his blood, to declare his righteousness for the remission of sins that are past, through the forbearance of God;
3.blb: whom God set forth as a propitiation through faith in His blood, for a demonstration of His righteousness, because of the passing over of the sins having taken place beforehand in the forbearance of God,
3.bbe: Whom God has put forward as the sign of his mercy, through faith, by his blood, to make clear his righteousness when, in his pity, God let the sins of earlier times go without punishment;

3.msb: He did this to demonstrate His righteousness at the present time, so as to be just and to justify the one who has faith in Jesus.
3.kjv: To declare, I say, at this time his righteousness: that he might be just, and the justifier of him which believeth in Jesus.
3.blb: for the demonstration of His righteousness in the present time, for Him to be just and justifying the one of the faith from Jesus.
3.bbe: And to make clear his righteousness now, so that he might himself be upright, and give righteousness to him who has faith in Jesus.

3.msb: Where, then, is boasting? It is excluded. On what principle? On that of works? No, but on that of faith.
3.kjv: Where is boasting then? It is excluded. By what law? of works? Nay: but by the law of faith.
3.blb: Where then is the boasting? It was excluded. By what kind of law? That of works? No, but by the law of faith.
3.bbe: What reason, then, is there for pride? It is shut out. By what sort of law? of works? No, but by a law of faith.

3.msb: Therefore we maintain that a man is justified by faith apart from works of the law.
3.kjv: Therefore we conclude that a man is justified by faith without the deeds of the law.
3.blb: For we reckon a man to be justified by faith apart from works of law.
3.bbe: For this reason, then, a man may get righteousness by faith without the works of the law.

3.msb: Is God the God of Jews only? Is He not the God of Gentiles too? Yes, of Gentiles too,
3.kjv: Is he the God of the Jews only? is he not also of the Gentiles? Yes, of the Gentiles also:
3.blb: Or is He the God of Jews only, not also of Gentiles? Yes, also of Gentiles,
3.bbe: Or is God the God of Jews only? is he not in the same way the God of Gentiles? Yes, of Gentiles:

3.msb: since there is only one God, who will justify the circumcised by faith and the uncircumcised through that same faith.
3.kjv: Seeing it is one God, which shall justify the circumcision by faith, and uncircumcision through faith.
3.blb: since indeed God is one, who will justify the circumcision by faith and the uncircumcision through the same faith.
3.bbe: If God is one; and he will give righteousness because of faith to those who have circumcision, and through faith to those who have not circumcision.

3.msb: Do we, then, nullify the law by this faith? Certainly not! Instead, we uphold the law.
3.kjv: Do we then make void the law through faith? God forbid: yea, we establish the law.
3.blb: Do we, then, nullify the law through faith? Never may it be! Rather, we uphold the law.
3.bbe: Do we, then, through faith make the law of no effect? in no way: but we make it clear that the law is important.

4.msb: What then shall we say that Abraham, our forefather according to the flesh, has discovered?
4.kjv: What shall we say then that Abraham our father, as pertaining to the flesh, hath found?
4.blb: What then will we say that Abraham, our forefather according to the flesh, has found?
4.bbe: What, then, may we say that Abraham, our father after the flesh, has got?
4.heading: Abraham Justified by Faith

4.msb: If Abraham was indeed justified by works, he had something to boast about, but not before God.
4.kjv: For if Abraham were justified by works, he hath whereof to glory; but not before God.
4.blb: For if Abraham was justified by works, he has a ground of boasting, but not before God.
4.bbe: For if Abraham got righteousness by works, he has reason for pride; but not before God.

4.msb: For what does the Scripture say? “Abraham believed God, and it was credited to him as righteousness.”
4.kjv: For what saith the scripture? Abraham believed God, and it was counted unto him for righteousness.
4.blb: For what does the Scripture say? “And Abraham believed God, and it was reckoned to him as righteousness.”
4.bbe: But what does it say in the holy Writings? And Abraham had faith in God, and it was put to his account as righteousness.

4.msb: Now the wages of the worker are not credited as a gift, but as an obligation.
4.kjv: Now to him that worketh is the reward not reckoned of grace, but of debt.
4.blb: Now to the one working, the wage is not reckoned according to grace, but according to debt.
4.bbe: Now, the reward is credited to him who does works, not as of grace but as a debt.

4.msb: However, to the one who does not work, but believes in Him who justifies the ungodly, his faith is credited as righteousness.
4.kjv: But to him that worketh not, but believeth on him that justifieth the ungodly, his faith is counted for righteousness.
4.blb: But to the one not working but believing on the One justifying the ungodly, his faith is reckoned as righteousness,
4.bbe: But to him who without working has faith in him who gives righteousness to the evil-doer, his faith is put to his account as righteousness.

4.msb: And David speaks likewise of the blessedness of the man to whom God credits righteousness apart from works:
4.kjv: Even as David also describeth the blessedness of the man, unto whom God imputeth righteousness without works,
4.blb: just as David also declares the blessedness of the man to whom God reckons righteousness apart from works:
4.bbe: As David says that there is a blessing on the man to whose account God puts righteousness without works, saying,

4.msb: “Blessed are they whose lawless acts are forgiven, whose sins are covered.
4.kjv: Saying, Blessed are they whose iniquities are forgiven, and whose sins are covered.
4.blb: “Blessed are those whose lawless deeds are forgiven, and whose sins are covered;
4.bbe: Happy are those who have forgiveness for their wrongdoing, and whose sins are covered.

4.msb: Blessed is the man whose sin the Lord will never count against him.”
4.kjv: Blessed is the man to whom the Lord will not impute sin.
4.blb: blessed is the man to whom the Lord shall never reckon sin.”
4.bbe: Happy is the man against whom no sin is recorded by the Lord.

4.msb: Is this blessing only on the circumcised, or also on the uncircumcised? We have been saying that Abraham’s faith was credited to him as righteousness.
4.kjv: Cometh this blessedness then upon the circumcision only, or upon the uncircumcision also? for we say that faith was reckoned to Abraham for righteousness.
4.blb: Is this blessedness, then, on the circumcision, or also on the uncircumcision? For we are saying faith was reckoned to Abraham as righteousness.
4.bbe: Is this blessing, then, for the circumcision only, or in the same way for those who have not circumcision? for we say that the faith of Abraham was put to his account as righteousness.

4.msb: In what context was it credited? Was it after his circumcision, or before? It was not after, but before.
4.kjv: How was it then reckoned? when he was in circumcision, or in uncircumcision? Not in circumcision, but in uncircumcision.
4.blb: How then was it reckoned—being in circumcision, or in uncircumcision? Not in circumcision, but in uncircumcision.
4.bbe: How, then, was it judged? when he had circumcision, or when he had it not? Not when he had it, but when he did not have it:

4.msb: And he received the sign of circumcision as a seal of the righteousness that he had by faith while he was still uncircumcised. So then, he is the father of all who believe but are not circumcised, in order that righteousness might be credited to them as well.
4.kjv: And he received the sign of circumcision, a seal of the righteousness of the faith which he had yet being uncircumcised: that he might be the father of all them that believe, though they be not circumcised; that righteousness might be imputed unto them also:
4.blb: And he received the sign of circumcision, a seal of the righteousness of the faith that he had while in the uncircumcision, for him to be father of all those believing through uncircumcision, for the righteousness to be reckoned also to them,
4.bbe: And he was given the sign of circumcision as a witness of the faith which he had before he underwent circumcision: so that he might be the father of all those who have faith, though they have not circumcision, and so that righteousness might be put to their account;

4.msb: And he is also the father of the circumcised who not only are circumcised, but who also walk in the footsteps of the faith that our father Abraham had before he was circumcised.
4.kjv: And the father of circumcision to them who are not of the circumcision only, but who also walk in the steps of that faith of our father Abraham, which he had being yet uncircumcised.
4.blb: and father of circumcision to those not only of circumcision, but also to those walking in the footsteps of the faith of our father Abraham in uncircumcision.
4.bbe: And the father of circumcision to those who not only are of the circumcision, but who keep to the way of that faith which our father Abraham had before he underwent circumcision.

4.msb: For the promise to Abraham and his offspring that he would be heir of the world was not given through the law, but through the righteousness that comes by faith.
4.kjv: For the promise, that he should be the heir of the world, was not to Abraham, or to his seed, through the law, but through the righteousness of faith.
4.blb: For not through law was the promise to Abraham or his seed for him to be heir of the world, but through the righteousness of faith.
4.bbe: For God's word, that the earth would be his heritage, was given to Abraham, not through the law, but through the righteousness of faith.
4.heading: Abraham Receives the Promise

4.msb: For if those who live by the law are heirs, faith is useless and the promise is worthless,
4.kjv: For if they which are of the law be heirs, faith is made void, and the promise made of none effect:
4.blb: For if those of the law are heirs, faith has been made void and the promise has been nullified.
4.bbe: For if they who are of the law are the people who get the heritage, then faith is made of no use, and the word of God has no power;

4.msb: because the law brings wrath. For where there is no law, there is no transgression.
4.kjv: Because the law worketh wrath: for where no law is, there is no transgression.
4.blb: For the law brings about wrath; and where there is no law, neither is there transgression.
4.bbe: For the outcome of the law is wrath; but where there is no law it will not be broken.

4.msb: Therefore, the promise comes by faith, so that it may rest on grace and may be guaranteed to all Abraham’s offspring—not only to those who are of the law, but also to those who are of the faith of Abraham. He is the father of us all.
4.kjv: Therefore it is of faith, that it might be by grace; to the end the promise might be sure to all the seed; not to that only which is of the law, but to that also which is of the faith of Abraham; who is the father of us all,
4.blb: Because of this it is of faith, so that it may be according to grace for the promise to be sure to all the seed, not only to that of the law, but also to that of the faith of Abraham, who is the father of us all
4.bbe: For this reason it is of faith, so that it may be through grace; and so that the word of God may be certain to all the seed; not only to that which is of the law, but to that which is of the faith of Abraham, who is the father of us all,

4.msb: As it is written: “I have made you a father of many nations.” He is our father in the presence of God, in whom he believed, the God who gives life to the dead and calls into being what does not yet exist.
4.kjv: (As it is written, I have made thee a father of many nations,) before him whom he believed, even God, who quickeneth the dead, and calleth those things which be not as though they were.
4.blb: (as it has been written: “A father of many nations I have set you”) before Him whom he believed—God, the One making alive the dead and calling existing the things not as existing—
4.bbe: (As it is said in the holy Writings, I have made you a father of a number of nations) before him in whom he had faith, that is, God, who gives life to the dead, and to whom the things which are not are as if they were.

4.msb: Against all hope, Abraham in hope believed and so became the father of many nations, just as he had been told, “So shall your offspring be.”
4.kjv: Who against hope believed in hope, that he might become the father of many nations; according to that which was spoken, So shall thy seed be.
4.blb: who against hope in hope believed, for him to become the father of many nations, according to that having been spoken, “So will your seed be.”
4.bbe: Who without reason for hope, in faith went on hoping, so that he became the father of a number of nations, as it had been said, So will your seed be.

4.msb: Without weakening in his faith, he acknowledged neither the decrepitness of his body (since he was about a hundred years old) nor the lifelessness of Sarah’s womb.
4.kjv: And being not weak in faith, he considered not his own body now dead, when he was about an hundred years old, neither yet the deadness of Sara’s womb:
4.blb: And not having become weak in the faith, he considered his body already having become dead, being about a hundred years old, and the deadness of Sarah’s womb.
4.bbe: And not being feeble in faith though his body seemed to him little better than dead (he being about a hundred years old) and Sarah was no longer able to have children:

4.msb: Yet he did not waver through disbelief in the promise of God, but was strengthened in his faith and gave glory to God,
4.kjv: He staggered not at the promise of God through unbelief; but was strong in faith, giving glory to God;
4.blb: Yet he did not doubt in unbelief in the promise of God, but was empowered in faith, having given glory to God,
4.bbe: Still, he did not give up faith in the undertaking of God, but was made strong by faith, giving glory to God,

4.msb: being fully persuaded that God was able to do what He had promised.
