2.msb: For if the message spoken by angels was binding, and every transgression and disobedience received its just punishment,
2.kjv: For if the word spoken by angels was stedfast, and every transgression and disobedience received a just recompence of reward;
2.blb: For if the word having been spoken by angels was firm, and every transgression and disobedience received a just recompense,
2.bbe: Because if the word which came through the angels was fixed, and in the past every evil act against God's orders was given its full punishment;

2.msb: how shall we escape if we neglect such a great salvation? This salvation was first announced by the Lord, was confirmed to us by those who heard Him,
2.kjv: How shall we escape, if we neglect so great salvation; which at the first began to be spoken by the Lord, and was confirmed unto us by them that heard him;
2.blb: how will we escape, having neglected such a great salvation, which, having received a beginning to be spoken by the Lord, was confirmed to us by those having heard,
2.bbe: What will come on us, if we do not give our minds to such a great salvation? a salvation of which our fathers first had knowledge through the words of the Lord, and which was made certain to us by those to whom his words came;

2.msb: and was affirmed by God through signs, wonders, various miracles, and gifts of the Holy Spirit distributed according to His will.
2.kjv: God also bearing them witness, both with signs and wonders, and with divers miracles, and gifts of the Holy Ghost, according to his own will?
2.blb: God testifying with them both by signs and wonders, and by various miracles, and distributions of the Holy Spirit according to His will.
2.bbe: And God was a witness with them, by signs and wonders, and by more than natural powers, and by his distribution of the Holy Spirit at his pleasure.

2.msb: For it is not to angels that He has subjected the world to come, about which we are speaking.
2.kjv: For unto the angels hath he not put in subjection the world to come, whereof we speak.
2.blb: For not to angels did He subject the world that is about to be, concerning which we are speaking,
2.bbe: For he did not make the angels rulers over the world to come, of which I am writing.
2.heading: Jesus like His Brothers

2.msb: But somewhere it is testified in these words: “What is man that You are mindful of him, or the son of man that You care for him?
2.kjv: But one in a certain place testified, saying, What is man, that thou art mindful of him? or the son of man, that thou visitest him?
2.blb: but someone somewhere solemnly testified, saying, “What is man that You are mindful of him, or the son of man that You care for him?
2.bbe: But a certain writer has given his witness, saying, What is man, that you keep him in mind? what is the son of man, that you take him into account?

2.msb: You made him a little lower than the angels; You crowned him with glory and honor,
2.kjv: Thou madest him a little lower than the angels; thou crownedst him with glory and honour, and didst set him over the works of thy hands:
2.blb: You made him a little less than the angels; You crowned him with glory and honor;
2.bbe: You made him a little lower than the angels; you gave him a crown of glory and honour, and made him ruler over all the works of your hands:

2.msb: and placed everything under his feet.” When God subjected all things to him, He left nothing outside of his control. Yet at present we do not see everything subject to him.
2.kjv: Thou hast put all things in subjection under his feet. For in that he put all in subjection under him, he left nothing that is not put under him. But now we see not yet all things put under him.
2.blb: You subjected all things under his feet.” For in subjecting all things to him, He left nothing unsubject to him. But now, not yet do we see all things having been subjected to him.
2.bbe: You put all things under his feet. For in making man the ruler over all things, God did not put anything outside his authority; though we do not see everything under him now.

2.msb: But we see Jesus, who was made a little lower than the angels, now crowned with glory and honor because He suffered death, so that by the grace of God He might taste death for everyone.
2.kjv: But we see Jesus, who was made a little lower than the angels for the suffering of death, crowned with glory and honour; that he by the grace of God should taste death for every man.
2.blb: But we see Jesus, the One having been made a little less than the angels, because of the suffering of death, having been crowned with glory and with honor, so that by the grace of God He might taste death for everyone.
2.bbe: But we see him who was made a little lower than the angels, even Jesus, crowned with glory and honour, because he let himself be put to death so that by the grace of God he might undergo death for all men.

2.msb: In bringing many sons to glory, it was fitting for God, for whom and through whom all things exist, to make the author of their salvation perfect through suffering.
2.kjv: For it became him, for whom are all things, and by whom are all things, in bringing many sons unto glory, to make the captain of their salvation perfect through sufferings.
2.blb: For it was fitting to Him, for whom are all things and through whom are all things, having brought many sons to glory, to make perfect the author of their salvation through sufferings.
2.bbe: Because it was right for him, for whom and through whom all things have being, in guiding his sons to glory, to make the captain of their salvation complete through pain.

2.msb: For both the One who sanctifies and those who are sanctified are of the same family. So Jesus is not ashamed to call them brothers.
2.kjv: For both he that sanctifieth and they who are sanctified are all of one: for which cause he is not ashamed to call them brethren,
2.blb: For both the One sanctifying and those being sanctified are all of one, for which reason He is not ashamed to call them brothers,
2.bbe: For he who makes holy and those who are made holy are all of one family; and for this reason it is no shame for him to give them the name of brothers,

2.msb: He says: “I will proclaim Your name to My brothers; I will sing Your praises in the assembly.”
2.kjv: Saying, I will declare thy name unto my brethren, in the midst of the church will I sing praise unto thee.
2.blb: saying: “I will declare Your name to My brothers; in the midst of the assembly I will sing Your praises.”
2.bbe: Saying, I will give the knowledge of your name to my brothers, I will make a song of praise to you before the church.

2.msb: And again: “I will put My trust in Him.” And once again: “Here am I, and the children God has given Me.”
2.kjv: And again, I will put my trust in him. And again, Behold I and the children which God hath given me.
2.blb: And again: “I will be trusting on Him.” And again: “Behold, I and the children whom God gave to Me.”
2.bbe: And again he says, I will put my faith in him. And again, See, I am here, and the children which God has given to me.

2.msb: Now since the children have flesh and blood, He too shared in their humanity, so that by His death He might destroy him who holds the power of death, that is, the devil,
2.kjv: Forasmuch then as the children are partakers of flesh and blood, he also himself likewise took part of the same; that through death he might destroy him that had the power of death, that is, the devil;
2.blb: Therefore, since the children have shared in blood and flesh, He also likewise partook of the same things, so that through death He might render powerless the one having the power of death, that is, the devil,
2.bbe: And because the children are flesh and blood, he took a body himself and became like them; so that by his death he might put an end to him who had the power of death, that is to say, the Evil One;

2.msb: and free those who all their lives were held in slavery by their fear of death.
2.kjv: And deliver them who through fear of death were all their lifetime subject to bondage.
2.blb: and might set free those who all their time to live were subject to slavery through the fear of death.
2.bbe: And let those who all their lives were in chains because of their fear of death, go free.

2.msb: For surely it is not the angels He helps, but the descendants of Abraham.
2.kjv: For verily he took not on him the nature of angels; but he took on him the seed of Abraham.
2.blb: For surely it is not the angels He lays hold of, but He lays hold of the seed of Abraham.
2.bbe: For, truly, he does not take on the life of angels, but that of the seed of Abraham.

2.msb: For this reason He had to be made like His brothers in every way, so that He might become a merciful and faithful high priest in service to God, in order to make atonement for the sins of the people.
2.kjv: Wherefore in all things it behoved him to be made like unto his brethren, that he might be a merciful and faithful high priest in things pertaining to God, to make reconciliation for the sins of the people.
2.blb: Hence it was necessary to be made like the brothers in all things, so that He might become a merciful and faithful high priest in the things relating to God, in order to make propitiation for the sins of the people.
2.bbe: Because of this it was necessary for him to be made like his brothers in every way, so that he might be a high priest full of mercy and keeping faith in everything to do with God, making offerings for the sins of the people.

2.msb: Because He Himself suffered when He was tempted, He is able to help those who are being tempted.
2.kjv: For in that he himself hath suffered being tempted, he is able to succour them that are tempted.
2.blb: For in that He Himself has suffered, having been tempted, He is able to help those being tempted.
2.bbe: For having been put to the test himself, he is able to give help to others when they are tested.

3.msb: Therefore, holy brothers, who share in the heavenly calling, set your focus on Jesus Christ, the apostle and high priest whom we confess.
3.kjv: Wherefore, holy brethren, partakers of the heavenly calling, consider the Apostle and High Priest of our profession, Christ Jesus;
3.blb: Hence, holy brothers, partakers of a heavenly calling, carefully consider Jesus, the Apostle and High Priest of our confession,
3.bbe: For this reason, holy brothers, marked out to have a part in heaven, give thought to Jesus the representative and high priest of our faith;
3.heading: Jesus Our Apostle and High Priest

3.msb: He was faithful to the One who appointed Him, just as Moses was faithful in all God’s house.
3.kjv: Who was faithful to him that appointed him, as also Moses was faithful in all his house.
3.blb: being faithful to the One having appointed Him, as Moses also in all His house.
3.bbe: Who kept faith with God who gave him his place, even as Moses did in all his house.

3.msb: For Jesus has been counted worthy of greater glory than Moses, just as the builder of a house has greater honor than the house itself.
3.kjv: For this man was counted worthy of more glory than Moses, inasmuch as he who hath builded the house hath more honour than the house.
3.blb: For this One has been counted worthy of more glory than Moses, by as much as the one having built it has more honor than the house itself.
3.bbe: And it was right for this man to have more honour than Moses, even as the builder of a house has more honour than the house.

3.msb: And every house is built by someone, but God is the builder of everything.
3.kjv: For every house is builded by some man; but he that built all things is God.
3.blb: For every house is built by someone, but the One having built everything is God.
3.bbe: For every house has a builder; but the builder of all things is God.

3.msb: Now Moses was faithful as a servant in all God’s house, testifying to what would be spoken later.
3.kjv: And Moses verily was faithful in all his house, as a servant, for a testimony of those things which were to be spoken after;
3.blb: And indeed Moses was faithful as an attendant in all His house, for a testimony of the things going to be spoken,
3.bbe: And Moses certainly kept faith as a servant, in all his house, and as a witness of those things which were to be said later;

3.msb: But Christ is faithful as the Son over God’s house. And we are His house, if we hold firmly to the end our confidence and the hope of which we boast.
3.kjv: But Christ as a son over his own house; whose house are we, if we hold fast the confidence and the rejoicing of the hope firm unto the end.
3.blb: but Christ as the Son over His house, whose house we are, if we should hold our confidence and the boast of our hope.
3.bbe: But Christ as a son, over his house; whose house are we, if we keep our hearts fixed in the glad and certain hope till the end.

3.msb: Therefore, as the Holy Spirit says: “Today, if you hear His voice,
3.kjv: Wherefore (as the Holy Ghost saith, To day if ye will hear his voice,
3.blb: Therefore, just as the Holy Spirit says: “Today, if you should hear His voice,
3.bbe: And so, as the Holy Spirit says, Today if you let his voice come to your ears,
3.heading: Do Not Harden Your Hearts

3.msb: do not harden your hearts, as you did in the rebellion, in the day of testing in the wilderness,
3.kjv: Harden not your hearts, as in the provocation, in the day of temptation in the wilderness:
3.blb: do not harden your hearts, as in the rebellion, in the day of testing in the wilderness,
3.bbe: Be not hard of heart, as when you made me angry, on the day of testing in the waste land,

3.msb: where your fathers tested and tried Me, and for forty years saw My works.
3.kjv: When your fathers tempted me, proved me, and saw my works forty years.
3.blb: where forty years your fathers tested Me by trial and saw My works.
3.bbe: When your fathers put me to the test, and saw my works for forty years.

3.msb: Therefore I was angry with that generation, and I said, ‘Their hearts are always going astray, and they have not known My ways.’
3.kjv: Wherefore I was grieved with that generation, and said, They do alway err in their heart; and they have not known my ways.
3.blb: Therefore I was angry with this generation, and I said, ‘Always they go astray in their heart; and did not know My ways;’
3.bbe: So that I was angry with this generation, and I said, Their hearts are in error at all times, and they have no knowledge of my ways;

3.msb: So I swore on oath in My anger, ‘They shall never enter My rest.’”
3.kjv: So I sware in my wrath, They shall not enter into my rest.)
3.blb: as I swore in My wrath, ‘They shall not enter into My rest.’”
3.bbe: And being angry I made an oath, saying, They may not come into my rest.

3.msb: See to it, brothers, that none of you has a wicked heart of unbelief that turns away from the living God.
3.kjv: Take heed, brethren, lest there be in any of you an evil heart of unbelief, in departing from the living God.
3.blb: See to it, brothers, lest ever there will be in any of you an evil heart of unbelief in the falling away from the living God.
3.bbe: My brothers, take care that there is not by chance in any one of you an evil heart without belief, turning away from the living God:
3.heading: The Peril of Unbelief

3.msb: But exhort one another daily, as long as it is called today, so that none of you may be hardened by sin’s deceitfulness.
3.kjv: But exhort one another daily, while it is called To day; lest any of you be hardened through the deceitfulness of sin.
3.blb: But encourage one another each day, as long as it is called today, so that not any of you may be hardened by the deceitfulness of sin.
3.bbe: But give comfort to one another every day as long as it is still Today; so that no one among you may be made hard by the deceit of sin:

3.msb: We have come to share in Christ if we hold firmly to the end the assurance we had at first.
3.kjv: For we are made partakers of Christ, if we hold the beginning of our confidence stedfast unto the end;
3.blb: For we have become partakers of Christ, if indeed we should hold firm until the end the assurance from the beginning.
3.bbe: For if we keep the substance of the faith which we had at the start, even till the end, we have a part with Christ;

3.msb: As it has been said: “Today, if you hear His voice, do not harden your hearts, as you did in the rebellion.”
3.kjv: While it is said, To day if ye will hear his voice, harden not your hearts, as in the provocation.
3.blb: As it is said: “Today if you should hear His voice, do not harden your hearts, as in the rebellion.”
3.bbe: As it is said, Today if you will let his voice come to your ears, be not hard of heart, as when you made him angry.

3.msb: For some heard and rebelled, but not all those Moses led out of Egypt.
3.kjv: For some, when they had heard, did provoke: howbeit not all that came out of Egypt by Moses.
3.blb: For who, having heard, rebelled? But was it not all those having come forth out of Egypt through Moses?
3.bbe: Who made him angry when his voice came to them? was it not all those who came out of Egypt with Moses?

3.msb: And with whom was God angry for forty years? Was it not with those who sinned, whose bodies fell in the wilderness?
3.kjv: But with whom was he grieved forty years? was it not with them that had sinned, whose carcases fell in the wilderness?
3.blb: And with whom was He angry forty years, if not with those having sinned, whose bodies fell in the wilderness?
3.bbe: And with whom was he angry for forty years? was it not with those who did evil, who came to their deaths in the waste land?

3.msb: And to whom did He swear that they would never enter His rest? Was it not to those who disobeyed?
3.kjv: And to whom sware he that they should not enter into his rest, but to them that believed not?
3.blb: And to whom did He swear that they will not enter into His rest, if not to those having disobeyed?
3.bbe: And to whom did he make an oath that they might not come into his rest? was it not to those who went against his orders?

3.msb: So we see that it was because of their unbelief that they were unable to enter.
3.kjv: So we see that they could not enter in because of unbelief.
3.blb: And we see that they were not able to enter because of unbelief.
3.bbe: So we see that they were not able to go in because they had no belief.

4.msb: Therefore, while the promise of entering His rest still stands, let us be careful that none of you be deemed to have fallen short of it.
4.kjv: Let us therefore fear, lest, a promise being left us of entering into his rest, any of you should seem to come short of it.
4.blb: Therefore we should fear, lest ever, the promise to enter into His rest left remaining, any of you should seem to have fallen short.
4.bbe: Let us then, though we still have God's word that we may come into his rest, go in fear that some of you may be unable to do so.
4.heading: The Sabbath Rest

4.msb: For we also received the good news just as they did; but the message they heard was of no value to them, since they did not share the faith of those who comprehended it.
4.kjv: For unto us was the gospel preached, as well as unto them: but the word preached did not profit them, not being mixed with faith in them that heard it.
4.blb: For also we are those having had the gospel proclaimed, even as also those; but the word of their hearing did not profit those not having been united with the faith of those having heard.
4.bbe: And, truly, the good news came to us, even as it did to them; but the hearing of the word did them no good, because they were not united in faith with the true hearers.

4.msb: Now we who have believed enter that rest. As for the others, it is just as God has said: “So I swore on oath in My anger, ‘They shall never enter My rest.’” And yet His works have been finished since the foundation of the world.
4.kjv: For we which have believed do enter into rest, as he said, As I have sworn in my wrath, if they shall enter into my rest: although the works were finished from the foundation of the world.
4.blb: For we enter into the rest—those having believed—just as He has said: “As I swore in My wrath, ‘They shall not enter into My rest.’” And yet the works were done from the foundation of the world.
4.bbe: For those of us who have belief come into his rest; even as he has said, As I said in my oath when I was angry, They may not come into my rest: though the works were done from the time of the making of the world.

4.msb: For somewhere He has spoken about the seventh day in this manner: “And on the seventh day God rested from all His works.”
4.kjv: For he spake in a certain place of the seventh day on this wise, And God did rest the seventh day from all his works.
4.blb: For He has spoken somewhere about the seventh day thus: “And God rested on the seventh day from all His works.”
4.bbe: For in one place he has said of the seventh day, And God had rest from all his works on the seventh day;

4.msb: And again, as He says in the passage above: “They shall never enter My rest.”
4.kjv: And in this place again, If they shall enter into my rest.
4.blb: And again in this: “They shall not enter into My rest.”
4.bbe: And in the same place he says again, They will not come into my rest.

4.msb: Since, then, it remains for some to enter His rest, and since those who formerly heard the good news did not enter because of their disobedience,
4.kjv: Seeing therefore it remaineth that some must enter therein, and they to whom it was first preached entered not in because of unbelief:
4.blb: Therefore, since it remains for some to enter into it, and those formerly having had the gospel proclaimed did not enter because of disobedience,
4.bbe: So that as it is clear that some have to go in, and that the first hearers of the good news were not able to go in because they went against God's orders,

4.msb: God again designated a certain day as “Today,” when a long time later He spoke through David as was just stated: “Today, if you hear His voice, do not harden your hearts.”
4.kjv: Again, he limiteth a certain day, saying in David, To day, after so long a time; as it is said, To day if ye will hear his voice, harden not your hearts.
4.blb: again He designates a certain day as “Today,” saying in David after so long a time, just as it has been said before, “Today, if you should hear His voice, do not harden your hearts.”
4.bbe: After a long time, again naming a certain day, he says in David, Today (as he had said before), Today if you will let his voice come to your ears, be not hard of heart,

4.msb: For if Joshua had given them rest, God would not have spoken later about another day.
4.kjv: For if Jesus had given them rest, then would he not afterward have spoken of another day.
4.blb: For if Joshua had given them rest, He would not have spoken after this about another day.
4.bbe: For if Joshua had given them rest, he would not have said anything about another day.

4.msb: There remains, then, a Sabbath rest for the people of God.
4.kjv: There remaineth therefore a rest to the people of God.
4.blb: So then, there remains a Sabbath rest for the people of God.
4.bbe: So that there is still a Sabbath-keeping for the people of God.

4.msb: For whoever enters God’s rest also rests from his own work, just as God did from His.
4.kjv: For he that is entered into his rest, he also hath ceased from his own works, as God did from his.
4.blb: For the one having entered into His rest, he also rested from his works, just as God did from His own.
4.bbe: For the man who comes into his rest has had rest from his works, as God did from his.

4.msb: Let us, therefore, make every effort to enter that rest, so that no one will fall by following the same pattern of disobedience.
4.kjv: Let us labour therefore to enter into that rest, lest any man fall after the same example of unbelief.
4.blb: Therefore we should be diligent to enter into that rest, so that no one should fall in the same exhibit of disobedience.
4.bbe: Because of this, let us have a strong desire to come into that rest, and let no one go after the example of those who went against God's orders.

4.msb: For the word of God is living and active. Sharper than any double-edged sword, it pierces even to dividing soul and spirit, joints and marrow. It judges the thoughts and intentions of the heart.
4.kjv: For the word of God is quick, and powerful, and sharper than any twoedged sword, piercing even to the dividing asunder of soul and spirit, and of the joints and marrow, and is a discerner of the thoughts and intents of the heart.
4.blb: For the word of God is living and effective, and sharper than any two-edged sword, piercing through and as far as the division of soul and spirit, and of joints and marrows, and able to judge the reflections and intentions of the heart.
4.bbe: For the word of God is living and full of power, and is sharper than any two-edged sword, cutting through and making a division even of the soul and the spirit, the bones and the muscles, and quick to see the thoughts and purposes of the heart.
4.heading: The Living Word

4.msb: Nothing in all creation is hidden from God’s sight; everything is uncovered and exposed before the eyes of Him to whom we must give account.
4.kjv: Neither is there any creature that is not manifest in his sight: but all things are naked and opened unto the eyes of him with whom we have to do.
4.blb: And there is no created thing hidden before Him, but all things are bare and exposed to the eyes of Him to whom is our account.
4.bbe: And there is nothing made which is not completely clear to him; there is nothing covered, but all things are open to the eyes of him with whom we have to do.

4.msb: Therefore, since we have a great high priest who has passed through the heavens, Jesus the Son of God, let us hold firmly to what we profess.
4.kjv: Seeing then that we have a great high priest, that is passed into the heavens, Jesus the Son of God, let us hold fast our profession.
4.blb: Therefore, having a great high priest having passed through the heavens, Jesus, the Son of God, let us hold fast to our confession.
4.bbe: Having then a great high priest, who has made his way through the heavens, even Jesus the Son of God, let us be strong in our faith.

4.msb: For we do not have a high priest who is unable to sympathize with our weaknesses, but we have one who was tempted in every way that we are, yet was without sin.
4.kjv: For we have not an high priest which cannot be touched with the feeling of our infirmities; but was in all points tempted like as we are, yet without sin.
4.blb: For we do not have a high priest not being able to sympathize with our weaknesses, but one having been tempted in all things by the same way, without sin.
4.bbe: For we have not a high priest who is not able to be touched by the feelings of our feeble flesh; but we have one who has been tested in all points as we ourselves are tested, but without sin.

4.msb: Let us then approach the throne of grace with confidence, so that we may receive mercy and find grace to help us in our time of need.
4.kjv: Let us therefore come boldly unto the throne of grace, that we may obtain mercy, and find grace to help in time of need.
4.blb: Therefore let us come with confidence to the throne of grace, so that we may receive mercy and may find grace for help in time of need.
4.bbe: Then let us come near to the seat of grace without fear, so that mercy may be given to us, and we may get grace for our help in time of need.

5.msb: Every high priest is appointed from among men to represent them in matters relating to God, to offer gifts and sacrifices for sins.
5.kjv: For every high priest taken from among men is ordained for men in things pertaining to God, that he may offer both gifts and sacrifices for sins:
5.blb: For every high priest being taken from among men is appointed for men in things relating to God, that he may offer both gifts and sacrifices for sins,
5.bbe: Every high priest who is taken from among men is given his position to take care of the interests of men in those things which have to do with God, so that he may make offerings for sins.
5.heading: The Perfect High Priest

5.msb: He is able to deal gently with those who are ignorant and misguided, since he himself is beset by weakness.
5.kjv: Who can have compassion on the ignorant, and on them that are out of the way; for that he himself also is compassed with infirmity.
5.blb: being able to deal gently with those being ignorant and going astray, since he himself also is encompassed by weakness;
5.bbe: He is able to have feeling for those who have no knowledge and for those who are wandering from the true way, because he himself is feeble;

5.msb: That is why he is obligated to offer sacrifices for his own sins, as well as for the sins of the people.
5.kjv: And by reason hereof he ought, as for the people, so also for himself, to offer for sins.
5.blb: and because of this, he is obligated, just as concerning the people, to offer for sins so also concerning himself.
5.bbe: And being feeble, he has to make sin-offerings for himself as well as for the people.

5.msb: No one takes this honor upon himself; he must be called by God, just as Aaron was.
5.kjv: And no man taketh this honour unto himself, but he that is called of God, as was Aaron.
5.blb: And no one takes upon himself the honor, but is being called by God, just as Aaron also.
5.bbe: And no man who is not given authority by God, as Aaron was, takes this honour for himself.

5.msb: So also Christ did not take upon Himself the glory of becoming a high priest, but He was called by the One who said to Him: “You are My Son; today I have become Your Father.”
5.kjv: So also Christ glorified not himself to be made an high priest; but he that said unto him, Thou art my Son, to day have I begotten thee.
5.blb: So also Christ did not glorify Himself to become a high priest, but the One having said to Him: “You are My Son, today I have begotten You.”
5.bbe: In the same way Christ did not take for himself the glory of being made a high priest, but was given it by him who said, You are my Son, this day I have given you being:

5.msb: And in another passage God says: “You are a priest forever in the order of Melchizedek.”
5.kjv: As he saith also in another place, Thou art a priest for ever after the order of Melchisedec.
5.blb: Just as that, He also says in another place: “You are a priest to the age, according to the order of Melchizedek.”
5.bbe: As he says in another place, You are a priest for ever after the order of Melchizedek.

5.msb: During the days of Jesus’ earthly life, He offered up prayers and petitions with loud cries and tears to the One who could save Him from death, and He was heard because of His reverence.
5.kjv: Who in the days of his flesh, when he had offered up prayers and supplications with strong crying and tears unto him that was able to save him from death, and was heard in that he feared;
5.blb: He in the days of His flesh having offered both supplications and entreaties with strong crying and tears to the One being able to save Him from death, and having been heard from reverence,
5.bbe: Who in the days of his flesh, having sent up prayers and requests with strong crying and weeping to him who was able to give him salvation from death, had his prayer answered because of his fear of God.

5.msb: Although He was a Son, He learned obedience from what He suffered.
5.kjv: Though he were a Son, yet learned he obedience by the things which he suffered;
5.blb: although being a Son, He learned obedience from the things He suffered,
5.bbe: And though he was a Son, through the pain which he underwent, the knowledge came to him of what it was to be under God's orders;

5.msb: And having been made perfect, He became the source of eternal salvation to all who obey Him
5.kjv: And being made perfect, he became the author of eternal salvation unto all them that obey him;
5.blb: and having been perfected, He became the source of eternal salvation to all those obeying Him,
5.bbe: And when he had been made complete, he became the giver of eternal salvation to all those who are under his orders;

5.msb: and was designated by God as high priest in the order of Melchizedek.
5.kjv: Called of God an high priest after the order of Melchisedec.
5.blb: having been designated by God as high priest according to the order of Melchizedek.
5.bbe: Being named by God a high priest of the order of Melchizedek.

5.msb: We have much to say about this, but it is hard to explain, because you are dull of hearing.
5.kjv: Of whom we have many things to say, and hard to be uttered, seeing ye are dull of hearing.
5.blb: Concerning this there is much speech from us, and difficult in interpretation to speak, since you have become dull in hearing.
5.bbe: Of whom we have much to say which it is hard to make clear, because you are slow of hearing.
5.heading: Milk and Solid Food

5.msb: Although by this time you ought to be teachers, you need someone to reteach you the basic principles of God’s word. You need milk, not solid food!
5.kjv: For when for the time ye ought to be teachers, ye have need that one teach you again which be the first principles of the oracles of God; and are become such as have need of milk, and not of strong meat.
5.blb: For even by the time you ought to be teachers, you have need of one to teach you again what is the beginning of the elements of the oracles of God; and you have become those having need of milk, and not of solid food.
5.bbe: And though by this time it would be right for you to be teachers, you still have need of someone to give you teaching about the first simple rules of God's revelation; you have become like babies who have need of milk, and not of solid food.

5.msb: For everyone who lives on milk is still an infant, inexperienced in the message of righteousness.
5.kjv: For every one that useth milk is unskilful in the word of righteousness: for he is a babe.
5.blb: For everyone partaking of milk is inexperienced in the word of righteousness, for he is an infant.
5.bbe: For everyone who takes milk is without experience of the word of righteousness: he is a child.

5.msb: But solid food is for the mature, who by constant use have trained their senses to distinguish good from evil.
5.kjv: But strong meat belongeth to them that are of full age, even those who by reason of use have their senses exercised to discern both good and evil.
5.blb: But solid food is for the mature, the ones by constant use having trained the senses for distinguishing both good and evil.
5.bbe: But solid food is for men of full growth, even for those whose senses are trained by use to see what is good and what is evil.

6.msb: Therefore let us leave the elementary teachings about Christ and go on to maturity, not laying again the foundation of repentance from dead works, and of faith in God,
6.kjv: Therefore leaving the principles of the doctrine of Christ, let us go on unto perfection; not laying again the foundation of repentance from dead works, and of faith toward God,
6.blb: Therefore, having left the word of the beginning of the Christ, we should carry on to maturity, not laying again a foundation of repentance from dead works, and of faith in God,
6.bbe: For this reason let us go on from the first things about Christ to full growth; not building again that on which it is based, that is, the turning of the heart from dead works, and faith in God,
6.heading: A Call to Maturity

6.msb: instruction about baptisms, the laying on of hands, the resurrection of the dead, and eternal judgment.
6.kjv: Of the doctrine of baptisms, and of laying on of hands, and of resurrection of the dead, and of eternal judgment.
6.blb: teaching of baptisms, and of laying on of hands, and of the resurrection of the dead, and of eternal judgment.
6.bbe: The teaching of baptisms, and of the putting on of hands, and of the future life of the dead, and of the judging on the last day.

6.msb: And this we will do, if God permits.
6.kjv: And this will we do, if God permit.
6.blb: And this we will do, if God may permit.
6.bbe: Now we will do this, if God lets us.

6.msb: It is impossible for those who have once been enlightened, who have tasted the heavenly gift, who have shared in the Holy Spirit,
6.kjv: For it is impossible for those who were once enlightened, and have tasted of the heavenly gift, and were made partakers of the Holy Ghost,
6.blb: For it is impossible for those once having been enlightened, and having tasted of the heavenly gift, and having become partakers of the Holy Spirit,
6.bbe: As for those who at one time saw the light, tasting the good things from heaven, and having their part in the Holy Spirit,

6.msb: who have tasted the goodness of the word of God and the powers of the coming age—
6.kjv: And have tasted the good word of God, and the powers of the world to come,
6.blb: and having tasted the goodness of God’s word and the power of the coming age—
6.bbe: With knowledge of the good word of God, and of the powers of the coming time,

6.msb: and then have fallen away—to be restored to repentance, because they themselves are crucifying the Son of God all over again and subjecting Him to open shame.
6.kjv: If they shall fall away, to renew them again unto repentance; seeing they crucify to themselves the Son of God afresh, and put him to an open shame.
6.blb: and then having fallen away—to restore them again to repentance, crucifying in themselves the Son of God and subjecting Him to open shame.
6.bbe: And then let themselves be turned away, it is not possible for their hearts to be made new a second time; because they themselves put the Son of God on the cross again, openly shaming him.

6.msb: For land that drinks in the rain often falling on it and that produces a crop useful to those for whom it is tended receives the blessing of God.
6.kjv: For the earth which drinketh in the rain that cometh oft upon it, and bringeth forth herbs meet for them by whom it is dressed, receiveth blessing from God:
6.blb: For land having drunk in the rain coming often upon it and producing vegetation useful for those because of whom also it is tilled partakes of blessing from God.
6.bbe: For a land, drinking in the frequent rain and producing good plants for those for whom it is worked, has a blessing from God:

6.msb: But land that produces thorns and thistles is worthless, and its curse is imminent. In the end it will be burned.
6.kjv: But that which beareth thorns and briers is rejected, and is nigh unto cursing; whose end is to be burned.
6.blb: But that bringing out thorns and thistles is unapproved and near to a curse, of which the end is unto burning.
6.bbe: But if it sends up thorns and evil plants, it is of no use and is ready to be cursed; its only end is to be burned.

6.msb: Even though we speak like this, beloved, we are convinced of better things in your case—things that accompany salvation.
6.kjv: But, beloved, we are persuaded better things of you, and things that accompany salvation, though we thus speak.
6.blb: But even if we speak thus. beloved, we are persuaded of better things concerning you, and things belonging to salvation.
6.bbe: But, my loved ones, though we say this, we are certain that you have better things in you, things which go with salvation;

6.msb: For God is not unjust. He will not forget your work and the labor of love you have shown for His name as you have ministered to the saints and continue to do so.
6.kjv: For God is not unrighteous to forget your work and labour of love, which ye have shewed toward his name, in that ye have ministered to the saints, and do minister.
6.blb: For God is not unjust to forget your work and the love that you showed for His name, having ministered to the saints, and still ministering.
6.bbe: For God is true, and will not put away from him the memory of your work and of your love for his name, in the help which you gave and still give to the saints.

6.msb: We want each of you to show this same diligence to the very end, in order to make your hope sure.
6.kjv: And we desire that every one of you do shew the same diligence to the full assurance of hope unto the end:
6.blb: And we desire each of you to show the same diligence toward the full assurance of the hope until the end,
6.bbe: And it is our desire that you may all keep the same high purpose in certain hope to the end:

6.msb: Then you will not be sluggish, but will imitate those who through faith and patience inherit what has been promised.
6.kjv: That ye be not slothful, but followers of them who through faith and patience inherit the promises.
6.blb: so that you may not be sluggish, but imitators of those through faith and patience inheriting the promises.
6.bbe: So that you may not be slow in heart, but may take as your example those to whom God has given their heritage, because of their faith and their long waiting.

6.msb: When God made His promise to Abraham, since He had no one greater to swear by, He swore by Himself,
6.kjv: For when God made promise to Abraham, because he could swear by no greater, he sware by himself,
6.blb: For God, having made the promise to Abraham, since He had no one greater to swear by, He swore by Himself,
6.bbe: For when God made his oath to Abraham, because there was no greater oath, he made it by himself,
6.heading: God’s Unchangeable Promise

6.msb: saying, “I will surely bless you and multiply your descendants.”
6.kjv: Saying, Surely blessing I will bless thee, and multiplying I will multiply thee.
6.blb: saying, “Surely blessing I will bless you, and multiplying I will multiply you.”
6.bbe: Saying, Be certain that I will give you my blessing, and make your numbers very great.

6.msb: And so Abraham, after waiting patiently, obtained the promise.
6.kjv: And so, after he had patiently endured, he obtained the promise.
6.blb: And thus having waited patiently, he obtained the promise.
6.bbe: And so, when he had been waiting calmly for a long time, God's word to him was put into effect.

6.msb: Men indeed swear by someone greater than themselves, and their oath serves as a confirmation to end all argument.
6.kjv: For men verily swear by the greater: and an oath for confirmation is to them an end of all strife.
6.blb: For men swear by the greater, and of all their disputes, an end for confirmation is the oath,
6.bbe: For men at all times make their oaths by what is greater; and any argument is ended by the decision of the oath.

6.msb: So when God wanted to make the unchanging nature of His purpose very clear to the heirs of the promise, He guaranteed it with an oath.
6.kjv: Where in God, willing more abundantly to shew unto the heirs of promise the immutability of his counsel, confirmed it by an oath:
6.blb: in which God, willing to show more abundantly the unchangeableness of His purpose to the heirs of the promise, guaranteed it by an oath,
6.bbe: So that when it was God's desire to make it specially clear to those who by his word were to have the heritage, that his purpose was fixed, he made it more certain with an oath;

6.msb: Thus by two unchangeable things in which it is impossible for God to lie, we who have fled to take hold of the hope set before us may be strongly encouraged.
6.kjv: That by two immutable things, in which it was impossible for God to lie, we might have a strong consolation, who have fled for refuge to lay hold upon the hope set before us:
6.blb: so that by two unchangeable things, in which it is impossible for God to lie, we may have strong encouragement, having fled for refuge to take hold of the hope being set before us,
6.bbe: So that we, who have gone in flight from danger to the hope which has been put before us, may have a strong comfort in two unchanging things, in which it is not possible for God to be false;

6.msb: We have this hope as an anchor for the soul, firm and secure. It enters the inner sanctuary behind the curtain,
6.kjv: Which hope we have as an anchor of the soul, both sure and stedfast, and which entereth into that within the veil;
6.blb: which we have as an anchor of the soul, both sure and firm and entering into that within the veil,
6.bbe: And this hope is like a strong band for our souls, fixed and certain, and going in to that which is inside the veil;

6.msb: where Jesus our forerunner has entered on our behalf. He has become a high priest forever in the order of Melchizedek.
6.kjv: Whither the forerunner is for us entered, even Jesus, made an high priest for ever after the order of Melchisedec.
6.blb: where Jesus, the forerunner for us, entered according to the order of Melchizedek, having become a high priest to the age.
6.bbe: Where Jesus has gone before us, as a high priest for ever after the order of Melchizedek.

7.msb: This Melchizedek was king of Salem and priest of God Most High. He met Abraham returning from the slaughter of the kings and blessed him,
7.kjv: For this Melchisedec, king of Salem, priest of the most high God, who met Abraham returning from the slaughter of the kings, and blessed him;
7.blb: For this Melchizedek, king of Salem, priest of God Most High, the one having met Abraham returning from the slaughter of the kings and having blessed him,
7.bbe: For this Melchizedek, the king of Salem, a priest of the Most High God, who gave Abraham his blessing, meeting him when he came back after putting the kings to death,
7.heading: Melchizedek and Abraham

7.msb: and Abraham apportioned to him a tenth of everything. First, his name means “king of righteousness.” Then also, “king of Salem” means “king of peace.”
7.kjv: To whom also Abraham gave a tenth part of all; first being by interpretation King of righteousness, and after that also King of Salem, which is, King of peace;
7.blb: to whom also Abraham apportioned a tenth of all, first indeed being translated, “king of righteousness;” and then also, “king of Salem,” which is, “king of peace,”
7.bbe: And to whom Abraham gave a tenth part of everything which he had, being first named King of righteousness, and then in addition, King of Salem, that is to say, King of peace;

7.msb: Without father or mother or genealogy, without beginning of days or end of life, like the Son of God, he remains a priest for all time.
7.kjv: Without father, without mother, without descent, having neither beginning of days, nor end of life; but made like unto the Son of God; abideth a priest continually.
7.blb: without father, without mother, without genealogy, having neither beginning of days nor end of life, but having been made like the Son of God, remains a priest in perpetuity.
7.bbe: Being without father or mother, or family, having no birth or end to his life, being made like the Son of God, is a priest for ever.

7.msb: Consider how great Melchizedek was: Even the patriarch Abraham gave him a tenth of the plunder.
7.kjv: Now consider how great this man was, unto whom even the patriarch Abraham gave the tenth of the spoils.
7.blb: Now behold how great this one was, to whom even Abraham the patriarch gave a tenth out of the best spoils.
7.bbe: Now see how great this man was, to whom our father Abraham gave a tenth part of what he had got in the fight.

7.msb: Now the law commands the sons of Levi who become priests to collect a tenth from the people—that is, from their brothers—though they too are descended from Abraham.
7.kjv: And verily they that are of the sons of Levi, who receive the office of the priesthood, have a commandment to take tithes of the people according to the law, that is, of their brethren, though they come out of the loins of Abraham:
7.blb: And indeed, those out from the sons of Levi receiving the priesthood have a commandment to take a tenth from the people, according to the law—that is, from their brothers, though having come forth out of the loin of Abraham.
7.bbe: And it is true that by the law, those of the sons of Levi who have the position of priests may take a tenth part of the people's goods; that is to say, they take it from their brothers though these are the sons of Abraham.

7.msb: But Melchizedek, who did not trace his descent from Levi, collected a tenth from Abraham and blessed him who had the promises.
7.kjv: But he whose descent is not counted from them received tithes of Abraham, and blessed him that had the promises.
7.blb: But the one not tracing his descent out from them has collected a tenth from Abraham and has blessed the one having the promises.
7.bbe: But this man, who was not of their family, took the tenth from Abraham, and gave a blessing to him to whom God had given his undertaking.

7.msb: And indisputably, the lesser is blessed by the greater.
7.kjv: And without all contradiction the less is blessed of the better.
7.blb: And apart from all dispute, the lesser is blessed by the greater.
7.bbe: But there is no doubt that the less gets his blessing from the greater.

7.msb: In the case of the Levites, mortal men collect the tenth; but in the case of Melchizedek, it is affirmed that he lives on.
7.kjv: And here men that die receive tithes; but there he receiveth them, of whom it is witnessed that he liveth.
7.blb: And here indeed, dying men receive the tenths; but there, it is being testified that he lives.
7.bbe: Now at the present time, men over whom death has power take the tenth; but then it was taken by one of whom it is witnessed that he is living.

7.msb: And so to speak, Levi, who collects the tenth, paid the tenth through Abraham.
7.kjv: And as I may so say, Levi also, who receiveth tithes, payed tithes in Abraham.
7.blb: and so to say a word, even Levi, the one receiving the tenths, has paid the tenth through Abraham.
7.bbe: And we may say that in Abraham, even Levi, who has a right to take the tenth part, gave it;

7.msb: For when Melchizedek met Abraham, Levi was still in the loin of his ancestor.
7.kjv: For he was yet in the loins of his father, when Melchisedec met him.
7.blb: For he was still in the loin of his father when Melchizedek met him.
7.bbe: Because he was still in his father's body when Melchizedek came to him.

7.msb: Now if perfection could have been attained through the Levitical priesthood (for on this basis the people received the law), why was there still need for another priest to appear—one in the order of Melchizedek and not in the order of Aaron?
7.kjv: If therefore perfection were by the Levitical priesthood, (for under it the people received the law,) what further need was there that another priest should rise after the order of Melchisedec, and not be called after the order of Aaron?
7.blb: Then indeed, if perfection were by the Levitical priesthood (for upon it the people had received the law) what need was still for another priest to arise, according to the order of Melchizedek and not to be called according to the order of Aaron?
7.bbe: Now if it was possible for things to be made complete through the priests of the house of Levi (for the law was given to the people in connection with them), what need was there for another priest who was of the order of Melchizedek and not of the order of Aaron?
7.heading: A Superior Priesthood

7.msb: For when the priesthood is changed, the law must be changed as well.
7.kjv: For the priesthood being changed, there is made of necessity a change also of the law.
7.blb: For the priesthood being changed, out of necessity a change of law also takes place.
7.bbe: Because if the priests are changed, it is necessary to make a change in the law.

7.msb: He of whom these things are said belonged to a different tribe, from which no one has ever served at the altar.
7.kjv: For he of whom these things are spoken pertaineth to another tribe, of which no man gave attendance at the altar.
7.blb: For he of whom these things are said belonged to another tribe, from which no one has attended at the altar.
7.bbe: For he of whom these things are said comes of another tribe, of which no man has ever made offerings at the altar.

7.msb: For it is clear that our Lord descended from Judah, a tribe as to which Moses said nothing about priesthood.
7.kjv: For it is evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda; of which tribe Moses spake nothing concerning priesthood.
7.blb: For it is evident that our Lord has sprung out of Judah, a tribe in regard to which Moses spoke nothing about priests.
7.bbe: Because it is clear that our Lord comes out of Judah, and Moses said nothing about priests from that tribe.

7.msb: And this point is even more clear if another priest like Melchizedek appears,
7.kjv: And it is yet far more evident: for that after the similitude of Melchisedec there ariseth another priest,
7.blb: And it is yet more abundantly evident if another priest according to the likeness of Melchizedek arises,
7.bbe: And this is even more clear if a second priest has come up who is like Melchizedek,

7.msb: one who has become a priest not by a law of succession, but by the power of an indestructible life.
7.kjv: Who is made, not after the law of a carnal commandment, but after the power of an endless life.
7.blb: who has become such not according to a law of a fleshly commandment, but according to the power of an indestructible life.
7.bbe: That is to say, not made by a law based on the flesh, but by the power of a life without end:

7.msb: For it is testified: “You are a priest forever in the order of Melchizedek.”
7.kjv: For he testifieth, Thou art a priest for ever after the order of Melchisedec.
7.blb: For it is testified: “You are a priest to the age, according to the order of Melchizedek.”
7.bbe: For it has been witnessed of him, You are a priest for ever after the order of Melchizedek.

7.msb: So the former commandment is set aside because it was weak and useless
7.kjv: For there is verily a disannulling of the commandment going before for the weakness and unprofitableness thereof.
7.blb: For indeed, there is a putting away of the preceding commandment because of its weakness and uselessness
7.bbe: So the law which went before is put on one side, because it was feeble and without profit.

7.msb: (for the law made nothing perfect), and a better hope is introduced, by which we draw near to God.
7.kjv: For the law made nothing perfect, but the bringing in of a better hope did; by the which we draw nigh unto God.
7.blb: (for the law perfected nothing), and the introduction of a better hope, by which we draw near to God.
7.bbe: (Because the law made nothing complete), and in its place there is a better hope, through which we come near to God.

7.msb: And none of this happened without an oath. For others became priests without an oath,
7.kjv: And inasmuch as not without an oath he was made priest:
7.blb: And inasmuch as it was not without an oath (for those indeed apart from an oath are become priests),
7.bbe: And as this is not without the taking of an oath

7.msb: but Jesus became a priest with an oath by the One who said to Him: “The Lord has sworn and will not change His mind: ‘You are a priest forever in the order of Melchizedek.’”
7.kjv: (For those priests were made without an oath; but this with an oath by him that said unto him, The Lord sware and will not repent, Thou art a priest for ever after the order of Melchisedec:)
7.blb: the One, however, was with an oath through the One saying to Him: “The Lord has sworn and will not change His mind; ‘You are a priest to the age.’”
7.bbe: (For those were made priests without an oath, but this one was made a priest with an oath by him who says of him, The Lord gave his oath, which he will not take back, that you are a priest for ever);

7.msb: Because of this oath, Jesus has become the guarantee of a better covenant.
7.kjv: By so much was Jesus made a surety of a better testament.
7.blb: By so much also, Jesus has become the guarantee of a better covenant.
7.bbe: By so much is it a better agreement which we have through Jesus.

7.msb: Now there have been many other priests, since death prevented them from continuing in office.
7.kjv: And they truly were many priests, because they were not suffered to continue by reason of death:
7.blb: And indeed those having become priests are many, because of by death being prevented from continuing.
7.bbe: And it is true that there have been a great number of those priests, because death does not let them go on for ever;

7.msb: But because Jesus lives forever, He has a permanent priesthood.
7.kjv: But this man, because he continueth ever, hath an unchangeable priesthood.
7.blb: But because of His remaining to the age, He has the permanent priesthood,
7.bbe: But this priest, because his life goes on for ever, is unchanging.

7.msb: Therefore He is able to save completely those who draw near to God through Him, since He always lives to intercede for them.
7.kjv: Wherefore he is able also to save them to the uttermost that come unto God by him, seeing he ever liveth to make intercession for them.
7.blb: wherefore also He is able to save to the uttermost those drawing near to God through Him, always living to intercede for them.
7.bbe: So that he is fully able to be the saviour of all who come to God through him, because he is ever living to make prayer to God for them.

7.msb: Such a high priest truly befits us—One who is holy, innocent, undefiled, set apart from sinners, and exalted above the heavens.
7.kjv: For such an high priest became us, who is holy, harmless, undefiled, separate from sinners, and made higher than the heavens;
7.blb: For such for us indeed was fitting—a high priest holy, innocent, undefiled, having been separated from sinners, and having become higher than the heavens,
7.bbe: It was right for us to have such a high priest, one who is holy and without evil, doing no wrong, having no part with sinners, and made higher than the heavens:

7.msb: Unlike the other high priests, He does not need to offer daily sacrifices, first for His own sins and then for the sins of the people; He sacrificed for sin once for all when He offered up Himself.
7.kjv: Who needeth not daily, as those high priests, to offer up sacrifice, first for his own sins, and then for the people’s: for this he did once, when he offered up himself.
7.blb: who has no need every day, as the first high priests, to offer up sacrifices for his own sins, then for those of the people; for He did this once for all, having offered up Himself.
7.bbe: Who has no need to make offerings for sins every day, like those high priests, first for himself, and then for the people; because he did this once and for ever when he made an offering of himself.

7.msb: For the law appoints as high priests men who are weak; but the oath, which came after the law, appointed the Son, who has been made perfect forever.
7.kjv: For the law maketh men high priests which have infirmity; but the word of the oath, which was since the law, maketh the Son, who is consecrated for evermore.
7.blb: For the law appoints as high priests men having weakness; but the word of the oath, which is after the law, appoints a Son having been perfected to the age.
7.bbe: The law makes high priests of men who are feeble; but the word of the oath, which was made after the law, gives that position to a Son, in whom all good is for ever complete.

8.msb: The point of what we are saying is this: We do have such a high priest, who sat down at the right hand of the throne of the Majesty in heaven,
8.kjv: Now of the things which we have spoken this is the sum: We have such an high priest, who is set on the right hand of the throne of the Majesty in the heavens;
8.blb: Now the main point of the things being said: We have such a high priest, who sat down at the right hand of the throne of the Majesty in the heavens,
8.bbe: Now of the things we are saying this is the chief point: We have such a high priest, who has taken his place at the right hand of God's high seat of glory in heaven,
8.heading: Christ’s Eternal Priesthood

8.msb: and who ministers in the sanctuary and true tabernacle set up by the Lord, not by man.
8.kjv: A minister of the sanctuary, and of the true tabernacle, which the Lord pitched, and not man.
8.blb: a minister in the holy places and in the true tabernacle, which the Lord pitched, not man.
8.bbe: As a servant of the holy things and of the true Tent, which was put up by God, not by man.

8.msb: And since every high priest is appointed to offer both gifts and sacrifices, it was necessary for this One also to have something to offer.
8.kjv: For every high priest is ordained to offer gifts and sacrifices: wherefore it is of necessity that this man have somewhat also to offer.
8.blb: For every high priest is appointed in order to offer both gifts and sacrifices, wherefore it was necessary for this One also to have something that He might offer.
8.bbe: Now every high priest is given authority to take to God the things which are given and to make offerings; so that it is necessary for this man, like them, to have something for an offering.

8.msb: For if He were on earth, He would not be a priest, since there are already priests who offer gifts according to the law.
8.kjv: For if he were on earth, he should not be a priest, seeing that there are priests that offer gifts according to the law:
8.blb: Then indeed, if He were on earth, not even would He be a priest, there being those offering the gifts according to law,
8.bbe: If he had been on earth he would not have been a priest at all, because there are other priests who make the offerings ordered by the law;

8.msb: The place where they serve is a copy and shadow of what is in heaven. This is why Moses was warned when he was about to build the tabernacle: “See to it that you make everything according to the pattern shown you on the mountain.”
8.kjv: Who serve unto the example and shadow of heavenly things, as Moses was admonished of God when he was about to make the tabernacle: for, See, saith he, that thou make all things according to the pattern shewed to thee in the mount.
8.blb: who serve as an example and shadow of the heavenly things, just as Moses was divinely warned being about to complete the tabernacle. For He says, “See that you will make all things according to the pattern having been shown to you in the mountain.”
8.bbe: Being servants of that which is a copy and an image of the things in heaven, as Moses, when he was about to make the Tent, had special orders from God: for, See, he said, that you make everything like the design which you saw in the mountain.

8.msb: Now, however, Jesus has received a much more excellent ministry, just as the covenant He mediates is better and is founded on better promises.
8.kjv: But now hath he obtained a more excellent ministry, by how much also he is the mediator of a better covenant, which was established upon better promises.
8.blb: But now He has obtained a more excellent ministry, as much as He is also the mediator of a better covenant, which has been enacted upon better promises.
8.bbe: But now his position as priest is higher. because through him God has made a better agreement with man, based on the giving of better things.
8.heading: The New Covenant

8.msb: For if that first covenant had been without fault, no place would have been sought for a second.
8.kjv: For if that first covenant had been faultless, then should no place have been sought for the second.
8.blb: For if that first had been faultless, no place would have been sought for a second.
8.bbe: For if that first agreement had been as good as possible, there would have been no place for a second.

8.msb: But God found fault with the people and said: “Behold, the days are coming, declares the Lord, when I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah.
8.kjv: For finding fault with them, he saith, Behold, the days come, saith the Lord, when I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah:
8.blb: For finding fault with them, He says: “Behold, the days are coming, says the Lord, and I will complete with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah a new covenant,
8.bbe: For, protesting against them, he says, See, the days are coming when I will make a new agreement with the house of Israel, and with the house of Judah;

8.msb: It will not be like the covenant I made with their fathers when I took them by the hand to lead them out of the land of Egypt, because they did not abide by My covenant, and I disregarded them, declares the Lord.
8.kjv: Not according to the covenant that I made with their fathers in the day when I took them by the hand to lead them out of the land of Egypt; because they continued not in my covenant, and I regarded them not, saith the Lord.
8.blb: not according to the covenant that I made with their fathers, in the day of My having taken hold of their hand to lead them out of the land of Egypt, because they did not continue in My covenant, and I disregarded them, says the Lord.
8.bbe: Not like the agreement which I made with their fathers when I took them by the hand, to be their guide out of the land of Egypt; for they did not keep the agreement with me, and I gave them up, says the Lord.

8.msb: For this is the covenant I will make with the house of Israel after those days, declares the Lord. I will put My laws in their minds and inscribe them on their hearts. And I will be their God, and they will be My people.
8.kjv: For this is the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel after those days, saith the Lord; I will put my laws into their mind, and write them in their hearts: and I will be to them a God, and they shall be to me a people:
8.blb: For this is the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel after those days, says the Lord, giving My laws into their mind, and I will inscribe them upon their hearts; and I will be unto them God, and they will be unto Me for a people.
8.bbe: For this is the agreement which I will make with the people of Israel after those days: I will put my laws into their minds, writing them in their hearts: and I will be their God, and they will be my people:

8.msb: No longer will each one teach his neighbor or his brother, saying, ‘Know the Lord,’ because they will all know Me, from the least of them to the greatest.
8.kjv: And they shall not teach every man his neighbour, and every man his brother, saying, Know the Lord: for all shall know me, from the least to the greatest.
8.blb: And they shall not teach, each his neighbor and each his brother, saying, ‘Know the Lord,’ because all will know Me, from the small to the great of them,
8.bbe: And there will be no need for every man to be teaching his brother, or his neighbour, saying, This is the knowledge of the Lord: for they will all have knowledge of me, great and small.

8.msb: For I will forgive their iniquities and will remember their sins and lawless acts no more.”
8.kjv: For I will be merciful to their unrighteousness, and their sins and their iniquities will I remember no more.
8.blb: because I will be merciful toward their iniquities, and I shall remember their sins no more.
8.bbe: And I will have mercy on their evil-doing, and I will not keep their sins in mind.

8.msb: By speaking of a new covenant, He has made the first one obsolete; and what is obsolete and aging will soon disappear.
8.kjv: In that he saith, A new covenant, he hath made the first old. Now that which decayeth and waxeth old is ready to vanish away.
8.blb: In saying, “new,” He has made old the first; and that which is growing old and aging is near to vanishing.
8.bbe: When he says, A new agreement, he has made the first agreement old. But anything which is getting old and past use will not be seen much longer.

9.msb: Now even the first covenant had regulations for worship and also an earthly sanctuary.
9.kjv: Then verily the first covenant had also ordinances of divine service, and a worldly sanctuary.
9.blb: Therefore also indeed, the first had ordinances of sacred service and a worldly sanctuary.
9.bbe: Now the first agreement had its rules of worship, and a holy order.
9.heading: The Earthly Tabernacle

9.msb: A tabernacle was prepared. In its first room were the lampstand, the table, and the consecrated bread. This was called the Holy Place.
9.kjv: For there was a tabernacle made; the first, wherein was the candlestick, and the table, and the shewbread; which is called the sanctuary.
9.blb: For a tabernacle was prepared, the first room in which were both the lampstand and the table, and the loaves of the presentation, which is called “Holy.”
9.bbe: For the first Tent was made ready, having in it the vessels for the lights and the table and the ordering of the bread; and this is named the holy place.

9.msb: Behind the second curtain was a room called the Most Holy Place,
9.kjv: And after the second veil, the tabernacle which is called the Holiest of all;
9.blb: Now behind the second veil was a tabernacle, being called “Holy of Holies,”
9.bbe: And inside the second veil was the place which is named the Holy of holies;

9.msb: containing the golden altar of incense and the gold-covered ark of the covenant. Inside the ark were the gold jar of manna, Aaron’s staff that had budded, and the stone tablets of the covenant.
9.kjv: Which had the golden censer, and the ark of the covenant overlaid round about with gold, wherein was the golden pot that had manna, and Aaron’s rod that budded, and the tables of the covenant;
9.blb: having the golden altar of incense and the ark of the covenant having been covered around in every part with gold, in which was the golden jar having the manna, and the staff of Aaron having budded, and the tablets of the covenant.
9.bbe: Having a vessel of gold in it for burning perfumes, and the ark of the agreement, which was covered with gold and which had in it a pot made of gold for the manna, and Aaron's rod which put out buds, and the stones with the writing of the agreement;

9.msb: Above the ark were the cherubim of glory, overshadowing the mercy seat. But we cannot discuss these things in detail now.
9.kjv: And over it the cherubims of glory shadowing the mercyseat; of which we can not now speak particularly.
9.blb: And far above it were the cherubim of glory, overshadowing the mercy seat—concerning which it is not now time to speak particularly.
9.bbe: And over it were the winged ones of glory with their wings covering the mercy-seat; about which it is not possible now to say anything in detail.

9.msb: When everything had been prepared in this way, the priests entered regularly into the first room to perform their sacred duties.
9.kjv: Now when these things were thus ordained, the priests went always into the first tabernacle, accomplishing the service of God.
9.blb: Now these things having been prepared thus, indeed the priests enter into the first tabernacle at all times, accomplishing the sacred services,
9.bbe: Now while these things were in existence, the priests went into the first Tent at all times, for prayer and the making of offerings.

9.msb: But only the high priest entered the second room, and then only once a year, and never without blood, which he offered for himself and for the sins the people had committed in ignorance.
9.kjv: But into the second went the high priest alone once every year, not without blood, which he offered for himself, and for the errors of the people:
9.blb: but only the high priest into the second, once in the year, not without blood, which he offers for himself and for the sins of ignorance of the people.
9.bbe: But only the high priest went into the second, once a year, not without making an offering of blood for himself and for the errors of the people:

9.msb: By this arrangement the Holy Spirit was showing that the way into the Most Holy Place had not yet been disclosed as long as the first tabernacle was still standing.
9.kjv: The Holy Ghost this signifying, that the way into the holiest of all was not yet made manifest, while as the first tabernacle was yet standing:
9.blb: By this the Holy Spirit was making clear that the way into the holy places had not yet been made manifest, the first tabernacle still having a standing,
9.bbe: The Holy Spirit witnessing by this that the way into the holy place had not at that time been made open, while the first Tent was still in being;

9.msb: It is an illustration for the present time, because the gifts and sacrifices being offered were unable to cleanse the conscience of the worshiper.
9.kjv: Which was a figure for the time then present, in which were offered both gifts and sacrifices, that could not make him that did the service perfect, as pertaining to the conscience;
9.blb: which is a parable for the present time, in which both gifts and sacrifices are offered, not being able to make perfect in regard to conscience the one doing sacred service,
9.bbe: And this is an image of the present time; when the offerings which are given are not able to make the heart of the worshipper completely clean,

9.msb: They consist only in food and drink and special washings and external regulations imposed until the time of reform.
9.kjv: Which stood only in meats and drinks, and divers washings, and carnal ordinances, imposed on them until the time of reformation.
9.blb: consisting only in foods and drinks and various washings—ordinances of the flesh being imposed until the time of reformation.
9.bbe: Because they are only rules of the flesh, of meats and drinks and washings, which have their place till the time comes when things will be put right.

9.msb: But when Christ came as high priest of the good things to come, He went through the greater and more perfect tabernacle that is not made by hands and is not a part of this creation.
9.kjv: But Christ being come an high priest of good things to come, by a greater and more perfect tabernacle, not made with hands, that is to say, not of this building;
9.blb: But Christ, having come as high priest of the good things coming, through the greater and more perfect tabernacle not made by hands, that is, not of this creation,
9.bbe: But now Christ has come as the high priest of the good things of the future, through this greater and better Tent, not made with hands, that is to say, not of this world,
9.heading: Redemption through His Blood

9.msb: He did not enter by the blood of goats and calves, but He entered the Most Holy Place once for all by His own blood, thus securing eternal redemption.
9.kjv: Neither by the blood of goats and calves, but by his own blood he entered in once into the holy place, having obtained eternal redemption for us.
9.blb: nor by blood of goats and calves, but through His own blood, He entered once for all into the holy places, having obtained eternal redemption.
9.bbe: And has gone once and for ever into the holy place, having got eternal salvation, not through the blood of goats and young oxen, but through his blood.

9.msb: For if the blood of bulls and goats and the ashes of a heifer sprinkled on those who are ceremonially unclean sanctify them so that their bodies are clean,
9.kjv: For if the blood of bulls and of goats, and the ashes of an heifer sprinkling the unclean, sanctifieth to the purifying of the flesh:
9.blb: For if the blood of goats and of bulls and the ashes of a heifer sprinkling the ones having been defiled sanctify them for the purification of the flesh,
9.bbe: For if the blood of goats and oxen, and the dust from the burning of a young cow, being put on the unclean, make the flesh clean:

9.msb: how much more will the blood of Christ, who through the eternal Spirit offered Himself unblemished to God, purify your consciences from works of death, so that we may serve the living God!
9.kjv: How much more shall the blood of Christ, who through the eternal Spirit offered himself without spot to God, purge your conscience from dead works to serve the living God?
9.blb: how much more will the blood of Christ, who through the eternal Spirit offered Himself unblemished to God, purify our conscience from dead works, in order to serve the living God!
9.bbe: How much more will the blood of Christ, who, being without sin, made an offering of himself to God through the Holy Spirit, make your hearts clean from dead works to be servants of the living God?

9.msb: Therefore Christ is the mediator of a new covenant, so that those who are called may receive the promised eternal inheritance, now that He has died to redeem them from the transgressions committed under the first covenant.
9.kjv: And for this cause he is the mediator of the new testament, that by means of death, for the redemption of the transgressions that were under the first testament, they which are called might receive the promise of eternal inheritance.
9.blb: And because of this, He is the mediator of a new covenant, so that, death having taken place for redemption of the transgressions upon the first covenant, those having been called might receive the promise of the eternal inheritance.
9.bbe: And for this cause it is through him that a new agreement has come into being, so that after the errors under the first agreement had been taken away by his death, the word of God might have effect for those who were marked out for an eternal heritage.

9.msb: In the case of a will, it is necessary to establish the death of the one who made it,
9.kjv: For where a testament is, there must also of necessity be the death of the testator.
9.blb: For where there is a covenant, there is a necessity to bring forth the death of the one having made it.
9.bbe: Because where there is a testament, there has to be the death of the man who made it.

9.msb: because a will does not take effect until the one who made it has died; it cannot be executed while he is still alive.
9.kjv: For a testament is of force after men are dead: otherwise it is of no strength at all while the testator liveth.
9.blb: For a covenant is firm upon death, since it is not in force at the time when the one having made it is living,
9.bbe: For a testament has effect after death; for what power has it while the man who made it is living?

9.msb: That is why even the first covenant was not put into effect without blood.
9.kjv: Whereupon neither the first testament was dedicated without blood.
9.blb: wherefore neither has the first been inaugurated without blood.
9.bbe: So that even the first agreement was not made without blood.

9.msb: For when Moses had proclaimed every commandment of the law to all the people, he took the blood of calves and goats, along with water, scarlet wool, and hyssop, and sprinkled the scroll and all the people,
9.kjv: For when Moses had spoken every precept to all the people according to the law, he took the blood of calves and of goats, with water, and scarlet wool, and hyssop, and sprinkled both the book, and all the people,
9.blb: For on every commandment having been spoken by Moses to all the people according to the law, having taken the blood of calves and of goats, with water and scarlet wool and hyssop, he sprinkled both the scroll itself and all the people,
9.bbe: For when Moses had given all the rules of the law to the people, he took the blood of goats and young oxen, with water and red wool and hyssop, and put it on the book itself and on all the people,

9.msb: saying, “This is the blood of the covenant, which God has commanded you to keep.”
9.kjv: Saying, This is the blood of the testament which God hath enjoined unto you.
9.blb: saying, “This is the blood of the covenant, which God commanded to you.”
9.bbe: Saying, This blood is the sign of the agreement which God has made with you.

9.msb: In the same way, he sprinkled with blood the tabernacle and all the vessels used in worship.
